## What is NATS
- path: nats-concepts/what-is-nats/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/what-is-nats
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [TOPO][SIZE] The NATS service infrastructure scales from a single nats-server on an end device to a global super-cluster; "the `nats-server` process is less than 20 MB in size!"
- [CLNT][SEC] A client needs only a NATS URL (IP/port + connection kind: plain TCP, TLS, or WebSocket) and, if needed, authentication (username/password, decentralized JWT, token, TLS certificates, NKey with challenge).
- [CORE] Messages are addressed by subject strings and "do not depend on network location".
- [CORE][MYTH] Core NATS is at-most-once: if no subscriber matches or the subscriber is not active when sent, the message is not received. "This is the same level of guarantee that TCP/IP provides."
- [CORE][ANTI] Core NATS "is a fire-and-forget messaging system. It will only hold messages in memory and will never write messages directly to disk."
- [STRM] For at-least-once / exactly-once, persistent streaming, de-coupled flow control, and Key/Value, use JetStream, which is built into the server "but needs to be enabled".
- [PATTERN] You can also add reliability in the client yourself "with proven and scalable reference designs such as acks and sequence numbers".

## Compare NATS
- path: nats-concepts/overview/compare-nats.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/overview/compare-nats
- version context: unstated (mentions NATS Streaming; [STALE?])

### Claims
- [MIG] Comparison covers NATS, Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, Apache Pulsar, gRPC; "by no means an exhaustive list".
- [MIG][SIZE][STALE?] "Core NATS: 48 known client types, 11 supported by maintainers, 18 contributed by the community. NATS Streaming: 7 client types supported by maintainers".
- [MIG][CORE] NATS offers streams and services via built-in pub/sub, request-reply, and load-balanced queue subscribers, with "Dynamic request permissioning and request subject obfuscation". Kafka/Pulsar/Rabbit: "Application code must correlate requests with replies over multiple topics" for request-reply.
- [MIG] Delivery guarantees: NATS "At most once, at least once, and exactly once is available in JetStream"; Kafka and Pulsar same three; Rabbit at most once and at least once; gRPC at most once.
- [MIG][SEC] "NATS supports true multi-tenancy and decentralized security through accounts and defining shared streams and services." Kafka: "Multi-tenancy is not supported." Pulsar tenants: no built-in cross-tenant data sharing. Rabbit vhosts: no data sharing.
- [MIG][SEC] NATS AuthZ: account limits (connections, message size, imports/exports count), user-level pub/sub permissions, connection restrictions, CIDR restrictions, time-of-day restrictions.
- [MIG][STRM] NATS persistence: memory and file; "Messages can be replayed by time, count, or sequence number, and durable subscriptions are supported." Rabbit: queue semantics, "no message replay is available".
- [MIG][TOPO] "Core NATS supports full mesh clustering with self-healing features"; "JetStream supports horizontal scalability with built-in mirroring." [STALE?] mentions NATS Streaming FT/full clustering.
- [MIG][TOPO] NATS server is "a small static binary" deployable from cloud instances to Raspberry Pi; single servers, leaf nodes, clusters, superclusters "can be combined in any fashion"; "Clients are unaware of topology and can connect to any NATS server".
- [MIG][SIZE] Kafka: "Clients are tied to partitions defined within clusters"; servers need a JVM, "eight cores, 64 GB to128 GB of RAM, two or more 8-TB SAS/SSD disks, and a 10-Gig NIC" (cites Cloudera sizing).
- [MIG][SIZE] Pulsar "requires a JVM and requires at least 6 Linux machines or VMs. 3 running ZooKeeper. 3 running a Pulsar broker and a BookKeeper bookie."
- [MIG][TOPO] RabbitMQ clusters "require low-latency networks where network partitions are rare"; server needs the Erlang VM.
- [MIG][OPS] NATS monitoring: Prometheus exporter, Grafana dashboards, nats-top, NATS surveyor ("side car deployment or a simple connect-and-view model").
- [MIG][OPS] "NATS separates operations from security. User and Account management in a deployment may be decentralized and managed through a CLI." Server config can be reloaded at runtime.
- [MIG] NATS integrations listed: WebSockets, Kafka bridge, IBM MQ Bridge, Redis Connector, Spark, Flink, Elastic, Prometheus, Telegraf, Fluent Bit/Fluentd, OpenFAAS, HTTP, MQTT.

## Subject-Based Messaging
- path: nats-concepts/subjects.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/subjects
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [SUBJ][CORE] NATS is "an `interest-based` messaging system, where the listener has to `subscribe` to a subset of `subjects`."
- [SUBJ] Other systems call subjects topics/channels/streams; in NATS "stream" means a JetStream message store.
- [SUBJ][TOPO] Location transparency: subscriptions "are automatically propagated within the server cloud", messages routed to all interested subscribers regardless of location, and "Messages with no subscribers to their subject are automatically discarded".
- [SUBJ] Publishers "will always send a message to a fully specified subject, without the wildcard"; only subscribers use wildcards.
- [SUBJ][SIZE] "There is no hard limit to subject size, but it is recommended to keep the maximum number of tokens in your subjects to a reasonable value. E.g. a maximum of 16 tokens and the subject length to less than 256 characters."
- [SUBJ][SIZE] "NATS can manage 10s of millions of subjects efficiently"; subjects are ephemeral and disappear when no longer subscribed.
- [SUBJ][SIZE][OPS] Subscriptions are cached in server memory: "when increasing your subscribed subject count to more than one million you will need more than 1GB of server memory and it will grow linearly from there."
- [SUBJ][SEC] Subject filtering happens in many places: per-user allow/deny, account import/export, automatic transformations, stream ingest, sourcing/mirroring, leaf node connections. "A well-designed subject hierarchy will make the job a lot easier".
- [SUBJ][ANTI] "you should refrain from over-complicating your subject design at the start of the project."
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Guidelines: first token(s) establish a general namespace (e.g. `factory1.tools.group42.unit17`); final token(s) are identifiers (e.g. `service.deploy.server-acme.app123`).
- [SUBJ] "A subject _should_ be used for more than one message." "Subscriptions _should_ be stable (exist for receiving more than one message)."
- [SUBJ] "Use wildcard subscriptions over subscribing to individual subjects whenever feasible."
- [SUBJ][ANTI] "Name business or physical entities. Refrain from encoding too much data into the subject." "Encode (business) intent into the subject, not technical details." Pragmatic: `orders.online.store123.order171711`; not useful: a 11-token subject encoding server, payment, tier, carrier, verb.
- [SUBJ] Headers can carry extra metadata; "There are subscription modes, which deliver headers only, allowing for efficient scanning of metadata".
- [SUBJ] `*` matches exactly one token and cannot match a substring inside a token (`time.New*.east` is invalid). `>` matches one or more tokens and only at the end. `*` may appear several times and be mixed with `>` (`*.*.east.>`).
- [SUBJ][OPS][PATTERN] Wire tap: subscribe to `>` to receive all messages, "subject to security settings", for monitoring.
- [SUBJ] Recommended characters for all user-created names (subjects, streams, durables, buckets, keys): alphanumeric, `-`, `_`; UTF-8 is supported "at your own risk". "NATS will enforce these constraints in most cases, but we recommend not relying on this."
- [SUBJ] Allowed: any Unicode except null, space, `.`, `*`, `>`. Names are case sensitive. Delimit words with PascalCase or `-`/`_`.
- [SUBJ] Names starting with `$` are reserved for system use (`$SYS`, `$JS`, `$KV`); many system subjects also use `_` (`_INBOX`, `KV_ABC`, `OBJ_XYZ`).
- [SUBJ][CLNT] By default subject names are not verified on publish; programmatically generated illegal subjects (e.g. containing wildcards) "may be ignored". Enable `pedantic` mode in the client to verify.

## Security (concept)
- path: nats-concepts/security.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/security
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [SEC] Authentication options: token, username/password, TLS certificate, NKEY with challenge, decentralized JWT, and auth callout to integrate an existing auth system.
- [SEC][PATTERN] Accounts provide multi-tenancy: "each account has its own independent 'subject namespace'" with controlled import/export of streams and services between accounts.
- [SEC] JWT administration is decentralized: account private key holders mint user JWTs themselves "without the need for any configuration change on the NATS servers"; the server never stores user private keys and only validates the signature chain of trust.
- [SEC][STRM] JetStream provides encryption at rest.

## NATS connectivity
- path: nats-concepts/connectivity.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/connectivity
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [CLNT] Direct connectivity kinds: plain NATS, TLS NATS, WebSocket, MQTT.
- [MIG] Bridges: Kafka Bridge (nats-kafka), JMS bridge (also covers MQ and RabbitMQ since both offer JMS).

## Acknowledgements (concept)
- path: nats-concepts/acks.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/acks
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [CORE][CLNT] With at-most-once semantics, request-reply "should use timeouts"; "It is always a good idea to place a timeout on a request and have code that deals with timeouts."
- [PATTERN] Turn a publish into request-reply with an ACK to make delivery known; "an ACK can simply be an empty message".
- [PATTERN] ACKs turn "fire-and-forget into a fire-and-know world"; with scatter-gather several receivers can ack.

## Sequence Numbers (concept)
- path: nats-concepts/seq_num.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/seq_num
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [PATTERN] Include a sequence id per message so receivers detect loss; "Sequence numbers combined with heartbeats, in the absence of new data, form a powerful and resilient pattern to detect loss."
- [PATTERN][ANTI] Persisted-message systems solve this too "but sometimes are overkill for the problem at hand and usually cause additional management and operational cost."
- [PATTERN] "Each sender will have to use their own sequence"; receivers should be able to ask for missing messages by id.
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Sequence ids can be a subject token (`updates.1`, `updates.2`, subscribe `updates.*`) when the payload cannot carry it.

## NATS Service Infrastructure
- path: nats-concepts/service_infrastructure.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/service_infrastructure
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [TOPO] Infrastructure ranges from one local process to "an 'Internet of NATS' of Leaf Nodes, and Leaf Node clusters all interconnected in a secure way over a global shared NATS super-cluster."
- [CLNT] Regardless of topology, clients need only NATS URLs and credentials.
- [TOPO] Go applications may embed the NATS server, but then need server configuration.
- [TOPO][PATTERN] Evolution path: single local server -> single server or cluster per VPC/region/on-prem -> connect them as leaf nodes to a backbone cluster/super-cluster, or directly via gateways -> clusters in multiple locations/providers joined into a global super-cluster plus "a scheme to intelligently direct your client applications to the right 'closest' NATS server cluster."
- [OPS] On Kubernetes, "we recommend you use the Helm charts" (nats-io/k8s).

## NATS Adaptive Deployment Architectures
- path: nats-concepts/adaptive_edge_deployment.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/adaptive_edge_deployment
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [TOPO] Single server: simplest deployment; nats-server is "highly optimized, very lightweight and extremely efficient".
- [TOPO] Cluster: "If you need a fault-tolerant NATS service or if you need to scale your service capacity"; clients hold a list of server URLs.
- [TOPO] Super-cluster: "disaster recovery and ... global deployments" by connecting clusters "via gateway connections (which are interest pruned)".
- [TOPO] Leaf nodes proxy/route between local clients and the infrastructure; locality can be physical, an edge device, a dev machine, a VPC, an app's process group, different accounts, or a business unit. Leaf nodes can connect over WebSocket.
- [TOPO][SEC] "Leaf nodes appear to the cluster as a single account connection."
- [TOPO] "Leaf nodes can provide continuous NATS service for their clients, even while being temporarily disconnected from the cluster(s)."
- [TOPO][STRM][PATTERN] JetStream on leaf nodes: local streams mirrored to global streams upstream; "mirroring is store and forward and therefore can recover from connectivity outages".
- [PATTERN] Video reference: "NATS Service Geo-affinity in Queues".

## Core NATS
- path: nats-concepts/core-nats/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/core-nats
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [CORE][PATTERN] Pub/sub with subject addressing gives "location independence and a default many-to-many (M:N) communication pattern", enabling microservices "without requiring additional technologies like load balancers, API gateways, or DNS configuration."
- [CORE][STRM] Core NATS is best-effort at-most-once; JetStream adds at-least-once and exactly-once.

## Publish-Subscribe / Messages
- path: nats-concepts/core-nats/publish-subscribe/pubsub.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/core-nats/publish-subscribe
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [CORE] Pub/sub is one-to-many (fan-out); wildcards "work a bit like a regular expression (but only a bit)".
- [CORE] A message has a subject, a byte-array payload, any number of headers, and an optional reply address.
- [CORE][SIZE] `max_payload` default is 1 MB, "can be increased up to 64 MB if needed (though we recommend keeping the max message size to something more reasonable like 8 MB)."

## Queue Groups
- path: nats-concepts/core-nats/queue-groups/queue.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/core-nats/queue-groups
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [CORE] Fan-out still reaches non-queue subscribers; among members of one queue group "only one randomly chosen subscriber of the queue group will consume a message".
- [CORE][PATTERN] Queue groups are built-in load balancing: fault tolerance, scale up/down "without duplicate messages", no configuration, defined by the application not the server.
- [CORE][SUBJ] Queue group names follow subject naming rules, are case sensitive, no whitespace; "Consider structuring queue groups hierarchically using a period" because queue permissions can wildcard-match them.
- [CORE][CLNT] Scale-down is "terminating the application with a signal that drains the in flight requests".
- [CORE] No responders: when no queue-group subscriber exists, the server sends a "no-responders" protocol message that breaks blocking request calls immediately.
- [STRM][CONS][PATTERN] "Stream as a queue": use `WorkQueuePolicy` retention with pull consumers for horizontal scaling, "or using an explicit ack push consumer with a queue group of subscribers" [STALE? push-consumer guidance].
- [TOPO][PATTERN] Queue geo-affinity in a super-cluster: "a service request message will only be routed to another cluster (i.e. another region) if there are no listeners on the cluster available to handle the request locally."

## Request-Reply
- path: nats-concepts/core-nats/request-reply/reqreply.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/core-nats/request-reply
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [CORE] Request-reply is built on pub/sub with a reply subject called an "inbox": unique subjects "dynamically directed back to the requester, regardless of the location of either party."
- [CORE] Responders form dynamic queue groups automatically; no manual membership management.
- [CLNT] "NATS applications 'drain before exiting'" so they can scale down without dropping requests.
- [OPS][PATTERN] Observability "is as simple as running another application that can view requests and responses to measure latency".
- [CORE][PATTERN] Multiple responses are allowed: "the first response is utilized and the system efficiently discards the additional ones" to reduce latency and jitter (scatter-gather).
- [CORE][CLNT] No-responders requires header-capable server and client; the requester immediately gets an empty reply with `503` status; clients surface it as an error (Go: `nats.ErrNoResponders`).

## JetStream (concept overview)
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream
- version context: unstated (mentions STAN replacement)

### Claims
- [STRM] JetStream captures messages and replays them; "Unlike NATS Core which requires you to have an active subscription to process messages as they happen".
- [STRM][TOPO] With a cluster of JetStream-enabled servers "you can enable data replication and thus guard against failures".
- [MIG] Stated motivation: existing streaming tech has "complexity, fragility, and a lack of scalability"; "no current streaming technology is truly multi-tenant, horizontally scalable, or supports multiple deployment models."
- [KV][OBJ] KV and Object Store are built on JetStream and "inherit the core capabilities of JetStream, replication, security, routing limits, and mirroring"; Object Store uses chunked transfers.
- [MIG][ANTI] "NATS does not intend to compete with the feature set of such tools" (in-memory DBs, deployment tools); goal is a reasonably complete data storage/replication set for microservices, edge, server management.
- [STRM] Design goals: easy to configure/operate/observe; secure with NATS 2.0 security; horizontally scalable at high ingestion rate; self-healing; payload agnostic; "must not have third party dependencies".
- [STRM][MYTH] Traditional temporal decoupling is imperfect: "durable subscribers need to be created before the messages get published"; "queues are meant for workload distribution and consumption, not to be used as a mechanism for message replay."
- [STRM] JetStream provides both consume-as-published (queueing) and replay-on-demand (streaming).
- [CONS] Replay options: all messages with replay policy `instant` or `original` ("at the rate they were published ... useful for example for staging production traffic"); last message; last per subject; from sequence; from start time.
- [STRM][SIZE] Stream limits: max message age, max total bytes, max message count, max individual message size, max number of consumers.
- [STRM] Discard policy is mandatory: discard old deletes oldest; discard new rejects and "the JetStream publish call returns an error indicating that a limit was reached".
- [STRM] Retention: `limits` (default, replay); `work queue` (removed as consumed, "exactly-once consumption"); `interest` (kept while consumers haven't delivered it). "regardless of the retention policy selected, the limits (and the discard policy) always apply."
- [STRM] Storage: memory or file; replication 1 (none), 2, or 3 "for Fault Tolerance" (contradicts R=5 max stated later on same page and in streams.md).
- [STRM] JetStream uses "a NATS optimized RAFT distributed quorum algorithm" with immediate consistency, not eventual consistency.
- [STRM] Writes are formally Linearizable; reads are in essence serializable (single global order, controllable via compare-and-publish); no atomic batching of multiple operations.
- [STRM][MYTH] Monotonic writes/reads guaranteed, but "We don't guarantee read your writes at this time, as reads through direct get requests may be served by followers or mirrors." Send gets to the stream leader for more consistent results.
- [STRM] Storage (Stream) is configured separately from consumption (Consumers).
- [STRM][SIZE][PATTERN] Replication guidance: "Replicas=1 - Cannot operate during an outage of the server servicing the stream. Highly performant." "Replicas=2 - No significant benefit at this time. We recommend using Replicas=3 instead." "Replicas=3 - Can tolerate the loss of one server ... An ideal balance". "Replicas=4 - No significant benefit over Replicas=3 except marginally in a 5 node cluster." "Replicas=5 - Can tolerate simultaneous loss of two servers ... at the expense of performance."
- [STRM][ANTI] "Rather than defaulting to the maximum, we suggest selecting the best option based on the use case behind the stream." Typical: file-based R=3; easily rebuilt/temporary streams can be memory R=1; R=5 is the replication factor limit.
- [STRM][TOPO] Mirrors between JetStream domains offer disaster recovery; a stream can source from one or more streams.
- [STRM][SIZE][OPS] File streams flush writes to the OS synchronously but by default do not fsync immediately; `sync_interval` default is 2 minutes; "The data will be fsync-ed no later than this interval."
- [STRM][OPS] Non-replicated: an OS failure (power loss, not just process kill) may lose acknowledged messages. Replicated: acknowledged after quorum, but simultaneous OS failures before fsync can lose recently acked messages; a data-losing server may rejoin and "form a new majority with nodes that have never received or persisted a given message".
- [STRM][OPS] `sync_interval: always` fsyncs after every message before ack; "combined with replication in different data centers or availability zones, provides the strongest durability guarantees but at the slowest performance." It has a server-wide performance impact.
- [STRM][OPS] Defaults chosen for "a typical production deployment scenario across multiple availability zones"; divergence for an R3 stream across 3 AZs needs a specific 5-step chain of failures.
- [STRM][OPS][PATTERN] Mitigation: don't auto-restart an OS-failed server until a majority has the new writes, or peer-remove it and re-admit as a wiped peer to recover over the network.
- [STRM][TOPO][PATTERN] Hybrid durability: add a dedicated cluster with `server_tags: ["sync:always"]` and `jetstream { sync_interval: always }`, then `nats stream add --replicas 3 --tag sync:always` for only the streams that need it.
- [STRM][CLNT] Flow control is decoupled, per client-server link, not end-to-end; publishers aren't limited to the slowest consumer. JetStream publish can be sync or async ("batched").
- [STRM][MYTH] Base QoS is at-least-once: rare failures make a publisher wrongly believe a publish failed and republish, or lose a consumer ack causing redelivery, leading to "perceived 'message duplication' at the application level".
- [STRM][CONS] Exactly-once = publisher attaches a unique message ID header tracked by the server "for a configurable rolling period of time" plus a double-acknowledgment on the consumer side.
- [CONS] Consumers are "views" on a stream.
- [CONS][STALE?] "fast un-acknowledged push (ordered) consumers" are "meant to be used to 'replay' rather than 'consume'".
- [CONS][PATTERN] Pull consumers are demand-driven, batch, require explicit ack, and "are meant to be shared between applications (just like queue groups)" for horizontal scaling "without having ... to worry about having to define partitions or worry about fault-tolerance."
- [CONS][MYTH] Pull consumers still get real-time updates: pass a reasonable timeout to Fetch and call it in a loop.
- [CONS] Ack kinds: ack-all up to a sequence; explicit per-message ack with an ack-wait timeout before redelivery to another process; negative ack; in-progress ack to extend time.
- [CONS][ANTI] "most processing is not idem-potent and requires higher qualities of service ... you will want to use acknowledged consumers."
- [KV] KV supports watch on bucket or key, optional history, atomic create/update enabling pessimistic locks (create and hold a key) and optimistic locks (CAS).
- [OBJ][SIZE] Object Store stores arbitrarily large objects by chunking, versus values "limited to 1Mb by default".
- [MIG][STALE?] "JetStream completely replaces the STAN legacy NATS streaming layer."

## Streams
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/streams.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/streams
- version context: config table lists introduction versions up to 2.14.0

### Claims
- [STRM] Streams capture normal NATS subjects; plain publish gives unacknowledged delivery; "it's better to use the JetStream publish calls instead as the JetStream server will reply with an acknowledgement".
- [STRM][PATTERN] "Relatively speaking the Stream is the most resource consuming component so being able to combine related data in this manner is important to consider." e.g. store all `ORDERS.*` in one stream and consume subsets; a stream may also add `SHIPPING.state`.
- [STRM] Deduplication uses the `Nats-Msg-Id` header within a sliding window.
- [STRM][SUBJ] Stream names must be unique per account and cannot contain whitespace, `.`, `*`, `>`, path separators, or non-printable characters.
- [STRM][SIZE] Replicas max is 5. MaxAge and DuplicateWindow are in nanoseconds. MaxConsumers `-1` = unlimited. MaxMsgSize counts payload plus headers.
- [STRM] NoAck (default false) is "mandatory when archiving messages which have a reply subject set. E.g. requests in an Request/Reply communication"; otherwise JetStream replies with an empty ack on the reply subject.
- [STRM] Not editable after creation: Name, Storage, MaxConsumers, Retention, DenyDelete, DenyPurge, FirstSeq, AllowMsgCounter. Mirror became editable in 2.12.0. Sealed can be set once. AllowMsgTTL and AllowMsgSchedules can only be enabled.
- [STRM] Version introductions: MaxMsgsPerSubject 2.3.0; Sealed/DenyDelete/DenyPurge/AllowRollup 2.6.2; RePublish 2.8.3; AllowDirect/MirrorDirect/DiscardNewPerSubject 2.9.0; Metadata/Compression(s2)/FirstSeq/SubjectTransform/ConsumerLimits 2.10.0; AllowMsgTTL/SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL 2.11.0; AllowAtomicPublish/AllowMsgCounter/AllowMsgSchedules 2.12.0; AllowBatchPublish 2.14.0.
- [STRM] AllowDirect: with more than one replica "each replica will respond to direct get requests ... not only the leader." MirrorDirect lets a mirror serve direct gets for the origin.
- [STRM] DiscardNewPerSubject requires DiscardNew and MaxMsgsPerSubject.
- [STRM] Compression is file-storage only; options: none or `s2` (Snappy).
- [STRM] Storage default is `File`.
- [STRM] A mirror cannot have subjects. Default subject = stream name. Removing a subject from a stream doesn't remove stored messages; overlapping consumers still see them.
- [STRM] LimitsPolicy: whichever of MaxMsgs/MaxBytes/MaxAge/MaxMsgsPerSubject is hit first deletes messages.
- [STRM][CONS] WorkQueuePolicy: FIFO, each message consumed once, enforced by "only allowing one consumer to be created per subject" (filters must not overlap); message deleted once acked.
- [STRM][CONS][ANTI] InterestPolicy with zero consumers deletes messages immediately: "consumers need to be bound to the stream ahead of messages being published"; deleted once acked by all consumers filtering on the subject.
- [STRM][ANTI] Limits still apply under Interest/WorkQueue: with MaxMsgs and default discard old, "messages will be automatically deleted even if the consumer did not receive them."
- [STRM] Interest streams may defer deleting messages after the last interested consumer is removed "until those messages reach the start of the stream", for performance.
- [STRM][CONS][ANTI] In WorkQueue streams, messages that hit the consumer's `MaxDeliver` "will remain in the stream and must be manually deleted via the JetStream API."
- [STRM] DiscardOld is default; DiscardNew rejects new messages that would exceed a limit; discard applies only if at least one limit is defined.
- [STRM][TOPO] Placement: "A given stream, including all replicas (not mirrors), are bound to a single cluster." Default: created in the cluster the client is connected to "assuming it has sufficient storage available."
- [STRM][TOPO][PATTERN] Explicit placement is useful "to co-locate with the most active clients (publishers or consumers) or may be required for data sovereignty reasons."
- [STRM][TOPO] Placement by cluster requires every server to set `cluster { name }`; super-cluster clusters must have distinct names.
- [STRM][TOPO][PATTERN] Tags (`server_tags`, e.g. `cloud:aws`, `region:us-east1`, `az:a`) plus `jetstream.unique_tag: "az"` force replicas onto servers with different tag values (one replica per AZ). Cluster and tags can be combined.
- [STRM] Sources/mirrors replicate asynchronously and may have their own retention, replication, and storage; changes to the copy don't affect the origin.
- [STRM][PATTERN] "We suggest to use Sources in new configurations." For a read-only replica: configure the stream without listen subjects, or disable listen subjects via client authorizations.
- [STRM] Sources aggregate one or more streams plus direct client writes into "a single interleaved stream", with subject transform and filtering.
- [STRM] A mirror sources exactly one stream; clients cannot publish to it, but messages can be deleted on demand and consumers work normally.
- [STRM][PATTERN] AllowRollup + `Nats-Rollup: all|sub` purges prior messages; "A common use case for rollup is for state snapshots".
- [STRM][PATTERN] RePublish: "For high scale needs where, currently, a dedicated consumer may add too much overhead, clients can establish a core NATS subscription to the destination subject". Fields Source (default `>`), Destination, HeadersOnly (adds `Nats-Msg-Size`). Reply subject is removed on republished messages even with no-ack.
- [STRM][SUBJ] SubjectTransform rewrites the subject before storing.

## Consumers
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/consumers.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/consumers
- version context: config table up to 2.14 (AckFlowControl)

### Claims
- [CONS] A consumer is "a stateful view of a stream" that tracks delivery and acknowledgments and provides at-least-once delivery.
- [CONS] Unacked or nacked messages are redelivered automatically; after the configured number of delivery attempts "an advisory notification is emitted."
- [CONS][PATTERN] Choice guidance: pull consumer for application-controlled processing and easy horizontal scaling; "ordered push consumer" for simple sequential replay; regular push consumer for load balancing or individual acks. [STALE? push guidance]
- [CONS] "We recommend pull consumers for new projects. In particular when scalability, detailed flow control or error handling are a concern."
- [CONS] Ordered consumers: always ephemeral, no acks (recreated on gap), automatic flow control, single-threaded dispatch, no load balancing; for data inspection/analysis.
- [CONS][MYTH] A consumer is durable only when `Durable` is set. "Setting `InactiveThreshold` does not make a consumer durable." Setting `Name` without `Durable` creates a named consumer that the server still treats as ephemeral.
- [CONS] InactiveThreshold applies to both durable and ephemeral consumers since 2.9 (before 2.9 ephemeral only).
- [CONS] Ephemeral consumers have no persisted state or fault tolerance (server memory only) and are cleaned up after inactivity with no bound subscriptions.
- [CONS] By default consumers "have the same replication factor as the stream they consume" and remain during inactivity unless InactiveThreshold is set.
- [CONS][SIZE] MaxAckPending default is 1000; -1 means unlimited (no flow control); applies across all bound subscriptions; delivery is suspended at the limit.
- [CONS][SIZE] MaxDeliver default is -1 (redeliver until acked); messages at max delivery count "will stay in the stream."
- [CONS] Backoff (2.7.1): list of delays on ack timeout, length must be <= MaxDeliver; not applied to nak (nak = immediate redelivery unless nakWithDelay); "When BackOff is set, it overrides AckWait entirely. The first value in the BackOff determines the AckWait value." Example: `MaxDeliver=5 backoff=[5s, 30s, 300s, 3600s, 84000s]` redelivers 5 times over one day.
- [CONS] AckWait is only effective when BackOff is not configured.
- [CONS] ReplayPolicy: ReplayInstant (default) as fast as possible honoring ack policy and MaxAckPending; ReplayOriginal simulates original timing.
- [CONS] Replicas (2.8.3): 0 inherits from stream. MemoryStorage (2.8.3): keeps consumer state in memory "reduces I/O from acknowledgments, useful for ephemeral consumers."
- [CONS][OPS] SampleFrequency: percentage of acks sampled for observability (`30` or `30%`).
- [CONS] Not editable: Durable, AckPolicy, DeliverPolicy, OptStartSeq/Time, ReplayPolicy, MemoryStorage, MaxWaiting, DeliverSubject.
- [CONS] AckPolicy: AckExplicit default "Recommended for most reliability and functionality"; AckNone assumes ack on delivery; AckAll acks all prior (and for pull consumers "all pending messages for all subscribers"); AckFlowControl (2.14) for sourcing/mirroring with a durable consumer.
- [CONS][MYTH] Out-of-window acks may still count: "if a first process fails to acknowledge within the window and the message has been redelivered to another consumer, the acknowledgment from the first consumer will be considered."
- [CONS] DeliverPolicy options: DeliverAll (default), DeliverLast, DeliverLastPerSubject, DeliverNew, DeliverByStartSequence (+OptStartSeq), DeliverByStartTime (+OptStartTime).
- [CONS] "For push consumers, MaxAckPending is the only form of flow control. For pull consumers, client-driven message delivery creates implicit one-to-one flow control".
- [CONS][PATTERN] "For high throughput, set MaxAckPending to a high value. For applications with high latency due to external services, use a lower value and adjust AckWait to avoid re-deliveries."
- [CONS][SUBJ] FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (2.10, multiple, e.g. `[factory-events.A.*, factory-events.B.*]`); they cannot be combined.
- [CONS][SEC][ANTI] Granular permissions: single filter uses `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.{stream}.{consumer}.{filter}`; multiple filters use `$JS.API.CONSUMER.DURABLE.CREATE.{stream}.{consumer}` without the filter token, so "Use a different strategy for granular permissions."
- [CONS] Pull options: MaxWaiting (max waiting pull requests), MaxRequestExpires (2.7.0), MaxRequestBatch (2.7.0), MaxRequestMaxBytes (2.8.3); batch constrained by whichever limit hits first.
- [CONS] Push options: DeliverSubject decides push vs pull; DeliverGroup is a queue group; FlowControl is per-subscription sliding-window working with MaxAckPending; IdleHeartbeat sends status 100 with no reply; RateLimit in bits per second.

## Headers
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/headers.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/headers
- version context: up to 2.14

### Claims
- [STRM][ANTI] "`Nats-` is a reserved namespace. Please use a different prefix for your own headers."
- [STRM] Publish headers: `Nats-Msg-Id` (dedup within Duplicate Window, 2.2.0); `Nats-Expected-Stream`; `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` and `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence` (stream-level optimistic concurrency); `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence` (2.3.1, subject-level); `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence-Subject` (2.11, wildcard subject to check against); `Nats-Rollup` (2.6.2, `all`/`sub`, wildcards "will result in undefined behavior"); `Nats-TTL` (2.11, go duration, requires stream flag).
- [STRM] Republish/direct-get headers set by server: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Subject`, `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Last-Sequence` (2.8.3), `Nats-Time-Stamp`, `Nats-Num-Pending` (2.10.0), `Nats-UpTo-Sequence` (2.11.0). "Do not set these headers on client published messages."
- [STRM] `Nats-Stream-Source` on sourced messages holds origin stream (with domain hash if cross-domain), original sequence, filters, transforms, original subject; "parse conservatively".
- [KV] `KV-Operation: DEL|PURGE`; purge must be combined with `Nats-Rollup`; since 2.14 PURGE can carry `Nats-TTL` to auto-delete the marker and avoid `nats kv compact`.
- [OPS] Tracing (2.11, ADR-41): `traceparent` (W3C, needs `msg_trace` account config) or `Nats-Trace-Dest`; `Nats-Trace-Only: true` skips delivery; `Accept-Encoding` gzip/snappy compresses traces.
- [STRM] Scheduler (2.12, repeating in 2.14, ADR-51): `Nats-Schedule` (`@at ...`, crontab, `@hourly`, `@every 5m`), `Nats-Schedule-Target` must differ from schedule subject, `Nats-Schedule-TTL`, `Nats-Schedule-Rollup`, `Nats-Schedule-Source` (2.14, no wildcards), `Nats-Schedule-Time-Zone` (default UTC).
- [STRM] Atomic batch publish (2.12, ADR-50): `Nats-Batch-Id` (<=64 chars), `Nats-Batch-Sequence` from 1, `Nats-Batch-Commit` `1` or `eob` (2.14); other value terminates the batch.
- [STRM][ANTI] Fast-ingest (2.14) is selected by reply subject ending `.$FI`, can combine with dedup headers, "MUST NOT be combined with atomic batch publish."
- [STRM] Internal: `Nats-Required-Api-Level` (2.12; servers >= 2.11 error if unsupported), `Nats-Request-Info` on cross-account messages, `Nats-Marker-Reason` (`MaxAge|Remove|Purge`, 2.11, ADR-48), `Nats-Incr` KV counters (2.12, ADR-49), `Nats-Counter-Sources`.

## Example configuration (ORDERS)
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/example_configuration.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/example_configuration
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [PATTERN][STRM][CONS] ORDERS pipeline: one stream for `ORDERS.*`; pull consumers NEW (`ORDERS.received`) and DISPATCH (`ORDERS.processed`) with explicit ack scale horizontally as work queues; each stage publishes the next message back into the same stream; a MONITOR push consumer with ack none gets all messages.
- [OPS][PATTERN] Sample 100% of acks on NEW/DISPATCH so redelivery counts and ack delays go to monitoring.
- [STRM][SIZE] Example: `--max-age=1y --storage file --retention limits --max-msgs=-1 --max-bytes=-1 --max-msg-size=-1 --discard=old`.

## Source and Mirror Streams
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/source_and_mirror.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/source_and_mirror
- version context: 2.14 for WorkQueue/Interest sourcing

### Claims
- [STRM][TOPO] Source/mirror "are designed to be robust and will recover from a loss of connection. They are suitable for geographic distribution over high latency and unreliable connections." Even a leaf node connecting "every few days" still syncs.
- [STRM][SEC][PATTERN] Another use case: connecting streams cross-account.
- [STRM] Options: Name, StartSeq, StartTime, FilterSubject (not with SubjectTransforms), SubjectTransforms (multiple, disjoint subjects while keeping order; not with FilterSubject), Domain ("commonly used in a hub cluster and leafnode topology").
- [STRM][MYTH] "Deletes in the origin stream are NOT replicated through a source or mirror agreement."
- [STRM] "All configurations are made on the receiving side"; origin needs no config; no cleanup on origin if receiver disappears.
- [STRM][PATTERN][SIZE] One stream can be origin for many streams: "fan out topologies where data needs to be distributed reliable to a large number (up to millions) of client connections."
- [STRM][TOPO] Leaf nodes and domains supported via the API prefix.
- [STRM][MYTH] "Sourcing messages does not retain sequence numbers. But it retain the in stream sequence of messages. Between streams sourced to the same target, the sequence of messages is undefined."
- [STRM] "Mirrored messages retains the sequence numbers and timestamps of the origin stream." Mirrors + MirrorDirect can be used "for (geographic) load distribution".
- [STRM][ANTI] Source/mirror are one-way replication, not full sync; "Quickly deleting messages after publishing them may result in inconsistent replication due to the asynchronous nature".
- [STRM][SIZE] Recovery interval after a disconnect is 10-20s.
- [STRM] Mirror/source agreements "do not create a visible consumer in the origin stream" (before 2.14 behavior; see below).
- [STRM][ANTI] Sourcing from WorkQueue/Interest streams supported since 2.14 with a visible durable consumer; before 2.14 it is "not supported ... the behavior is undefined" though not forbidden.
- [STRM][SEC][PATTERN] 2.14 "bring your own" sourcing consumer (`Consumer.Name`, `Consumer.DeliverSubject`) must use `AckFlowControl`; useful for monitoring or "when you're not in control of 'the other side' ... from a security point of view."

## Key/Value store (concept)
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/key-value-store/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/key-value-store
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [KV] Buckets are "immediately (as opposed to eventually) consistent, persistent associative arrays"; materialized as streams named `KV_...`; "everything you can do with a bucket you can do with a Stream" and using the stream directly gives more control.
- [KV][MYTH] Monotonic writes/reads guaranteed; "We don't guarantee read your writes at this time, as reads through direct get requests may be served by followers or mirrors." Send gets to the underlying stream leader for stronger consistency.
- [KV][PATTERN] Atomic ops: create (compare-to-null-and-set) and update (CAS) for locking and concurrency control.
- [KV][SIZE] Bucket limits: max bucket size, max single value size, TTL. History default is 1 (only latest value/operation stored).
- [KV] watch / watch all / history make the KV a message stream.
- [KV][SUBJ] Valid key characters: `a-z A-Z 0-9 _ - . = /`; dot-separated keys allow wildcard watching of key hierarchies.

## Object Store (concept)
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/object-store/obj_store.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/object-store
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [OBJ] Buckets correspond to streams; files stored and transmitted in chunks so "files of arbitrary size" transfer safely.
- [OBJ][ANTI][MYTH] "Object store is not a distributed storage system. All files in a bucket will need to fit on the target file system."
- [OBJ] Operations: add bucket, put, get, del, watch (notifies on put and del).

- [STRM][OPS] "Streams with source and mirror configurations are best managed through a client API"; from CLI use a JSON config (`nats stream add --config`).

## JetStream walkthrough
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/js_walkthrough.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/js_walkthrough
- version context: 2.11.0-dev in sample output

### Claims
- [OPS] Enable JetStream with `nats-server -js`; `nats account info` shows "JetStream is not supported in this account" when disabled.
- [STRM][SIZE] CLI defaults when creating a stream: storage file, replication 1, retention limits, discard old, all limits -1 (unlimited), duplicate window 2m0s, rollups no, deletion allowed, purge allowed, "Direct Get: true".
- [CONS][SIZE] Consumer defaults shown: Ack Wait 30.00s, Max Ack Pending 1,000, Max Waiting Pulls 512.
- [CONS][PATTERN] A durable pull consumer "can be shared between as many consuming processes as you want"; two `nats consumer next` instances split the messages.
- [CONS] To replay again, create a new consumer or delete and recreate it. Deleting a stream deletes all its consumers.
- [CORE][STRM][MYTH] A Core NATS subscriber only receives messages published after it started; replaying history requires a consumer.

## Subject Mapping and Transforms
- path: nats-concepts/subject_mapping.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/subject_mapping
- version context: `{{wildcard(n)}}` since 2.8.0; `nats trace` since 2.11

### Claims
- [SUBJ] Transforms can be defined at config root ($G account), per account, on imports, and in JetStream (stream ingress, republish, source/mirror where they also filter).
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Uses: translating namespaces between accounts or cluster/leaf semantics; suppressing subjects; backward compatibility after renaming hierarchies; merging subjects; disambiguation/isolation on super-clusters or leaf nodes; testing reroutes; partitioning; filtering sourced/mirrored data; weighted chaos/sampling.
- [SUBJ] Transforms apply as soon as a message enters the scope, before routing or interest; "The message will appear as if published from the transformed subject under all circumstances."
- [SUBJ] "Transforms are not applied recursively in the same scope" (prevents loops; only the first matching rule applies), but they apply "in sequence as they pass through different scopes" (publish -> leaf -> stream ingest -> republish).
- [SUBJ][TOPO][PATTERN] Hub/leaf disambiguation example: hub maps `orders.* -> orders.central.{{wildcard(1)}}`; leaf maps `orders.central.* -> orders.local.{{wildcard(1)}}`; leaf stream stores under `orders.{{wildcard(1)}}` and republishes to `orders.trace.*`.
- [SUBJ][SEC][OPS] With config-file accounts, reload the config to apply transform changes; with operator JWT, transforms and imports/exports live in the account JWT and apply when pushed.
- [OPS] Test rules with `nats server mapping`; from 2.11 observe with `nats trace`.
- [SUBJ] A full wildcard `>` may be used once in source and must appear exactly once in destination.
- [SUBJ] Token reordering with `{{wildcard(n)}}` (2.8.0+); `$1`/`$2` syntax is deprecated.
- [SUBJ] Tokens can be dropped by not using all wildcards, "with the exception of mappings defined as part of import/export between accounts in which case all the wildcard tokens must be used". "Import/export mapping must be mapped bidirectionally unambiguous."
- [SUBJ] Functions: `split(idx, sep)`, `splitfromleft/right(idx, offset)`, `slicefromleft/right(idx, n)`, `random(n)` (0..n-1), `partition(buckets, tokens...)`.
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] `partition(n, pos...)` is deterministic hash-based; "may not be fair for a small number of subjects"; distribution "tends towards 'perfectly balanced'" as keys grow; multiple positions form a composite key. `partition(n)` alone hashes the full subject.
- [SUBJ][CORE][CONS][MYTH] Queue groups and durable consumers "are partition-less and non-deterministic": no guarantee two sequential messages on one subject reach the same subscriber, so ordering can be lost.
- [CONS][ANTI] Strict ordering otherwise requires "one at a time" per consumer/queue-group via max acks pending, "which in turn hurts scalability".
- [PATTERN][STRM] Deterministic partitioning keeps per-subject order while scaling: insert a partition token in the stream's subject transform, then a consumer per partition via subject filters.
- [STRM][SIZE][PATTERN] At extreme publish rates "a single nats-server process is acting as the RAFT leader (coordinator) for any given stream and can therefore become a limiting factor"; partition into several smaller streams so leaders spread across JetStream servers.
- [PATTERN] Partitioning also helps when subscribers rely on local data caching per key.
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Weighted mappings for canary: `myservice.requests -> v1 98%, v2 2%`; traffic shaping to a failure-simulating service (e.g. 20%); artificial loss by mapping <100% (`foo.loss.>` at 50% drops half).
- [SUBJ][TOPO][PATTERN] Cluster-scoped mappings (`cluster: "west"` in destination) let an app publish to `foo` and get `foo.west` etc. without knowing its cluster.
- [STRM][SUBJ] In mirror/source/republish, transforms are filters (non-matching ignored); the stream-level `subject_transform` only rewrites matches and leaves others untouched.

## KV walkthrough / Object Store walkthrough
- path: nats-concepts/jetstream/key-value-store/kv_walkthrough.md, nats-concepts/jetstream/object-store/obj_walkthrough.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/key-value-store/kv_walkthrough
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [KV][SIZE] Default bucket: History Kept 1, unlimited bucket size/value size/age, backing stream `KV_<name>`, file storage.
- [KV][PATTERN] Semaphore/exclusive lock: `create` a key (first come first served; concurrent creates error "wrong last sequence ... key exists"); make it resilient with a bucket TTL and keep-alive via `update` with revision.
- [KV][PATTERN] Optimistic locking: `update` with a revision; a second update with a stale revision fails "wrong last sequence".
- [OBJ] Object bucket backs onto stream `OBJ_<name>`; a 1.5 GiB file was stored in 12,656 chunks; sealed buckets "can not be unsealed or modified".
- [OBJ] After deleting an object the bucket still reports size (16 MiB in the example), i.e. metadata/chunks are not immediately reclaimed to zero.

## Clustering
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering
- version context: 2.1.4 in sample logs

### Claims
- [TOPO] Clustering is for "high volume messaging systems and resiliency and high availability"; servers gossip and connect to all known servers "thus dynamically forming a full mesh"; a cluster "can grow, shrink and self heal".
- [TOPO][MYTH] "NATS clustered servers have a forwarding limit of one hop": a server forwards client-received messages only to adjacent routed servers; "Messages received from a route will only be distributed to local clients."
- [TOPO][OPS] The full mesh requires that servers can connect to each other and clients can connect to each server in the cluster.
- [TOPO][OPS] Seed servers have no special configuration; they are the discovery starting point for servers (routes) and clients (connect URLs); "the ability for other server and clients to successfully connect depends on seed server running." Multiple seeds should route to each other.
- [TOPO] `-routes` requires `-cluster`; a routing server advertises its own cluster URL to all others, creating the mesh.
- [CLNT] Clients connecting to any server discover the others; on interruption they try all known servers.
- [OPS] Cluster `listen` with no host binds all interfaces (0.0.0.0); port is the minimum required.

## Clustering Configuration
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/cluster_config.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/cluster_config
- version context: connect_backoff 2.12.0

### Claims
- [TOPO] Cluster `name` is "recommended for NATS +v2.2".
- [SEC][TOPO] Cluster `tls`: "`verify` is always enabled and `cert_file` is used for client and server."
- [TOPO][OPS] `advertise`/`cluster_advertise` is useful behind NAT; with TLS it controls the hostname clients use when discovering routes, "otherwise TLS hostname verification may fail with an IP SANs error."
- [TOPO][OPS][PATTERN] `no_advertise: true` stops gossiping server URLs to clients (also disables client_advertise); useful when reachable "via different load balancers and interfaces from different networks. Automatically advertising an internal IP address could result in reconnect delays due to failed attempts."
- [SIZE] `connect_retries` default `0` (no retry) for discovered routes; when enabled, attempts once per second. `connect_backoff` (2.12.0) starts at 1s up to 30s.
- [SEC][TOPO] Route `authorization` with a single username/password applies to discovered routes only; explicit routes need credentials in the URL. "either use the same credentials throughout the system or list every route explicitly on every server." `users` and `token` are not supported and prevent startup; `permissions` is ignored.
- [SIZE] `pool_size` default `3`; `compression` default `accept`.

## TLS Authentication in clusters
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/cluster_tls.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/cluster_tls
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [SEC][TOPO] Cluster TLS verifies certificates in both directions; cluster identity certs can be separate from client-facing certs.
- [SEC][TOPO] "TLS Mutual Authentication is the only way of securing routes."

## v2 Routes
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/v2_routes.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/v2_routes
- version context: 2.10.0

### Claims
- [TOPO][SIZE] Before 2.10.0 two servers shared a single route connection for all accounts, "which could lead to slow down and increased memory usage"; 2.10.0+ creates 3 route connections by default (`pool_size`).
- [TOPO][OPS] Each pooled connection handles a fixed subset of accounts; "It is required that each server in the cluster have the same pool size value" or clustering fails ("Mismatch route pool size").
- [TOPO][OPS] When one pool connection breaks, traffic for its accounts stops until reconnect (not rerouted through other connections).
- [OPS] Changing `pool_size` via reload breaks route connections unless done as a rolling reload with the same value; client connections stay up.
- [TOPO] `pool_size: -1` disables pooling (pre-2.10 behavior, single route); then no `accounts` list may be defined.
- [TOPO][PATTERN] Account pinning (`cluster { accounts: [...] }`) gives an account a dedicated route: "improves performance and reduces latency" and saves bytes because the account name isn't in the route protocol. The system account gets a dedicated route by default.
- [OPS] Pinned `accounts` list must match on all servers, but rolling reload works: traffic for a newly pinned account stops until the peer reloads too.
- [OPS] "it is recommended that all servers part of the same cluster be at the same version number"; a 2.10 server connects to older servers with a single route.
- [TOPO][SIZE] Route compression (2.10.0) uses S2; default off (mode `accept` doesn't initiate). Modes: off, accept, s2_fast, s2_better, s2_best, s2_auto. Modes need not match between peers.
- [SIZE] `s2_auto` default `rtt_thresholds: [10ms, 50ms, 100ms]`: under 10ms none, then s2_fast, s2_better, s2_best.
- [OPS] Toggling compression between `off` and anything else closes and recreates route connections; other mode changes are dynamic.

## JetStream Clustering
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/jetstream_clustering/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/jetstream_clustering
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [TOPO][STRM] "Clustering in JetStream is required for a highly available and scalable system." It uses a NATS-optimized RAFT that combines the data plane for replication with consensus messages.
- [TOPO] Each participating server needs a unique `server_name` (only within the same domain).
- [TOPO][SIZE] "A quorum is 1/2 cluster size + 1": cluster of 3 needs at least 2 JetStream servers up to store new messages; cluster of 5 needs 3.
- [TOPO] RAFT groups: Meta Group (all servers; owns the API and server placement), Stream Group (one per stream; leader handles ACKs; "if there is no leader the stream will not accept messages"), Consumer Group (one per consumer, lives on the stream group's machines).
- [TOPO][SIZE][PATTERN] "Generally, we recommend 3 or 5 JetStream enabled servers in a NATS cluster." With 5, place 2+2+1 across three zones so "you can lose any one 'zone' at any time and continue operating."
- [TOPO][PATTERN] Mixing JetStream and non-JetStream servers in one cluster "is possible and even recommended in some cases": storage-optimized machines for JetStream, compute-optimized for core NATS, "reducing operational expense".
- [TOPO][OPS] Unlike core clustering, each JetStream node "must specify a server name and cluster name".
- [SEC][OPS] A system account (`$SYS`) user/password should be configured (example uses a bcrypted password).
- [OPS] Choose a store directory "ideally a fast SSD"; "After two servers are running you'll be ready to use JetStream" (3-node example).

## JetStream Administration (cluster)
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/jetstream_clustering/administration.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/jetstream_clustering/administration
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [STRM][SIZE] When choosing replicas "we suggest 1, 3 or 5". Replica count can be edited after creation.
- [OPS] Stream info reports Cluster name, Leader, replicas with `current`/`outdated` and last-seen time.
- [OPS][PATTERN] "Leader elections will represent short interruptions to the stream so if you know you will work on a node later it might be worth moving leadership away from it ahead of time" (`nats stream cluster step-down`, consumer and meta variants). Step-down doesn't remove the node or stop it from being re-elected.
- [OPS][SEC] Meta group management (step-down, peer-remove, `nats server report jetstream`) requires a SYSTEM user; system users see the meta group but not individual streams/consumers.
- [OPS] `nats server report jetstream` shows per-server streams/consumers/messages/bytes/API errors and the RAFT meta group (Leader, Current, Offline, Active, Lag); raw data from `/jsz` or `nats server req jetstream`.
- [OPS] Normal shutdown including Lame Duck Mode is noticed by the cluster and it keeps functioning; peer-remove is for a node that "will never return".
- [OPS] After peer-remove "the cluster will notice that the replica count of a stream is not honored anymore and will immediately pick a new node and start replicating data to it" using the stream's placement rules.
- [OPS][ANTI] "Peer-removing nodes from the cluster is a destructive operation, and decreases the size of the cluster." The node should be offline; if online, JetStream is disabled on it; it must not restart under the same `server_name` if its disk was wiped.
- [OPS] Stream-level peer-remove (`nats stream cluster peer-remove`) moves a stream (and its consumers) off a node that stays in the cluster.

- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/clustering/jetstream_clustering/troubleshooting
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [OPS] By default only warning and error logs are produced; `-D` debug, `-DV` trace.
- [OPS][SEC] "Make sure that ... at least one system user is configured" under `$SYS`.
- [OPS] Diagnostic CLI: `nats server ls/ping/info/check`, `nats server report connections|accounts|jetstream`, `nats server request jetstream|subscriptions|variables|connections|routes|gateways|leafnodes|accounts`, `nats server cluster step-down|peer-remove`; `nats traffic` is experimental.

## Super-cluster with Gateways
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/gateways/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/gateways
- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [TOPO] Gateways join clusters into a full mesh of clusters (superclusters); "Clustering is used for adjacent servers; gateways are for joining clusters together." Cluster and gateway protocols use different ports.
- [TOPO] Unlike clusters, gateways have names (their cluster), form a mesh between clusters not between nodes, use uni-directional connections, and "don't gossip gateway nodes to clients".
- [TOPO] Gateways exist to "reduce the number of connections required between servers" and "optimize the interest graph propagation".
- [TOPO][ANTI] "all servers of this cluster need to have a gateway configuration with the same name" and "every gateway node needs to be able to connect to any other gateway node and vice versa. Everything else is considered a misconfiguration."
- [TOPO][OPS] "It is recommended to have all seed server of a cluster listed in the gateways section"; discovery depends on those servers running.
- [TOPO][SIZE] Each node makes one outbound connection to a single node in every remote cluster; with 3 gateway nodes locally there are 3 outbound connections per remote cluster. Cluster connections are N(N-1)/2; for 3 clusters of 5 nodes: full mesh 105 vs gateway 30; of 30 nodes: 4005 vs 180.
- [TOPO] Gateways work with single servers too but "start to be useful when participating cluster consist of more than one server".
- [TOPO] Interest propagation: interest-only mode (A sends only subjects B has expressed interest in) and queue subscriptions (propagated once per account and subject).
- [TOPO][CORE][PATTERN] Queue semantics across a super-cluster: "a server will always try to serve local queue subscribers first and only failover when a local queue subscriber is not found. The server will pick the cluster with the lowest RTT."

## Gateway Configuration
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/gateways/gateway.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/gateways/gateway
- version context: 2.0.0 sample log; connect_backoff 2.12.0

### Claims
- [TOPO] Self-gateway entries are ignored, so one gateway config can be shared across all servers.
- [TOPO][SEC] `reject_unknown_cluster: true` rejects connections from clusters not listed in `gateways`, disabling gossip of new clusters (but not growth of configured ones).
- [TOPO][SEC] Gateway `tls`: "`verify` is always enabled". Authorization: single user/password for discovered gateways only; explicit gateways need creds in URL; `users`/`token` unsupported; `permissions` ignored.
- [SIZE] `connect_retries` default 0 (once per second when enabled); `connect_backoff` (2.12.0) 1s to 30s.
- [TOPO] With `urls` list per remote gateway, a server picks one randomly and establishes "a single outbound gateway connection to one of the members from another cluster."
- [SEC][OPS][ANTI] Certificate rotation: clusters rarely rotate at the same time; "Make sure that the ca_file contains both old and new root or intermediate CAs." Using only the CA from an issuance bundle "is ill-advised"; keep a separate verification bundle so "when DC-B rolls before DC-A, it will not be cut off from your supercluster." Reload config to apply.
- [TOPO][OPS][ANTI] Behind a load balancer set `advertise` to the LB hostname/port; "Otherwise, they will advertise their own private IP and port, and can generate failures and downtime if any reconnection is required."

## Leaf Nodes
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/leafnodes/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/leafnodes
- version context: TLS-first 2.10.0

### Claims
- [TOPO][SEC] A leaf node "extends an existing NATS system of any size, optionally bridging both operator and security domains"; it authenticates local clients with local policy and routes to one or more remote systems.
- [TOPO][USECASE] "Leaf nodes are useful in IoT and edge scenarios and when the local server traffic should be low RTT and local unless routed to the super cluster." Queue semantics are honored "by serving local queue consumers first."
- [TOPO][SEC] Traffic between leaf and cluster takes the restrictions of the user used for the leaf connection: subjects the user may publish are exported to the cluster; subjects it may subscribe to are imported into the leaf.
- [TOPO] "leaf nodes do not need to be reachable themselves and can be used to explicitly configure any acyclic graph topologies."
- [TOPO][OPS] Configure a leaf with all seed servers; each seed must accept leaf connections; each URL in a remote must point to the same cluster; a leaf may have multiple remotes to different clusters.
- [TOPO][ANTI] "If one node in a cluster is configured as leaf node, all nodes need to. Likewise, if one server in a cluster accepts leaf node connections, all servers need to."
- [TOPO][USECASE] Leaf nodes bridge servers you control with third-party managed servers (e.g. NGS) "to inexpensively connect geographically distributed servers or small clusters."
- [SIZE] Default leaf node port is 7422.
- [SEC] Restrict leaf import/export by limiting what the leaf connection user can publish/subscribe.
- [SEC][TOPO] TLS-first handshake (2.10.0): normally the server sends INFO in clear text first; `handshake_first` avoids any clear-text traffic when websocket isn't desired.
- [SEC][SIZE] NGS free account example limits: 10 connections, leaf nodes not allowed, 1.0 GB data, 2 exports, 7 imports, 1.0 kB max payload, 10 subscriptions.

## LeafNode Configuration
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/leafnodes/leafnode_conf.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/leafnodes/leafnode_conf
- version context: WebSocket leaf 2.2.0; signature handler 2.9.0; TLS-first 2.10.0

### Claims
- [TOPO][SIZE] Leaf `compression` defaults to `s2_auto` (unlike routes which default to accept).
- [SEC][ANTI] `handshake_first: true` must be set on both accepting side and remote; a mismatch fails the connection in either direction.
- [SEC] Leaf connections can authenticate against any user account on the hub; the dedicated authorization block is optional. Singleton mode binds all leaf connections to one account (which must exist); multi-users mode binds per user; an `account`-only block binds credential-less connections.
- [TOPO][SEC] Remote `account` selects which local account is bound to the remote; `deny_imports`/`deny_exports` block subject propagation per direction.
- [TOPO] Remote `urls` are shuffled by default (`no_randomize` to connect in sequence).
- [TOPO] `hub: true` reverses roles so the hub initiates the connection to the leaf.
- [SIZE] `first_info_timeout` default `1s` prevents waiting forever when the port isn't a leaf-accepting NATS server.
- [TOPO][ANTI] WebSocket leaf remotes (2.2.0): all URLs in a list must be `ws`; mixing `ws` and `nats` prevents startup. TLS is decided by presence of a tls config, not by `wss://`.
- [SEC] `verify_and_map` maps certificate values to a user for auth; `cipher_suites` must match the Go version used to build the server.

## JetStream on Leaf Nodes (domains)
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/leafnodes/jetstream_leafnodes.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/leafnodes/jetstream_leafnodes
- version context: 2021 examples (pre-2.10 CLI output); "known issues" may be stale [STALE?]

### Claims
- [TOPO][STRM][USECASE] Leaf nodes can "provide a local NATS network even when the connection to a hub or the cloud is down"; JetStream supports this via "independent JetStream islands" (domains).
- [TOPO][STRM] `domain` in the jetstream block disambiguates which JetStream answers `$JS.API.>`; the API is also exposed as `$JS.<domain>.API.>`.
- [TOPO][ANTI] "Every server in a cluster and super cluster needs to have the same domain name"; domains can change only across a leaf node connection; domain names must be unique.
- [TOPO][SEC] Connecting system accounts across a leaf link gives: monitoring of all servers, account resolver across the network, and "extended JetStream cluster". "You probably don't want to connect your cloud and edge device system accounts" except when only firewalls prevent a super-cluster.
- [TOPO][STRM] When `domain` is set, JetStream traffic on the system account and `$JS.API.>` traffic are suppressed across the leaf link, so clients use the local JetStream; other domains are reached via `$JS.<domain>.API`.
- [TOPO][STRM] Each domain is an independent namespace: the same stream name may exist in different domains within one account.
- [TOPO][STRM][ANTI] Regular message flow is not restricted by domains: if streams in two domains (same account) subscribe to the same subject, both store the message while the leaf link is up. Avoid with different subjects, different accounts, or isolated accounts.
- [TOPO][STRM][STALE?] Known issue: with more than one JetStream-enabled leaf in a different cluster, the connected cluster also needs JetStream enabled and a domain set. Known issue: extending a central JetStream (leaf without domain) requires the central JetStream to be clustered.
- [TOPO][STRM][PATTERN] "If you want to connect a leaf to the hub and get commands, even when the leaf node connection is offline, mirroring a stream located in the hub is the way to go."
- [TOPO][STRM][PATTERN] "if you want to aggregate streams located in any number of leaf nodes use source ... it is recommended to aggregate them in the hub for processing via source."
- [STRM][PATTERN] Source/mirror copy data so access "is independent of the leaf node connection being online" and avoid a custom program: "This is the recommended way to exchange persistent data across domains."
- [SEC][STRM] Cross-account JetStream import renames `$JS.hub.API` to e.g. `JS.acc@hub.API`; "the general recommendation is to export the domain specific API `$JS.<domain>.API` as this allows you to pin the export to a particular domain."
- [SEC][STRM][STALE?] "Known issue: Currently, across accounts, push consumer are not supported."
- [SEC][STRM][PATTERN] Minimum cross-account exports for source/mirror: `$JS.<domain>.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.*` (service, response_type stream), a delivery stream `deliver.<acc>.<domain>.>`, and `$JS.FC.<stream>.<consumer>.>`; for client pull consumers add `$JS.<domain>.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.<stream>.<consumer>` and `$JS.ACK.<stream>.<consumer>.>`.
- [SEC][SUBJ][PATTERN] Delivery prefix convention to avoid overlaps across multiple imports: `<static type>.<exporting account>.<exporting domain>.<importing account>.<importing domain>.<importing stream name>`.
- [CLNT] With limited API access, clients set the API prefix (`nats.APIPrefix("JS.acc@hub.API")`) and bind explicitly (`nats.Bind(stream, durable)`) to avoid stream/durable inference calls.
- [CONS][SIZE] 2021 CLI output shows a pull consumer default Max Ack Pending of 20,000 (contradicts 1,000 in newer walkthrough output, nats-concepts/jetstream/js_walkthrough.md).

## Configuring JetStream (resource management)
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/jetstream-config/resource_management.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/jetstream-config/resource_management
- version context: request_queue_limit since v2.10.21

### Claims
- [OPS] Enable with `jetstream: enabled` (or `-js`, `-sd <dir>`).
- [SEC][STRM] JetStream is compatible with NATS 2.0 multi-tenancy: "fully isolated JetStream environments for different accounts."
- [TOPO][STRM] "JetStream environments in leaf nodes should be isolated in their own JetStream domain".
- [OPS][SIZE] Resources are dynamically determined by default, but "It's recommended that you set specific limits": example `max_mem: 1G`, `max_file: 100G`, `domain: acme`.
- [SEC][ANTI] Without accounts enabled, "all users in the server would have access to JetStream." Per-account limits: `max_mem`, `max_file`, `max_streams`, `max_consumers` (example 512M / 1G / 10 / 100).
- [SEC] Configuring JetStream for an account without global enablement warns; "the account designated as System cannot have JetStream enabled."
- [OPS][SIZE] Since v2.10.21 "the NATS JetStream API has a limit of 10K inflight requests after which it will start to drop requests"; tunable via `request_queue_limit` (example 1000). "When the request limit is reached, all pending requests are dropped". Log: "JetStream API queue limit reached, dropping N requests"; advisory `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.API.LIMIT_REACHED`; clients must retry.
- [OPS][SIZE] `limits { max_ha_assets }` caps the number of R3/R5 streams and consumers per server (example 2000).
- [SEC][OPS] In operator mode account JetStream limits live in the account JWT (`nsc edit account --js-mem-storage 1G --js-disk-storage 512M --js-streams 10 --js-consumer 100`).

- version context: unstated

### Claims
- [OPS][PATTERN] "In many cases managing the configuration in your application code is the best model, many teams though wish to pre-create Streams and Consumers." Tools: `nats --config` JSON files, Terraform provider `terraform-provider-jetstream`, GitHub Actions `jetstream-gh-action`, Kubernetes CRDs (`nack`).
- [OPS] Extract a stream config with `nats stream info X -j | jq .config` and apply with `nats str add|edit --config`.
- [OPS] NACK CRDs: `jetstream.nats.io/v1beta1` `Stream` and `Consumer`; `kubectl describe` on Errored state.

## Configuration (server config reference)
- path: running-a-nats-service/configuration/README.md
- url: https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration
- version context: options up to 2.12.0

### Claims
- [OPS] The config file is the standard way to configure; "We strongly recommend using only ASCII for names and values"; "JSON config files should be limited machine generated configuration files."
- [OPS][SIZE] Numbers support units: 1K = 1000, 1KB = 1024. String values starting with a digit must be quoted (e.g. `token: "3secret"`).
- [OPS] Variables are block-scoped, `$`-prefixed, must be used or parsing fails with `unknown field`; undefined references fall back to environment variables; env values starting with a number may fail to resolve.
- [OPS] `include` uses relative paths from the main config.
- [OPS] The config is read at startup only; reload via `nats-server --signal reload`; since v2.10.0 via `$SYS.REQ.SERVER.<server-id>.RELOAD` with a system user.
- [SIZE][CLNT] Defaults: `host 0.0.0.0`, `port 4222`; no TLS by default; gateway/leafnodes/mqtt/websocket/cluster inactive by default.
- [OPS][TOPO] `client_advertise` is useful behind a load balancer or when TLS server auth needs the correct DNS name; fully disable with `no_advertise: true`.
- [SIZE][CLNT] `ping_interval` default `2m`, `ping_max` 2; "it is recommended to keep this value bigger than what clients use". `write_deadline` default `10s`: exceeding it closes the connection (slow consumer).
- [SIZE] Limits defaults: `max_connections 64K`, `max_control_line 4KB` (subject plus queue group), `max_payload 1MB` ("It is not recommended to use values over 8MB but max_payload can be set up to 64MB"; must be <= `max_pending`), `max_pending 64MB` per client connection, `max_subscriptions 0` unlimited.
- [OPS][STRM][ANTI] "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."
- [OPS][STRM][ANTI] "each JetStream enabled server MUST use its own individual storage directory"; "JetStream does not implement standby and fault tolerance through a shared file system"; shared directories: "Access conflicts are not detected. We do not recommend such a setup."
- [SIZE][STRM] JetStream server defaults: `store_dir /tmp/nats/jetstream`, `max_memory_store` 75% of available memory, `max_file_store 1TB`, `max_outstanding_catchup 64MB` (2.9.0), `max_buffered_msgs 10.000` and `max_buffered_size 128MB` (2.11.0, OOM protection during write bursts), `request_queue_limit 10.000` (2.11.0), `sync_interval 2m` (2.10.0), `strict true` (2.11.0).
- [TOPO][STRM] `domain` (2.2.3): "Isolates the JetStream cluster to the local cluster. Recommended use with leaf nodes."
- [TOPO][STRM] `extension_hint` (2.2.3) `no_extend`/`will_extend` only matters when the system account is shared between leaf and hub: a standalone leaf extending the hub domain needs `will_extend`; a leaf cluster with a different domain should set `no_extend` or "JetStream will NOT become ready on first startup until the hub can be connected." Only matters at initial start.
- [SEC][STRM] Encryption at rest: `cipher` `chacha`/`chachapoly` or `aes` (2.3.0); key of at least 32 bytes recommended; `prev_encryption_key` (2.10.0) for rotation. TPM-based encryption (2.11.0) with `keys_file`, `encryption_password`, `pcr` default 22.
- [STRM][SIZE][OPS] `sync_interval`: "By default JetStream relies on stream replication in the cluster to guarantee data is available after an OS crash. If you run JetStream without replication or with a replication of just 2 you may want to shorten the fsync/sync interval." `always` "will slow down the throughput to a few hundred msg/s."
- [TOPO][STRM] `unique_tag` (2.8.0) "MUST be the same across all nodes in a cluster AND supercluster"; with `az` tags an R3 stream lands in all three AZs.
- [SEC][SIZE] Account JetStream settings: `max_memory`/`max_file` (sums must be under the server limit), `max_streams`, `max_consumers` ("per stream(!)"), `max_ack_pending` (2.8.0), `max_bytes_required` (2.7.0, default false), `store_max_stream_bytes`/`memory_max_stream_bytes` (2.8.0).
- [TOPO][STRM] `cluster_traffic` (2.11.0): `system` (default; all replication/RAFT traffic in the system account, as in all prior versions) or `owner` (traffic in the stream's own account).
- [OPS] Account `msg_trace { dest, sampling 0-100 }` enables OpenTelemetry-style tracing for `traceparent` messages.
- [SIZE][STRM] Server-wide `limits`: `max_ack_pending`, `max_ha_assets` (RAFT assets per node; not counting R1), `max_request_batch` ("Use with caution. May break existing clients"), `duplicate_window` (max allowed; "default for new streams is 120s").
- [SEC] A default server has no auth; default account is `$G`; once any user is configured, `$G` and no-auth access are disabled unless `no_auth_user` is set.
- [SEC] Accounts: "Each account forms its own subject and stream namespace, with no data shared unless explicit import and export is configured."
- [OPS] `disable_sublist_cache: true` "saves resources in situations where different subjects are used all the time."
- [OPS][SIZE] `lame_duck_duration` default `2m` ("cannot be set lower than 30 seconds"); `lame_duck_grace_period` default `10s`; started with `nats-server --signal ldm`.
- [OPS][CLNT] `no_fast_producer_stall` default false: server stalls the fast producer when a consumer is slow; `true` drops the message for that consumer instead.
- [OPS][TOPO] `server_name` defaults to server id; "within a domain, all server names need to be unique." `server_tags` recommended in `key:value` notation; `server_metadata` (2.12.0).
- [OPS] `system_account` default `$SYS`. `connect_error_reports` default 3600 (approx hourly at 1 attempt/s); `reconnect_error_reports` default 1.
- [OPS] `trace` excludes the system account; `trace_verbose` includes it.

- [SEC][MYTH] "The default global account `$G` does not publish advisories."
