README index groups ADRs by server version (2.11, 2.12, 2.14, 2.15), Client, JetStream, Security, Server, Spec, Deprecated. Template statuses: `Proposed`, `Approved`, `Partially Implemented`, `Implemented`, `Deprecated`.

## ADR-1: JetStream JSON API Design
- path: adr/ADR-1.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-1.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2020-04-30

### Claims
- [CORE][CLNT] JetStream API is built on NATS request-reply; every API has a unique subject under `$JS.API.` with tokens naming the item, "to assist in generating ACLs giving people access to either subsets of API or even down to a single Stream or Consumer."
- [CLNT] Server accepts nil payload, empty string, or `{}` as an empty request body.
- [CLNT] Responses carry a `type` field like `io.nats.jetstream.api.v1.stream_info_response`; requests generally do not include a type ("it's inferred from which subject is accessed").
- [SIZE][CLNT] Paged APIs (e.g. `$JS.API.STREAM.NAMES`) return `total`, `offset`, `limit`; default page limit shown is 1024; pass `{"offset": N}` to page.
- [CLNT] Error responses have `error.code` (HTTP-style), `error.err_code` (unique NATS code, e.g. 10059 stream not found vs 10014 consumer not found), and `error.description` which "is variable and can change it's content between server versions." Absence of `error` indicates success.
- [CLNT] JSON Schema Draft 7 documents describe all JSON requests/responses; schemas live in the jsm.go repo `schemas/` directory; `nats schema list|show|validate` inspects them.
- [SIZE][CLNT] Sequence fields are unsigned 64-bit ("JetStream can store up to the limit of an unsigned 64bit integer messages"); this "exceeds what is possible with JSON, languages might need to have custom JSON parsers."
- [SIZE][CLNT] Some fields are platform-dynamic (e.g. `max_deliver`): "in practise you have to assume they are 64bit integer."
- [SIZE][CLNT] `max_msg_size` is a signed 32-bit integer, min -1 (unlimited), max 2147483647.
- [CLNT] Durations are sent to the server as nanoseconds; timestamps are RFC 3339 strings with sub-second precision, ideally UTC, but server accepts and may return zoned times.
- [CLNT] Text-based `-ERR <reason>` API errors "are very uncommon now in the API and will likely be entirely removed in time."
- [OPS] `nats --trace` logs raw API subjects and bodies; "an invaluable way to observe the interaction model."

## ADR-2: NATS Typed Messages
- path: adr/ADR-2.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-2.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2020-05-06

### Claims
- [CORE][CLNT] All outward-facing JSON (monitoring, JetStream API, advisories) is described by JSON Schema Draft 7; "Specifically this is not for server to server communication protocols."
- [CORE] Two typed-message kinds: `Message` (has `type` hint) and `Event` (adds `id` + `timestamp`, "suitable for transformation to Cloud Events. Typically, published unsolicited").
- [CORE] Type naming: `io.nats.<source>.<category>.v<version>.<name>`; sources are `server` and `jetstream`; categories in use: `api`, `advisory`, `metric`. `io.nats.unknown_message` is returned for anything without valid type hints.
- [CORE] Versioning philosophy: "we only add fields and do not significantly change the meaning of existing ones, this means the messages stay `v1`, but major changes will require bumps."
- [CORE] Advisories must carry `timestamp` (RFC 3339 UTC, sub-second) and `id` ("Any sufficiently unique ID such as those produced by `nuid`").
- [CORE] The `error` object is omitted on success; "acceptable error codes are between `300` and `599`."
- [OPS] `nats events` displays any event; consider adding formatting support whenever a new event is added.
- [OPS] Consequence: "/varz" and similar data "move into the realm of being controlled and versioned."

## ADR-3: NATS Service Latency Distributed Tracing Interoperability
- path: adr/ADR-3.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-3.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a | date: 2020-05-21

### Claims
- [OPS][SEC] Service latency tracking is configured per exported service via `latency: { sampling: 50%, subject: ... }` on an account export; today sampling is a static percentage.
- [OPS] Proposal: additional sampling value `headers` makes the server "interpret the headers ... to determine if a request should be sampled." (ADR: proposed)
- [OPS] The `io.nats.server.metric.v1.service_latency` advisory gains a `headers` field containing "only the headers used for the sampling decision."
- [OPS] Advisory includes `requestor` and `responder` blocks (acc, rtt, start, user, lang, ver, ip, cid, server) plus `service`, `system`, `total` durations and `status`.
- [OPS] Supported trace header formats intended: Zipkin B3 (`X-B3-TraceId`, single `b3`), Jaeger `uber-trace-id: {trace-id}:{span-id}:{parent-span-id}:{flags}` (bit 0x01 = sampled), W3C Trace Context `traceparent`/`tracestate` (`01` flag = sampled); OpenTelemetry uses Trace Context.
- [OPS] Author's long-term view: "every server that handles a message should emit a unique trace" but "I don't think we'll be doing that in the hot path of the server." (See ADR-41 for what was later built.)

## ADR-4: NATS Message Headers
- path: adr/ADR-4.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-4.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-05-12 (rev 2 2025-05-15 "Clarified ASCII")

### Claims
- [CORE][CLNT] NATS headers are HTTP-like (rfc7230/rfc822 field syntax): `name: value`, no space before the colon, keys may repeat, values may have surrounding whitespace.
- [CORE][SIZE] Field names must be printable ASCII 33-126 except colon; field body any ASCII except CR/LF.
- [CORE] Header block starts with version string `NATS/1.0␍␊` instead of an HTTP request line.
- [CORE][MYTH] NATS headers are case preserving, unlike HTTP: "NATS treats application headers as a part of the message _payload_ ... The server will not change the case in message conveyance." Case sensitivity "is the responsibility of the application and client participants."
- [CLNT] Server advertises header support via `headers` boolean in `INFO`; a client that wants to send headers must set `"headers": true` in `CONNECT`.
- [CORE] Wire form: `HPUB <SUBJ> [REPLY] <HDR_LEN> <TOT_LEN>` and `HMSG <SUBJECT> <SID> [REPLY] <HDR_LEN> <TOT_LEN>`; `HDR_LEN` spans from `NATS/1.0` through the blank-line ␍␊; `TOT_LEN` = payload + HDR_LEN.
- [CLNT] Client header API operations (`GET`, `VALUES`, `SET`, `DELETE`, `APPEND`) "are _case-sensitive_"; `SET` = case-sensitive `DELETE` then `APPEND`; case-insensitive variants "are only suggested, and not required."
- [CLNT] Multiple values for one key "should be serialized one per line", not comma-joined: comma lists "introduces additional parsing requirements and ambiguity."

## ADR-5: Lame Duck Notification
- path: adr/ADR-5.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-5.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2020-07-20

### Claims
- [OPS][TOPO] In lame duck mode a server "removes itself from being advertised in the cluster, and slowly starts evicting connected clients as per `lame_duck_duration`."
- [CLNT] Server signals lame duck by an `INFO` update with `ldm: true`; "the client should initiate an orderly self-disconnect or close."
- [CLNT] `ldm` is only present on servers that implement the notification.
- [CLNT] Consequence: "Currently clients have no automatic support to _disconnect_ while keeping current state."

## ADR-6: Naming Rules
- path: adr/ADR-6.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-6.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a | date: 2021-08-17

### Claims
- [SUBJ] Subjects are case-sensitive, non-empty, tokenised by `.`; `*` matches one token; `>` "is only valid as the last token and matches all tokens past that point."
- [SUBJ] Character encoding: "Subject names should be ascii characters for maximum interoperability ... No guarantees of non-ASCII support are provided."
- [SUBJ] Grammar: `term = (printable ascii 33-126 except dot, asterisk or gt)+`; `message-subject = term (dot term | asterisk)* (dot gt)?`; `reply-to = term (dot term)*` (no wildcards in reply subjects); `queue-name = term`.
- [SIZE][STRM][CONS] `stream-name`, `durable-name`, `consumer-name`, `account-name` are `filename-safe`: printable except dot, asterisk, gt, fwd-slash, backslash, "maximum 255 characters"; on Windows also excludes `< : " | ?`. "The server will reject names (return an API error) when it cannot build a valid path."
- [SUBJ] JetStream prefixes: `js-internal-prefix = dollar (prefix dot)+`; `js-user-prefix = (prefix dot)+` where prefix excludes dot, asterisk, gt, dollar.
- [KV][SUBJ] `kv-key-name = limited-term (dot limited-term)*` with `limited-term = (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dash, underscore, fwd-slash, equals)+`; `kv-bucket-name = restricted-term = (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dash, underscore)+`. "Keys starting with `_kv` are limited to internal use."
- [OBJ] `os-bucket-name = restricted-term`; `os-object-name = (any-character)+`.
- [CLNT] Go client only checks stream/consumer names are non-empty and lack `.`; NATS CLI additionally rejects `. * > / \`.

## ADR-7: NATS Server Error Codes
- path: adr/ADR-7.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-7.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-05-12

### Claims
- [CLNT][ANTI] Do not parse error description strings: "If users are parsing our error strings it means our error text form part of the Public API, we can never improve errors."
- [CLNT] `code` and `err_code` are the Public API; `description` is "specifically out of scope for SemVer protection."
- [SIZE] Error code ranges: `1xxxx` JetStream, `2xxxx` MQTT.
- [OPS] Errors are defined in `server/errors.json` in nats-server; `go generate` regenerates constants; `nats error 10059` shows details/help/URL.
- [CLNT] Example codes: 10059 stream not found (404), 10014 consumer not found, 10040 peer not a member (400), 10039 "JetStream not enabled for account" (503).

## ADR-9: JetStream Consumer Idle Heartbeats
- path: adr/ADR-9.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-9.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a | date: 2021-05-12

### Claims
- [CONS] Consumer config `idle_heartbeat` (nanoseconds) makes the server send a heartbeat "only after the specified interval has elapsed and no new messages have been delivered"; delivering a message resets the interval.
- [CONS][CLNT] Heartbeat is a regular message with status `100` and description `Idle Heartbeat`, headers `Nats-Last-Consumer` (last consumer seq delivered; 0 = none) and `Nats-Last-Stream` (newest stream seq).
- [CLNT] Purpose: "an aid to clients to detect when they have been disconnected" when "the server might have simply gone away and recovered elsewhere."
- [CLNT] Clients may count missed heartbeats and "re-create a subscription to resume messages."

## ADR-10: JetStream Extended Purge
- path: adr/ADR-10.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-10.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-06-30

### Claims
- [STRM] Purge API `$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.<stream>` returns `success` and `purged` (count).
- [STRM] Options: `seq` = upper-bound sequence, non-inclusive; `keep` = max messages retained; "The options `seq` and `keep` are mutually exclusive"; `filter` = subject (wildcards allowed).
- [STRM] `filter`+`keep` keeps at most N per filter; "To `keep` _N_ number of messages for multiple subjects, invoke `purge` with different `filter`s."
- [STRM] "If no options are provided, all messages are purged."
- [PATTERN] Use case: periodically sum samples in a stream and replace them with a single aggregate.

## ADR-11: Hostname resolution
- path: adr/ADR-11.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-11.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a | date: 2021-07-21

### Claims
- [CLNT] When a server URL is a hostname resolving to >1 IP, the client "should be randomized, unless the existing `NoRandomize` option is enabled", then try IPs in order and stop at first success.
- [CLNT][ANTI] Rationale: "Some users have DNS where the order almost never change ... would cause all clients to connect to the same server."
- [CLNT] "This should be considered as a CHANGE for client libraries, since we are changing the default behavior."

## ADR-12: JetStream Encryption At Rest
- path: adr/ADR-12.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-12.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-07-20

### Claims
- [SEC][STRM] Server-side encryption at rest is "an alternative to an encrypted filesystem or block storage that would be provided by a cloud provider."
- [SEC] Key hierarchy: EK (external key from config/env), KEK derived `KEK := PRF(EK, IV, Context)` (never stored), AEK (asset key, encrypted by KEK, stored alongside the asset).
- [SEC] Assets = account info, stream and consumer metadata and data; "each block will have a different asset key."
- [SEC] Cipher: AEAD ChaCha20-Poly1305.
- [SEC][OPS] No key rolling in the initial release: "a backup and restore will be equivalent to changing all of the encryption keys." KMS access and client-supplied EK are future ideas (ADR: proposed/not implemented).

## ADR-13: Pull Subscribe internals
- path: adr/ADR-13.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-13.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-07-20
- note: pre-simplification (legacy JetStream API era); ADR-37 supersedes the client-side workflow.

### Claims
- [CONS] A pull consumer "does not have a `delivery subject`, that is the server _does not know_ where to send the messages"; clients request via `$JS.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.<stream>.<consumer>` with an inbox reply.
- [CONS] "all pull subscribers have to be durable" (as of this 2021 ADR; ADR-37 later relaxes this).
- [CONS][SIZE] Pull request body fields: `batch` (min 1, "There is not a limit on the batch size at the level of the library"), `no_wait` (bool, default false), `expires` (ns from now; <= 0 means no expiry). "No wait takes precedence over expires if both are supplied."
- [CONS] Empty payload = batch of 1. Delivered messages arrive with the subject rewritten to the stored subject (not the inbox); reply subject is the `$JS.ACK...` subject.
- [CONS][SIZE] "At most, a consumer can only have 512 inflight pull requests, though this can be changed when creating the consumer with the `max_waiting` option." `num_waiting` in consumer info counts inflight pulls.
- [CONS][SIZE] Example consumer defaults shown: `ack_wait` 30s, `max_deliver` -1, `max_waiting` 512, `max_ack_pending` 20000.
- [CONS][CLNT] `no_wait` gives "a guaranteed instant response" which is either a message or a status; most commonly `404 No Messages`. `503` if JS unavailable; `408 Request Timeout` when too many inflight pull requests.
- [CLNT] Client pattern: first a `no_wait` request, then on 404 a long pull with `expires` set "100ms before the client side timeout" (e.g. 5s → 4990000000 ns).
- [CLNT] Clients should auto-unsubscribe at `batch+1` (to account for the leading status message) and unsubscribe when leaving early, "otherwise this risks the server sending messages to an inbox from a connected client that is no longer expecting messages."
- [CLNT] Status messages "is not returned to the user as a processable message and instead handle is as the error condition."
- [CLNT][TOPO] Pull(1) optimization uses a wildcard inbox subscription and no-wait first; "works better with topologies where JetStream is running as a leafnode on the edge." "Each pull subscriber must have its own pull request/response handler."

## ADR-14: JWT library free jwt user generation
- path: adr/ADR-14.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-14.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a | date: 2021-07-20

### Claims
- [SEC] With scoped signing keys "limits and permissions are **attached to the signing key instead of the user**", so a user-JWT issuer needs no jwt data model.
- [SEC][PATTERN] "The use of scoped signing keys is highly encouraged as a compromised key can only be used to issue certain user, NOT user with arbitrary permissions."
- [SEC][CLNT] Proposed `IssueUserJWT(signingKey, accountId, publicUserKey, name, expiration, tags)`; expiration is "optional but recommended"; "If not set, JWT will not expire." Target languages first: go, java, csharp.
- [SEC] JWT header is static `{"typ":"JWT","alg":"ed25519-nkey"}`; body has `iss` (signing key public), `sub` (user public key), `nats.issuer_account` (account id), `nats.type: user`, `nats.version: 2`.
- [SEC] `jti` is base32 sha256 of the body computed with `jti:""`; encoding is base64url without padding; signature over `header.body`.
- [SEC][PATTERN] "The `user nkey` can be generated by the signer or a requestor can provide it so the signer is unaware of the private nkey portion."

## ADR-17: Ordered Consumer
- path: adr/ADR-17.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-17.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-09-29
- note: legacy push-based ordered consumer; ADR-37 redefines ordered consumer for the new API (pull-based).

### Claims
- [CONS][CLNT] Ordered consumer is "an ordered push subscription ... that automatically checks and recovers when a gap occurs in the consumer sequence."
- [CLNT] "The subscription must track the last good stream and consumer sequences. When a gap is observed, the subscription closes its current subscription, releases its consumer and creates a new one starting at the proper stream sequence."
- [CLNT] "If hearbeats are missed, consumer might be gone (deleted, lost after reconnect, node restart, etc.), and it should be recreated from last known stream sequence."
- [CONS][ANTI] Cannot be a pull consumer, durable, bind/direct, or use queue/deliver groups.
- [CONS][SIZE] Forced config: ack_policy none, max_deliver 1, flow_control true, mem_storage true, num_replicas 1; defaults `idle_heartbeat` 5s, `ack_wait` "something large like 22 hours."

## ADR-18: URL support for all client options [STALE?]
- path: adr/ADR-18.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-18.md
- status: Deprecated | since: n/a | date: 2021-07-21

### Claims
- [CLNT][ANTI] Client authors decided NOT to encode connect options in URLs: URLs "could expose sensitive information in logs", parity across clients "would be forever churn", and URL-vs-option precedence is ambiguous.
- [CLNT] Superseded by nothing specific; ADR-40 (NATS Connection) is the spec for connect options.

## ADR-19: API prefixes for materialized JetStream views
- path: adr/ADR-19.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-19.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-11-18

### Claims
- [TOPO][CLNT] "Each JetStream only listens to default API subjects with the prefix `$JS.API`"; API prefixes let a client pick a JetStream in another account or domain.
- [TOPO][SEC] Isolation mechanisms: cross-account requires an import with an altered prefix ("an import without a prefix set will result in an error as JetStream is imported as well and we error on import overlaps"); "On leaf node connections, the nats server adds in denies for `$JS.API.>`."
- [TOPO] Crossing an account import strips the prefix back to `$JS.API`; crossing a leaf node between domains uses "an automatically inserted mapping" to do the same.
- [KV][OBJ] KV and Object Store must reuse the same API prefix: `$KV` and `$OBJ` are the default first tokens; with prefix `JS.from-acc1` a put goes to `JS.from-acc1.$KV.bin.key`, translated back to `$KV.bin.key`. Domain form: `$JS.<domain>.API.$KV.bin.key`.
- [SUBJ][ANTI] Implication: JetStream must "NOT start the first token after the API prefix with `$`"; "JetStream will never expose any functionality under `$JS.API.$KV.>`."
- [OPS] Test config exports `$JS.API.>` and `$KV.>` as services and imports them under `fromA.>` / `fromA.$KV.>`; `nats ... --js-api-prefix fromA`.

## ADR-15: JetStream Subscribe Workflow [STALE?]
- path: adr/ADR-15.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-15.md
- status: Deprecated ("Deprecate in favor of ADR-37", 2024-07-17) | since: n/a | date: 2021-08-11
- note: legacy push/pull subscribe workflow; the JSAck, ack-type, heartbeat, flow-control, and gap rules below are still the wire-level basis the newer ADRs assume.

### Claims
- [CLNT][ANTI] "If a queue name is provided, configuring heartbeat or flow control is a mistake, since the server would send those message to random members."
- [CLNT][ANTI] "For pull subscriptions ack policy of "none" or "all" is an error."
- [CLNT] Stream lookup by subject uses `<JS prefix>.STREAM.NAMES` with `{"subject": "..."}`; error unless exactly one stream matches.
- [CLNT][MYTH] Common queue-subscribe mistake: two `js.QueueSubscribe("foo","bar")` calls each create their own ephemeral consumer, so "both members were receiving the same message." Go's fix: use the queue name as the durable name when no durable/bind given.
- [CONS] `ConsumerInfo.push_bound` (server v2.3.5+) "indicates that the server has already registered an interest on the push consumer's deliver subject."
- [CLNT][ANTI] Errors to raise: non-queue sub on a consumer with `DeliverGroup`; queue name mismatch with `DeliverGroup`; pull sub on a consumer with `DeliverSubject`; "only a deliver subject can be changed for an existing JS consumer."
- [CLNT] The NATS subscription must be created before the consumer create "because for durable subscriptions, this is the only way for the server to detect if the durable is already in use."
- [CONS] JSAck reply subject "will always start with `$JS.ACK`"; v1 = 9 tokens `$JS.ACK.<stream>.<consumer>.<num delivered>.<stream seq>.<consumer seq>.<timestamp>.<num pending>`; v2 = 11+ tokens inserting `<domain>.<account hash>` after `$JS.ACK.`; no domain is encoded as `_` ("the server will make sure that users can't pick this as a domain name").
- [CLNT] Clients "must ensure that your client can support the 9 token version (v1) and versions with 11 or more tokens (v2), as new tokens may be added to the end."
- [TOPO] Why domain/account tokens are near the front: "to simplify the export/import subject, ie `$JS.ACK.<domain>.<account>.>`."
- [CONS][CLNT] Ack types: terminal `+ACK`, `-NAK`, `+TERM`; progress `+WPI`. "Once a terminal Ack Type has been published for a message, the client should ignore all other user requests to send any type of ack." With ack policy `none`, ignore all acks.
- [CLNT] Automatic Status Management (ASM) is the default: heartbeats, flow control, pull 404/408, gap awareness handled by the library.
- [CLNT][SIZE] Heartbeat alarm: "The time allowed before an alarm is raised should be 3 times the idle heartbeat interval."
- [CLNT] Gap detection compares consumer sequences from JSAck / `Nats-Last-Consumer`; "Gap checking should be disabled on queue / deliver group subscriptions."
- [CONS][CLNT] Flow control (push only): reply to the FC message's reply-to with an empty message; "The format of the Flow Control subject should not to be inspected." Server "requires that when flow control is turned on, an idle heartbeat is set." Missed FC shows as `Nats-Consumer-Stalled` header on heartbeats; respond once, "The server will ignore duplicates."
- [CLNT] Status handling: pull 404/408 never surfaced; 409 ("trying to pull from a push consumer, exceeding max ack pending") and 503 raised as errors; unknown statuses raised as errors.
- [CLNT][ANTI] Auto-deleting a library-created consumer on Unsubscribe/Drain breaks queue groups: the first member creates it and deleting it "will cause member2 to stop receiving messages."

## ADR-20: JetStream based Object Stores
- path: adr/ADR-20.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-20.md
- status: Implemented | since: compression "for NATS Server 2.10" | date: 2021-11-03 (rev 2 2023-06-14 metadata; rev 3 2024-02-05 compression)

### Claims
- [OBJ] Object store = one stream per bucket; objects stored as chunk messages; object info stored as JSON on a meta subject that "is always rolled up (per subject)."
- [OBJ][SIZE] Default chunk size: "128k (128 * 1024)"; "Clients may tune this as appropriate." Can be overridden per object via `max_chunk_size`.
- [OBJ][SUBJ] Templates: stream `OBJ_<bucket>`; chunk subject `$O.<bucket>.C.<object-nuid>`; meta subject `$O.<bucket>.M.<name-encoded>` (name base64-encoded); bucket name is `restricted-term` (A-Z a-z 0-9 dash underscore).
- [OBJ][STRM] Backing stream config: `rollup_hdrs: true`, `allow_direct: true`, `discard: "new"`, `max_age` = TTL, `max_bytes`, storage, replicas, placement; compression bool maps to stream `compression: "s2"`.
- [OBJ] Digest: "Currently `SHA-256` is the only supported digest", formatted `SHA-256=<base64>`.
- [OBJ] "Modified time is never stored"; clients set `mtime` from the message timestamp on read, current UTC on put.
- [OBJ] ObjectInfo fields: name, description, headers, metadata, options{link, max_chunk_size}, bucket, nuid, size, chunks, digest, deleted.
- [OBJ] Semantics: "Deleted objects should be treated the same as objects that don't exist" for Get; `UpdateMeta` may change only name, description, headers; renaming onto an existing object is an error; Delete of a non-existent object is an error, of an already-deleted object may no-op.
- [OBJ] `Seal()` makes the bucket immutable ("no further modifications will be allowed"); status exposes `Sealed()`, `Size()`, `IsCompressed()`, `BackingStore()` (only `JetStream`).
- [OBJ] Links: "It is an error to link to a deleted object. It is an error to link to a link."; a link may overwrite another link or a deleted object but not a live regular object. "Links are currently under discussion whether they are necessary."
- [OBJ] Future (ADR: proposed/not implemented): event notifications, locking, tiered archiving, indexing, versioning, content-type, per-chunk encoding, single-chunk read.

## ADR-21: NATS Configuration Contexts
- path: adr/ADR-21.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-21.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2021-12-14 (revs through 2024-12-03 adding Windows cert store, user JWT, TLS first)

### Claims
- [CLNT][OPS] A context is a named JSON config used by the `nats` CLI (`--context`) holding credentials, servers, domains, API prefixes; "This reflects a current implementation in use widely via the CLI as such it's a stable release. Only non breaking additions will be considered."
- [OPS] Paths follow XDG: `~/.config/nats/context.txt` (selected context name) and `~/.config/nats/context/<name>.json`; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` honoured.
- [CLNT][SIZE] Context keys: `url` (default `nats://localhost:4222`, comma-separated), `token`, `user`, `password`, `creds`, `nkey`, `cert`, `key`, `ca`, `nsc`, `jetstream_domain`, `jetstream_api_prefix`, `jetstream_event_prefix`, `inbox_prefix`, `user_jwt`, `tls_first`, `windows_cert_store`, `windows_cert_match_by`, `windows_cert_match`, `windows_ca_certs_match`. All optional, none `omitempty`.
- [SEC][OPS] `nsc` key takes URLs like `nsc://operator/account/user`; the context runs `nsc generate profile <url>` to fill `creds` and `url`; explicit `url`/`creds` override nsc output.
- [CLNT] Go sample API: `Connect(name, opts...)` or `Load(name, overrides...)`; empty name = selected context; no selected context and empty name is an error.

## ADR-22: JetStream Publish Retries on No Responders
- path: adr/ADR-22.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-22.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2022-03-18

### Claims
- [STRM][CLNT] In clustered JetStream "there can be occasional blips in leadership which can result in a number of `no responders available` errors during the election."
- [CLNT] A JetStream publish is a `Request`; if JS is not ready "the server will send to the requestor a 503 status message right away."
- [CLNT][SIZE] Go default retry: "waits for `250ms` and will retry 2 times sending the message (so that in total it would have attempted to send the message 3 times)." Options `RetryWait`, `RetryAttempts`; `RetryAttempts(-1)` retries until the context/AckWait deadline.
- [CLNT] After exhausting attempts the error is a timeout or `nats: no response from stream` if the last attempt was still no-responders.

## ADR-26: NATS Authorization Callouts
- path: adr/ADR-26.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-26.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2022-11-28

### Claims
- [SEC] Auth callout lets "an external NATS service ... generate NATS authorization and credentials by authenticating connection requests"; works in both server-config mode and operator mode.
- [SEC][SUBJ] Server sends a signed authorization request JWT to `$SYS.REQ.USER.AUTH` on `$G` (or the configured account in config mode; in operator mode the connected account). "This subject is automatically protected in the system for all users on the authorization callout account."
- [SEC] Request includes `client_info`, `client_opts` (incl. user/pass/token/nkey/JWT as sent), optional `client_tls` (cipher, version, PEM certs, verified chains), `server_id`, and `user_nkey` (server-generated) that "must be the subject of the response" ("This assists against replay attacks").
- [SEC] Response is a user JWT signed by the configured `issuer` account key (config mode) or by the account bound to the client (operator mode); `aud` must be the issuing server's public key.
- [SEC][PATTERN] "A good pattern to follow is that the authorization service runs isolated in its own account, since the system can bind a user to any authorized account."
- [SEC] Config: `auth_callout { issuer: <account public nkey>, auth_users: [ ... ], xkey: <optional> }`; users listed in `auth_users` bypass the callout (so the callout service itself can connect); any other configured user still triggers the callout.
- [SEC] Account switching: the response "can override the account that the request was processed in"; in operator mode the auth account claim lists allowed target accounts and "The response user JWT must be signed by the private key of one of these other accounts."
- [SEC] Encryption uses xkeys (x25519, NaCl Seal/Open); when `xkey` is set the request is encrypted and the server's public xkey appears in `ServerID` and plaintext header `Nats-Server-Xkey`; response may be encrypted for the server. Operator mode: xkey lives in the account's `ExternalAuthorization` claim.
- [SIZE] Example config uses `authorization { timeout: 1s ... }`.

## ADR-28: JetStream RePublish
- path: adr/ADR-28.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-28.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2022-07-08

### Claims
- [STRM][PATTERN] RePublish lets subscribers "monitor messages that have been ingested by a stream ... without incurring the overhead of defining and using a JS Consumer"; use cases: dashboards, no-side-effect monitoring of WQ/interest streams, "KV or Object Store update events as an alternative to watches, e.g. an option for cache invalidation."
- [STRM] "Re-publish occurs only after the original published message is ingested in the stream (with quorum for R>1 streams) and is _At-Most-Once_ QoS."
- [STRM] Config `republish { src (default `>`), dest (required), headers_only (default false) }`; "Destination MUST have at least 1 non-wildcard token"; "Destination MAY not match or subset the subject filter(s) of the stream"; "RePublish option configuration MAY be edited after stream creation."
- [STRM] RePublished headers: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Subject` (original), `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Last-Sequence` ("last message ingested to the same original subject (or 0 if none or deleted)"); with headers_only also `Nats-Msg-Size`. Application headers preserved.
- [STRM][ANTI] Loop prevention only checks the immediate stream: "It is possible to create a loop condition between two streams sharing an overlap in republish destinations and subject filters within a single account."

## ADR-30: Subject Transform
- path: adr/ADR-30.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-30.md
- status: Implemented | since: mapping functions "Currently (2.9.0)"; cluster-scoped weighted mappings and dropping wildcards "as of 2.10" | date: 2022-07-17

### Claims
- [SUBJ] Transforms are used in: core account subject mapping, stream definitions, stream sourcing, RePublish, cross-account service/stream imports, shadow subscriptions across leafs.
- [SUBJ][TOPO] Core account mappings support multiple weighted destinations per source (weights sum to 100%); "as of 2.10" mappings can be `cluster`-scoped and "take precedence" when published from that cluster; a non-scoped 100% set is the catch-all for other clusters or non-clustered servers.
- [SUBJ] Rules: literal source tokens are not usable by mapping functions; `*` tokens are referenced by cardinal position `$x` / `{{wildcard(x)}}`; `>` maps to the `>` position in the destination.
- [SUBJ][SEC] "For transforms that are defined in inter-account imports (streams and services) the destinations _MUST_ make use of _ALL_ of the wildcard-tokens"; from 2.10 all other uses may drop wildcard tokens. In imports "the _ONLY_ allowed mapping function is `{{Wildcard(x)}}`."
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Mapping functions (2.9.0): `Wildcard(x)`, `Partition(x,a,b,c,...)` ("a partition number between `0` and `x-1` assigned from a deterministic hashing" of the named wildcard tokens), `Split(x,y)`, `SplitFromLeft(x,y)`, `SplitFromRight(x,y)`, `SliceFromLeft(x,y)`, `SliceFromRight(x,y)`. Names valid in CamelCase or lowercase.
- [OPS] `nats server mappings` CLI utility tests transforms.

## ADR-31: JetStream Direct Get
- path: adr/ADR-31.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-31.md
- status: Implemented | since: base feature pre-2.11; multi/batch "for Server 2.11"; `start_time` "since server 2.11" | date: 2022-08-03 (rev 8 2026-04-29)

### Claims
- [STRM][MYTH] The classic `$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.<stream>` API "All such reads are routed to the current stream leader ... tracked as administrative and incur tracking overhead."
- [STRM][PATTERN] Direct Get "enables all stream peers (R>1), not just the stream leader, to respond to stream read calls as a service responder _queue group_" from their local store; "the number of servers eligible to respond to read requests is the same as the replica count of the stream."
- [STRM][TOPO][PATTERN] Mirrors with `mirror_direct: true` join the upstream's Direct Get queue group `_sys_` on `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<SRC>` and `.<SRC>.>`; mirrors "can be strategically placed for client latency-reduction" and "may be available to clients when the upstream is offline."
- [STRM] `mirror_direct` lives on the mirror stream's config; "it has no meaning when set on a non-mirror stream"; independent of the mirror's own `allow_direct`.
- [STRM][OPS] On mirror create, `mirror_direct` is aligned to the upstream's `allow_direct` when the upstream is visible (pedantic mode rejects disagreement; non-pedantic silently aligns); for External/cross-domain upstreams the user value is kept.
- [STRM][OPS] "The mirror only joins the upstream queue group once it has caught up to within a small lag window of the source"; a fresh mirror "does not yet contribute to read availability."
- [STRM][OPS][ANTI] `mirror_direct` "is captured on the mirror at create time and is not automatically refreshed when the upstream's `allow_direct` changes later"; operator must update upstream AND re-issue `STREAM.UPDATE` on each mirror. "it's suggested that users always set `mirror_direct` to their desired value."
- [STRM][MYTH] Read-after-write: the classic Get API "provides read-after-write coherency by routing requests to a stream's current peer leader"; "_Direct Get_ does not assure read-after-write coherency as responders may be non-leader stream servers ... or MIRROR downstream servers."
- [STRM][SIZE] `allow_direct` default `false`, opt-in; "The server does not enable it implicitly"; KV helper sets it for buckets. Auto-promotion on `max_msgs_per_subject > 0` "existed only briefly and was removed in server v2.9.0."
- [STRM][CLNT] If `allow_direct` is false "there will be no responder at the Direct Get API ... Clients that make requests will receive no reply message and will time out."
- [STRM] Request fields: `seq`, `last_by_subj`, `next_by_subj`, `batch`, `max_bytes`, `start_time` (2.11), `multi_last`, `up_to_seq`, `up_to_time`.
- [STRM][SEC] Subject-Appended form `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<stream>.<subject>` is a `last_by_subj` shortcut so "subject-based interest restrictions ... such that only specific subjects in stream may be read" can be applied via permissions/imports. Payload with this form is a `408` error.
- [STRM][SIZE] Batched requests send "multiple messages without any flow control"; if `max_bytes` unset "the server will use the `max_pending` configuration setting or the server default (currently 64MB)."
- [STRM] Batch ends with a zero-length message, `Status: 204`, `Description: EOB`, headers `Nats-Num-Pending` and `Nats-Last-Sequence`. Old servers "can be detected by the absence of the `Nats-Num-Pending` header in the first reply."
- [STRM] `batch: 0` or omitted = single-message Get with no EOB; batch with neither `seq` nor `start_time` defaults to `seq: 1`; both supplied is "implementation-defined and clients should pick one."
- [STRM][SIZE] Multi-subject get "may only allow matching up to 1024 subjects. Any more will result in a `413` status reply."
- [STRM][KV][PATTERN] `multi_last` + `up_to_seq`/`up_to_time` gives "consistent point in time reads" ("temporal querying"), e.g. reading a KV record as it was at seq 3.
- [STRM][CLNT] Multi pagination: pass EOB's `Nats-UpTo-Sequence` back as `up_to_seq` (stable snapshot) and `Nats-Last-Sequence + 1` as `seq` (inclusive lower bound); ends when `Nats-Num-Pending` is 0.
- [STRM] Status codes: 204 EOB, 404 no match, 408 empty/invalid request, 413 too many subjects. Success = `NATS/1.0` with no code.
- [STRM] Reply headers: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Time-Stamp`, `Nats-Subject`, plus batch/multi headers; payload is "A _regular_ (not JSON-encoded) NATS message."

## ADR-32: Service API
- path: adr/ADR-32.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-32.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2022-11-23 (rev 6 2025-02-17)

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CLNT] Goal: "reduce development to having a complexity similar to that of writing a NATS subscription" plus metadata "for standardization of discovery and observability."
- [SUBJ][SIZE] Service `name` "can only have `A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dash, underscore`"; `version` must be validated as SemVer with the official regex; `metadata` "Must be immutable once set."
- [SUBJ][CLNT] Discovery verbs `PING`, `STATS`, `INFO` under `$SRV` (prefix must be overridable like `$JS`): `$SRV.<VERB>`, `$SRV.<VERB>.<name>`, `$SRV.<VERB>.<name>.<id>`; services respond to all three levels.
- [CLNT] Response types: `io.nats.micro.v1.info_response`, `io.nats.micro.v1.ping_response`, `io.nats.micro.v1.stats_response`; common fields `type,name,id,version,metadata`.
- [OPS] STATS per endpoint: `num_requests`, `num_errors`, `last_error`, `data` (custom stats handler), `processing_time`, `average_processing_time` (nanos), plus service `started` (ISO UTC).
- [PATTERN] Groups are subject prefixes (`{group}.{name}`); group names "cannot contain `>` wildcard"; endpoints can be added after start; "there is no option to remove an endpoint or a group."
- [CLNT] Error convention: responses must include headers `Nats-Service-Error` and `Nats-Service-Error-Code` (numeric); "clients making request from the service _must_ check if the response is an error by looking for these headers."
- [PATTERN][SIZE] "All service request handlers operate under the default queue group `q`" so scaling = add/stop instances; use different `queueGroup` to fan out a request to multiple instances for fastest responder. Endpoints may opt out of queue groups (normal subscribe).
- [SUBJ][ANTI] "Handler subject does not contain the `$SRV` prefix. This prefix is reserved for internal handlers."
- [CLNT] Handlers behave like normal subscription handlers: "no assumption is made on whether returning from the callback signals that the request is completed."

## ADR-33: Metadata for Stream and Consumer
- path: adr/ADR-33.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-33.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a (server PR #3797) | date: 2023-01-23

### Claims
- [STRM][CONS] Both stream and consumer config gain a `metadata` map of string→string; previously "The only solution was using `Description` field, which is a not ergonomic workaround."
- [SIZE] "the size of it is limited to 128KB. Size is equal to len of all keys and values summed."
- [ANTI] "`_nats` is a reserved prefix" for server/client internals; "Server can lock its metadata to be immutable and deny any changes." Example `_nats.mirror.domain`.

## ADR-34: JetStream Consumers Multiple Filters
- path: adr/ADR-34.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-34.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a (server PR #3500) | date: 2023-01-18
- note: a stray duplicate copy of this file also sits at repo root `ADR-33.md` (title "JetStream Consumers Multiple Filters").

### Claims
- [CONS] Consumer config gains `filter_subjects []string`; motivation: feature requests and "That could also reduce the number of Consumers in general."
- [CONS][ANTI] "Subjects can't overlap each other and have to fit the interest of the Stream. In case of overlapping subjects, error (10136) will be returned."
- [CONS] Only one of `filter_subject` / `filter_subjects` may be passed (error 10134); at the time, only the old consumer create API (without filter in subject) could be used (error 10135).
- [CLNT] Clients must check returned consumer info to confirm filters "to ensure compatibility with old servers that are not aware of `filter_subjects`."
- [CONS] Server keeps "a buffer of first message for each subject filtered and will deliver them in order", refilled per subject after delivery.

## ADR-35: JetStream Filestore Compression
- path: adr/ADR-35.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-35.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a (server PRs #4004, #4072; 2.10 era) | date: 2023-05-01

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Motivation: "filestore encryption can almost completely prevent host filesystem compression or deduplication from working"; server compresses "before encryption takes place."
- [STRM] Stream config field `compression`: `"none"` or `"s2"`; settable on create and update, shown in info. Clients need no change to publish/consume.
- [STRM] Blocks are compressed asynchronously "when they cease to be the tail block" to avoid hurting publish throughput; compaction/truncation compress synchronously.
- [STRM] Block-level (not per-message) compression chosen because it "provides significantly better compression ratios" on repetitive structured data such as JSON; checksum stays uncompressed for integrity checks without decompressing.
- [STRM][OPS] Changing the algorithm later only affects new blocks; "this will not result in existing blocks being proactively compressed or decompressed."
- [OPS] "a compressed stream may suffer some performance penalties compared to an uncompressed stream."

## ADR-36: Subject Mapping Transforms in Streams
- path: adr/ADR-36.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-36.md
- status: Implemented | since: "version 2.10 of the NATS server" | date: 2023-02-10

### Claims
- [SUBJ][STRM] Rationale: core-level mapping needs server config or the account key; stream-level transforms "makes it very easy for the application developers or the NATS administrators to define and manage those mappings."
- [STRM] Transforms can be applied in a mirror, in each source, at stream ingress (`subject_transform {src,dest}` at top level, applied "before limits are applied"; "it does not filter messages, it only transforms"), and in RePublish.
- [STRM][PATTERN] Ingress transform "enables the ability to insert a partition number as a token in the message subjects."
- [STRM] "there can not be any subject mapping transformation without an associated subject filter"; empty `dest` = filter only, no transform.
- [STRM] Mirrors/sources take `subject_transforms: [{src,dest}]`; "if you use the `subject_transforms` array then you can _NOT_ also use the single string subject filters."
- [STRM] "it is now possible to source not just from different streams but also from the same stream more than once."
- [STRM][MYTH] Ordering: a single source with multiple non-overlapping filters "the ordering of the messages is guaranteed to be preserved"; multiple sources from the same stream may overlap (duplicating messages) "but the order of the messages between the sources is not guaranteed to be preserved."
- [KV][PATTERN] KV bucket sourcing: bucket B sourcing A adds transform `{"src": "$KV.A.>", "dest": "$KV.B.>"}` on the source.
- [SIZE] Example configs show `duplicate_window: 120000000000` (2 minutes) as the default dedup window.

## ADR-37: JetStream Simplification
- path: adr/ADR-37.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-37.md
- status: Approved | since: n/a (rev 1 stable 2023-05-30; rev 2 2024-06-07 reconnect; rev 3 2026-02-10 adds 423/408 statuses) | date: 2022-11-23

### Claims
- [CLNT][ANTI] Problem with legacy API: clients "create and update a consumer definition on the fly as `subscribe()` ... is invoked. This leads to some unexpected behaviors as different clients ... attempt to consume from the same consumer." Also forced Push vs Pull choice.
- [CLNT] New API components: JetStreamContext (stream mgmt + direct consumer mgmt), Stream (consumer mgmt, purge, info, getMsg, deleteMsg), Consumer (`consume()`, `fetch()`, `next()`, `info()`, optional `delete()`).
- [CLNT] Consumer creation: `createConsumer`, `updateConsumer`, `createOrUpdateConsumer`.
- [CLNT][SIZE] "pull requests issued by clients should have client-side timeouts in addition to server-side timeout (`expiry`). Client-side timeout value should always be larger than expiry."
- [CLNT] Fetch: ends when the request expires or the requested count/bytes are delivered; at least one of `max_messages` / `max_bytes` is required; "For requests with `expires > 30s`, heartbeats should be enabled by default."
- [CLNT] Next: "The pull request to fetch the message should only be sent once `Next` is invoked."
- [CLNT] Consume: keeps a refillable buffer; "`max_messages` and `max_bytes` are exclusive"; if `max_bytes` set, "set `batch_size` in requests to a large number (e.g., 1 000 000)" because "`batch_size == 0`" makes the server send only one message.
- [CLNT][SIZE] Consume defaults: `max_messages` "probably between 100 and 1000"; `expires` default 30s, minimum 1s; `idle_heartbeat` = 1/2 of expires, min 500ms, max 30s; `threshold_messages` 50% of max_messages; `threshold_bytes` 50% of max_bytes. Must work when `max_messages` is 1.
- [CLNT] Consume uses "a single subscription to handle responses for all pull requests"; tracks aggregate pending messages/bytes; new pull when threshold reached; each pull sized "so that the pull request will fill the buffer."
- [CLNT] Pending counters are corrected from termination statuses carrying `Nats-Pending-Messages` / `Nats-Pending-Bytes` headers: 408 Request Timeout, 409 Message Size Exceeds MaxBytes, 408 Interest Expired, 423 Nats-Wrong-Pin-Id.
- [CLNT][SIZE] Message size for byte accounting = `len(subject) + len(ackReply) + len(hdr) + len(msg)` (server's formula, transport subject excluded).
- [CLNT] Status classes: Errors = 400 Bad Request, 409 Consumer Deleted, 409 Consumer is push based. Warnings = 409 Exceeded MaxRequestBatch / MaxRequestExpires / MaxRequestMaxBytes / MaxWaiting. Not telegraphed = 404 No Messages, 408 Request Timeout, 409 Message Size Exceeds MaxBytes, 408 Interest Expired, 423 Nats-Wrong-Pin-Id.
- [CLNT] `next()`/`fetch()` conclude when the pull terminates; `consume()` recovers by re-pulling "unless the status is `409 Consumer Deleted` or `409 Consumer is push based`."
- [CLNT][SIZE] "`Consume()` should always use idle heartbeats"; warning if timer reaches "2 * request's idle_heartbeat"; timer reset on any message; "Heartbeat errors are not terminal."
- [CLNT] Reconnect behaviour (rev 2): on disconnect pause heartbeat timer and stop publishing pulls; on reconnect reset timer and publish a new pull. "Clients should never terminate the `Consume()` call on disconnect and reconnect events and should not check if consumer is still available after a reconnect."
- [CLNT][TOPO] `info()` and `delete()` are optional because "a consumer that is exported across an account" may not have those APIs available.
- [CLNT] "The legacy functionality will be deprecated."

## ADR-38: OCSP Peer Verification
- path: adr/ADR-38.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-38.md
- status: Implemented | since: examples show server 2.10.0-beta.41; OCSP Stapling prior work "Server 2.3+" | date: 2023-06-20

### Claims
- [SEC] OCSP Peer verifies an external peer's cert chain against the CA's OCSP responder during TLS handshake, "after trust-chain verification is successful"; applies to CLIENT (NATS, MQTT, WebSocket) and LEAF connections only; "does not overlap or supersede the OCSP Stapling feature" (which covers ROUTE/GATEWAY).
- [SEC][OPS][ANTI] Adding OCSP responder dependency "necessarily adds a single point of failure (SPOF) from the NATS Server point of view and will in any case slow overall connection time"; mitigated by a local response cache.
- [SEC][SIZE] `ocsp_peer` in a `tls` map: short form bool (default false) or long form with `verify` (false), `ca_timeout` (2s), `allowed_clockskew` (30s), `warn_only` (false), `unknown_is_good` (false), `allow_when_ca_unreachable` (false), `cache_ttl_when_next_update_unset` (3600s).
- [SEC] mTLS `verify: true` is required for inbound NATS/MQTT/WebSocket/leaf-hub OCSP peer; outbound leaf (spoke) verifies the TLS server and does not require mTLS.
- [SEC][SIZE] `ocsp_cache`: default `true`/`local` when any listener has ocsp_peer; long form `type` (local|none), `local_store` (default `_rc_`, "Setting a fully qualified directory path for `local_store` is recommended"), `preserve_revoked` (false), `save_interval` (300s, min 1s).
- [SEC] Verification passes if: self-signed cert, or a chain with zero OCSP-eligible links, or a chain whose eligible links all return Good. Eligibility = issuing CA declares an http/https OCSP URI in the AIA extension; trust anchors are not evaluated.
- [SEC] Responder non-response or non-200 → "consider the certificate not OCSP valid" (no advisory emitted); `allow_when_ca_unreachable` treats non-response as Good unless a cached Revoked entry exists ("even if expired").
- [SEC][OPS] Rejection handshake errors: `client not OCSP valid` / `server not OCSP valid`; advisories `io.nats.server.advisory.v1.ocsp_peer_reject` on `$SYS.SERVER.<server>.OCSP.PEER.CONN.REJECT` and `ocsp_peer_link_invalid` on `$SYS.SERVER.<server>.OCSP.PEER.LINK.INVALID`.
- [OPS] Cache eviction is passive (only when the cert is evaluated again); `varz` gains `tls_ocsp_peer_verify` and `ocsp_peer_cache` stats (misses, cached/good/revoked counts).

## ADR-39: Certificate Store
- path: adr/ADR-39.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-39.md
- status: Implemented | since: n/a | date: 2023-06-22

### Claims
- [SEC][OPS] TLS map gains `cert_store`, `cert_match_by` (default `Subject`), `cert_match` so the server's TLS identity can come from a credential store instead of files; "Edge computing scenarios involving large 'fleets' of managed servers may especially require credential store integration."
- [SEC][ANTI] `cert_store` replaces `cert_file`/`key_file`; configuring both errors at startup: `'cert_file' and 'cert_store' may not both be configured`; `key_file` is ignored if `cert_store` is set.
- [SEC] Providers: `WindowsCurrentUser`, `WindowsLocalMachine` (Microsoft KSP "MY" store); provider name case-insensitive; unknown provider errors `cert store type not implemented`.
- [SEC] Server tries to build a trust chain from the Windows store and includes non-self-signed intermediates in the presented chain; if none found, presents the leaf only.
- [SEC] `cert_match_by` is `Subject` or `Issuer`, matched against individual RDN values (e.g. `example.com` matches, `CN = example.com` does not); recommended: look up by the unique Subject CN "to avoid TLS negotiation failure caused by return of the wrong certificate."

## ADR-40: NATS Connection
- path: adr/ADR-40.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-40.md
- status: Implemented | since: TLS-first "since NATS Server 2.10.4" | date: 2023-10-12 (rev 4 2025-11-05 custom server pool + reconnect handler)

### Claims
- [CLNT][CORE] Connect flow: TCP → server `INFO` → client `CONNECT` → PING/PONG. With `protocol >= 1` in CONNECT "Server can send subsequent `INFO` on a ongoing connection" and clients must update server lists.
- [CLNT][SEC] Explicit TLS: upgrade after INFO if `tls_required` or client demands TLS. TLS First (implicit) requires server `tls { handshake_first }` and client `tls_first`; "available since NATS Server 2.10.4".
- [SEC][SIZE] `handshake_first` values: `false` (default), `true` (enforced; "Clients that do not use this flow will fail to connect"), a duration (hybrid wait), `auto` ("By default it waits 50ms for TLS upgrade before sending the INFO").
- [CLNT][TOPO] INFO may carry additional cluster URLs; clients store them for reconnect; "A client should have an option to turn off using advertised URLs. By default, those URLs are used."
- [CLNT] On-demand `reconnect()` for auth refresh / rebalancing: drops the connection and performs standard reconnect with full resubscribe.
- [CLNT] Custom server pool (rev 4): option to use only a provided pool; "By default, advertised servers are merged with the provided pool"; new pool follows the same randomisation/max-reconnect rules. Reconnect-to-specific-server callback may pick only from the pool and may return a delay.
- [CLNT] Disconnect detection: "Missing two consecutive PONGs from the Server" (configurable) or network errors.
- [CLNT] Reconnect rules: immediate first attempt; then "Exponential backoff with jitter" ("to avoid thundering herd problems"); random order over advertised servers unless randomisation disabled; success resets timers; resubscribe everything.
- [CLNT] Disconnect buffer aggregates publishes during outage; when full "publish attempts should return error."
- [CLNT][SIZE] Defaults: ping interval 2 minutes; max pings out 2; retry on failed initial connect false; max reconnects "3 / none" ("can also be a footgun and surprise for users who do not expect that the client can give up entirely"); connection timeout 5s; tls required false; ignore advertised servers false; retain servers order false.
- [CLNT][SEC] `-ERR Permissions Violation` matches `/(Publish|Subscription) to (\S+)/` and optionally `/using queue "(\S+)"/`; for subscriptions "errors are _terminal_ for the subscription, as the server cancels the clients interest"; notify the first matching subscription (server sends one error per offense).
- [CLNT][SEC] `Authorization Violation` → server disconnect; `User Authentication Expired` and `Account Authentication Expired` → disconnect, then reconnect is rejected with `Authorization Violation` until refreshed.
- [CLNT][SIZE] `Maximum Payload Violation` → disconnect; "clients should test payload sizes and fail publishes that exceed the server configuration." `maximum subscriptions exceeded` "is not terminal to the connection."
- [CLNT] `maximum connections exceeded` and `Connection throttling is active...` (from tls `connection_rate_limit`) → reconnect loop; `invalid client protocol`, `Unknown Protocol Operation` → disconnect; `no responders requires headers support` should not occur since "Current clients hardcode `headers: true`" and "`headers` connect option shouldn't be exposed by the clients."
- [CLNT] `maximum account active connections exceeded` is not notified; the client just sees a refused connection.
- [CLNT][OPS] Client statistics (persist across reconnects): bytes in/out (socket level), messages in (`MSG`/`HMSG`), messages out (`PUB`/`HPUB`), connects/reconnects; new parity fields should use new names (e.g. Go `TotalBytesIn`).

## ADR-41: NATS Message Path Tracing
- path: adr/ADR-41.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-41.md
- status: Implemented | since: "a feature of the NATS Server 2.11" | date: 2024-02-22

### Claims
- [OPS][TOPO] Motivation: with super clusters, leafnodes, accounts and JetStream "knowing the path that messages take through the system is hard to predict" and "it's hard to know where messages can be lost, denied or delayed."
- [OPS] Trace event types: `in` Ingress, `sm` Subject Mapping, `se` Stream Export, `si` Service Import, `js` JetStream, `eg` Egress; one trace message per server traversed, each holding multiple events.
- [OPS] Activation is per-message via headers, "there is no flag to enable it on all messages": `Nats-Trace-Dest` (subject for traces), `Nats-Trace-Only` (`1`/`true`/`on`: trace without delivering; also "messages will also not traverse any Route, Gateway or Leafnode that does not support the Tracing feature"), `Accept-Encoding` (`gzip`, `snappy`).
- [OPS] W3C `traceparent` `sampled` flag can trigger tracing when the account sets `msg_trace { dest, sampling }`; sampling default "100%"; ad-hoc `Nats-Trace-Dest` "has precedence."
- [SEC][TOPO] "By default a trace will end at an account boundary when crossing an Import or Export. This is a security measure"; opt in with `allow_trace: true` on the service export (exporter side) or on the stream import (importer side).
- [OPS] `nats trace <subject>` CLI renders the path; parsing helper in jsm.go `api/server/tracing`.
- [OPS] Trace messages carry `server` info, `request` (headers, msgsize, `Nats-Trace-Hop`), `hops` (remote destinations this server forwards to), `events`. Hop numbering: origin has none; forwarded copies get `1`, `2`, then `1.1`, `2.1`, forming a DAG.
- [OPS] `kind` values: 0 CLIENT, 1 ROUTER, 2 GATEWAY, 3 SYSTEM, 4 LEAF, 5 JETSTREAM, 6 ACCOUNT.
- [OPS][MYTH] For non-client egresses "the subscription and queue group will be omitted. This is because NATS Servers optimize and send a single message across servers, based on a known interest, and let the remote servers match local subscribers."
- [OPS] Ingress `error` is filled when ACLs deny a publish (e.g. `Permissions Violation for Publish to "deny.x"`); JetStream event `nointerest: true` means "an `Interest` type Stream did not persist the message because it had no interest."

## ADR-42: Pull Consumer Priority Groups
- path: adr/ADR-42.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-42.md
- status: Approved | since: 2.11 (tag); `failover` "As of NATS Server 2.14 ... not implemented" | date: 2024-05-14 (rev 8 2026-04-29)

### Claims
- [CONS] Consumer config gains `PriorityGroups: [...]` and `PriorityPolicy`; the policy activates the feature; "PriorityGroups require at least one entry."
- [CONS][SIZE][ANTI] "In the initial implementation we should limit `PriorityGroups` to one per consumer only and error should one be made with multiple groups." Group names must match ADR-6 `limited-term` "and may not exceed 16 characters."
- [CONS][ANTI] "This is only supported on Pull Consumers, configuring this on a Push consumer must raise an error."
- [CONS][MIG][ANTI] "we cannot support updating a consumer from one with groups to one without and vice versa ... We also cannot switch between different policies." Only `PriorityTimeout` is updatable today.
- [CONS][PATTERN] `overflow` policy: pulls are served only when `num_pending >= min_pending` OR `num_ack_pending >= min_ack_pending`; otherwise they idle like empty pulls (still get heartbeats). Use case: `us-west-1` takes overflow when `us-east-1` backlog is high. Requires `AckPolicy: explicit` (pedantic mode errors otherwise).
- [CONS][SIZE] Pull fields: `group` (mandatory; unknown group = error), `min_pending`, `min_ack_pending`, `failover` (seconds; min 5, max 3600; nearest failover value wins; nearer pulls reset timers). "As of NATS Server 2.14 the `failover` option is not implemented; the server silently ignores the field."
- [CONS][PATTERN] `pinned_client` policy: one client receives all messages; standbys keep pulls waiting; server re-pins on `PriorityTimeout` expiry or admin unpin. Default example `PriorityTimeout: 2*time.Minute`; requires explicit ack.
- [CONS][MYTH] "We should not describe this in terms of exclusivity as there is no such guarantee, there will be times when one client thinks it is pinned while processing messages when it isn't anymore because the server switched."
- [CONS][CLNT] Pinned flow: server sets `Nats-Pin-Id: xyz` header on delivered messages; the client must send that `id` on all later pulls; pulls with a wrong `id` get a `423` status (`Nats-Wrong-Pin-Id` / `Nats-Pin-Id mismatch`) and the client "will clear its stored ID and issue subsequent pull requests with no ID set so it remains in the candidate pool."
- [CONS] Pulls that omit `id` while another client is pinned "is **not** rejected" and stay queued as standby candidates.
- [CONS] Re-pin procedure: stop delivery for the group, "wait for all in-flight messages to be completed, continue to serve heartbeats", pick new client, store nuid, deliver with ID, emit advisory, `423` to stale-ID pulls.
- [CONS][SIZE][PATTERN] "The `PriorityTimeout` is recommended to be sufficiently above the `Expires` value of the pull request"; with 2-minute timeout "a recommended maximum value of `Expires` could be 1 minute"; a new pull acts as a liveness heartbeat for the pin.
- [CONS][OPS] Unpin API: `$JS.API.CONSUMER.UNPIN.<STREAM>.<CONSUMER>` with payload `{"group": "groupName"}`. Consumer state adds `priority_groups: [{group, pinned_client_id, pinned_ts}]`.
- [OPS] Advisories: `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.PINNED` (`io.nats.jetstream.advisory.v1.consumer_group_pinned`) and `...UNPINNED` (`consumer_group_unpinned`, reason `admin` or `timeout`).
- [CONS][PATTERN] `prioritized` policy: pulls carry `priority` 0–9 (default 0); "Lower priorities will always be served first"; round-robin within a priority. Trade-off vs overflow: "zero delay and with less configuration, it could however result in some flip-flop in work moving between regions quite frequently."
- [CLNT] Clients must expose `group`, `min_pending`, `min_ack_pending`, `priority` on fetch/consume, track and clear `Nats-Pin-Id`, and implement `unpin`. Callbacks for becoming pinned / losing pin are suggested.

## ADR-43: JetStream Per-Message TTL
- path: adr/ADR-43.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-43.md
- status: Implemented | since: 2.11 (tag); Delete/Purge API markers "As of Server version 2.14 ... not currently implemented" | date: 2024-07-11

### Claims
- [STRM][USECASE] Motivation: KV tombstones "forever clog up the buckets with noise"; server-applied limits could leave short-TTL tombstones to notify KV watchers; some messages (schema/type hints) need infinite retention inside a stream with MaxAge.
- [STRM] Header `Nats-TTL` takes seconds or a Go duration (`1h`); deadline = stream timestamp + duration.
- [STRM][MYTH] `Nats-TTL: never` "will result in a message that will never be expired. This applies to both per-message TTL processing and stream-level age limits: a `never` message is not removed by the stream's `MaxAge` setting."
- [STRM][SIZE][ANTI] Unparsable values, or durations "below the 1 second minimum (including a literal `0`)", cause an error in the Pub Ack and the message is discarded (err_code 10165 `invalid per-message TTL`). Publishing `Nats-TTL` to a stream with the feature disabled → 10166 `per-message TTL is disabled`.
- [STRM][KV] Limit markers: when age-based removal (stream MaxAge or per-message TTL) removes the last message on a subject, the server places a marker with `Nats-Marker-Reason: MaxAge` and `Nats-TTL` = `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` (e.g. `1m0s`). "This behavior is off by default unless opted in on the `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL`."
- [STRM] `Nats-Marker-Reason: Remove` (delete API) and `Purge` (purge API) markers are specified but "As of Server version 2.14 this feature is not currently implemented."
- [STRM][TOPO] "Sources and Mirrors will always accept and store messages with `Nats-TTL` header present, even if the `AllowMsgTTL` setting is disabled"; with it disabled "the messages are just stored" (enables audit-trail replication of tombstones).
- [STRM][ANTI] "Mirrors may not enable `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` since it would insert new messages into the Stream it might make it impossible to match sequences" (err 10052 `subject delete markers forbidden on mirrors`).
- [STRM] Config: `allow_msg_ttl` bool, `subject_delete_marker_ttl` duration. Restrictions: `AllowMsgTTL` "can be enabled on existing streams but not disabled" (10052 `message TTL status can not be disabled`); both TTLs have "a minimum value of 1 second"; requires API level 1; `AllowRollup` must be true and `DenyPurge` false (auto-set unless pedantic).
- [STRM][SIZE][MYTH] "Unless `MaxMsgsPer` equals 1 the server treats `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` as the minimum effective `Nats-TTL`. A publish with a `Nats-TTL` below this floor is **not** rejected — instead the server raises the effective TTL to the floor and rewrites the stored `Nats-TTL` header."

## ADR-44: Versioning for JetStream Assets
- path: adr/ADR-44.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-44.md
- status: Implemented | since: 2.11 (metadata), 2.12.0 (`Nats-Required-Api-Level`, "fully implemented") | date: 2024-07-22

### Claims
- [OPS][TOPO][MYTH] Version skew problem: the connected server may be an old leafnode without JetStream; the meta-leader "would not forward the API fields it is unaware of"; asset hosts "would silently drop fields." "Our current approach is to check the connected-server version and project that it's representitive of the cluster as a whole but this is a known incorrect approach especially for Leafnodes."
- [OPS] "our stance is to insist on homogenous cluster versions in the general case but it's not reasonable to expect this for leafnode servers nor is it possible during upgrading."
- [OPS][SIZE] API Support Level: 0 = < 2.11.0, 1 = 2.11.x, 2 = 2.12.x; "we do not require strict SemVer adherence" (may bump mid-release). Advertised in `jsz`, `varz`, `$JS.API.INFO`, and logged at JetStream startup.
- [STRM][CONS] Server-set metadata keys: `_nats.ver` (hosting server version), `_nats.level` (hosting API level), `_nats.req.level` (required level to start the asset); e.g. consumer `PauseUntil` set → required level 1. Also created-version/level keys on create.
- [OPS][ANTI] "tools like Terraform and NACK will need to understand to ignore these fields when doing their remediation loops."
- [OPS] Offline assets: incompatible streams/consumers load in offline mode with a reason map in `stream_list_response` / `consumer_list_response`; also added to the existing `missing` list "This ensure older tools will still understand these streams as inaccessible." Offline streams still reserve their subjects to keep overlap protection.
- [OPS] Strict JSON: use `DisallowUnknownFields` for API and meta-layer; incompatible API calls error, incompatible assets go offline; "This will prevent assets inadvertently reverting some settings and changing behaviour during downgrades."
- [CLNT] Clients may send `Nats-Required-Api-Level` header on any `$JS.API.>` request; server errors `api level not supported` if lower. "A single server does not represent a cluster-wide supported API level" (future: cluster-agreed level).

## ADR-47: Request Many
- path: adr/ADR-47.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-47.md
- status: Partially Implemented | since: n/a (tagged orbit) | date: 2024-09-26

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CLNT] Request Many lets a client receive multiple replies to one request, supporting "patterns like scatter-gather and sentinel."
- [CLNT] "The client doesn't assume success or failure - only that it might receive messages"; "Request Many is not a recoverable operation, but it could be wrapped in a retry pattern."
- [CLNT][SIZE] Config: total timeout (always used; defaults to connection request timeout; first wait always uses total); stall timer (optional; "Less than 1 or greater than or equal to the total timeout behaves the same as if not supplied"); max messages; sentinel predicate ("standard sentinel ... a message with a null/nil or empty payload").
- [CLNT] A status such as 503 or an error in place of a user message "is terminal" and should be conveyed at end of data.
- [CLNT] Blocking callbacks: user processing time must not count against timeouts.
- [CLNT][SIZE] Strategies: "Timeout or Wait" (default, total only); "Stall" ("lessor of 1/10th of the total wait time ... or the default connection timeout"); "Max Responses".
- [CLNT] "it should always unsubscribe upon completion of the request handling instead of leaving it up to the server to time it out"; max-responses may `UNSUB <count>` immediately but "you still must check the count manually"; mux inbox variant cannot use that optimisation.

## ADR-48: TTL Support for Key-Value Buckets (updates ADR-8)
- path: adr/ADR-48.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-48.md
- status: Implemented | since: "Since NATS Server 2.11" (API level 1) | date: 2025-04-09 (rev 1 2025-06-30)

### Claims
- [KV][USECASE] Goals built on per-message TTL: notify watchers of MaxAge-deleted keys, "Improve Purge so that old subjects can be permanently removed, removing the need for costly compacts", and "Creating keys with a custom lifetime." KV calls these Limit Markers.
- [KV] Bucket option "Limit Markers" sets `allow_msg_ttl: true` and `subject_delete_marker_ttl` = supplied duration; "must larger than or equal to 1 second"; requires API level >= 1 (check `$JS.API.INFO`).
- [KV][MIG] Can be enabled on existing buckets "but should not support disabling it."
- [KV] `Status.LimitMarkerTTL()` returns the configured duration, "0 meaning markers are not supported."
- [KV][CLNT] `Create()` and `Purge()` accept a TTL (adds `Nats-TTL` header).
- [KV][ANTI] "do not accept a TTL for other API ... a TTL on `Put()` might mean older revisions could come back from the dead once the TTL expires."
- [KV][CLNT] `Nats-Marker-Reason` mapping for readers/watchers: `MaxAge` → treat as PURGE, `Purge` → PURGE, `Remove` → DEL.

## ADR-49: JetStream Distributed Counter CRDT
- path: adr/ADR-49.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-49.md
- status: Approved | since: 2.12.0 (API level 2) | date: 2025-04-14 (rev 8 2026-05-27)

### Claims
- [STRM][PATTERN] A stream opts in with `allow_msg_counter: true`; then "All subjects in the stream must be counters." Publishing with `Nats-Incr` loads the last value on the subject, adds, and stores the new total in the body `{"val":"101"}`; PubAck returns `val` "avoiding a Get to get the latest value."
- [STRM] Only addition/subtraction; "automatically behave as a CRDT and be order independent." Header must match `^[+-]\d+$` (BigInt; `0` valid); unparsable → reject. Server "will always use `big.Int`". Value is a JSON string "since JavaScript would only support up to `2^53`."
- [STRM][ANTI] Counter streams reject messages without `Nats-Incr`; reject messages carrying `Nats-Rollup`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Subject-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Stream`, or `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id`; `Nats-Incr` to a non-counter stream is rejected.
- [STRM][TOPO] Received via Source (feature off) or Mirror: "the message is stored verbatim."
- [STRM][TOPO] Source-aware tracking: `Nats-Counter-Sources` header (keyed by source stream name + pre-transform subject) holds last seen `val` per source; on a sourced message the server rewrites `Nats-Incr` to the delta vs last seen value, so recounts stay correct "even if some messages from the source were lost"; adding a source with existing value 10 yields first `Nats-Incr: 10`. Source keys "is not ever removed."
- [STRM] "aggregated counters will always be eventually consistent with their sources, even if the aggregating stream also has local additions or subtractions."
- [STRM][PATTERN] Global counters: regions publish on e.g. `count.es.hits`, sourcing rewrites to `count.eu.hits` then `count.hits`; aggregate streams may listen on no subject; mirror ES→EU then source into aggregate to keep both regional and total values.
- [STRM][OPS][ANTI] Resets: "a purge will not replicate, a roll-up would replicate and destroy the entire counter everywhere so the only real option is to publish a negative value"; preferred reset = negative value then purge up to that message; subject purge only for full deletes.
- [STRM][ANTI] Config restrictions: error on Mirror; only Limits retention; "can only be enabled during creation"; no Discard New; not with Per-Message TTL; "Message schedules (see ADR-51) are not supported"; requires API level 2.
- [CLNT][PATTERN] Client lands in Orbit as a dedicated Counter module (not KV) because counter management "would not belong in KV"; requires `AllowMsgCounter` and `AllowDirect` (batch direct get for `GetMultiple`); API `Add`, `AddInt`, `Get`, `GetMultiple` with wildcard subjects; `Entry{Subject, Value *big.Int, Sources, Incr}`.

## ADR-50: JetStream Batch Publishing
- path: adr/ADR-50.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-50.md
- status: Approved | since: atomic batch 2.12.0 (API level 2); dedup 2.12.1; EOB commit + fast ingest 2.14.0 (API level 4) | date: 2025-06-10 (rev 10 2026-03-13)

### Claims
- [STRM][PATTERN] Goals: performance, "Atomic Batch writes - where an entire batch is stored or abandoned", and batching RAFT append entries (the last is out of scope here).
- [STRM][KV][USECASE] Atomic use case: a KV user record spanning 5 keys (address) "Performing updates on these related keys is not safe today as writes might fail after a first update resulting in an address line in one city but a post code in another."
- [STRM][CLNT] Atomic protocol: first message is a *request* with `Nats-Batch-Id:<uuid>` and `Nats-Batch-Sequence:1` (server replies error or zero-byte); subsequent messages increment the sequence (optional reply gets zero-byte ack); final message has `Nats-Batch-Commit:1` (stored) or `Nats-Batch-Commit:eob` (2.14; not stored, `BatchSize` excludes it) and receives the pub ack.
- [STRM][SIZE] Batch ID max 64 characters (err 10179); missing sequence 10175; sequence exceeds server limit "default 1000" (10199); batch not enabled 10174; incomplete/abandoned 10176; unsupported header `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` 10177; duplicate `Nats-Msg-Id` inside a batch 10201.
- [STRM][SIZE] Atomic server limits: "Each stream can only have 50 batches in flight"; "Each server can only have 1,000 batches in flight"; abandoned after "10 seconds since the last message" (advisory, no error reply); "Each batch can have maximum 1000 messages."
- [STRM] Gaps in batch sequence reject the batch; expected-header checks (`ExpectedLastSeq` etc.) are evaluated "at the time when the batch is committed under lock"; "Only the first message of the batch may contain `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence`"; `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence` only valid if no earlier batch entry writes the same subject.
- [STRM][ANTI] "If a stream is operating on the `PersistMode: async` mode, any batch published to it must fail" (atomic). `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` unsupported in batches. Dedup via `Nats-Msg-Id` supported "Starting from 2.12.1"; duplicates reject the batch.
- [STRM][OPS] Abandonment advisory `io.nats.jetstream.advisory.v1.stream_batch_abandoned` with reasons `timeout`, `large`, `incomplete`, `unsupported`.
- [STRM] Pub ack gains `batch` (id) and `count` (size); ack sequence is the final message's; earlier messages occupy the preceding sequences.
- [STRM][PATTERN] Fast-ingest batches (2.14): "not reliable, meaning messages can be lost and the batch will not be abandoned"; "not pre-staged and so will not be limited to 1000 messages"; "The goal is to replace Async publish with one built on these behaviors." Motivation includes ObjectStore concurrent-writer failures "due to pending API counts."
- [STRM][CLNT] Fast-ingest control channel: reply subject `<prefix>.<uuid>.<initial flow>.<gap ok|fail>.<batch seq>.<operation>.$FI`; operations 0 start, 1 append, 2 commit+store, 3 commit EOB, 4 ping; "this must be an old style inbox" subscribed to `<prefix>.uuid.>` so unsubscribing short-circuits acks on error.
- [STRM][CLNT] "The client MUST wait for the first reply" before blasting messages; server dictates actual flow: starts low (e.g. client asks 100, server starts at 1), "usually doubles" to ramp up, "usually halves" to slow down, never exceeds the client's initial flow ("the server must treat the initial flow parameters as the upper bound").
- [STRM][CLNT] `BatchFlowAck {"type":"ack","seq":N,"msgs":M}`: with `gap: fail` "messages up to and including Sequence were persisted"; with `gap: ok` "_some_ of the messages ... were persisted." Acks are cumulative: a later ack implies earlier ones were received ("critical to avoid unrecoverable stalls").
- [STRM][SIZE][PATTERN] Outstanding acks guidance: 1 = flow-controlled async; "Outstanding acks = 2 ... generally optimal"; 3 only for high RTT "not a default".
- [STRM] `BatchFlowGap {"type":"gap","last_seq":10,"seq":15}` is informational, may arrive out of order, "MUST NOT be used to know whether ... was persisted." With `fail` the batch is abandoned and final ack `BatchSize` = last received before gap; with `ok` the batch continues. Leader change in `ok` mode continues with a gap message; in `fail` mode abandons.
- [STRM] `BatchFlowErr {"type":"err","seq":N,"error":{...}}` sent immediately on expected-header failures; PubAck never carries both error and persisted info, hence the separate message. Single-message batch that immediately commits returns a plain `PubAck`.
- [STRM][SIZE] Fast-ingest errors: 10205 not enabled, 10206 invalid pattern, 10207 ID > 64, 10208 unknown ID. Limits: "Each stream can only have 1,000 batches in flight"; "Each server can only have 50,000 batches in flight"; 10 s idle abandon; "no maximum size for fast ingest batches"; "`PersistMode: async` set are compatible with fast ingest."
- [STRM] Config: `allow_atomic` (API level 2) and `allow_batched` (API level 3); both toggleable via update, may coexist; `allow_atomic` + `PersistMode: async` "must error."
- [STRM][TOPO] "Mirrors can't enable these settings, and will ignore the various headers"; sourcing streams may enable them but "sources will ignore the batching headers when sourced."

## ADR-51: JetStream Message Scheduler
