- path: adr/ADR-51.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-51.md
- status: Approved | since: 2.12.0 (base); 2.14.0 (time zones, `Nats-Schedule-Rollup`, stop semantics); Discard New note "TBD" | date: 2025-03-21 (rev 8 2026-05-27)

### Claims
- [STRM][PATTERN] One message holds a cron-like schedule and the stream produces new messages into the same stream on that schedule; "the last message on a subject holds the current schedule. In other words every schedule must have its own unique subject."
- [STRM][USECASE] Use cases: delayed publish (`@at <RFC3339>`), recurring publish (`@hourly`, cron, `@every 1m`), and subject sampling (`Nats-Schedule-Source` republishes the last message on a subject on a schedule; wildcards not supported; falls back to the schedule's own body if the source has no message).
- [STRM] Headers on the schedule message: `Nats-Schedule`, `Nats-Schedule-Target` (must be a subject in the same stream), `Nats-Schedule-Source`, `Nats-Schedule-TTL` (requires `AllowMsgTTL`), `Nats-Schedule-Time-Zone` (cron only), `Nats-Schedule-Rollup` (only `sub`). Produced messages get `Nats-Scheduler`, `Nats-Schedule-Next` (next time, or `purge` for one-shot), plus `Nats-TTL`/`Nats-Rollup` if requested; other headers pass through verbatim.
- [STRM][MYTH][ANTI] "If a message is made with a schedule in the past it is immediately sent. If a server was down for a month and a scheduled message is recovered ... it will be sent immediately. To avoid this, add a `Nats-TTL` header."
- [STRM][PATTERN] Many delayed messages for one target: put schedules on `orders.schedule.<UUID>` with `Nats-Schedule-Target: orders`.
- [STRM][SIZE] Cron is 6-field (seconds first); predefined `@yearly/@annually`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily/@midnight`, `@hourly`; `@every <go duration>` "The minimum supported interval is `1s`; shorter intervals are rejected."
- [STRM][OPS] Time zones via `time.LoadLocation()` names (IANA recommended; abbreviations "are ambiguous ... not DST-aware"); fixed offsets like `+02:00` rejected; empty header rejected; "Operators must therefore install and keep tzdata up to date on every server"; DST-boundary schedules "could be skipped" or "executed twice."
- [STRM] Stopping a schedule: delete its message by sequence, purge its subject (wildcards allowed), or atomically publish to another subject with `Nats-Schedule-Next: purge` and `Nats-Scheduler: <schedule subject>`; may combine with `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence(-Subject)` to stop only if the schedule still exists. `Nats-Scheduler` may not equal the publish subject (err 10212) "because ... the cancel message would be purged together with the schedule via the auto-applied `Nats-Rollup: sub`."
- [STRM][ANTI] Config `allow_msg_schedules`: denied on Source or Mirror; "Stream should not support Discard New"; "can be enabled on existing streams but not disabled"; requires API level 2; implicitly enables `AllowRollup` and clears `DenyPurge` (server auto-applies `Nats-Rollup: sub` to schedules, so a new schedule on the same subject replaces the prior one).
- [STRM][PATTERN] Stream subjects should include a wildcard like `schedules.>` for schedule subjects, plus the target subjects.
- [STRM][OPS][ANTI] Retention interaction: "Once a schedule message is removed from storage, by any mechanism, its schedule stops firing" (MaxAge shorter than the interval, MaxMsgs/MaxBytes/DiscardOld, WorkQueue ack, Interest with no interest). "**Limits** is the simplest configuration ... recommended."
- [STRM][PATTERN] With Interest retention: option 1 pin a filtered consumer on schedule subjects (not recommended: "the pinning consumer becomes load-bearing configuration"); option 2 keep schedules in a dedicated WorkQueue stream and have the Interest stream source the target subjects ("generally the more robust configuration").

## ADR-52: No Headers support for Direct Get [STALE?]
- path: adr/ADR-52.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-52.md
- status: Deprecated ("targeted for 2.12 but the outcome was to increase inconsistency in the msg get API while at the same time being a potentially premature optimisation") | since: n/a | date: 2025-06-19

### Claims
- [STRM][ANTI] Proposed `no_hdr` option on `JSApiMsgGetRequest` to return body only (motivated by ADR-49 counters); "headers like `Nats-Sequence` will also be unset." Not implemented; superseded by nothing (ADR-31 remains the Direct Get spec).

## ADR-53: Feature flags
- path: adr/ADR-53.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-53.md
- status: Proposed | since: `js_ack_fc_v2` "Introduced 2.14" (opt-in) | date: 2026-02-20

### Claims
- [OPS][MIG] Problem: breaking behaviour changes (e.g. switching to the ADR-15 v2 `$JS.ACK.<domain>.<account hash>...` format) cannot ship in minor releases because older servers "will not know how to parse the new format", clients/tooling may lag, mixed-version systems need both formats, and "Subject permissions could be using the old format."
- [OPS] New config block `feature_flags { js_ack_fc_v2: true }` (`map[string]bool`); logged at startup as default / opt-in / opt-out; "The server will not support reloading these flags at runtime"; unknown flags are ignored but logged.
- [OPS][SIZE] Flag table: `js_ack_fc_v2` = "Use domain/account-aware JetStream ACK and FC subjects (ADR-15 v2 format)", type Opt-in, introduced 2.14, default flip TBD. In 2.14 the server "uses the V1 ack/fc format by default, but supports parsing the V2 format."
- [OPS] Convention: opt-in flags for gradual rollout that later become default; opt-out flags should be prefixed e.g. `revert_` "clearly signaling that the server reverts to old/non-default behavior."

## ADR-55: Trusted Protocol Aware Proxies
- path: adr/ADR-55.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-55.md
- status: Approved | since: 2.12 (proxy detects proxy-aware server by `api_lvl` >= 2) | date: 2025-08-04

### Claims
- [SEC][TOPO] A NATS-protocol-aware proxy connects on behalf of clients/leafnodes and must securely pass source IP, TLS properties, etc.; trust is established by listing proxy public nkeys in `proxies { trusted = [ {key: ...} ] }`.
- [SEC][OPS] `proxies` block supports config reload; "should a trusted proxy be removed we will disconnect all connections that came from that proxy"; exposed in `VARZ`.
- [SEC] `proxy_required: true` per user (config), on `leafnodes.authorization`, and a `ProxyRequired` boolean in JWTs.
- [SEC][CORE] With any proxies configured the server "always include a `nonce` in the `INFO` line" and always reports `api_lvl`; the proxy injects `proxy_sig` (signature over the nonce plus all client CONNECT fields) into `CONNECT`.
- [SEC] Server rejects a present-but-invalid `proxy_sig`; auth callout may set `ProxyRequired` so "Auth Callout does not need to know which proxies are trusted"; the proxy is recorded in `CONNZ`/`LEAFZ`; rejected clients "get the same nondescript error message as today" while logs, CONNZ reason and `client_disconnect` advisory carry the real reason.

## ADR-56: JetStream Consistency Models
- path: adr/ADR-56.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-56.md
- status: Approved | since: 2.12 (API level 2) | date: 2025-09-12
- note: "This document is a living document; at present we will only cover the `async` persistence model."

### Claims
- [STRM][MYTH] `PersistMode: async` "will result in asynchronous flushing of data to disk ... at the expense of data loss during severe disruptions in power, server or disk subsystems"; "The Publish Ack will be sent before the data is known to be written to disk."
- [STRM][OPS] Stream-level `async` overrides server `sync: always` for that stream. Modes: `default`+`sync:always` = flushed and synced; `default` without `sync:always` = flushed, synced per sync interval; `async` = PubAck first, writes batched in memory, background write.
- [STRM][ANTI] "this mode cannot support batch publishing at all" (atomic batches; ADR-50 later allows fast-ingest with async).
- [STRM][SIZE][ANTI] "Setting it on anything other than a R1 stream will result in an error"; stated verbatim: "Scaling a R1 stream up to greater resiliency levels will fail if the `PersistMode` is not set to `async`" (ADR wording; reads as if intended "is set to async"). Default is unset/`default` and the server leaves it unset in INFO; any explicit value requires API level 2.

## ADR-54: KV Codecs (updates ADR-8)
- path: adr/ADR-54.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-54.md
- status: Proposed (orbit) | since: n/a | date: 2025-08-06

### Claims
- [KV][CLNT] Client-side codec layer wraps a KV bucket with independent `KeyCodec` (string↔string) and `ValueCodec` (bytes↔bytes) for "character escaping, path notation conversion, encryption, and custom transformations." (ADR: proposed; Orbit.)
- [KV][USECASE] Motivating cases: keys with characters invalid in subjects (spaces, dots), filesystem-path keys, end-to-end encryption, app-specific encodings.
- [KV][CLNT] Codecs must be transparent across Put/Get/Watch/Keys/History/Delete/Purge; a `FilterableKeyCodec.EncodeFilter` preserves wildcards for watch/list; codecs may be chained (encode in order, decode in reverse).
- [KV] Built-ins: NoOp, Base64 (url-safe; "Acme Inc.contact" → "QWNtZSBJbmMuY29udGFjdA=="), Path (`/`→`.`; leading slash encoded as `_root_`, trailing slashes trimmed).

## ADR-57: KV Subject Transforms (updates ADR-8)
- path: adr/ADR-57.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-57.md
- status: Proposed | since: n/a | date: 2025-12-09

### Claims
- [KV][CLNT] KV mirror: clients "Prefix the mirror stream name with `KV_` if not already prefixed" and "Enable `MirrorDirect` on the underlying stream configuration" so mirrored buckets "Support direct reads via the Direct GET API" and "Automatically participate in RTT-based replica selection."
- [KV][CLNT] KV sources without explicit transforms: clients prefix `KV_` and auto-add `{"src": "$KV.<source>.>", "dest": "$KV.<bucket>.>"}` (with key filter folded into src, e.g. `$KV.ORDERS.NEW.>` → `$KV.NEW_ORDERS.>`).
- [KV][PATTERN] Explicit `SubjectTransforms` are preserved exactly and skip auto-generation, enabling a non-KV stream as a KV source (`events.processed.>` → `$KV.EVENT_CACHE.>`) or custom key mapping (`$KV.INVENTORY.warehouse.*.product.>` → `$KV.PRODUCTS.>`, so `warehouse.nyc.product.item123` becomes `item123`). In that case "Do not modify the source stream name prefix."

## ADR-58: Key-Value Store Roadmap and future considerations (updates ADR-8)
- path: adr/ADR-58.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-58.md
- status: Proposed (roadmap moved out of ADR-8) | since: n/a | date: 2026-01-06

### Claims
- [KV][CLNT] Read-only KV handle (`RoKV`: Get, History, Watch, Keys, Close, Status) must be supportable "against a read replica and cannot support `Put()`." (ADR: proposed)
- [KV][TOPO][MYTH] "A bucket, being backed by a Stream, lives in one Cluster only. To make buckets available elsewhere we have to use JetStream Sources and Mirrors."
- [KV][TOPO][PATTERN] KV Mirror (Replica): "Copy of exactly 1 other bucket. Used primarily for scaling out the `Get()` operations"; always read-only; may filter keys; "Replicas are automatically picked using a RTT-nearest algorithm"; replicas can be added/removed at runtime "without any re-configuration of already running KV clients"; "Writes and Watchers are transparently sent to the origin bucket"; can span accounts and domains.
- [KV][TOPO][PATTERN] KV Aggregate (Source): combines one or many buckets into a new bucket "to provide a full local copy of other buckets that support watchers and gets locally in edge scenarios"; accessed by its own name; read-only or read-write; may hold key subsets; hosts watchers; "Writes are not transparently sent to the origin Bucket ... they either fail (default) or succeed and modify the Aggregate (opt-in)"; sources can be added later.
- [KV][ANTI] "The existing domain based mirrors that are supported in KeyValueConfig will be deprecated but supported for the foreseeable future."
- [KV] Read-only aggregate stream config: `subjects: []`, `deny_delete: true`, `deny_purge: true`, sources with transform `$KV.ORDERS.NEW.>` → `$KV.NEW_ORDERS.>`; "When writable, configure as normal just add the sources."
- [KV][ANTI] Mirrors "are not called `Bucket` and may not have the `KV_` string name prefix as they are not buckets ... we have done this in the leafnode mode and decided it's not a good pattern." Requires `mirror_direct: true` and origin `allow_direct`; "We should also set the options to deny deletes and purges."
- [KV][OPS] `nats s info KV_ORDERS` shows `Alternates:` RTT-sorted; direct get reply header `Nats-Stream: MIRROR_ORDERS_NYC` confirms which replica served.
- [KV] Future list: merged buckets, replica auto-discovery, read cache, ranged ops, limits-deleted marker op, zero-trust codecs, "Formalise leader election against keys", set management for service discovery, "Distributed locks against a key", pluggable storage backends. (ADR: proposed/not implemented)

## ADR-8: JetStream based Key-Value Stores
- path: adr/ADR-8.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-8.md
- status: Implemented | since: 2.6.0 (base), 2.10.0 (sourcing, compression, metadata), 2.11.0 (limit markers, "remove non direct gets") | date: 2021-06-30 (rev 13 2026-02-02)
- note: refined by ADR-48 (TTL), ADR-54 (codecs), ADR-57 (subject transforms), ADR-58 (roadmap).

### Claims
- [KV] "The API is now stable and considered version 1.0"; "All tier-1 clients support KV."
- [KV][CLNT] `Entry` exposes Bucket, Key, Value, Created, Revision (stream sequence), Delta ("distance from the latest value", 0 = latest), Operation (PUT/DEL/PURGE). `Status` exposes Values, History, TTL, LimitMarkerTTL, IsCompressed, BackingStore (`JetStream`), Bytes, Metadata.
- [KV][CLNT] KV interface: `Put`, `Create` ("only succeeds when the key does not exist if last historic event is a delete or purge"), `Update(key, value, lastRevision)`, `Delete` (preserves history), `Purge` (removes history, leaves the purge entry), `Get`, `GetRevision`, `History`, `Watch` ("the same Entry might be delivered more than once"), `Keys` (with filters), `Status`, `Info`.
- [KV][CLNT] Manager: `KeyValue` (bind), `CreateKeyValue`, `UpdateKeyValue`, `CreateOrUpdateKeyValue`, `DeleteKeyValue`, `KeyValueBucketNames`, `KeyValueBuckets`.
- [KV][MYTH] Consistency: "We do not provide read-after-write consistency. Reads are performed directly to any replica, including out of date ones. If those replicas do not catch up multiple reads of the same key can give different values between reads." "Historically we had read-after-write consistency, this has been deprecated."
- [KV][STRM][SUBJ] Bucket = stream `KV_<Bucket>` with subjects `$KV.<Bucket>.>`; history = `max_msgs_per_subject`.
- [KV][SIZE] History: "The maximum allowed size is 64. The minimum allowed size is 1. When creating a stream, 1 should be used when the user does not supply a value."
- [KV][SIZE] TTL via `max_age`; if set: "if `max_age` is greater than 2 minutes, `duplicate_window` must be set to 2 minutes"; "if `max_age` is less than or equal to 2 minutes, `duplicate_window` must be set the same as `max_age`"; if no TTL "The server will set it to 2 minutes if not supplied." (Note: server applies this logic itself if `duplicate_window` is omitted.)
- [KV][STRM][SIZE] Fixed stream settings: `discard: new`, `rollup_hdrs: true`, `deny_delete: true`, `allow_direct: true` ("can be modified out-of-band only if desired, but not through KV bucket update"); `max_msg_size` caps value size; `max_bytes` caps bucket; "Maximum number of keys cannot currently be limited"; placement, republish, metadata allowed; compression → `s2`; storage file; R value varies.
- [KV][SIZE] Limit markers need `allow_msg_ttl: true` and `subject_delete_marker_ttl` > 1 s; require API level 1 (2.11+) "clients should assert this using the `$JS.API.INFO` call or similar means (not connected server version)."
- [KV] Writes are JetStream requests to `$KV.<bucket>.<key>`; CAS via `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence`; value `0` = "only be accepted if it's the first message on a subject. This is purge aware."
- [KV][CLNT] `Create()` on a deleted key: on `0`-failure, load current value; if it is a delete, retry with expected sequence = the delete's sequence.
- [KV][ANTI] TTL accepted only on `Create()` (not `Put`) because Put "might have the effect of surfacing history once the latest value is removed."
- [KV] Deleted data carries `KV-Operation: DEL` or `PURGE`; basic Get turns a delete into `key not found`; watchers/history return the Entry with the operation set. `Nats-Marker-Reason` mapping: MaxAge→PURGE, Purge→PURGE, Remove→DEL.
- [KV][MYTH] Gets use Direct Get `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<STREAM>.<SUBJECT>`; non-direct `last_by_subj` is legacy: "we do not support disabling direct get on any buckets."
- [KV][CONS] History and Watch use ephemeral Ordered Consumers; History = `deliver_all` filtered by key; Watch starts with `last_per_subject`; latest value has pending 0.
- [KV] Delete = message with nil body and `KV-Operation: DEL`; Purge = `KV-Operation: PURGE` + `Nats-Rollup: sub` (server deletes prior messages on that key); purge TTL adds `Nats-TTL`.
- [KV][CONS] `Keys` uses a headers-only consumer with deliver last per subject; delete bucket = delete stream.
- [KV][CLNT] Watchers must emit an End Of Initial Data signal "the first time any message has a `Pending==0`" and "must also be sent if no data is present." Options: `IncludeHistory`, `IgnoreDeletes`, `MetaOnly`, `UpdatesOnly` (EOID sent immediately). Default sends all `last_per_subject` values including delete/purge ops.
- [CLNT] API design prior art: 20+ Consul/etcd libraries reviewed; `Get()` returns an `Entry` (not raw bytes); `Create`/`Update` as helpers over Put options.

## ADR-59: JetStream Stream Sourcing and Mirroring
- path: adr/ADR-59.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-59.md
- status: Implemented | since: "documents features up to 2.12.5" | date: 2026-03-03 (rev 2 2026-04-29)
- note: "This ADR serves as the authoritative reference for stream sourcing and mirroring." Refined by ADR-60 for WQ/Interest upstreams.

### Claims
- [STRM][TOPO][PATTERN] Mirroring = "an exact, read-only copy of a single upstream stream ... primarily used for read scaling, disaster recovery, and geographic distribution." Sourcing = aggregate one or more upstreams "suitable for data aggregation, fan-in patterns, and building derived data views." Both work in one account, across accounts, and across domains.
- [STRM] `StreamSource` fields: `name` (required), `opt_start_seq` / `opt_start_time` (mutually exclusive; "Only applies on first creation"; if both set "`opt_start_seq` takes precedence"), `filter_subject` vs `subject_transforms` (mutually exclusive), `external {api, deliver}`.
- [STRM][MYTH] Mirror behaviour: "Messages are delivered in the same order and with the same sequence numbers and timestamps as the upstream stream"; read-only; "cannot have `subjects` configured"; retention/limits independent of upstream; "A stream can mirror at most one stream. Multiple streams can mirror the same stream"; `mirror` and `sources` mutually exclusive.
- [STRM][MIG][ANTI] "Mirror configuration **cannot be changed** after creation"; promote a mirror by removing the origin's subjects, then removing the mirror config and adding the subjects to the former mirror.
- [STRM][TOPO] `mirror_direct` on the mirror lets it serve `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<UPSTREAM>`; "particularly useful for KV store mirrors where reads should land on the closest replica"; joins only after catching up "within a small lag window"; captured at create, not auto-refreshed; "we recommend that operators always set `mirror_direct` explicitly."
- [STRM][OPS] With `mirror_direct: true` the upstream's StreamInfo gets an `alternates` list "sorted by RTT proximity."
- [STRM][ANTI] Mirrors cannot use: `subjects`, `sources`, `first_seq`, `allow_msg_counter`, `allow_atomic`, `allow_msg_schedules`, `subject_delete_marker_ttl`. Mirrors can use: stream-level `subject_transform`, `republish`, `compression`, `allow_msg_ttl`.
- [STRM][MYTH] Sourcing: "Messages from each individual source maintain their relative ordering. When sourcing from multiple streams, messages are interleaved in arrival order. There is no guaranteed ordering across different sources." A sourced stream "**can** also have its own `subjects`."
- [STRM] Sources "can be added, updated or removed after stream creation." Duplicate-source detection key = stream name + filter subject + subject transforms + external API prefix; same upstream may be sourced multiple times with different filters.
- [STRM][ANTI] Sourced streams cannot use `mirror` or `allow_msg_schedules`.
- [STRM] Multiple `subject_transforms` per source: `src` patterns "must not overlap"; `dest` optional (defaults to src). Order of application: source-level filter/transform first, then stream-level `subject_transform`.
- [TOPO][SEC] Cross-account sourcing needs three exports/imports: `$JS.API.CONSUMER.>` (service), `deliver.mirror.>` (stream), `$JS.FC.>` (service). "Getting the type wrong (e.g., using a stream import for the API subject) will cause silent failures."
- [TOPO][ANTI] "Cycle detection **does not** apply across external streams in different domains. It is the operator's responsibility to ensure that cross-domain configurations do not create replication cycles." Within an account the server prevents cycles when subjects overlap.
- [OPS] `StreamSourceInfo`: `lag` (messages pending), `active` (ns since last activity), `error` (ApiError). Error codes 10029 "Mirror consumer setup failed", 10045 "Source consumer setup failed"; consumer-create timeout 30 seconds; error clears on reconnect; visible via STREAM.INFO, `/jsz`, `$SYS.REQ.SERVER.PING.JSZ`.
- [STRM] `Nats-Stream-Source` header: `<stream-index[:hash]> <sequence> <filter-subject|>> <dest-subject|>> <original-subject>`; multiple transforms joined with `\f`; on daisy-chaining "the server replaces any existing `Nats-Stream-Source` header so the header always reflects the immediate upstream origin."
- [OPS] `/jsz?streams=true&consumers=true&direct-consumers=true` exposes internal replication consumers (`Direct` flag, `AckNone`, flow control, heartbeats; named `mirror-<id>` / `src-<id>` when a single filter exists, else random name).
- [STRM][OPS] Reconnection "uses exponential backoff with jitter"; resumes "from the last successfully stored sequence — no manual intervention is required."
- [STRM] Upstream expiry: gap in upstream `sseq` with contiguous `dseq` → skip markers recorded and continue; gap in `dseq` → consumer "must be recreated to redeliver." "This gap detection is reliable only for streams using the **Limits** retention policy."
- [STRM][SIZE] Internal replication consumers have "a short inactive threshold (10 seconds)."
- [STRM][ANTI] "Work queue streams are **not recommended** as upstream streams" (replication consumers "bypass the work queue's subject overlap validation", breaking single-consumer-per-partition). "Interest retention streams are **not recommended**" (messages may be removed while the replication consumer is absent). Limits retention "is the recommended and best-supported."
- [STRM][TOPO] "In a cluster, only the stream leader manages the replication consumers. If leadership changes, the new leader takes over replication from the last known position."

## ADR-60: JetStream reliable stream sourcing/mirroring on WQ/Interest streams (updates ADR-59)
- path: adr/ADR-60.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-60.md
- status: Implemented | since: 2.14 | date: 2026-03-11

### Claims
- [STRM][MYTH] Pre-2.14 sourcing/mirroring uses "an ephemeral ordered push consumer using `AckNone`"; "really reliable if the stream that's being mirrored/sourced is a Limits stream" but on WorkQueue/Interest "any messages that are sent are immediately acknowledged and removed. If this message is not received on the other end, this message will be lost"; on Interest "interest will be lost while there's no active connection ... This also results in messages being lost."
- [STRM][CONS] Fix: when the upstream is WQ or Interest the server "upgrade[s]" to a durable consumer, replicated if the upstream is replicated, reused for the life of the source config, best-effort deleted on removal.
- [CONS][OPS] Naming/metadata: mirror consumers `JS_MIRROR_<suffix>` with `_nats.mirror.stream`, `_nats.mirror.acc`, `_nats.mirror.domain`; source consumers `JS_SRC_<suffix>` with `_nats.src.*`.
- [CONS] New `AckPolicy=AckFlowControl`: "will function like `AckAll`" but flow-control replies (with `Nats-Last-Stream` and `Nats-Last-Consumer` headers) act as acks; requires `FlowControl` and `Heartbeat`; idle heartbeat also advances the ack floor; `MaxAckPending` bounds in-flight and triggers an automatic FC message.
- [CONS][ANTI] With `AckFlowControl` "the consumer cannot have an `AckWait` or `BackOff` setting ... or an error will be returned"; "`MaxDeliver` must be set to `-1`."
- [STRM][PATTERN] "Durable sourcing": user pre-creates the durable consumer (monitorable, pausable, security-controlled); stream source config carries `consumer: {name, deliver_subject}`; then `OptStartSeq`, `OptStartTime`, `FilterSubject` "are not allowed" on the source and must live on the consumer; enables `DeliverPolicy=last_per_subject` and `ReplayPolicy=original` sourcing.
- [STRM][ANTI] "WorkQueue streams don't allow having multiple consumers with overlapping filter subjects" so a durable sourcing consumer blocks other overlapping consumers; "an Interest or Limits stream should be used" in that case.
- [STRM][PATTERN] Guidance: "It's generally recommended to use sourcing defined in the stream configuration for most use cases"; durable sourcing is for security needs, advanced consumer options, or bootstrapping a leaf node before it connects ("all available messages will be reliably mirrored/sourced" once connected).
- [CONS][OPS] New API `$JS.API.CONSUMER.RESET.<STREAM>.<CONSUMER>`: resets delivery sequence to 1 and redelivers pending; empty payload keeps the ack floor stream seq; `{"seq":N}` sets ack floor to N-1 so next delivered `msg.seq >= N`; only for `DeliverPolicy` all / by_start_sequence / by_start_time, and cannot go before `opt_start_seq`/`opt_start_time`; response looks like a consumer create response plus `ResetSeq`.
- [STRM] Server handles manual resets of a sourcing consumer: forward resets skip messages; backward resets "should guarantee that mirrored messages are not duplicated"; a server consumer create/update for durable sourcing "will implicitly also perform a consumer reset."
- [CLNT] "clients should not fail when the consumer delivery sequence is not monotonic, except when needed for the 'ordered consumer' implementations"; a reset on an ordered consumer is treated as a gap and the consumer recreated.

## ADR-61: Unsafe meta group quorum rescue for disaster recovery
- path: adr/ADR-61.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-61.md
- status: Implemented | since: 2.15 | date: 2026-07-07 (rev 2 2026-07-24)

### Claims
- [TOPO][OPS][MYTH] Meta group quorum "is computed from the configured peer set, not from the set of currently live peers. A peer that is shut down and intended to not come back, without being explicitly peer-removed still counts toward the quorum requirement."
- [TOPO][ANTI] Disaster trap: grow 3→5 for a migration, turn off the 2 extras without peer-removing, then lose one original: "only 2 peers remain reachable, the metagroup loses quorum ... With no quorum there is no leader to process a peer-remove either."
- [OPS] Previous remedy: bring every configured peer back "under the same server name, at the same time" and run `$JS.API.SERVER.REMOVE`.
- [OPS] New operator-only broadcast API `$JS.API.META.RESCUE` on the system account with `{"quorum_needed": N}` (>= 1 and <= current effective quorum); non-system-account requests are silently ignored; "The peer set is not rewritten by this API."
- [OPS] `JSZ meta_cluster` now populates `replicas` on every server (not only the leader) plus `quorum_needed` and `rescue` (true while active).
- [OPS] Safety gate: server must be a voting member, must see no meta leader ("a healthy meta layer must not be reconfigured through this API"), and must have a non-empty Raft log ("a lowered quorum could let it be elected on empty votes alone while the lost peers holding the only copies of the data remain unreachable").
- [OPS][SIZE] On accept: lowers effective quorum, "starts a 5 minute rescue timeout", logs WARN and emits advisory `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.SERVER.META_RESCUE` (`io.nats.jetstream.advisory.v1.meta_rescue` with `prev_quorum`, `new_quorum`, cluster, domain). During rescue, empty-log peers' votes count only when the candidate has data.
- [OPS] Quorum recalculation is suppressed during the timeout unless a peer-set change yields a quorum "at or below" the rescued value, which cancels the rescue; on expiry quorum returns to the natural value. A repeat rescue "can only ever lower the value, never raise it" and resets the timeout.
- [OPS][SIZE] Rejection error code `10224` (400) "JetStream system rescue not applied: {err}" (leader known, not voting member, empty log, out of bounds, node closed).
- [OPS][ANTI] "The API is intentionally unsafe. Lowering the meta quorum weakens the guarantees Raft relies on ... misuse against a not-actually-wedged meta layer can split-brain the meta group"; must be documented "as a last-resort disaster recovery tool." No client library changes.

## ADR-62: JetStream desired state reconciliation
- path: adr/ADR-62.md
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md
- status: Implemented | since: 2.15 (with a 2.14 compatibility release) | date: 2026-08-26

### Claims
- [TOPO][MYTH] Raft membership "can't just be swapped for a new one in a single step: adding or removing several peers at once can produce two quorums that never overlap, which risks electing two independent leaders over the same data." Every change is "a sequence of safe, single-peer adds/removes."
- [TOPO][ANTI] Pre-2.15 flaw: the Raft layer "automatically adds peers that it hears from ... During a scale-down, move, or peer-remove it means a peer that was meant to be evicted can silently reappear." Progress was inferred from peer-list shape ("more peers than configured replicas" meant "a move is in progress").
- [TOPO] New model: `raftGroup.Desired` (peers, cluster, `move`, `scale_down`, `removed`, `origin`) fenced by assignment `id` and leader `term`; "The meta layer is in control of the desired state in the assignment, but the group leader is in control of the assignment's peer set."
- [TOPO] `origin` "captured once and never overwritten" so any pending change can be cancelled back; "A stream keeps running at its origin configuration (placement, retention) until desired state is reached." Legacy moves (peers > replicas) are converted to desired state on upgrade.
- [OPS] `STREAM.INFO`/`CONSUMER.INFO` expose `cluster.desired` {name, replicas, origin, status}; `cluster.replicas[].pending` flags a Raft add/remove not yet reflected in the assignment.
- [OPS] Status types: `meta`, `membership`, `snapshot`, `catchup`, `quorum` ("adding a peer would risk losing quorum"), `blocked` ("waiting for consumer 'X' to migrate"), `unavailable`.
- [TOPO] Stream leader loop: request desired state → snapshot if growing ("when scaling up from R1 to R3, the snapshot is what makes sure that the new peers require catchup") → drop peers no longer in cluster → add desired peers (assignment first, then Raft log) → select scale-down victims → remove one old peer at a time (Raft log first, then assignment; check quorum and consumer dependence) → finalize. Consumers "may only add a peer if it's already in the stream's peer set."
- [OPS] Meta peer/assignment reconciliation backfills a replacement peer after peer-remove or when a new eligible peer appears ("to heal an under-replicated group"), respecting placement constraints.
- [OPS][STRM][CONS] Scale up stream: consumers without explicit replicas scale too; "Interest/WorkQueue consumers are also scaled up to match the stream's replica count." Scale down: "Prefers keeping the stream leader and online and caught up peers"; R1 consumers on a doomed peer are moved first.
- [OPS][MIG] Retention change Limits→Interest on a replicated stream: "the consumers will need to scale up first since their replica count needs to match that of the stream if it's Interest or WorkQueue"; back to Limits allows scaling consumers down.
- [OPS] Move: `$JS.API.STREAM.UPDATE` or `$JS.API.ACCOUNT.STREAM.MOVE.<account>.<stream>` (system account); adds new peers, catches up, drops old; consumers follow. Evacuate: `$JS.API.STREAM.PEER.EVACUATE.<stream>` / `$JS.API.SERVER.EVACUATE` (evacuating peer can still help catch-up, even for R1).
- [OPS][ANTI] Peer remove (`$JS.API.STREAM.PEER.REMOVE.<stream>` / `$JS.API.SERVER.REMOVE`): removes immediately and assigns a replacement if available, else "the group will run under-replicated"; removing the last (R1) peer "moves the stream to a new peer without preserving the data"; "Prefer evacuating a stream peer if it's still able to catch up." Valid no-quorum escape: peer-remove dead nodes then scale config down to match; "Be careful though with peer-removing liberally when peers are planned to come back ... it does not get re-added."
- [OPS] Cancel via `$JS.API.STREAM.CANCEL_MOVE.<stream>` / `$JS.API.ACCOUNT.STREAM.CANCEL_MOVE.<account>.<stream>`: stream peers "will always return to their original peer set" but consumers may land differently.
- [OPS][ANTI] Overlap rules: scale/retention changes may stack; "A move change while another move is in progress is not allowed"; "Scale or retention changes while a move is in progress is not allowed"; consumers can be scaled independently at any time (but may keep moving until stream ops finish).
- [OPS][MIG][ANTI] "Upgrading directly to 2.15 is **not recommended**"; path is 2.14 → 2.14-compat (adds desired-state encoding only) → 2.15; during mixed versions "any in-flight operation stalls" until all servers are on 2.15. Downgrading below 2.14-compat "is **not recommended**"; let pending changes settle first. Inconsistent state after a direct upgrade/downgrade "may be (partially) repaired by performing a rolling restart of all nodes while on the same version."

### 15 ADR-derived facts most important for designing a large NATS system
1. **KV and Direct Get are NOT read-after-write consistent** (ADR-8, ADR-31): reads go to any replica or mirror, "multiple reads of the same key can give different values." Only the classic leader-routed `STREAM.MSG.GET` gives read-after-write.
2. **Dedup window default is 2 minutes** (`duplicate_window: 120000000000`, ADR-36 examples; ADR-8 rule: KV sets it to min(max_age, 2m)). Atomic batches reject duplicate `Nats-Msg-Id` inside the batch (2.12.1+) and forbid `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` (ADR-50).
3. **Ordering guarantees**: a mirror keeps upstream order, sequences and timestamps; a single source with multiple non-overlapping filters preserves order; "There is no guaranteed ordering across different sources" (ADR-36, ADR-59). Consumer multi-filters must not overlap (ADR-34, err 10136).
4. **Ordered consumer recreation**: on a sequence gap or missed heartbeats the client must drop the consumer and recreate it from the last known stream sequence; forced config ack none / max_deliver 1 / mem_storage / R1 / flow control (ADR-17). Server-side sourcing uses the same trick, and since 2.14 `$JS.API.CONSUMER.RESET` avoids delete+recreate for durable sourcing consumers (ADR-60).
5. **Sourcing/mirroring from WorkQueue or Interest streams loses messages pre-2.14** (ephemeral AckNone consumer); 2.14 upgrades to durable `JS_SRC_*`/`JS_MIRROR_*` consumers with `AckFlowControl`; Limits retention remains "recommended and best-supported" (ADR-59, ADR-60).
6. **Mirror config is immutable** after creation; mirrors cannot have subjects, sources, counters, atomic batches, schedules, or delete markers; sources may be added/removed live; cycle detection does not cross domains (ADR-59).
7. **Pull consumer limits/defaults**: `max_waiting` 512 inflight pulls, `ack_wait` 30s, `max_ack_pending` 20000 (ADR-13); Consume defaults expires 30s (min 1s), heartbeat = expires/2 capped 30s, thresholds 50%; client timeout must exceed server `expires` (ADR-37).
8. **Heartbeat/flow-control contract**: alarm at 3× idle heartbeat (push, ADR-15) or 2× (Consume, ADR-37); flow control requires idle heartbeat; queue-group subscriptions must not use heartbeats, flow control, or gap detection (ADR-15).
9. **Priority groups (2.11)**: pull-only, one group of ≤16 chars, policies `overflow` (min_pending / min_ack_pending), `pinned_client` (no exclusivity guarantee; `PriorityTimeout` default 2m, keep pull `Expires` ≤ 1m), `prioritized` (0–9, lower first); cannot switch policies or add/remove groups on an existing consumer; `failover` unimplemented as of 2.14 (ADR-42).
10. **Per-message TTL (2.11)**: min 1s, `never` beats MaxAge, cannot be disabled once enabled, mirrors may not set delete markers, `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` becomes the TTL floor unless MaxMsgsPer=1; KV limit markers require API level 1 and TTL only on Create/Purge (ADR-43, ADR-48).
11. **Batch publishing limits (ADR-50)**: atomic = 64-char ID, ≤1000 msgs, 50 in flight per stream, 1000 per server, 10s idle abandon, incompatible with `PersistMode: async`; fast ingest (2.14) = unlimited size, 1000/stream, 50,000/server, "outstanding acks = 2 ... generally optimal".
12. **`PersistMode: async` is R1-only and acks before fsync** ("increased chance of data loss"); default mode is strongest consistency (ADR-56).
13. **Naming limits**: stream/consumer/account names ≤255 chars filename-safe; KV bucket `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, KV keys `[A-Za-z0-9/_=-]` tokens, `_kv` reserved; metadata ≤128KB with `_nats` reserved; service names `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` (ADR-6, ADR-33, ADR-32). KV history max 64, min 1 (ADR-8).
14. **Version skew and API levels**: connected-server version is "a known incorrect approach"; use `$JS.API.INFO` API level (0 <2.11, 1 = 2.11, 2 = 2.12, 4 = 2.14 batch); `Nats-Required-Api-Level` header; tools must ignore `_nats.*` metadata; 2.15 requires the 2.14-compat hop and stalls in-flight moves on mixed versions (ADR-44, ADR-62).
15. **Cluster membership pitfalls**: meta quorum counts configured, not live, peers (shrinking without peer-remove wedges the cluster; ADR-61 rescue is "intentionally unsafe"); scale/move/retention changes are single-peer Raft steps; no overlapping moves; Interest/WQ consumers must match stream replicas; peer-removing the last R1 peer loses data, prefer evacuate (ADR-62). Publishers must retry on 503 no-responders during leader elections (default 250ms × 2 retries, ADR-22), and clients reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter, 2-minute ping, 2 max pings out (ADR-40).

- [TOPO][SIZE] Leader steps down when overrun: more than 100,000 uncommitted OR more than 100,000 committed-but-unapplied entries. `pauseQuorumThreshold = 100_000` (server/raft.go:4966); comment "Stepping down means the system gets to 'breathe' for a bit, until a new leader can be elected." (server/raft.go:995-1011)
- [TOPO][SIZE] Pending append-entry cache: warn at 10,000 (every 5,000), stop caching at 20,000. `paeDropThreshold = 20_000`, `paeWarnThreshold = 10_000`, `paeWarnModulo = 5_000` (server/raft.go:4967-4969, 5016-5028)
- [TOPO] Servers in lame duck mode start their Raft nodes as observers so they never become leader: "This will stop us from taking on the leader role when we're about to shutdown anyway." (server/raft.go:625-630)

- [TOPO][OPS][ANTI] RescueQuorum (unsafe, disaster-recovery): quorum can only be lowered, only when no leader is known, only on a voting non-observer member, and NEVER on a server with an empty log ("a lowered quorum could let it be elected off empty votes while the lost peers hold the only copies of the data... ## Routes, gateways, leaf nodes (server/route.go, server/gateway.go, server/leafnode.go)
- source: nats-server server/route.go, server/gateway.go, server/leafnode.go (commit 8e54a5954)

### Claims
- [TOPO][SIZE] Route ping interval capped at 30s (below client default 2 min) because S2-auto compression uses RTT from ping/pong. `defaultRouteMaxPingInterval = 30 * time.Second` (server/route.go:132-141)
- [TOPO] Route pooling: an account is hashed (FNV-32a) to a fixed pool index in [0..poolSize-1], "constant and same on all servers (given the same poolSize value)"; poolSize <= 1 always maps to 0 (server/route.go:530-540); since v2.11.0 remotes may have a different pool size (server/route.go:630-636)
- [TOPO] Routes are Implicit ("we learned from speaking to other routes") or Explicit ("explicitly configured"); gossip modes default/disabled/override (server/route.go:39-44, 104-108)
- [TOPO][ANTI][SEC] Insecure TLS on routes/gateways/leafnodes logs: "TLS certificate chain and hostname of solicited ... will not be verified. DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION!" (server/route.go:127-128, server/gateway.go:71, server/leafnode.go:46)
- [TOPO][SIZE] Gateway timers: solicit delay 1s, connect delay 1s backing off to 30s max, reconnect 1s, recent-sub expiration 2s, ping at most every 15s regardless of traffic. `defaultSolicitGatewaysDelay = time.Second`, `defaultGatewayConnectDelay = time.Second`, `defaultGatewayConnectMaxDelay = 30 * time.Second`, `defaultGatewayReconnectDelay = time.Second`, `defaultGatewayRecentSubExpiration = 2 * time.Second`, `gwMaxPingInterval = 15 * time.Second` (server/gateway.go:35-58)
- [TOPO][SIZE] Gateway switches an account from optimistic to interest-only after 1000 remote unsubs/no-interest notices. `defaultGatewayMaxRUnsubBeforeSwitch = 1000` (server/gateway.go:41)
- [TOPO] Gateway interest modes: Optimistic ("a cluster will send to a gateway unless it is been told that there is no interest (this is for plain subscribers only)"), Transitioning, InterestOnly ("a cluster sends all it subscriptions interest to the gateway, which in return does not send a message unless it knows that there is explicit interest") (server/gateway.go:96-110)
- [TOPO] Since 2.9.0 optimistic mode is being phased out: all accounts are switched to interest-only on gateway connect; JetStream-enabled accounts always switch (server/gateway.go:1219-1245)
- [TOPO] Outbound gateway connections are ordered by lowest RTT (server/gateway.go:1751-1775)
- [TOPO] Gateway reply prefix is `_GR_.<6-char cluster hash>.<6-char server hash>.` (old prefix `$GR.`) (server/gateway.go:43-54)
- [TOPO][SIZE] Leaf node reconnect delays: 30s after a loop is detected, 30s after a permission violation, 30s when leaf and hub share the same cluster name. `leafNodeReconnectDelayAfterLoopDetected = 30 * time.Second`, `leafNodeReconnectAfterPermViolation = 30 * time.Second`, `leafNodeReconnectDelayAfterClusterNameSame = 30 * time.Second` (server/leafnode.go:48-56)
- [TOPO][ANTI] Leaf loop detection: each account subscribes to a `$LDS.<nuid>` subject; seeing your own LDS subject come back over a leaf means a loop; error text "Loop detected for leafnode account=%q. Delaying attempt to reconnect for %v" and the connection is closed as a protocol violation (server/leafnode.go:58-59, 2497, 2963-2969, 3061-3073)

## Client connection handling: slow consumers, stalls, buffers (server/client.go, server/opts.go)
- source: nats-server server/client.go, server/opts.go, server/dios.go (commit 8e54a5954)

### Claims
- [CLNT][SIZE][ANTI] Slow consumer by pending bytes: a CLIENT whose outbound pending exceeds max_pending (default 64 MiB) is closed with "Slow Consumer Detected: MaxPending of %d Exceeded" (server/client.go:2595-2612)
- [CLNT][SIZE] Stall gate: when a client's outbound pending exceeds 75% of max_pending, fast producers publishing to it are stalled. `c.out.pb > c.out.mp/4*3` (server/client.go:2615-2621). Stall durations: 2ms minimum, 5ms when at/over the limit, at most 10ms total per readLoop pass. `stallClientMinDuration = 2 * time.Millisecond`, `stallClientMaxDuration = 5 * time.Millisecond`, `stallTotalAllowed = 10 * time.Millisecond` (server/client.go:124-127, 3708-3722)
- [CLNT][SIZE] Slow consumer by write deadline: an i/o timeout on flush (write_deadline, default 10s) marks the connection slow consumer; routes count each event once; a write timeout before CONNECT is handled as slow consumer without incrementing the counter "as that can be misleading" (server/client.go:1944-1985)
- [CLNT][SIZE] Per-connection read buffer grows from 512 B to 64 KiB and shrinks to 64 B; readLoop reports if a pass takes over 2s. `startBufSize = 512`, `minBufSize = 64`, `maxBufSize = 65536`, `readLoopReport = 2 * time.Second` (server/client.go:110-116)
- [CLNT][SIZE] Server will not send an RTT PING before the first PONG, capped at 2s. `maxNoRTTPingBeforeFirstPong = 2 * time.Second` (server/client.go:118-122)
- [CLNT][SIZE] Permission/result caches per client: 512 sublist results, 256 deny-perm, 128 perm entries; reply-permission tracking limit 4096 entries pruned every 1s. `maxResultCacheSize = 512`, `maxDenyPermCacheSize = 256`, `maxPermCacheSize = 128`, `replyPermLimit = 4096`, `replyPruneTime = time.Second` (server/client.go:471-479)
- [CLNT][SIZE] On close, a minimal flush uses a 100ms write deadline. `lowWriteDeadline = 100 * time.Millisecond` (server/client.go:6002)
- [CLNT] Connection kinds: CLIENT, ROUTER, GATEWAY, SYSTEM, LEAF, JETSTREAM, ACCOUNT; client sub-types NATS, MQTT, WS (server/client.go:46-79)
- [OPS][SIZE] Baseline option defaults (server/opts.go setBaselineOptions:5998-6190): max_connections 65536, ping_interval 2m, ping_max 2, tls timeout 2s, auth_timeout = tls timeout + 1s when TLS is configured else 2s (`getDefaultAuthTimeout` server/opts.go:6192-6200), cluster pool_size 3, max_control_line 4096, max_payload 1 MiB, max_pending 64 MiB, write_deadline 10s, max_closed_clients 10000, lame_duck_duration 2m, lame_duck_grace_period 10s, leafnode reconnect 1s, leafnode first_info_timeout 1s
- [TOPO] Cluster compression default is `accept` ("compression is not initiated, but if the remote selects compression, this server will use the same"); leafnode compression default is `s2_auto` (server/opts.go:6062-6070, 6085-6108)
- [STRM][SIZE] JetStream option defaults: max_memory_store -1 (dynamic), max_file_store -1 (dynamic), sync_interval 2m, request_queue_limit 10000, info queue limit = request queue limit, concurrent IOs 4096. `defaultConcurrentIOs = 4096` (server/dios.go:21; server/opts.go:6171-6189)

Files read (nats-server @ 8e54a5954, server/ package): const.go (full), jetstream.go (config/limits/dynamic config/name validation/startup banner/recovery warnings), jetstream_api.go (API subjects, advisories, headers, name/description/metadata limits, request queue drop), jetstream_versioning.go (full), jetstream_cluster.go (consts, selectPeerGroup placement, catch-up consts, compression threshold), stream.go (StreamConfig struct, consts, checkStreamCfgLocked full, configUpdateCheckLocked full, publish path dedup/size/limit errors, source/mirror retry consts, interest check), consumer.go (consts, setConsumerConfigDefaults full, checkConsumerCfg full, addConsumerWithAssignment WQ/limit checks, updateConfig, checkNewConsumerConfig, updateInactiveThreshold, deleteNotActive, processNak, checkPending), raft.go (consts, quorum/rescue/evict/overrun/observer logic), filestore.go (consts, dynBlkSize, record sizes), store.go (errors), route.go (consts, pool index), gateway.go (consts, interest modes), leafnode.go (consts, JS domain/extension rules, loop detection, perm reversal), client.go (consts, slow consumer/stall gate, subscribe limits), opts.go (setBaselineOptions, JSLimitOpts, getDefaultAuthTimeout), accounts.go (limits struct, response types, import cycle check), errors.go (full error list), errors.json (full, 224 entries), events.go (subjects, intervals), auth.go (perm template limit), mqtt.go (consts, ack/retained defaults), websocket.go (consts, payload limit), sublist.go (cache consts), monitor.go (list sizes), reload.go (reload refusals), server.go (startup warnings), dios.go (concurrent IOs). conf/simple.conf, doc/README.md (pointer to ADR repo only), README.md (no architecture guidance).
Files read (jsm.go @ 49d3148): schema_source/jetstream/api/v1/definitions.json (stream/consumer config, placement, sources, cluster/peer info), audit/*_checks.go (all check codes and thresholds), monitor/*.go (metadata keys).
Files read (natscli @ 3726a32): cli/cheats/*.md (all 17), cli/stream_command.go (flags, interactive help, peer-remove guard), cli/consumer_command.go (flags, interactive help), cli/kv_command.go, cli/object_command.go, cli/server_check_command.go (defaults).

Areas skipped or only sampled: memstore.go (no design constants beyond timers), reload.go per-option reloadability table (only refusals captured), auth.go/jwt claim mapping details, ocsp, tpm, subject mapping/transform syntax (subject.go), KV/Object-store semantics (they live in client libraries, not in these repos; only CLI flags captured), MQTT session/QoS2 protocol flow, websocket handshake details, gateway queue-sub handling internals, leafnode permission merge details, jsm.go Go-level option builders (schema was the richer source), natscli bench/context/latency cheats, `nats server report` internals. errors.json: 116 of 224 errors listed; the rest are `{err}` wrappers, not-found errors, or format errors with no design content.

Total claims: 411 (tag counts: ANTI 194, STRM 143, SIZE 121, CONS 107, TOPO 57, OPS 53, SEC 22, CLNT 19, CORE 11, MIG 7, PATTERN 4, KV 2, OBJ 1, SUBJ 1). 19 sections.

### The 20 numbers and rules a designer of a large NATS system must know (all sourced above)
1. max_payload default 1 MiB; server warns above 8 MiB ("generally discouraged and could lead to poor performance") (server/const.go:94-99, server/server.go:2349-2352)
2. max_pending default 64 MiB per client; slow consumer disconnect above it; producers are stalled once a consumer passes 75% of it (server/const.go:102, server/client.go:2595-2621)
3. write_deadline 10s; ping 2m with max 2 outstanding; auth timeout 2s (TLS timeout + 1s when TLS on) (server/const.go:117-132, server/opts.go:6192-6200)
4. Stream replicas max 5; standalone server rejects R>1; consumers on interest/workqueue streams must match stream replicas (server/stream.go:730, 771-774; server/consumer.go:728-736)
5. Raft quorum = N/2+1; election timeout 4-9s; heartbeat 1s; lost-quorum after 10s; leader steps down at 100,000 uncommitted/unapplied entries (server/raft.go:297-308, 1236, 4966)
6. Placement fails unless r eligible peers exist AND at least quorum of them are online; peers ranked by free storage then HA-asset count; `!jetstream` tag and `unique_tag` prefix control spreading (server/jetstream_cluster.go:9323-9600)
7. Account reservation = max_bytes x replicas without tiers (single replica against a tier); server-side footprint is one replica (server/jetstream.go:2500-2545)
8. Duplicate window default 2 min, capped to max_age; dedup returns the ORIGINAL sequence with duplicate=true; mirrors cannot dedupe (server/stream.go:1674, 1776-1806, 6754-6775)
9. AckWait default 30s; MaxAckPending default 1000 (delivery suspends at the limit); MaxDeliver default -1; MaxWaiting default 512 pulls; ephemeral inactive threshold 5s (+ up to 1s jitter) (server/consumer.go:572-582, server/jetstream_api.go:756)
10. WorkQueue streams: consumers must be AckExplicit + DeliverAll, and filters of concurrent consumers must partition without overlap; a second unfiltered consumer is rejected (server/consumer.go:1140-1176)
11. Consumer filter subjects may not overlap each other; FilterSubject and FilterSubjects are mutually exclusive (server/consumer.go:863-888)
12. Immutable on update: stream storage type, retention to/from workqueue, sealed/deny_delete/deny_purge (true->false), persist_mode, mirror config; consumer deliver/ack/replay policy, start seq/time, heartbeat, flow control, max waiting, pull<->push (server/stream.go:2331-2394, server/consumer.go:2467-2525)
13. Stream subjects may not overlap each other or `$JS.>`/`$SYS.>` (without no_ack); `>` requires no_ack and R1; mirrors can not have subjects, sources, first_seq, counters, batch publish or schedules (server/stream.go:1909-1929, 2188-2218)
14. Names: streams/consumers max 255 chars, no whitespace or `. * > \ /`; description 4 KiB; metadata 128 KiB; priority group `^[a-zA-Z0-9/_=-]{1,16}$` (server/jetstream_api.go:381-389, server/jetstream.go:2811-2816, server/consumer.go:49)
15. JetStream API request queue limit 10,000: on overflow the WHOLE queue is dropped and `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.API.LIMIT_REACHED` is published (server/jetstream_api.go:393, 916-944)
16. File store block sizes: 8 MiB (limits), 4 MiB (workqueue/interest/KV), 2 MiB cap when encrypted; fsync every 2 min by default; 30-byte per-message header+checksum overhead (server/filestore.go:329-381, 809-843, 1111-1114)
17. Default JetStream sizing: max_memory_store = 75% of RAM (or GOMEMLIMIT), max_file_store = available disk (1 TiB constant if forced); store_dir defaults to a temp dir with a data-loss warning (server/jetstream.go:2716-2768)
18. Gateways: since 2.9 all accounts run interest-only; switch after 1000 no-interest notices; gateway pings every 15s; outbound ordered by RTT (server/gateway.go:35-58, 96-110, 1237-1245)
19. Leaf nodes: loop detection via `$LDS.` with 30s reconnect delay; same cluster name rejected; JetStream API denied across a leaf unless system account shared and domains match; extension incompatible with empty default_js_domain (server/leafnode.go:48-59, 2034-2134, 3061-3073)
20. Async persist mode only on file storage, R1, no atomic batch; counters require limits retention and no discard-new/TTL/schedules; subject delete markers need >= 1s TTL and are forbidden on mirrors (server/stream.go:1813-1880, 1950-1953)
