# Source class: GitHub discussions and issues

## Inquiry on Limits for Streams and Consumers in a NATS JetStream Cluster
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5128
- date: 2024-02-26 | asker: suchen-sci | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10 era
- question (one line): What is the max number of streams per cluster and consumers per stream (10, 100, 1k, 10k)?

### Claims
- [SIZE][STRM] Synadia's global clusters cap each server at 2k HA (replicated) assets; some customers run higher and are fine — derekcollison. "In our global clusters we limit servers, at the moment, to 2k HA Assets."
- [PATTERN][STRM] Prefer muxed (multiplexed) streams with consumers filtering what they need, or R1 mirrors that filter, over many streams — derekcollison. "We suggest folks use muxed streams and have consumers filter out what they need, or R1 mirrors that do the same."
- [CONS][SIZE] Consumers that inherit R3 from the parent stream are heavy (state machine with consensus) and expected to be limited in number; lighter consumer variants scale further — derekcollison.
- [SIZE][CONS] Over 100k consumers is possible "with custom solutions"; reach out to Synadia — derekcollison.
- [SIZE] When all HA assets are active the limit is mostly hardware; idle/low-volume streams leave room for server-side improvement — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][CONS][KV] For ~100k browser-ish subscribers: use R1 (possibly memory) consumers that clients recreate on demand, plus a single R3 muxed KV storing each consumer's last sequence; recreate with OptStartSeq from the KV — derekcollison. "have a single muxed KV that stores the sequences for the 100k ... consumers that is an R3 and highly available."

## Jetstream Max Consumers per Stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4797
- date: 2023-11-15 | asker: beatrausch | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Can a stream have ~50 million consumers?

### Claims
- [ANTI][CONS][SIZE] 50M traditional consumers per stream is not supported; consumers can be heavyweight state machines with consensus (NRG) — derekcollison. "you can not use a traditional consumer here"
- [PATTERN][CONS] Massive fan-out to millions of endpoints should use stream re-publish plus client-side gap logic with a muxed KV holding per-endpoint sequence offsets — derekcollison. "look into stream re-publish and gap logic with a mux'd KV for sequence offsets"

## Maximum number of consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7863
- date: 2026-02-22 | asker: Mierunski | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.12-2.14 (main branch)
- question (one line): One durable R3 consumer per endpoint for millions of endpoints; consumer creation bursts of 2000/s time out. What is the intended consumer count?

### Claims
- [SIZE][CONS] Shard streams so no stream has more than ~20K consumers — wallyqs. "it would be better if you shard the streams so that you do not have more than 20K consumers or so per stream."
- [SIZE][CONS][OPS] Main branch has optimizations toward millions of consumers by raising `meta_compact_size` — wallyqs.
- [SIZE][OPS] Consumer create rates above ~2K/s on a single cluster is being actively worked on; monitor the raftz WAL size, growth means consumer creates are falling behind — wallyqs. "if it keeps increasing that is when your consumer creates will start getting increase latency."
- [PATTERN][CONS] With very many consumers use R1 memory-based consumers to reduce I/O; or run many clusters capped at ~200K consumers each — wallyqs. "create many clusters and cap the number of consumers per cluster to 200K or so."
- [SIZE][OPS] Sharding streams also balances memory use across the cluster — wallyqs.
- [SIZE][OPS] 5,000 push consumers with R3 state on 2 vCPU / 8Gi nodes gives publish timeouts; recommend at least 4 vCPU, or v2.14.6 and tune the disk I/O setting — wallyqs (replying to pamle17, 17-node stretch cluster across 3 DCs).
- [MYTH] Belief: NATS consumers are as cheap as subscriptions, so millions of durable R3 consumers is a natural design. Correction: durable replicated consumers are Raft state machines; shard streams, use R1/memory consumers, or cap per cluster — wallyqs/derekcollison.

## Number of consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6240
- date: 2024-12-10 | asker: niondir | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): One consumer per organisation (subject `integration.{orgId}`) on a WorkQueue stream, hundreds to a few thousand — does that scale?

### Claims
- [CONS][SIZE] 100-1,000 (under 10k) filtered consumers on an R1 WorkQueue stream is fine — derekcollison. "That should be fine.."
- [PATTERN][CONS] Per-tenant consumers isolate a slow tenant from the others; that isolation is a valid reason for per-tenant consumers — niondir (asker's rationale, implicitly accepted by derekcollison).
- [CONS] Maintainer's first diagnostic questions for consumer-count designs: retention policy, replica count, total expected count — derekcollison.

## Maximum known-good value for `MaxMsgs` in a JetStream stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7032
- date: 2025-07-03 | asker: asymmetric | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Is an unlimited/very large MaxMsgs stream (5M msgs/yr, ~100B each, R3) safe long-term?

### Claims
- [STRM][SIZE] There is no hard limit on stream size; many users run unlimited streams; the practical limit is disk or memory, since the server keeps per-subject indexing in memory — jnmoyne. "practically you will eventually run out of some kind of resource, be it disk space or memory space on the servers (as they maintain some per subject indexing)."
- [PATTERN][STRM] When a stream outgrows a server, shard onto multiple streams by time (stream per year or decade) and add servers — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][PATTERN] For fast ordered replay of many messages use ordered consumers — jnmoyne.
- [OPS] Validate with `nats bench` producing many small messages, then measure read-back rate and server resources — jnmoyne.

## Does Stream Per Subject have any performance benefits over multiple subjects within same stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6100
- date: 2024-11-11 | asker: YashasAnand | answered by: Jarema | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): 100 subjects: 100 streams or one stream with 100 filtered consumers?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][STRM] Many consumers on a single stream is the simple, good starting pattern; a stream per subject is rarely a good idea — Jarema. "It's rarely a good idea to have stream per subject."
- [STRM][SIZE] Each replicated stream (R3+) carries overhead for its own RAFT group — Jarema.
- [PATTERN][STRM] Split into separate streams only when subjects need different retention policies — Jarema. "I would stick to one stream, unless you need different retention policies for some subjects"
- [CONS][TOPO] Consumers scale across a stream's replicas: each replicated consumer's leader can sit on a different stream replica, balancing load — Jarema.
- [CONS] One slow/down filtered consumer does not block other filtered consumers on the same stream — YashasAnand (tested, [UNVERIFIED] but consistent with maintainer answer).

## Jetstreams publisher performance decreases rapidly with large number of parallel consumers (50x drop at 100 consumers)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6274
- date: 2024-12-17 | asker: mranish592 | answered by: derekcollison, neilalexander | server version context: 2.10 (bench), improved in 2.11
- question (one line): 100K ephemeral push consumers on one stream via `nats bench --js --sub N`; publisher throughput falls from 19k/s (1 sub) to 83/s (1000 subs) on m5.2xlarge, even with 5-node clusters. Why?

### Claims
- [CONS][SIZE] Publisher throughput with 1000 parallel JS consumers was measured at ~83 msg/s vs ~19k msg/s with 1 consumer (10KB payload, single stream); horizontal scaling to 3-5 servers did not help; CPU stayed under 25% — mranish592 [UNVERIFIED, benchmark data].
- [CONS][OPS] The many-consumers-per-stream throughput collapse "should have improved quite significantly since the more recent 2.11 versions" — neilalexander.
- [PATTERN][TOPO] A super-cluster with consumers on a separate cluster from publishers helped up to ~1000 consumers but not beyond — mranish592 [UNVERIFIED].
- [OPS] Maintainer's response to a large-scale consumer design at 100K consumers was to take it to a call (Synadia) rather than a public recipe — derekcollison.

## Why JetStream doesn't achieve linear scalability through partitioning?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6315
- date: 2025-01-02 | asker: penghuazhou | answered by: derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Tens of millions of messages on a topic: must I split into multiple streams from the business side since a stream cannot be spread across machines?

### Claims
- [STRM][MYTH] A Kafka partition, not a Kafka topic, is the equivalent of a NATS stream — derekcollison. "A partition in Kafka is equivalent to a stream in NATS."
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Use core NATS subject mapping with `{{partition(N,token)}}` to have the server insert the partition number; partition count and which tokens hash are then administrative decisions, not client code — jnmoyne.
- [STRM][TOPO] An R1 stream is served by exactly one server; R3 by three; R5 by five. Placement tags select which servers participate — jnmoyne.

## Sharding Jetstream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3495
- date: 2022-09-25 | asker: maxpert | answered by: derekcollison, bruth | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): How to shard a change-log across cluster nodes, and does the Raft leader stay involved in every publish?

### Claims
- [STRM][SIZE] A single R3 stream can run ~250k msgs/sec with proper hardware and setup; question whether sharding is needed at all — derekcollison. "A single stream, even an R3 can run ~250k msgs/sec with proper hardware and setup."
- [STRM][CORE] The stream leader receives the message directly from the app, replicates to followers, and replies to the app once a quorum has acknowledged — derekcollison.
- [SEC][PATTERN] To ensure only JetStream receives a subject, restrict that subject with authorization for all other users/apps — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Deterministic partitioning: pick N partitions, define a server-config subject mapping `test.{{wildcard(1)}}.{{partition(7,1)}}`, then one stream per partition filtered like `test.*.0`; test with `nats server mappings` — bruth.

## Can JetStream support multiple partitions distributed to multiple machines, like Kafka?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3739
- date: 2022-12-23 | asker: Doslin | answered by: Jarema | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Wants "3 backups and 10 shards" for disaster resilience of one subject's data.

### Claims
- [MYTH][STRM] Partitions/shards are not needed for HA or disaster resilience; that is what replicas (R3) are for. Sharding is only for performance scaling — Jarema. "You don't need partitions (or shards) to improve HA... Those are needed for performance scalability."
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Design the subject hierarchy with scaling in mind so a stream can later be split by subject tokens into several R3 streams — Jarema.
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Only if token-based splitting is not enough, use deterministic subject token partitioning to spread one subject over many R3 streams — Jarema.

## NATS JetStream Sharding (placement tags on Kubernetes)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5884
- date: 2024-09-12 | asker: c1moore | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Does NATS spread streams across servers, or must I generate placement tags on k8s to shard?

### Claims
- [MYTH][TOPO] Belief: NATS picks the fastest-responding servers for a new stream, so streams cluster on a few nodes. Correction: peer selection at stream creation is load balanced using the current distribution of JS assets — jnmoyne. "the selection of the peers at stream creation time is load balanced (it looks at the current distribution of JS assets when making the selection)."
- [TOPO] Load-balanced placement only works when the number of tag-matching servers exceeds the stream's replication degree — jnmoyne.
- [OPS][TOPO] On the official Helm chart, server tags can be generated with an initContainer that reads node labels via kubectl into `server-tags/tags.conf` and `$include`s it — jnmoyne (full values example in thread).

## Subject Indexing and Ordering Internals
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4170
- date: 2023-05-16 | asker: Zetanova | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9, improvements planned for 2.10
- question (one line): For event sourcing with millions of unique aggregate IDs as subjects: how are subjects indexed, does memory grow, and is ordering the same on `a.s1.t1`/`a.s1.t2` as on `a.s1`?

### Claims
- [STRM][SUBJ] Streams keep meta state indexed by sequence and by subject; walking a filtered subject set is efficient in the modern server — derekcollison.
- [STRM][SIZE] Memory for a stream's subject-addressing layer grows with the number of unique subjects; work to reduce this was planned for 2.10 — derekcollison. "the subject addressing layer to a stream takes more memory the more unique subjects that you have." [STALE?] (2.10/2.11 later improved this)
- [CORE][STRM] JetStream consumption is globally ordered; core NATS only guarantees ordering per publishing connection — derekcollison. "For NATS core the only ordering guarantee is per publishing connection."
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Lookup in a stream is by sequence or by subject (with wildcards); design the subject space so every set you need to filter on is a token — derekcollison. "make sure they represent tokens in the subjects."
- [MYTH] "Publisher" in docs means the publishing connection, not the application — Zetanova (clarified from derekcollison's wording).

## Using Nats Jetstream as an event store
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3772
- date: 2023-01-08 | asker: cloudcompute | answered by: bruth | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Is JetStream suitable as an event-sourcing store at millions of events, and is there tiered/cold storage?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][STRM][USECASE] Event sourcing: a stream `orders` with subjects `orders.*` where each subject is an aggregate; concurrent appends across subjects have no contention, per-subject linearizability via `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence`, and total order across the stream for consumption — bruth.
- [STRM] Subjects are indexed within a stream, so the optimistic-concurrency header check adds no overhead; a filtered replay does a linear scan only over blocks between the subject's earliest and latest messages — bruth.
- [STRM][MYTH] Kafka topic vs NATS stream is the wrong comparison; a Kafka partition is the comparable unit of total ordering and replication — bruth. "a single *partition* is comparable to NATS stream since it is the unit of total ordering and replication."
- [STRM] Write and read throughput and latency of one NATS stream beat one Kafka partition "in nearly every way" (unpublished Synadia benchmark) — bruth [maintainer claim, benchmark not shown].
- [SIZE][TOPO] Theoretical upper bounds of one cluster: Raft heartbeat traffic per replicated asset (hundreds of thousands of assets could saturate network and CPU), and full-mesh gossip between servers limits cluster size; no large users had hit these in practice — bruth. "A theoretical upper may be on the order of 100s of thousands of assets could likely saturate the network and CPU"
- [STRM][OPS] Tiered/cold storage was not built in as of 2023; a separate archiving consumer is the workaround — bruth. [STALE?] (still no built-in tiering as of 2026 per later threads)
- [STRM] Storage is a custom append-only log with per-message get/delete and subject indexing, both memory and file backed — bruth.

## Need Some General Info Regarding Client Design & partitioning
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6437
- date: 2025-01-31 | asker: YashasAnand | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10/2.11
- question (one line): Producer per subject? Replication factor for a 3-node k8s cluster? How do producers write to 5 partitioned streams, and what are the trade-offs?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CONS] Distributing messages across instances of one consuming app needs no partitioning: all instances share one durable consumer — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][PATTERN] Strict ordering of consumption requires `max acks pending` = 1, which cuts throughput to one message at a time — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Strict ordering plus parallelism: put a partition number in the subject (stream config subject transform) and create one durable consumer per partition with max acks pending 1 — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][STRM] Only when inbound throughput exceeds what one stream can write do you use account-level (Core NATS) subject transforms to insert a partition number and create one stream per partition — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Example: apps publish `foo.<id>`; account mapping `foo.*` to `foo.{{partition(5,1)}}.{{wildcard(1)}}`; five streams on `foo.0.*` ... `foo.4.*` — jnmoyne.
- [SEC][SUBJ] Core NATS mappings live at the account level: server config with static auth, or inside the account JWT with operator mode — jnmoyne.

## Consuming partitioned stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6745
- date: 2025-03-31 | asker: ealeykin | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11 (pinned consumers)
- question (one line): After partitioning subjects, how should consumers be set up to read per-customer in order while scaling replicas?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CONS] Partitioned consumption needs only one stream: the stream's subject transform inserts the partition number as the first token, then one consumer per partition via subject filter; one consumer per app instance may hold several partitions — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][CLNT] Orbit.go `pcgroups` (released 2025-05) implements static and elastic partitioned consumer groups; it depends on 2.11 pinned consumers for member failover — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Static groups: membership list plus max members (= partition count); the library assigns partitions to members and creates a consumer with the matching filter list; a single goroutine consumes all assigned partitions — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Elastic groups: an intermediary WorkQueue stream sources from the original stream and adds the partition token; member consumers' filter lists adjust as membership changes — jnmoyne.
- [CONS] Pinned consumer: several instances of the same member can run, only one is pinned and receives messages until it steps down, crashes or is suspended — jnmoyne.

## Are Client-side Partitioned Consumer Groups equivalent to Pulsar Key-Shared subscriptions?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7296
- date: 2025-09-11 | asker: CoenraadS | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Can NATS deliver per-key ordering while consumers scale up and down, like Pulsar Key-Shared?

### Claims
- [CONS] Only two consumer modes deliver strictly in order: ordered consumers (ephemeral, no ack/nak, single client, offset must be persisted by you e.g. in KV) and explicit-ack consumers with max acks pending 1 (one message at a time regardless of client count) — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][PATTERN] Orbit partitioned consumer groups give Kafka/Pulsar consumer-group semantics: per-key strict order with individual ack/nak and redelivery, parallel via consistent hashing, elastic membership up to a pre-configured maximum — jnmoyne.
- [CLNT] pcgroups is Go only as of 2025-09 but not Go specific; portable — jnmoyne.

## Ordering guarantees per entity
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3908
- date: 2023-02-24 | asker: arnarg | answered by: bruth, ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Per-entity strict order with parallel processing: re-publish with `{{partition(100,1)}}` into a WorkQueue stream with 100 MaxAckPending=1 consumers and 100 goroutines?

### Claims
- [CONS] One stream plus one consumer with one subscription already gives ordered processing per entity (barring redeliveries) — bruth.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Before partitioning, benchmark a single stream/consumer baseline; 100 goroutines cap out at CPU cores and add context-switch cost — bruth.
- [PATTERN][STRM] To scale out: subject-mapping partition on the server, N streams (one per partition), one consumer per stream; publishers keep publishing to the unpartitioned subject — bruth.
- [PATTERN][KV] Active-failover for HA consumers: use a KV bucket to grab a lease giving exclusivity to one instance — bruth.
- [CONS] Nak counts as an outstanding ack, so MaxAckPending=1 still preserves order under Nak — ripienaar. "You can control ordering by forcing only max 1 outstanding ack. A Nak is considered outstanding"
- [CONS] WorkQueue retention with MaxAckPending=1 is still a work queue; partitioning scales it out — ripienaar.
- [CONS][PATTERN] For high speed plus order use an ordered consumer: lightweight, 1:1 — derekcollison.
- [MYTH] Belief: WorkQueue retention breaks ordering when a message is Nak'd. Correction: with MaxAckPending=1 the Nak is outstanding and order holds — ripienaar (correcting Zetanova [UNVERIFIED]).
- [ANTI][CONS] Automatic partition rebalancing (Kafka/Pulsar style) was not available out of the box in 2023 — arnarg (later addressed by Orbit pcgroups in 2025).

## Use thousands of leaf nodes at the edge
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5974
- date: 2024-10-08 | asker: pgentile2 | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10 (formalized in 2.11)
- question (one line): 1,700 store leaf nodes to one central cluster with source/mirror; will interest gossip between leaf nodes blow up bandwidth?

### Claims
- [TOPO] Leaf nodes do not gossip to other leaf nodes unless there is legitimate interest — ripienaar.
- [TOPO][OPS] Each new leaf node received `LS+` subscriptions from the N-1 other leaf nodes (including per-domain `$JS.<domain>.API.>` subs), which is normal but can be a problem at thousands of leaves — pgentile2 (observed), confirmed "that's normal and I agree can be an issue" — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][TOPO] To stop interest-graph propagation between leaf nodes that never need east-west traffic, give all leaf nodes the same cluster name; to be formalized in 2.11 — derekcollison. "The trick ... is to have them use the same cluster name. This prevents the hub/cloud side from having to deal with interest graph propagation between each leafnode."
- [TOPO] Putting each store in its own account did NOT by itself suppress `LS+` between leaf nodes; the shared cluster name did — pgentile2 (verified by asker).
- [TOPO][SEC] One account per store is "probably a good idea in general" for isolation — ripienaar.
- [ANTI][STRM][OPS] A central stream sourcing from 1000+ edge domains needs every edge listed in `sources` manually; no auto-discovery of leaf JetStream sources exists (as of 2025-12), acknowledged as a management gap — derekcollison.

## Multi-Region Without Sacrificing Availability
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7438
- date: 2025-10-17 | asker: ryansun96 | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Three regions with unequal node counts: a gateway super-cluster makes stream/consumer creation depend on a global quorum. Is there an architecture keeping regions independent?

### Claims
- [TOPO][PATTERN] With imbalanced cluster sizes or bad inter-region connectivity, run one cluster (the largest) and connect the other regions as leaf nodes each with its own JetStream domain — jnmoyne. "you are better off using one cluster (using your largest one) and the others connecting as Leaf Nodes, each one with their own JS domain name."
- [TOPO][CLNT] Sourcing and consuming across regions works the same, but JS API calls must specify the target domain; default is the domain of the server the client is connected to — jnmoyne.
- [TOPO][CORE] Through a leaf node, core NATS publish/subscribe is transparent (subject to leaf permissions); publishing to a subject captured by a stream in another region stores it there — jnmoyne.
- [MYTH] Belief: a gateway super-cluster is the only "one virtual cluster" option for multi-region. Correction: hub cluster plus leaf-node regions gives the same client transparency without the cross-region meta quorum — jnmoyne.

## Nats SuperCluster with Gateways Adding Jetstream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5317
- date: 2024-04-16 | asker: wilstoff | answered by: ripienaar, MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): 3 DCs, 9-node super-cluster; does JetStream Raft cross DCs, and can we get eventually-consistent cross-DC replication with local consensus?

### Claims
- [TOPO] Raft groups: one meta group spanning the whole super-cluster (all nodes; placement, resource availability) plus per-stream and per-consumer groups that live in one cluster only — ripienaar. "the bulk of the replication lives in your datacenter and needs kind of LAN latencies."
- [TOPO][SIZE] A "stretch" cluster (a normal cluster over long-latency links) works up to roughly 100-150 ms and is "a very advanced use case example and to be used as a last resort" — ripienaar. "max around 100 to 150m"
- [TOPO] When the DC holding a stream is unreachable, mirrors/sources in other clusters are read-only; circular replication keeps read and write during outages — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][TOPO][SUBJ] Circular replication: per-cluster subject mapping rewrites `stream.in.>` to `stream.in.A.>`, streams `STREAM_A/B/C` each capture their own token and source the others; apps publish the same subject everywhere; subscribers need awareness — ripienaar.
- [TOPO][SIZE] All 9 nodes of a 3x3 super-cluster belong to the meta group; you can lose 3 nodes before things break — ripienaar.
- [TOPO][OPS] While the meta group has no quorum: publishing to existing streams and consuming from existing consumers works; creating streams/consumers and operations like moving streams do not — ripienaar.
- [MIG][USECASE] STAN-style custom cross-DC replicators (per-DC subject prefix + queue-group forwarders) are replaced by built-in sources; drawbacks (no cross-DC ordering, possible duplicates on retry) remain the same — ripienaar.
- [TOPO] Reference for circular replicated streams: Synadia blog "multi-cluster-consistency-models" — MauriceVanVeen.

## Is non-clustered JetStream possible with Gateways?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6328
- date: 2025-01-06 | asker: Nintron27 | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): 3-node US cluster plus single nodes in EU/Asia/SA; want a read replica of an auth-session KV per region; super-cluster?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][TOPO][KV] No super-cluster needed: single regional nodes connect as leaf nodes with JetStream enabled and hold read-replica streams sourcing from the hub cluster — jnmoyne.
- [MYTH] Belief: a leaf node in Asia must route through the US hub before the EU sees an update, so gateways are better. Correction (implicit): leaf plus source replica is the recommended shape for regional read replicas — jnmoyne.

## Super-cluster, geolocation and temporary broken gateway link
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4961
- date: 2024-01-16 | asker: kzozulya1 | answered by: ripienaar, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Subscribe in east, publish in west; gateway link breaks; messages are lost. How to queue them?

### Claims
- [TOPO][STRM] A stream lives in exactly one cluster; mirror/source to other clusters if needed — ripienaar, jnmoyne. "Streams are located in one and only one cluster"
- [TOPO][SIZE] For JetStream in a super-cluster you need 3 clusters to keep the meta layer up during a cluster outage — ripienaar. "For JetStream you need 3 clusters to keep things up during an outage."
- [TOPO] `nats: no response from stream` when publishing from a cluster cut off from the cluster hosting the stream is expected — jnmoyne.

## Duplicate messages on a leafnode cluster connected to a supercluster
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4823
- date: 2023-11-28 | asker: smolp | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9.24
- question (one line): Leaf cluster in Asia connected via remotes to both EU clusters of a super-cluster sees messages duplicated many times.

### Claims
- [ANTI][TOPO] A leaf node bridges NATS systems; a super-cluster is a single system, so a leaf cluster must connect once to the super-cluster, not to each member cluster — derekcollison. "the LN connections from cluster 3 in Asia should only connect once to the supercluster, not to each cluster 1 & 2."
- [OPS][TOPO] For super-clusters use CNAME DNS per cluster and geo-aware global DNS for the whole system, as Synadia Cloud does — derekcollison.
- [TOPO][SEC] Loops can also be created through account imports/exports; ordinary misconfiguration loops are caught when leaf connections are established — derekcollison.

## Produce from anywhere, consume from the same availability zone
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5989
- date: 2024-10-10 | asker: huttotw | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): R3 on GKE across zones; inter-zone egress is expensive; how do consumers always read from a server in their zone?

### Claims
- [CONS][TOPO] Reads from a consumer always go through the consumer leader; in a multi-AZ cluster the leader can move on election, so the app must find the leader and connect there — derekcollison. "Reading from consumers is always done from the leader"
- [PATTERN][TOPO] If the consumer's cluster is known in advance, give consuming apps a DNS name resolving only to that cluster's servers; otherwise read cluster info to locate it — derekcollison.
- [SIZE][CONS] Asker runs ~100,000 partition-mapped consumers; maintainer response was a Synadia consult, not a public recipe — derekcollison.

## Zone-aware consumer reads for JetStream (similar to Kafka's KIP-392)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/8007
- date: 2026-04-06 | asker: bobo | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.12/2.13
- question (one line): R3 across AZs crosses AZ boundaries up to three times per message; could local replicas serve pull consumers like AllowDirect does?

### Claims
- [TOPO][OPS] With R3 across AZs one payload can cross AZ boundaries up to three times: Raft replication, consumer leader delivery, core routing to subscribers — bobo [UNVERIFIED, plausible mechanism, not disputed].
- [TOPO] AllowDirect already lets any replica serve Direct Get, trading read-after-write consistency for read distribution — bobo [UNVERIFIED but matches docs].
- [OPS] Synadia is researching cost optimization for cross-AZ ingest and consumption; nothing definite as of 2026-04 — derekcollison.

## NATS Witness Node
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6108
- date: 2024-11-11 | asker: CallumLangdaleSaab | answered by: neilalexander | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Can a server be a vote-only witness that stores no data?

### Claims
- [TOPO] No witness concept: each replicated asset holds its own election and only the nodes the asset is placed on vote — neilalexander. "only nodes that an asset is placed on participate in an election."
- [TOPO][PATTERN] Servers can join the meta-layer election without hosting assets via placement tags restricting streams/consumers to a subset, but this does not improve stream/consumer availability — neilalexander.
- [OPS][TOPO] The `!jetstream` server tag keeps a server in the meta group while preventing stream placement on it — ramonberrutti [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer].

## Cluster can't tolerate more than one service failure
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3417
- date: 2022-08-30 | asker: AhmedAbouelkher | answered by: kozlovic | server version context: 2.8.4
- question (one line): 3-node docker cluster stops when 2 of 3 are down, and even one node down "crashes" it.

### Claims
- [TOPO] A 3-server cluster survives exactly one failure; quorum rules as in any Raft system — kozlovic.
- [MYTH][STRM] Belief: any stream on a cluster is HA. Correction: an R1 stream hosted on the stopped server is unavailable; make it R3 — kozlovic.
- [CLNT][OPS] Clients must be given all cluster URLs (or be able to use gossiped URLs); in docker the gossiped ports may be internal and unreachable — kozlovic.

## 2 Node High Availability cluster for nats stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2869
- date: 2022-02-15 | asker: msg2man | answered by: derekcollison, neilalexander | server version context: 2.7 / 2.10
- question (one line): Only 2 nodes and no shared storage; how to get HA JetStream?

### Claims
- [TOPO][ANTI] A 2-node JetStream cluster gives durability but blocks all streams when either server is down until both return — derekcollison. "if any of the servers has an issue the system and all streams will be blocked until both servers are back"
- [PATTERN][TOPO] The supported 2-server replication path is a leaf-node connection between them plus source/mirror stream config, which backfills gaps after interruptions — neilalexander.

## Active-active, eventually consistent replication for JetStream?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3866
- date: 2023-02-14 | asker: lewisl9029 | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Global app wants fast local writes and eventual global replication; docs only show one-way mirrors or consensus clustering.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][TOPO][SUBJ] Per-region streams `ORDERS_LON/SFO/NYC` on `orders.<region>.>` plus a central `ORDERS` that sources all, or cross-sourcing between regions for eventually consistent full views — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][TOPO][SUBJ] Two streams A and B on `ORDERS.A.>` and `ORDERS.B.>` can source each other as long as subject spaces do not overlap; a node-local subject mapping `ORDERS.>` to `ORDERS.A.>` lets apps publish the plain subject and land in the local stream, replicated asynchronously — derekcollison.
- [KV][TOPO] KV mirrors and sources were coming in the next major release (2023); Object store replication was not supported — ripienaar. [STALE?] (KV mirror/source now supported)
- [TOPO][KV] To replicate between otherwise unconnected servers, leaf-node them together so native replication works; else an external watcher-based replicator for KV is easy — ripienaar.

## Source stream from multiple leaf nodes
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5889
- date: 2024-09-15 | asker: ZarkoRunjevac | answered by: jnmoyne, derekcollison | server version context: 2.11-dev
- question (one line): IoT leaf nodes added dynamically; how to aggregate their streams into one hub stream, and is there a limit on sources?

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Stream sources can be added or removed at any time by editing the stream config (`nats stream info --json | jq .config`, edit, `nats stream edit --config`) — jnmoyne.
- [STRM][SIZE] No hard-coded limit on the number of sources per stream — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][STRM] Scale many sources with intermediary streams (each sourcing half the leaves) feeding a final central stream — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][TOPO][SIZE] Edge fleets: the hub side uses muxed streams holding up to N fleet nodes, grouped into "cells" with fixed capacity deployed as the fleet grows — derekcollison. "the hub/cloud side has muxed streams that hold up to N fleet nodes. Each architecture here is usually referred to as a 'cell'"
- [ANTI][STRM] Do not create a 1:1 stream on the cloud side for every fleet member — derekcollison. "We do not recommend cloud side has a 1:1 stream for every fleet member."
- [MYTH] Belief: a stream with sources cannot be updated after creation. Correction: sources are editable at any time — jnmoyne.

## Leaf node with standalone (non-cluster) Primary NATS server
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5797
- date: 2024-08-16 | asker: rdkumavat1 | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Replicate a leaf-node stream subject into a hub stream, surviving disconnects.

### Claims
- [TOPO] By default the two sides of a leaf connection are different JetStream domains; domain names must differ unless the system account is shared — derekcollison. "Unless you also share the system account, the domain names need to be different."
- [TOPO][SEC] Share the system account across a leaf link only when truly extending one system, not when connecting two systems — derekcollison. "we only suggest to share the system account if you are truly extended a system through a leafnode vs connecting two systems via a leafnode."
- [STRM][TOPO] Cross-domain sourcing uses `external.api: $JS.<domain>.API`; catch-up after a leaf disconnect is expected behavior — derekcollison.

## Distributing messages across leaf nodes
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7477
- date: 2025-10-28 | asker: roded | answered by: (self) | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Deliver each message to exactly one of two leaf nodes; is sourcing from a WorkQueue stream safe?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][STRM] For once-only delivery to either leaf: a WorkQueue stream on the hub with an explicit-ack consumer that clients on the leaves pull from, instead of per-leaf source streams — roded [UNVERIFIED, self-answer; consistent with docs warning about sourcing WorkQueue streams].

## Jetstream KV/ObjectStore as a database?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5468
- date: 2024-05-23 | asker: formula349 | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Can KV/Object store replace Postgres as the primary source of truth?

### Claims
- [KV][OBJ][USECASE] JetStream covers "no SQL" needs: KV, Object store, subject-addressed streams, compare-and-set instead of transactions. Full SQL, schemas, joins, transactions and isolation are the domain of real databases — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][USECASE] CDC tools (e.g. Conduit) streaming Postgres changes into NATS is the suggested way to get live client updates from a relational source of truth — nickchomey [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer].

## locks/leases with KV similar to SETNX
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4803
- date: 2023-11-19 | asker: aep | answered by: jnmoyne, ripienaar | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Can NATS KV replace Redis SETNX locks, and how do locks expire when the holder dies?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][KV][STRM] Distributed lock via a stream with `DiscardNewPerSubject`, max 1 message per subject, and a max age: publish succeeds = lock acquired; delete the message = release; publish fails = lock held — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][KV] With the KV API: `Create()` to obtain the lock, `Update()` (CAS on revision) to keep it, bucket TTL to expire stale locks — ripienaar.
- [KV] The KV lease pattern does not guarantee exclusivity but is on par with widely used Kubernetes lease options — ripienaar. "it does not guarantee exclusivity but its on par with options in K8s etc"
- [CONS][CLNT] `InProgress` (`+WPI`) extends ack wait; the client library call never fails, but `nc.Request(msg.Reply, "+WPI")` returns an error when the server is gone, so it can double as a liveness check on the lock — ripienaar (verified by aep).
- [ANTI][PATTERN] "Exclusive worker token" pattern (inbox stream with MaxMsgsPerSubject=1 sourced into a WorkQueue stream with DiscardNewPerSubject) was tested in production and discarded: sourcing retries every 2 s while a token is held, flooding logs, and messages that exhaust MaxDeliver stay in the WorkQueue and block the subject — rafsawicki [UNVERIFIED, user report].
- [MYTH] Belief: exactly-once delivery keeps two workers off the same key. Correction: dedup prevents the same message being replayed, not parallel delivery of different messages for the same key — aep (asker's own discovery, consistent with maintainer replies).

## JetStream file-store ~65x slower than memory-store on KV mirror (83% of seq space is deleted)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/8417
- date: 2026-07-24 | asker: cyqsign | answered by: MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.14.2
- question (one line): A file-backed KV mirror with 2M live keys over 12M sequences reads at ~4k msg/s vs ~267k msg/s for the memory mirror. Why?

### Claims
- [KV][STRM] A KV bucket with many overwrites leaves a sparse sequence space (here 83% interior deletes), which hurts file-store scans — cyqsign (measured), acknowledged by MauriceVanVeen who is "working on an improvement in the filestore for a situation like this where the number of deletes are greater than the number of unique subjects."
- [CONS][ANTI] Do not pass a `FilterSubject` that matches everything on a mirror: a mirror has no ingest subjects so the server cannot recognize the filter as "all", the 4x messages-vs-subjects heuristic uses the huge first/last range, and every message lookup does an expensive per-subject-state read. Removing the filter gave 150k+ msg/s — MauriceVanVeen. "best is to just not pass a filter subject if you don't intend on filtering"
- [STRM] A message block never starts with deleted messages; interior deletes are tracked in the block's delete map and tail deletes are compacted away; the linear scan covers only that range — MauriceVanVeen.
- [STRM][PATTERN] Purging many subjects needs a proper subject hierarchy: `js.PurgeStream` with filter `event.foo.>` purges without storing a marker message; do not publish a rollup message just to delete — MauriceVanVeen.
- [STRM] There is no atomic swap between distinct subjects; rollup atomically replaces only the same subject. Redesign the subject hierarchy so rollup on one subject works — MauriceVanVeen.
- [OPS] Maintainer recommends 4+ vCPU when running large consumer counts; general baseline elsewhere is 4 cores / 16 GB / SSD — (see 6397, 7863).

## KV storage operations timeout [v2.10.20]
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6397
- date: 2025-01-22 | asker: Inkathu | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.10.20, fix in 2.10.24/25
- question (one line): 40 streams, 400 consumers, KV-based role election; one busy node sees 20 s `$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET` latency and client timeouts.

### Claims
- [OPS][SIZE] General server sizing recommendation: at least 4 cores and 16 GB memory plus SSD volumes — wallyqs. "general recommendation is to use at least 4 cores and 16GB of mem ... (plus SSD volumes)"
- [OPS] Diagnose stalls with system-account profiles: `nats server request profile goroutine --level=1|2` and `profile cpu` — wallyqs.
- [KV][CLNT] Seeing `$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.<stream>` in logs means the KV client is not using `allow_direct`; newer clients default to direct gets served by any replica instead of the leader — wallyqs.
- [OPS] Lock contention with large data volumes was improved in 2.10.24/2.10.25 — wallyqs.
- [STRM][OPS] A stream with 17M interior deletes (2.2M live of 23M sequences) was the suspected cause of stalls; frequent purge streams and old clients aggravate it — wallyqs (inferred from thread).

## ObjectStore to share audio/video files between microservices
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5262
- date: 2024-03-31 | asker: ealeykin | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Is Object store viable versus MinIO/S3/NFS for sharing media files between services?

### Claims
- [OBJ][USECASE] Object store is used in production for sharing media between microservices — derekcollison.
- [OBJ] Object store reads use ordered consumers so transfers are flow controlled end to end; KV uses direct gets that core NATS routes to the nearest replica — derekcollison.
- [OBJ][TOPO][PATTERN] With many mirrors ("digital twins") of an Object store, ask StreamInfo/ObjectInfo on the origin: it lists alternates in RTT order from the requesting app; bind to the closest for low-latency reads — derekcollison.

## Why a 64 MB message size limit?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6501
- date: 2025-02-12 | asker: Marko19907 | answered by: neilalexander, Jarema | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Why cap messages at 64 MB when others allow 1 GB, and what breaks if I raise it?

### Claims
- [CORE][SIZE] Very large messages exhaust memory fast and cannot be buffered before triggering slow-consumer disconnects — neilalexander.
- [CORE] Core NATS works entirely in memory, so an upper bound keeps the server from OOM and per-client queues from growing to gigabytes; a client that cannot keep up is marked slow consumer and disconnected — neilalexander. "we only allow queued traffic for a specific client to build up to a certain size"
- [OBJ][PATTERN] For large payloads in JetStream use Object store, which chunks for you — neilalexander.
- [CLNT][PATTERN] For core NATS, chunk with "request many" strategies from Orbit natsext; the .NET client has request-many built in — Jarema.

## max_payload - issues if we increase it to more than 8MB
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7068
- date: 2025-07-16 | asker: Santhoshbesagarahalli | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Docs say keep max_payload at or under 8 MB (max 64 MB); what breaks above 8 MB?

### Claims
- [CORE][SIZE] Above 8 MB expect head-of-line blocking, delivery timeouts, memory consumption and processing cost; sensitivity depends on latency-sensitive traffic sharing the system, memory, network, super-cluster use — jnmoyne. "Just don't come and complain about any of those side-effects if you go above the recommendation in the docs."
- [OPS][PATTERN] Validate large-message configs with `nats bench` at production-like load including server stop faults — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN] Send large data out of band (S3/FTP) and put only the URI (plus key/token) in the message — Zetanova [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer, standard advice].

## Automatic Chunking
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6320
- date: 2025-01-03 | asker: Material-Scientist | answered by: ripienaar, Jarema | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): 40 MB KV put failed even with 64 MB max_payload; why not auto-chunk in KV and pub/sub like Object store does?

### Claims
- [SIZE][CORE] NATS is not optimized for big payloads; 2 or 3 MB max is a good rule — ripienaar. "Nats isn't optimised for big payloads 2 or 3MB max is a good rule"
- [OBJ] Object store is the intended home for large values — ripienaar.
- [CORE][KV] Core pub/sub is at-most-once with no persistence, so chunking there with a JetStream layer "is not a way to go"; KV chunking would complicate the KV API, maybe revisited after batched publishes — Jarema.
- [OBJ][KV] Object get costs a metadata request, a temporary subscription, a content request, a pipe, and a completion signal; KV get is one request. KV values fitting in RAM is a guarantee — jgaskins [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer, cites nats.go source].

## Automatic Message Payload Preservation in DLQ Stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7590
- date: 2025-11-28 | asker: Atanusaha143 | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.11/2.12
- question (one line): MAX_DELIVERIES advisories carry only metadata and the message is gone from the stream; add payload to DLQ advisories?

### Claims
- [ANTI][CONS] Including payloads in DLQ advisories was rejected on user feedback: payloads can be sensitive and advisories often leave NATS; a per-consumer opt-in might be acceptable — ripienaar.
- [OPS] Feature prioritization happens roughly twice a year; a PR is the fast path — ripienaar.
- [CONS][MYTH] Belief: a WorkQueue message is removed when it hits max_deliver. Correction: it stays in the stream (removed only on ack or TTL) and can be fetched by the advisory's sequence with payload; verified on 2.12.4 R1, with a suspected loss on R3 — jgriegershs [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer].

## AckWait does not publish to dead letter queue with zero clients
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4994
- date: 2024-01-24 | asker: gongy | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Many work queues with pull consumers polled by a scale-to-zero pool; with no fetchers, AckWait expiry never triggers MaxDeliver advisories.

### Claims
- [CONS] NATS has no automated DLQ by design because consumer semantics are kept separate from stream semantics — derekcollison. "We do not have automated DLQs ... since we truly separate consumers from stream semantics."
- [PATTERN][STRM] Instead of many work-queue streams, run one large muxed stream and have consumers pull only the subjects they need, keyed by event type — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][CONS] DLQ pattern: Term the message and run a service that captures the advisory and moves the message to a chosen stream — derekcollison.
- [CONS] Redelivery/MaxDeliver processing for pull consumers happens when clients fetch; with zero fetchers a message sits in AckPending after AckWait (issue 1716, by design) — gongy (asker, confirmed behaviour).

## Message Scheduler vs NAK-with-delay for scheduled notifications at scale
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7628
- date: 2025-12-09 | asker: jan-krueger | answered by: MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.12
- question (one line): 100K+ pending schedules per stream: native scheduler (ADR-51) or NakWithDelay loops?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][STRM] Use the 2.12 message scheduler over NakWithDelay; Nak is not meant for scheduling and only worked as a workaround before 2.12 — MauriceVanVeen.
- [SIZE][STRM] The scheduler is built on per-message TTL machinery and should support a very large number of schedules; test for your use case — MauriceVanVeen.

## ack-wait and dupe-window behavior when used together
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6628
- date: 2025-03-10 | asker: s4iko | answered by: MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): AckWait 8m and DupeWindow 10m, still seeing redeliveries; shouldn't the dupe window prevent double processing?

### Claims
- [MYTH][CONS][STRM] AckWait (consumer redelivery timer) and DupeWindow (stream publish dedup by Nats-Msg-Id) are unrelated settings — MauriceVanVeen.
- [CONS] To process at most once set MaxDeliver=1 or always Ack/Term; defaults are DupeWindow 2 min and AckWait 30 s — MauriceVanVeen.
- [CONS][CLNT] Fetching a batch of 100 with long per-message processing caused AckWait expiry and redelivery; fetching one at a time fixed it — s4iko (asker, verified fix).

## Message prioritization to certain consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3534
- date: 2022-10-10 | asker: plaisted | answered by: derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.9 / 2.11
- question (one line): Work queue with pull consumers on Kubernetes; prefer the worker on the node holding a local cache, else any worker.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][KV][OBJ] For data locality, use KV or Object store with real-time mirrors on every node, with expiry or replacement on new entries — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][CONS] For deterministic routing of related requests to the same worker, use partitioned consumer groups (Orbit pcgroups) keyed on a subject token — jnmoyne.

## Sharing many distributed account streams with a server-side account
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5788
- date: 2024-08-13 | asker: brettinternet | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Thousands of IoT tenant accounts must publish to a central "server account"; importing every account's stream export into the server account is unmanageable.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][SEC] Reverse the direction: the central account exports one service that every new tenant account imports; new tenants need no change to the central account's JWT — derekcollison. "have the server account export a single service that all new accounts import ... makes management easier at those scales."
- [SEC][STRM] Publishing to a stream requires a response, so a service export from the central account fits; a stream export from each new account would force a central import per account — derekcollison.
- [SEC] Tenant to central: export a stream from the tenant, or a service from the central account; services expect responses — derekcollison.

## Max Ack Pending per Subject?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5211
- date: 2024-03-13 | asker: praveenperera | answered by: Jarema, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10 / 2.11
- question (one line): One consumer on `client.node.*`; want MaxAckPending=1 per node subject but parallel across nodes.

### Claims
- [CONS] MaxAckPending cannot be set per subject; strict per-subject order needs a consumer per subject, because MaxAckPending above 1 can cause out-of-order redeliveries on missed acks — Jarema.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Hash the entity ID into buckets and create one consumer per bucket — praveenperera (asker workaround, later endorsed as the pcgroups model by jnmoyne).
- [PATTERN][CONS] If strict per-device order is not needed: MaxAckPending greater than the worker-thread count, one fetch loop handing off to a thread pool, so slow messages do not block fast ones — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Two-level partitioning: hash device ID modulo thread count inside the app, and pcgroups across app instances — jnmoyne.
- [CLNT] pcgroups has a Java implementation in orbit.java (2025) — jnmoyne.

## JetStream. "Queue group" feature with pull subscribers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5415
- date: 2024-05-13 | asker: ruslan528 | answered by: derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Can a dynamic pool of apps share one subject's work with pull consumers like a Kafka consumer group?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CONS] One durable pull consumer, any number of app instances bound to it; messages are distributed automatically; drain subscriptions when scaling down — derekcollison.
- [CONS] Two clients on the same durable cannot receive the same message unless it is a redelivery; check the delivery count in the message metadata — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][CLNT] If `backoff` is set, the first backoff value overrides AckWait (server behaviour); a backoff of [1s, 60s] with AckWait 30s gives 1 s before redelivery — EvilaMany (asker, cites consumer.go) [UNVERIFIED but source-cited].

## Memory usage when replaying messages with filter subject on a large stream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4906
- date: 2023-12-21 | asker: david-wakeo | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10.5 to 2.10.11
- question (one line): Filtered replay (`domain.*.<uuid>.*`) on a 7 GiB R3 stream spikes memory to the GOMEMLIMIT and times out other clients.

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Filtered replays where matches sit at the end of a large stream caused multi-GiB memory spikes on 2.10.5-2.10.9; fixed via PR 4969 and 2.10.11 — derekcollison.
- [STRM] Per-block subject index (fss) lingers up to the sync interval (default 2 min) if the block is idle; block data cache expires faster — derekcollison.
- [OPS] Grab memory/CPU profiles with `nats server request profile` using a system-account context — derekcollison.
- [OPS] Without a memory limit the Go runtime delays GC and pool cleanup, so raw container memory overstates need — derekcollison.

## Why increasing of "Unprocessed Messages" leads to increasing nats memory usage?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6820
- date: 2025-04-23 | asker: tierpod | answered by: MauriceVanVeen, wallyqs | server version context: 2.10/2.11
- question (one line): WorkQueue stream (R3, file) with a stalled consumer: backlog grows on disk, but why does host memory grow?

### Claims
- [STRM][SIZE] Interior deletes (acked messages behind an unacked head in a WorkQueue) are tracked in a bitmask; at 175-196 million interior deletes this measurably costs memory — MauriceVanVeen. "We keep track of interior deletes by sequence number in a bit mask data structure. So efficient but at those numbers will have an impact"
- [STRM] "Deleted Messages" in stream info counts interior deletes only; FirstSeq not advancing means one consumer holds the oldest message — MauriceVanVeen.
- [CONS][CLNT][PATTERN] Set `MaxBytes` on fetches (e.g. 8-16 MiB, never below max message size or `max_payload`); a client behind with MaxAckPending 56,000 makes the server allocate many buffers at once that are slow to release — wallyqs.
- [OPS] To see real message sizes on the wire briefly `nats sub '$JS.ACK.>'` on a raw connection — wallyqs.

## JetStream recovery latency increases sub-linearly with backlog size for stalled durable consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7681
- date: 2025-12-27 | asker: Abubakarsidiq01 | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.14.0-dev
- question (one line): After an abrupt server kill, restart-to-first-delivery time grows with backlog (2.8 s at 100 msgs, 4.8 s at 5000).

### Claims
- [OPS] Stop the server with USR2 (lame duck, graceful); after an unclean stop the server reads all blocks to repair state on restart, logged as a WRN on the stream — wallyqs.

## JetStream startup seems slow for ~50M messages
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/8001
- date: 2026-04-02 | asker: zig | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.12.5
- question (one line): 50M-message, 39 GiB, S2-compressed R1 stream on Ceph takes 6m38s to restore on restart; expected?

### Claims
- [OPS] Versions after 2.11.11 restore streams in parallel — wallyqs.
- [OPS] After a clean shutdown startup should be very fast; an unclean shutdown forces rebuilding stream metadata and indexes — wallyqs.
- [OPS][MYTH] `config reload not supported for jetstream max memory and store`: changing JetStream limits needs a restart, not a HUP — server log in thread.
- [OPS] A full 20 MB/s scan of 39 GiB on restart with only 6 subjects after a clean exit was called "not normal"; a startup CPU profile was requested — wallyqs (unresolved in thread).

## Mirror leaf node stream on the main server
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7584
- date: 2025-11-26 | asker: maurice-freitag | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Customer-site leaf nodes each with their own account; want to mirror a leaf stream into the hub and see leaf JS status from the hub's system account.

### Claims
- [TOPO][SEC] To extend one NATS system (one JS domain) across a leaf, connect the system accounts across the leaf link; for separate JS domains, do not — derekcollison. "If you are trying to extend a NATS system, and hence a JS domain, yes you should connect the system accounts across the leafnode. If you want separate JS domains, do not."
- [TOPO][STRM] Mirroring streams across a leaf node is "very common" — derekcollison.

## Cross-domain JetStream sourcing, how do I set that up?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7881
- date: 2026-02-26 | asker: tbalbers | answered by: (none maintainer) | server version context: 2.12
- question (one line): TLS super-cluster plus standalone leaf nodes with JetStream, no shared system account; how to source streams both ways between accounts?

### Claims
- [TOPO][SEC] `service import not authorized` on `$JS.<domain>.API.>` means the JS API subjects were not exported/imported between the accounts on each side — tbalbers (error), mg1986jp [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer explanation].
- [OPS] No maintainer answer in 6 months; cross-domain sourcing with config-file accounts and TLS is a documentation gap — thread evidence.

## Is $JS.ACK purposefully domain-unaware? Potential interference with leaf nodes
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6136
- date: 2024-11-15 | asker: cbecker | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Two leaf domains with same-named streams/consumers; `$JS.ACK` from one leaf reaches consumers on the other.

### Claims
- [TOPO][CONS] In the domain design, `$JS.ACK` and message gets (direct and original) are not domain-aware; a fix is planned — derekcollison. "ACK and MSG gets (both direct and original) are not domain aware. We plan to fix for sure."
- [ANTI][TOPO] Identically named streams and consumers in different leaf domains sharing a hub can cross-talk on ACK subjects; workaround is deny rules on `$JS.ACK` across the leaf link — cbecker (asker workaround, confirmed problem by derekcollison).

## Leaf-node JetStream retention policy for hub-sourced streams
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4694
- date: 2023-10-24 | asker: AlexeiSosnov | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Leaf stream is sourced by a hub stream; which leaf retention policy frees space once the hub has the message?

### Claims
- [STRM][TOPO] The consumer between a source/mirror and its origin is ephemeral, so Interest retention on the origin (leaf) stream gives inconsistent results and can lose messages published while the link is down — derekcollison.
- [STRM][ANTI] Some users run WorkQueue on the leaf origin stream, but there were reports of messages not cleaned up after long outages — derekcollison. [STALE?] (2.11 work planned)
- [PATTERN][STRM][TOPO] Recommended: Limits retention on the leaf stream with max age set to the longest expected network outage, plus a max bytes limit so the leaf does not run away with disk or memory — derekcollison. "The age limit should be your maximum outage window allowance."

## Leaf-node -> cluster connection pooling plans and simulation
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4704
- date: 2023-10-25 | asker: AlexeiSosnov | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): One leaf connection carries everything; bulk low-priority traffic can starve request/reply. Any pooling?

### Claims
- [TOPO][PATTERN] Each leaf server has a single connection per account; separate traffic classes by using different local accounts on the leaf, each with its own remote connection — derekcollison.

## What are strategies for moving a stream to a different set of nodes in the cluster?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2730
- date: 2021-12-05 | asker: bruth | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.6 (placement tags later)
- question (one line): Migrate a 3-node JetStream cluster to new hardware with zero client-visible downtime.

### Claims
- [OPS][MIG] Keep server names static; replace nodes one at a time on the same name; after a clean shutdown the replacement syncs all streams assigned to it; wait for full sync before touching the next node; always use Lame Duck Mode — ripienaar.
- [OPS][MIG] Removing a peer (`nats cluster peer-remove`) makes the stream pick a new peer at random; with old nodes still present it may pick an old one — ripienaar, derekcollison.
- [OPS][MIG] Alternative: put the departing server in LDM then remove it from the cluster with `nats server raft` to move all its data; for lots of data do it per stream to spread replication load — ripienaar.
- [OPS][MIG] Safe pattern: 3 nodes, add 2 temporary, replace the 3 one by one on the same names, then remove the 2; clients learn topology via gossip — ripienaar.
- [ANTI][OPS] Data loss risk: if R3 on 1,2,3 loses 1 and 4 joins, removing 2 before 4 has fully synced every stream in every account can lose data — ripienaar.
- [OPS] LDM moves leadership away but a new peer is only chosen when the node is removed from the Raft group — ripienaar.
- [OPS][MIG] Backup and restore into a new cluster is the simplest path if downtime is allowed — derekcollison.
- [OPS] Placement tags (2.10+) let you move existing streams within or between clusters without interruption and transparently to clients — jnmoyne. [STALE?] earlier manual steps superseded.

## How to distribute load from one stream to all JetStream cluster nodes?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5350
- date: 2024-04-25 | asker: Envek | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): One WorkQueue stream on a 3-node cluster; one node carries all traffic, the others only replicate.

### Claims
- [STRM][CONS][TOPO] A consumer is bound to a single node and writes to a stream go through one node; WorkQueue and Interest add further constraints, so this is the hardest combination to scale horizontally — ripienaar. "Consumers are bound to a single node and writes into a stream also"
- [PATTERN][STRM] Spread with server-side subject mapping so producers stay unaware of partitions, or one Limits stream that sources into N WorkQueue streams; consumers enumerate the streams programmatically — ripienaar.
- [CONS][TOPO] Consumer leaders need not sit on the stream leader's server; move a leader with a step-down to rebalance — derekcollison.

## has NO quorum, stalled on jetstream consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3210
- date: 2022-06-22 | asker: 1995parham | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.8.4 / 2.9.17
- question (one line): Consumer logs "has NO quorum, stalled" and clients get "JetStream system temporarily unavailable" on 1 CPU / 4Gi pods.

### Claims
- [OPS][SIZE] Recommended JetStream server resources: 4 CPU and at least 8Gi memory; for 7k in / 9k out msgs/s raise CPU to at least 4 — derekcollison. "We recommend 4 cpu and at east 8Gi for JetStream enabled servers." [STALE?] (later guidance says 4 cores / 16 GB)
- [CONS] Ephemeral consumers default to R1 unless the stream uses WorkQueue or Interest retention; consumer replica count and store can be set explicitly — derekcollison.
- [TOPO] An R3 stream that loses two of its three peers cannot progress; surviving two down needs R5, "generally not recommended since cloud providers do things in 3s" — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][TOPO] Use placement tags so an R3 stream's peers land in different AZs, so one AZ loss removes one peer — derekcollison.
- [MYTH] Belief: a 5-node cluster with R3 streams survives any two node failures. Correction: survival is per stream, depending on which peers hold it — derekcollison.

## Which NATS JetStream Setup is Better? (WorkQueue plus mirror vs one Limits stream)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6571
- date: 2025-02-24 | asker: nrapendra-singh | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): One fast consumer and one slow analytics consumer: WorkQueue source plus Limits mirror, or a single Limits stream?

### Claims
- [MYTH][STRM] A larger stream does not slow delivery to consumers; one Limits stream with two consumers is simpler and more efficient than WorkQueue plus mirror — jnmoyne. "It's not because a stream is larger that delivery of messages to consumers takes longer"
- [STRM][SIZE] The main cost of a large stream is memory for per-subject indexing when there are many distinct subjects — jnmoyne.

## Hot scaling core NATS (no JetStream) for bursty traffic
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7738
- date: 2026-01-16 | asker: NevinDry | answered by: ripienaar, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11/2.12
- question (one line): 4-node core cluster on Fargate with ~18M subscriptions and 3,800 connections; adding nodes raises CPU; use burst super-clusters?

### Claims
- [TOPO][OPS] Adding cluster nodes needs no restarts; a new node pointed at a few seeds joins the full mesh; keep a stable core and scale out against it — ripienaar.
- [SIZE][CORE] Full-mesh route and interest-propagation overhead is very small unless you have many hundreds of thousands of subscriptions — ripienaar. "These overheads are very small unless you have many 100s of k of subscriptions."
- [OPS][ANTI] Fargate is "not, imo, a good place to run nats"; EC2-style hosts are better for this workload — ripienaar.
- [SUBJ][ANTI] 18M subscriptions came from per-team subjects `usecase.$user_id`; collapse to `$team.$user.>` style namespacing to shrink the interest graph. "Just punting the hard work of having multiple teams onto the software will forever cause failures" — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][CLNT][OPS] Rebalancing after adding servers: periodically kick connections from crowded servers, throttled to avoid a thundering herd; clients reconnect using gossiped server lists — jnmoyne. The CLI has a connection rebalance command built in — ripienaar.
- [TOPO] A separate burst cluster via gateways is not better than adding nodes; the real problem is rebalancing existing connections — jnmoyne.

## Accounts - Best way to add new accounts and reload running servers in a cluster
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5890
- date: 2024-09-15 | asker: apuckey | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Adding config-file accounts to a 5-node cluster via rolling reload did not work until a full restart; procedure?

### Claims
- [SEC][OPS] The JWT-based auth system exists to solve dynamic account management; config-file accounts are not designed for rolling adds — ripienaar.
- [MIG][SEC] To migrate from config accounts to JWT: stand up a new server/cluster with JWT auth and leaf-node the old one to it, moving apps gradually; auth callout is another option — derekcollison.

## NATS Jetstreams creation and management (streams in server config?)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4457
- date: 2023-08-31 | asker: CodeTherapist | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Consumers start before producers create the stream; why can't streams be declared in the server config?

### Claims
- [OPS][STRM] Streams are API-first by design: NATS is multi-tenant with decentralized auth where account definitions may not live in the server config, and users of a centrally run system cannot touch config files — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][OPS] Provision streams with client APIs, CLI, Terraform or GitHub Actions, e.g. a setup container in the scheduler or a boot step — ripienaar.

## Account Question (SYS account listing all streams)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3021
- date: 2022-04-11 | asker: zbindenren | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.7
- question (one line): Can the system account list all streams and consumers across accounts?

### Claims
- [SEC] The system account provides JetStream and `nats server report jetstream`, but there is no cross-account roll-up of streams; that would violate the account security model — derekcollison. "We have no plans to violate the security model of accounts"
- [PATTERN][SEC] For fleet-wide monitoring write a multiplexer using limited credentials for each account — derekcollison.

## InterestPolicy variation (per-user subjects, millions of subjects)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4218
- date: 2023-06-06 | asker: agufagit | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): One subject per user in one stream (millions of subjects); keep messages until at least one device consumed them, deliver to all logged-in devices.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CONS] Per-device durable consumers that are only active while the device is online keep persistent state and prevent deletion under Interest retention — derekcollison. "You will have persistent consumer state for each device, but those consumers are only active when the device is online and connected. Will work fine for you."
- [STRM] A stream with millions of per-user subjects was accepted as a workable design — derekcollison (implicit).

## NATS pub-sub, publish rate affected by the number of subscribers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5641
- date: 2024-07-11 | asker: kevinignas | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Publish rate drops as subscriber count rises; is that expected?

### Claims
- [CORE] Fan-out costs CPU and bandwidth per copy; publish rate falls as subscribers are added — jnmoyne.
- [CORE] A subscriber that cannot keep up becomes a slow consumer and can raise publisher latency (issue 5394) — jnmoyne.

## Impact of server cluster internal slow consumer and how to handle it?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4975
- date: 2024-01-18 | asker: SirDave0 | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.10.3
- question (one line): Rolling restarts report routes as slow consumers; message loss? Raise write_deadline?

### Claims
- [OPS] The server cannot say how many messages were dropped when a route becomes a slow consumer — wallyqs.
- [OPS] `connz` pending_bytes shows early back pressure on a connection; once it dissipates the bytes left that server, nothing more can be asserted — wallyqs.

## Symptom: Unexpected `nats: timeout`
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5859
- date: 2024-08-28 | asker: RitikaLaddha | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.10.18/2.10.20
- question (one line): Intermittent request timeouts on a k8s cluster with one route URL; later a Java JetStream publishAsync "Future cancelled" through leaf hops.

### Claims
- [OPS][TOPO] On Kubernetes the routes list must contain every StatefulSet pod DNS name; a single service name will not work; the official Helm chart does this — wallyqs.
- [OPS] `Delaying PING due to remote client data` is normal ping-interval logging (every 2 minutes) — wallyqs.
- [OPS][SIZE] `GOMAXPROCS=1` from tight cgroup CPU limits can block or delay the server; set at least GOMAXPROCS=2 — wallyqs.
- [OPS] The server logs "Maximum payloads over 8.00 MB are generally discouraged and could lead to poor performance" at startup — server log.

## Time-sensitive messages (expiry and deferred delivery)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2731
- date: 2021-12-06 | asker: c16a | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.7 (features shipped in 2.11/2.12)
- question (one line): Add `Nats-Before` / `Nats-Not-Before` headers for TTL and deferred delivery?

### Claims
- [STRM] Per-message TTL and deferred delivery were "being considered" in 2022; per-message TTL shipped in 2.11 and message scheduling in 2.12 — derekcollison. [STALE?]
- [ANTI][STRM] Re-injecting a message with the same Nats-Msg-Id inside the dedup window makes it vanish; requires a new ID plus an Original-Id header — andreib1 [UNVERIFIED, user report].

## JetStream and NATS server Data Store
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5217
- date: 2024-03-15 | asker: alberk8 | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): What storage engine backs JetStream?

### Claims
- [STRM] JetStream has its own store implementation with no dependency on an external database; storage is file or memory — ripienaar, derekcollison.

## Backup data in nats-server with jetstream enabled where storage is memory
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4342
- date: 2023-07-27 | asker: anil1996 | answered by: derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): How to back up memory streams and survive restarts?

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Memory streams survive restarts only when R3 with rolling restarts and healthz checks; for backup create a file-backed mirror and back that up — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][OPS] Controlled restart of an R1 stream without interruption: edit to R3, wait for replicas to catch up in `nats stream info`, restart, edit back to R1. Unscheduled restarts need R3 — jnmoyne.

## Is Tiered Storage currently planned?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3871
- date: 2023-02-15 | asker: shafqatevo | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9 through 2.11
- question (one line): When will S3-style tiered storage for streams arrive?

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Tiered storage is planned with no schedule (2023); still absent as of 2025 with users running custom offload jobs to cloud storage — derekcollison, thread.
