## how to recover from DiscardNew policy?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2794
- date: 2022-01-17 | asker: lukasGemela | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.7
- question (one line): Limits stream with DiscardNew stays full after consumers ack; expected producer back pressure that recovers?

### Claims
- [STRM][MYTH] Stream state is separate from consumer state; acks do not delete messages under Limits retention. Interest retention removes a message once all interested consumers ack it — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][STRM] Producer back pressure that recovers as consumers catch up: Interest retention plus DiscardNew — derekcollison (implicit "That is probably what you want").

## How to find out what caused a corruption in JetStream Cluster?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7463
- date: 2025-10-22 | asker: KenLR | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.9.8 (fixed by upgrading to 2.12)
- question (one line): Raft "Wrong index" and "malformed or corrupt message" corruption spreading between replicas on 2.9.8.

### Claims
- [OPS] 2.9.x is unsupported and hundreds of fixes behind; upgrade to 2.12.x; upgrading fixed the corruption — ripienaar (confirmed by asker).

## How do I inspect the contents of a workqueue stream?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4778
- date: 2023-11-09 | asker: vamshiaruru | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): `nats stream view` refuses WorkQueue streams; how to see pending messages and redelivery state?

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Viewing a WorkQueue stream requires `allow_direct` on the stream and a CLI that uses direct gets instead of consumers (top of main in late 2024; error 10099 otherwise) — ripienaar, derekcollison.
- [CONS] Redelivery counts and next-delivery time live in the consumer and are visible only in delivered message metadata, not by inspecting the stream — ripienaar.

## Specializing Websocket connections between read-only and write-only
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2760
- date: 2021-12-26 | asker: dsidirop | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.6
- question (one line): One websocket connection for subscribe and one for publish?

### Claims
- [CLNT][PATTERN] Start with one bidirectional connection; head-of-line blocking is mostly server-to-app on subscriptions, so move latency-sensitive subscriptions to separate connections only if needed — derekcollison.

## Smart-cancellation between competing consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2758
- date: 2021-12-24 | asker: dsidirop | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.6
- question (one line): Does NATS cancel slower responders once the first reply arrives?

### Claims
- [CORE] No automatic cancellation of competing responders; handle in the application — derekcollison.

## How nodes work in a cluster (slow consumers on routes, max_payload, reconnects)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4314
- date: 2023-07-17 | asker: Gutaicheng | answered by: derekcollison, wallyqs, scottf | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Is there buffering/slow-consumer detection between cluster nodes, does max_payload apply to routes, and how does maxReconnects count?

### Claims
- [CORE][OPS] Route/gateway slow consumers are time-based only (pwrite exceeding the write deadline, default 10 s, configurable), not size-based like clients — derekcollison.
- [CORE][OPS] `write_deadline` applies to client, route, leaf and gateway connections; `max_pending` applies only to clients; `max_control_line` to all — wallyqs.
- [CORE] System-originated (routed) messages are not bound by the receiving server's max_payload, by design — derekcollison.
- [OPS] When a route backlog exceeds the write deadline the server closes the route and reconnects — derekcollison.
- [OPS] There is no total memory setting; use cgroups plus `GO_SOFT_MEMLIMIT` (GOMEMLIMIT) as the Helm chart does — derekcollison.
- [CLNT] maxReconnects is per known server and resets on a successful connect; the server-provided list is merged with the bootstrap list — scottf.

## Mirror Stream sync is ~2.9x slower when a Consumer cold-scans the mirror during catch-up
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/8444
- date: 2026-08-10 | asker: cyqsign | answered by: (no maintainer yet) | server version context: 2.14.2
- question (one line): A DeliverAll scanner on a sparse KV-like mirror slows mirror catch-up from 64k to 23k seq/s.

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Mirror catch-up of a sparse (75% holes) 4M-sequence stream: 14.2 s alone vs 41.0 s with a concurrent cold-scan consumer — cyqsign [UNVERIFIED, reproducible package attached].
- [STRM] Hypothesis: a single store-wide RWMutex is shared by the mirror write path and consumer reads, and holes double writer lock acquisitions — gitsult4n [UNVERIFIED, code-reading, non-maintainer].

## Is there performance issues possible with a high cardinality subjects for a stream?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/8333
- date: 2026-06-23 | asker: ashumkin | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.12/2.13
- question (one line): ~1M UUID subjects under `subject.>` in a 10 GB file stream on 3 nodes; problems?

### Claims
- [STRM][SIZE] Many subjects (well beyond a million) are not a performance problem; the cost is RAM for the radix-tree subject index, roughly 100 MB for about 1 million small subjects — jnmoyne. "for something around 1 million subjects it would be in the order of 100 megs of RAM (with small subjects)."

## Is jetstream message count capped at 1 billion for a single stream?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7147
- date: 2025-08-04 | asker: ftong2020 | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.11.7
- question (one line): Messages appeared to be discarded at 1 billion; is there a cap?

### Claims
- [STRM][SIZE] No 1-billion cap: a Limits stream ran past 1.17 billion messages (36 GiB) on 2.11.7 — wallyqs.

## JetStream async publish throughput much lower than documentation example
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7599
- date: 2025-12-02 | asker: sereins | answered by: neilalexander, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10.14 vs 2.12.2
- question (one line): `nats bench js pub async` gives 134k msg/s vs 404k in docs.

### Claims
- [OPS] Docs benchmark numbers come from an M4 MacBook over loopback; physical network latency, bandwidth and file storage dominate elsewhere; run your own bench in your own environment — jnmoyne.
- [OPS] Old servers (2.10.14) should be upgraded before benchmarking — neilalexander.

## Should we use hostPath for jetstream cluster running in K8S
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7749
- date: 2026-01-21 | asker: royatanu94 | answered by: (non-maintainer) | server version context: 2.12
- question (one line): hostPath PVCs for JetStream pods?

### Claims
- [ANTI][OPS] Do not use hostPath: a rescheduled pod lands on a node with no data and forces a full resync; use StatefulSet PVCs with SSD classes (gp3, premium-rwo) as the Helm chart does — MILLERMARRU [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer, matches chart defaults].

## Inquiry on hardcoded stream state flush timeout to 2 minutes
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6683
- date: 2025-03-15 | asker: souravagrawal | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10/2.11
- question (one line): After OOM kill of a single-node WorkQueue, stream state resets; can the 2-minute state flush be tuned?

### Claims
- [OPS] The filestore sync interval is configurable via `jetstream { sync: 1s }` — derekcollison.
- [OPS][ANTI] Lowering sync did not prevent stale stream state after abrupt kill in the asker's test (issue 6600); single-node file streams are exposed to unclean shutdown — souravagrawal [UNVERIFIED].

## kvBuckets are unexpectedly slow (list and compact at 100k keys)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5334
- date: 2024-04-23 | asker: EgusCpp | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.10.7
- question (one line): KV put/delete fine, but `kv ls` and `kv compact` take 30-48 minutes at ~100k keys with 100% CPU.

### Claims
- [KV] KV is optimized for Get, Put, Update, Create, Delete; listing keys is a slow client-side operation and should be rare — ripienaar. "listing keys is not fast and probably something that in typical use cases should not be done that often."
- [KV] KV delete writes a delete marker per key for audit and watch semantics and cannot be turned off; purge of a subject hierarchy is the fast bulk delete — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][KV] Design keys hierarchically so whole subtrees can be purged with wildcards (`$KV.BUCKET.prefix.>`) — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][KV][STRM] When the KV abstraction does not fit, use the underlying stream directly: purge by subject, stream-info subject listing (fast, paged, up to 100k subjects), batched gets in 2.11 — ripienaar.
- [KV][STRM] Thousands or more subjects with one message each is exactly how KV works — ripienaar.
- [CORE][STRM] No responders from a stream publish means the stream is unhealthy; a stream captures messages without any subscriber — ripienaar.

## Subject token limit
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5097
- date: 2024-02-16 | asker: albionb96 | answered by: MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Does "16 tokens max" mean 16 characters per token or 16 dot-separated tokens?

### Claims
- [SUBJ][SIZE] The guidance is 16 dot-separated tokens; not strictly enforced, but performance is guaranteed only up to that — MauriceVanVeen.

## Key Value with TTL (bucket MaxAge vs per-key TTL)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7264
- date: 2025-09-06 | asker: alberk8 | answered by: MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.11.8
- question (one line): Bucket TTL 1m, key TTL 2m; key vanished at 1m. Bug?

### Claims
- [KV][MYTH] Bucket MaxAge takes precedence over a longer per-key TTL; set MaxAge longer than any per-key TTL — MauriceVanVeen.
- [KV] Limit Marker TTL is how long the delete marker created by MaxAge or per-message TTL removal stays around — MauriceVanVeen.

## KV per message TTL event
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6878
- date: 2025-05-08 | asker: alberk8 | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Do watchers see per-message TTL expiry?

### Claims

## Remove deleted/purged data from bucket not possible?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6015
- date: 2024-10-17 | asker: pablitovicente | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): KV delete then purge then compact; bucket never shrinks.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][KV] To reclaim space for keys that will never return, purge the underlying stream with subject filter `$KV.<bucket>.<key path>` — jnmoyne (verified by asker).

## Are there tradeoffs with `AllowDirect: true`?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3984
- date: 2023-03-21 | asker: jgaskins | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Why is AllowDirect off by default outside KV?

### Claims
- [STRM] AllowDirect can be enabled by editing any stream; the maintainer gave no stated tradeoff — derekcollison (first answer retracted as about direct consumers).

## How does compression work?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5259
- date: 2024-03-29 | asker: pmajocha | answered by: derekcollison, ripienaar | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Compressed stream uses 100 GB on disk but reports 626 GB and hits limits; what does compression buy?

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Compression is per block in the filestore; all limits (MaxBytes, account limits, and the server's max_file_store check) apply to raw message bytes, not bytes on disk — derekcollison, ripienaar. "Compression works per block under filestore but we do report raw usage and that is what is used for limits."
- [STRM][MYTH] Belief: compression lets you store more within the server's storage limit. Correction: it saves physical disk for operators only; set `max_file_store` and stream limits in raw terms — derekcollison.

## Prevent a NATS user from creating durable consumers
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5044
- date: 2024-02-06 | asker: pontus-andersson-wowgroup | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Browser clients over websocket with JetStream access; restrict them to ephemeral, subject-filtered consumers.

### Claims
- [SEC][PATTERN] Allow only the extended `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.<stream>.<consumer>.<filter>` subject form and deny the plain `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.<stream>` to constrain consumer filters; subject restriction is easy for push consumers via deliver subject, more involved for pull — derekcollison.
- [SEC][ANTI] The API subject alone does not distinguish durable from ephemeral creation (both use `CONSUMER.CREATE.<stream>.<name>`), so a pure permission rule cannot block durables — 0xeb-bp [UNVERIFIED, protocol trace shown].

- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7679
- date: 2025-12-25 | asker: veilag | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Replace REST with browser NATS clients using auth callout and inbox-only subscribe permissions?

### Claims
- [USECASE][SEC] Many users and customers run NATS as the API layer all the way to the browser with auth callout scoping — derekcollison.

## NATS supercluster server/cluster discovery from client
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7328
- date: 2025-09-17 | asker: NevinDry | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Clients only learn servers of the cluster they connect to, never other clusters of the super-cluster.

### Claims
- [TOPO][CLNT] Server auto-discovery and INFO updates are cluster-scoped; clients never learn other clusters' URLs — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][TOPO] Cross-cluster failover today: two DNS names (primary, DR), client set not to shuffle resolved addresses so it exhausts the primary before falling to DR; no automatic switch-back yet — derekcollison.

## How to find number of subscriptions on jetstream
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6117
- date: 2024-11-13 | asker: YashasAnand | answered by: Jarema | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Core subscribing with queue groups to stream subjects shows no consumers; how many consumers am I creating with 6 same-named consumers?

### Claims
- [ANTI][STRM] Core publishing into a stream subject works but returns no ack and gives no back pressure; use JetStream publish — Jarema.
- [CONS] Consumers are named and unique; creating "6 consumers" with the same name yields one consumer with 6 bound clients, round-robin for pull; 6 distinct consumers each get every message — Jarema.
- [CONS][OPS] Whether many filtered consumers beat one shared consumer depends on subject cardinality and replication; benchmark with `nats bench` — Jarema.

## Jetstream durable queue-group subscription based MaxAckPending
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2799
- date: 2022-01-19 | asker: ccapuano-ssc | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.6/2.7
- question (one line): Push queue-group subscribers want per-subscription MaxAckPending for elastic scaling.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CONS] Scale-out work queues belong on pull consumers, which scale by design with batch size and MaxBatch; long-poll (2.7+) lets push be built on pull — derekcollison. [STALE?] pre-2.10 API shown.

## Understanding jetstream warnings ("high message lag")
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6490
- date: 2025-02-10 | asker: astelmashenko | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9.19
- question (one line): What does "JetStream stream has high message lag" mean?

### Claims
- [OPS][STRM] "high message lag" means publishers send faster than the system can store into the stream, typically from core publishes into a stream or many async JetStream publishers — derekcollison.

## Sync and self-healing problems amongst Stream replicas
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5308
- date: 2024-04-12 | asker: Kawon1 | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.10.x, fix in 2.10.14
- question (one line): Wiping one replica's store causes OOM kills during catch-up under live traffic and "last sequence mismatch".

### Claims
- [OPS] Replica catch-up has no rate limiter and runs as fast as it can — Kawon1 (observed) [UNVERIFIED].
- [OPS] "last sequence mismatch" from replica drift addressed in 2.10.14; use longer startup probes so streams can catch up; recovery may need scaling the stream to R1 on the healthy replica and back — wallyqs.

## Some questions about NATS (Limits vs Interest, pagination, fetch expiry)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7554
- date: 2025-11-15 | asker: wf-soft | answered by: neilalexander, ripienaar, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Why can't a Limits stream delete on ack; how to paginate a stream; can fetch expiry be under 1 s?

### Claims
- [STRM] Interest retention removes a message when all interested (filter-matching) consumers ack; with no interested consumers the publisher still gets a PubAck but the message is dropped and the sequence skipped — neilalexander.
- [STRM][PATTERN] Paginate a stream with the message get API combining sequence and batch size — neilalexander.
- [OPS] Stream/consumer info calls have server-side cost; do not poll them often to check existence — neilalexander.
- [CONS] Push and pull consumers deliver identical metadata (stream, consumer, sequences, pending) via the ack reply subject — ripienaar.
- [CLNT] Fetch max wait below 1 s is allowed by the server; a floor is a client-library limitation — jnmoyne.

## Recording Connection & Disconnection events (100k clients)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6445
- date: 2025-02-03 | asker: msaboor35 | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10.25 / 2.11
- question (one line): Track online/offline for 100k clients via `$SYS.ACCOUNT.*.CONNECT/DISCONNECT`; events arrive late or never.

### Claims
- [PATTERN][KV] Presence via KV: clients put a key with TTL; TTL expiry reported to watchers landed on main for 2.11 — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][SEC] Export `$SYS.ACCOUNT.*.CONNECT/DISCONNECT` to another account and capture them in a no-ack stream to avoid duplicate processing; events are core NATS before capture so loss is possible — borjaetxebarria [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer].

## NATS Task Scheduler
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5733
- date: 2024-08-01 | asker: tamis-laan | answered by: (community) | server version context: 2.10 (scheduler shipped in 2.12)
- question (one line): Native delayed message scheduling?

### Claims
- [STRM] Native message scheduling arrived in 2.12 (see 7628); before that choria-io/asyncjobs (Go) was the community option — thread. [STALE?]

## Event Synchronization with NATS (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/970
- date: 2022-05-04 | asker: beatrausch | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.8 (partition mapping introduced)
- question (one line): Kafka-style partition-key ordering so all events for an order land on one consumer; does NATS support that?

### Claims
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Since 2.8, subject mapping can insert a partition token computed by deterministic hashing of one or more subject tokens; partitioning is administrative (count changeable dynamically) and invisible to publishers — jnmoyne.
- [STRM][MYTH] Kafka partitions one topic by an app-provided key; NATS splits a subject space into partitions and creates one stream per partition, with the key being part of the subject — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] To scale strictly ordered consumption: one stream on `foo.bar.*` with one durable consumer per partition (`foo.bar.0`, `foo.bar.1`...). Only when a single stream's write throughput is exceeded create one stream per partition — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Elasticity without repartitioning: treat the partition count as the maximum number of consumers you will ever need and redistribute partitions over the present members when membership changes — jnmoyne.

## Client struggles with 400+ concurrent ordered consumers (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1981
- date: 2025-12-12 | asker: ramasauskas | answered by: wallyqs, derekcollison | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): ~500 ordered ephemeral consumers on one connection; connection resets with broken pipe; fine at 100.

### Claims
- [CLNT][SIZE] Many ordered consumers on one connection instantly request more than the server's 64 MB default `max_pending` per client, so the connection is closed as a slow consumer — wallyqs. "By default the server will allocate up to 64 MB of pending data to be flushed to a client"
- [OPS] Raising `max_pending` (e.g. 512 MiB) fixes it but every connection may then hold that much; size server memory for the worst case — wallyqs.
- [PATTERN][CLNT] Spread ordered consumers across multiple connections, about 100 per connection — derekcollison.

## Can I use JetStream KV as cache? (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1507
- date: 2023-12-25 | asker: tzq0301 | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): KV as a Redis-style cache benchmarked slower than no cache; wrong usage?

### Claims
- [KV][SIZE] Loopback benchmark: NATS KV sync get ~24,000 ops/s (about 41.7 us) vs Redis ~18 us on an M1 Ultra; over a real LAN the network RTT dominates and the difference becomes insignificant — jnmoyne.
- [KV] KV "can be on par with Redis when there is a real network"; enable direct get; use KV watchers to keep a local subset hot — derekcollison (disagreeing with ripienaar's "not optimised as a very fast cache").
- [KV][PATTERN] Sync KV get/put throughput is RTT bound (~16k/s single client); parallel clients or async batches scale it (10 clients ~43-54k/s, 25 clients ~55-66k/s); batched direct gets reach hundreds of thousands/s and are served by all replicas — jnmoyne.
- [KV][STRM] File vs memory KV: if the block is cached, file get is ~50 us like memory; an uncached block costs a couple of milliseconds — jnmoyne.
- [KV] NATS is a few percent faster than Redis on writes and a few percent slower on cached reads in the maintainer's testing — jnmoyne.

## OrderedConsumer Usage (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1736
- date: 2024-11-12 | asker: arhoads | answered by: Jarema | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Need durable in-order consumption; is OrderedConsumer required?

### Claims
- [CONS] Ordered consumer is a client-side construct: ephemeral no-ack consumer with client-side sequence tracking and recreation on gaps; meant for fast one-off passes — Jarema.
- [CONS] For long-lived ordered processing, a durable consumer with MaxAckPending=1 is all you need — Jarema.

## Ephemeral Consumer Cleanup Rate? (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1534
- date: 2024-01-25 | asker: alexang-zh | answered by: derekcollison, ripienaar | server version context: 2.10.3 to 2.10.9
- question (one line): One ephemeral consumer per API call at high RPS (>1M consumers accumulating) to fetch a user's last 100 messages.

### Claims
- [ANTI][CONS] Creating and discarding consumers at API-call rate "will not really work well"; use message get APIs (batched direct get, ADR-31 batches) instead — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][STRM][KV] Streams are optimized for the tail, not random access; compact per-entity history into one key with rollups (as KV does) — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][CONS] If a consumer is needed to read history, make it R1 memory-backed, or use an ordered consumer (R1, flow controlled); or walk with NextFor by start sequence — derekcollison.
- [PATTERN][STRM] JetStream publish returns an ack via request/response without any consumer; for loop-back results use one long-lived wildcard consumer or Republish plus a core subscription — Jarema.

## Prevent data loss in lame duck mode (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1376
- date: 2023-08-25 | asker: ritmas | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9/2.10
- question (one line): A publish during a server's lame-duck transition fails with EOF and the message is lost; best practice?

### Claims
- [CLNT][PATTERN] Reconnects are automatic; clients do not retry a publish that failed mid-reconnect, so retries belong in the app; for latency-critical requests use multiple responders and take the fastest reply — derekcollison.
- [CLNT] "Intelligent reconnect" reacting proactively to the LDM signal was promised for end of 2023 and as of 2024-05 was "not released or started" — derekcollison. [STALE?]

## Multiple instances of the same durable pull consumer (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1223
- date: 2023-02-28 | asker: kamikazechaser | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Autoscaled pods sharing one durable pull consumer?

### Claims
- [PATTERN][CONS] JetStream is partition-less: any number of app instances bind to the same durable and messages are distributed automatically, add or remove at any time, regardless of cluster size — jnmoyne.

## Sourcing streams between hub and leaf instances, both directions (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1495
- date: 2023-12-14 | asker: cbrake | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Bidirectional hub/leaf sourcing duplicates messages after leaf restart.

### Claims
- [ANTI][STRM][TOPO] If the sourcing stream also lists the same subjects as the origin, and core traffic flows across the leaf link, both streams capture the message directly and the source adds it again, duplicating — jnmoyne. Fix: sourcing stream has no `subjects`, only `sources` with a filter — cbrake (verified).
- [STRM][TOPO] After a leaf reconnect, sourced messages published during the outage arrived in about 6 s — cbrake [UNVERIFIED, observed].

## How to create queue group consumer with new jetstream api (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1687
- date: 2024-07-27 | asker: gudron | answered by: Jarema, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): New API has no push/queue-group consumers; how to load balance and fan out?

### Claims
- [CONS] The new JetStream API is built on pull consumers; a pull consumer load-balances across all subscriptions bound to it, so queue groups are unnecessary — Jarema.
- [CONS] Push and pull are two APIs over the same server construct differing in back pressure (flow control vs message requests); pull handles back pressure much better; new features (overflow, priority groups, pinning) are pull-only — Jarema.
- [CONS] The only missing old-API feature is "push consumer without a queue group", which is almost never needed; performance is equivalent or better — jnmoyne.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Fan-out with persistence: one consumer per receiving application; work-queue semantics: one durable with many workers — Jarema, jnmoyne.
- [CONS][STRM] A WorkQueue stream may have many durable consumers as long as their subject filters do not overlap — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][CLNT] `BackOff` overrides `AckWait`: the first backoff value becomes the effective ack wait — eau-u4f (verified), jnmoyne.

## Queued pull consumers with WorkQueue retention (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/963
- date: 2022-04-24 | asker: bounoable | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.7/2.8
- question (one line): Event bus wants several services each with their own consumer on the same subjects under WorkQueue retention.

### Claims
- [STRM][CONS] WorkQueue binds a stream to single-consumer semantics per subject; bind many pull subscribers to that consumer for scale. For multiple mutually exclusive consumers on the same subjects use Interest retention — derekcollison.

## Aggregate KV? (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/2015
- date: 2026-02-02 | asker: uli42 | answered by: jnmoyne | server version context: 2.11/2.12
- question (one line): Central KV that sources from two mirrored site KVs stays empty.

### Claims
- [KV][PATTERN] Aggregating KV buckets requires a subject transform per source (`$KV.A.>` to `$KV.C.>`) because the bucket name is part of the key subject — jnmoyne.
- [KV][ANTI] When the source is itself a mirror, the transform source must use the ORIGIN bucket's subject prefix (`$KV.kv1.>`), not the mirror bucket's name; the CLI's automatic transform used the mirror name and yielded nothing — uli42 (verified fix).
- [KV][STRM] Mirroring and sourcing propagate only new messages, never deletes — jnmoyne.

## Jetstream kv store - Prefix search / Wildcard search (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/957
- date: 2022-04-13 | asker: codeKrowe | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.7 to 2.10
- question (one line): Prefix or wildcard key lookup in KV?

### Claims
- [KV][SUBJ][PATTERN] Use `.` in keys so they become subject tokens; then wildcard filters on watchers/consumers give prefix search; a watch with key ranges is the same idea — derekcollison.
- [KV][SIZE] A wildcard watch over 3M keys took ~400 ms for 10 matches on 2.9.16 because the per-block subject state was a map; a sublist/patricia tree was planned for 2.10 — HeavyHorst (measured), derekcollison. [STALE?]

## Why are push consumers not implemented? (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1721
- date: 2024-09-26 | asker: c3mb0 | answered by: Jarema, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Batch-for-10-seconds-then-ack workload is throttled by pull consumer flow control; need push?

### Claims
- [CONS] Push would not help: MaxAckPending applies to both; use `FetchNoWait`/fetch with high message limit and a 10 s expiry, or `Consume` for sustained flow — Jarema.
- [CONS][SIZE] Set MaxAckPending greater than fetch batch size times number of fetching clients, or some fetches get partial batches — jnmoyne.
- [CONS] Ordered consumers get messages fast with reliable ordered delivery without explicit acks — jnmoyne.
- [CLNT] Old JetStream API is not being deprecated, but overflow, priority groups and pinning land only in the new pull-based API — Jarema.

## load balancing in a queue group (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1499
- date: 2023-12-16 | asker: jaijiv | answered by: derekcollison, Jarema | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Core queue groups distribute randomly; can I get round robin?

### Claims
- [CORE][CONS] Core queue groups are random; JetStream pull consumers round-robin across fetches — derekcollison, Jarema.
- [CORE] Request/reply over JetStream is "something we are considering"; do it yourself with a reply subject in a header or payload — Jarema.

## Auto deletion of inactive durable consumers (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/924
- date: 2022-03-11 | asker: beatrausch | answered by: bruth, derekcollison | server version context: 2.7 to 2.10
- question (one line): Delete durable consumers after N months of inactivity?

### Claims
- [CONS] Consumer state is small; idle durables cost little. Inactivity can be detected from the consumer's delivered `Last` time — bruth.
- [CONS] `InactiveThreshold` applies to durable consumers too (later servers); for pull it means no pull requests in the window, for push no binding — derekcollison.

## FetchBatch bug with large RTT (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1683
- date: 2024-07-19 | asker: ashumkin | answered by: piotrpio | server version context: nats.go 1.36
- question (one line): `nats: timeout` from FetchBatch when RTT is ~100 ms.

### Claims
- [CLNT] The client's internal fetch timeout must exceed the pull expiry by an RTT-dependent margin; the 10 ms margin was too small and was increased (PR 1689); very high RTTs can still hit it — piotrpio.

## Trigger client reconnect on discovering a new cluster node (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1509
- date: 2023-12-27 | asker: YanKawaYu | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): New nodes get no traffic until clients reconnect.

### Claims
- [OPS][CLNT] Connect to the closest cluster (lowest RTT); rebalancing is done by a system user kicking clients (`nats server request kick`), to be wrapped in a CLI auto-rebalance over time — derekcollison.

## Need help in understanding MaxAckPending behaviour (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/969
- date: 2022-05-04 | asker: apmcodes | answered by: kozlovic, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.8
- question (one line): Do NAK'd messages with a 4-hour delay count toward MaxAckPending?

### Claims
- [CONS] NAK resets AckWait; the message stays delivered-but-unacked and counts toward MaxAckPending for the whole delay — kozlovic.
- [ANTI][CONS] Many long NAKs indicate a design problem; move such messages to a different stream rather than inflating MaxAckPending — kozlovic.
- [PATTERN][CONS] Prefer pull consumers with a very high MaxAckPending and let `Fetch(n)` per client provide flow control (10 clients x Fetch(100) = 1000 in flight) — jnmoyne.

## How to get notifications for expiry of keys in KV (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1629
- date: 2024-05-09 | asker: UltraNemesis | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.10 (planned 2.11/2.12)
- question (one line): Watchers don't report key expiry.

### Claims
- [KV] Expiry notifications were unsupported in 2.10 and planned for 2.11/2.12 (shipped as marker TTLs in 2.11) — ripienaar. [STALE?]

## How to resume fetching messages after restart (nats.go)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go/discussions/1199
- date: 2023-01-27 | asker: dvaldivia | answered by: piotrpio | server version context: 2.9.6
- question (one line): Durable pull consumer shows pending messages but delivers nothing after app restart.

### Claims
- [CONS][CLNT] A durable pull consumer resumes after the last acked message; PullSubscribe looks up the stream by subject (subjects cannot overlap across streams); BindStream skips that round trip — piotrpio.
- [ANTI][CONS] Unacked messages with MaxAckPending 10 and AckWait 1 h block delivery of the next messages after restart — zerlok (root cause of a similar report) [UNVERIFIED, plausible].

## k8s: OOM killed when using JetStream WorkQueue on cpu:1 and mem:1GB machines (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/5739
- date: 2024-08-02 | asker: kohlisid | answered by: neilalexander, ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10.18
- question (one line): 3-node R3 WorkQueue cluster on 1 CPU / 1 GiB pods with 64 MiB max_payload OOMs; how to size memory?

### Claims
- [OPS][SIZE] JetStream `Max Memory` limits memory-storage streams only, not the server's working memory — ripienaar. "The `Max Memory` shown does not limit how much memory NATS uses."
- [OPS][SIZE] "I wouldn't run nats with below 3GB memory when using Jetstream"; large payloads make it worse — ripienaar.
- [OPS] Set GOMEMLIMIT to ~75% of the container limit; the Go runtime may see host memory and not GC before the kernel OOM-kills — derekcollison.
- [OPS][SIZE] Memory need is dynamic (connections, subscriptions, streams, consumers, access patterns); model the upper bound on a larger system and watch RSS peaks; website memory guidance "is definitely wrong" — derekcollison, ripienaar.
- [OPS] A server-wide cap on filestore buffer memory was planned "probably in 2.12" — derekcollison.
- [ANTI][OPS] A 64 MiB max_payload (default 1 MB) drove large allocations; bring it back down and use Object store for large blobs — neilalexander.
- [OPS] Memory spikes with Limits streams looked like a build-up of Raft append entries — neilalexander.

## Cluster size scalability question (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/3533
- date: 2022-10-09 | asker: melaraj2 | answered by: derekcollison, ripienaar, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.9 to 2.11
- question (one line): Docs mention a "recommended cluster size"; can a 10-server cluster hold R3 streams, and are partitioned streams planned?

### Claims
- [TOPO][SIZE] Clusters can be any size; if they get too big, use a super-cluster of many clusters, as NGS does — derekcollison. "if they get too big we might recommend a super cluster (many clusters). This is how we setup NGS ourselves."
- [TOPO] R5 makes little sense where cloud providers have only 3 AZs — derekcollison.
- [STRM] Segmented streams remain "on the fuzzy roadmap"; 2.11's new filestore targets petabyte scale; TB streams are fine with reasonable subject cardinality and interior deletes — derekcollison (2024-01).
- [SUBJ][OPS] Partition count changes without server reload: account JWT mappings in operator mode, or per-stream subject transforms since 2.10 — derekcollison, ripienaar, jnmoyne.
- [ANTI][KV][STRM] One KV or stream per customer is "ultimately not a good design pattern"; 33,931 streams took over 10 minutes to restart on 48 CPUs because restore was serial; prefer few buckets with millions of hierarchical keys and per-user permissions on `$JS.API` subjects — jnmoyne, williamstein (measured).
- [KV][PATTERN] Keys can be multi-token, so many users fit in one KV under `uuid.>` with permissions — derekcollison.

## Message Group / Sequential Convoy pattern (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/2043
- date: 2021-03-27 | asker: stepin | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison, jnmoyne, bruth | server version context: 2.2 through 2.11
- question (one line): Process messages in parallel except those sharing a key (order ID), which must be sequential; Kafka-style key partitioning?

### Claims
- [CONS] Pulling a message gives a lock on it for AckWait — ripienaar.
- [SUBJ][PATTERN] Deterministic subject token partitioning (2.8): `"neworders.*" : "neworders.{{wildcard(1)}}.{{partition(3,1)}}"`; hashing tends toward balanced distribution; composite keys via `{{partition(10,1,2)}}` — jnmoyne.
- [CONS][MYTH] JetStream has no consumer groups or rebalancing; a JetStream "consumer" is like a Kafka partition and a JetStream "subscriber" is like a Kafka consumer; container orchestration provides worker elasticity — jnmoyne. "a 'consumer' in JetStream is like a 'partition' in Kafka and a 'subscriber' in JetStream is like a 'consumer' in Kafka."
- [PATTERN][CONS] Multiple workers on one MaxAckPending=1 partition consumer give HA with strict order: only one message in flight, but a worker can die or roll without losing the partition — bruth, jnmoyne.
- [CONS] MaxAckPending and MaxWaiting are independent: MaxWaiting=1 limits outstanding pull requests, MaxAckPending limits in-flight messages; MaxAckPending=1 returns only one message per pull — jnmoyne.
- [CONS] Elastic consumer groups shipped in Orbit.go in 2025-05 (static and elastic flavors), requiring 2.11 pinned consumers — jnmoyne.

## Cannot use Subscribe when ephemeral consumers reach ~30,000 (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/4841
- date: 2023-12-04 | asker: VuongUranus | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.9.21 / 2.10.6
- question (one line): 20-50k ephemeral consumers created and abandoned continuously on an R3 memory stream; "Consumer assignment not cleaned up" and context deadline errors.

### Claims
- [OPS] "Consumer assignment ... not cleaned up, retrying" means the meta leader is not cleaning up an inactive consumer deleted by another server; a known issue fixed in 2.9.24/2.10.6 — derekcollison.
- [ANTI][CONS] Creating and abandoning tens of thousands of consumers continuously prompted an architecture-review recommendation rather than a tuning fix — derekcollison.

## NATS server panics when creating many consumers (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/4831
- date: 2023-11-30 | asker: aimichelle | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10.5
- question (one line): 4 streams x 4096 partition consumers (16k R3 consumers) on 1.5 CPU / 7.5 GiB pods panics and times out.

### Claims
- [SIZE][CONS] 16k R3 consumers are "alot of HA assets": each is a complete Raft group; heartbeats alone would be ~16k msgs/sec plus memory — derekcollison. "Heartbeats alone would be ~16k msgs/sec not to mention the memory footprint."

## Jetstream: transactional batch publish messages (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/2384
- date: 2021-07-29 | asker: sloveridge | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.3 (atomic batch publish shipped later in 2.12)
- question (one line): All-or-nothing multi-message publish across subjects in one stream?

### Claims
- [STRM][CLNT] Async publish (track PubAcks asynchronously, bounded outstanding) is the throughput path; async publishes preserve order — derekcollison.
- [STRM] Full transactional semantics "would need quite a bit of work" (2021); users were pointed at async publish and saga-style decomposition — derekcollison. [STALE?] (atomic batch publish exists in 2.12+)
- [PATTERN][USECASE] Alternative: publish the whole order as one message and have a listener fan out idempotently to per-part subjects, acking the parent last — tpihl [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer, endorsed in discussion].

## Include payload in term advisories (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/5049
- date: 2024-02-08 | asker: ripienaar | answered by: ripienaar, neilalexander | server version context: 2.10 to 2.14
- question (one line): Put the original payload in MAX_DELIVERIES/term advisories to build a DLQ?

### Claims
- [ANTI][CONS] Parked because of data-leakage feedback; blanket publishing of payloads "wouldn't help or work for many" — ripienaar.
- [CONS] DLQ is per consumer, not per stream, because streams deliver the same message to many consumers; consumers can be ephemeral or single-use, so DLQ design is application-specific — ripienaar. "you need a DLQ per consumer not per stream."
- [PATTERN][CONS] Consume the advisories in real time, fetch the message by sequence for reprocessing; WorkQueue streams keep messages that were not successfully processed; set MaxAge to your operational window — ripienaar.

## Subject mapping partition distribution (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/3660
- date: 2022-11-22 | asker: OpenGuidou | answered by: jnmoyne, ripienaar | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): `foo.*.*` mapped with `{{partition(4,1)}}` puts everything in one partition.

### Claims
- [SUBJ][MYTH] `partition(N, tokens...)` hashes only the listed wildcard tokens; a constant token maps every message to one partition. Use `{{partition(4,1,2)}}` for a composite key — jnmoyne.
- [OPS] Test mappings offline with `nats server mapping` — ripienaar.

## JetStream HA when part of a 2-cluster super-cluster goes down (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/4502
- date: 2023-09-07 | asker: donghoang89 | answered by: ripienaar, wallyqs | server version context: 2.8.4
- question (one line): Two EKS clusters joined by gateways; losing one stops JetStream.

### Claims
- [TOPO] HA needs an odd number of nodes and an odd number of clusters; with two clusters any split leaves no majority. "3 clusters minimum." — ripienaar.
- [OPS][TOPO] For cross-cluster gateways on Kubernetes use node ports with static names, external DNS, or an L4 load balancer with static IPs per pod — ripienaar, wallyqs.

## JetStream pre-allocates memory reservations based on max_bytes (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/6993
- date: 2025-06-19 | asker: vCillusion | answered by: neilalexander | server version context: 2.10.18
- question (one line): 100 memory streams with 128 MB max_bytes fail after four with "insufficient resources" on a 512 MB memory store.

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Stream `max_bytes` is reserved against the server's JetStream store limits at creation; over-committing reservations is intentionally unsupported — neilalexander.

## Invalidate deduplication window after ack (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/5142
- date: 2024-02-28 | asker: ro0NL | answered by: ripienaar, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Messages with the same Msg-Id are still deduped after the first was acked; can acking clear the window?

### Claims
- [STRM] Dedup exists to protect publish retries when the ack was lost; acked messages must still be deduped; Msg-Id must be unique per event (UUID), not per entity — ripienaar. "This feature exist to ensure that ... the server got the message but the ack got lost - does not result in a duplicate message."
- [PATTERN][STRM] Exactly-once-ish job intake: an audit (Limits) stream with the "infinite deduplication window" technique (per-subject DiscardNew, max 1 per subject) feeding a WorkQueue stream by source — jnmoyne.

## Ability to reset consumer start sequence (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/4121
- date: 2023-05-02 | asker: bruth | answered by: ripienaar, jnmoyne, neilalexander | server version context: 2.9 to 2.11
- question (one line): Event sourcing needs to rebuild projections by resetting a durable consumer to the start.

### Claims
- [CONS] Start options are used once at creation; resetting means blowing away consumer state, so delete and recreate with the same name — ripienaar.
- [CLNT][OPS] Expect consumer info and metadata fetches to fail at any time; production JetStream client code needs retries and backoff — ripienaar.
- [CONS][STRM] On Interest retention, deleting and recreating a consumer signals no interest and can lose messages; a native reset would be safer — neilalexander.

## Decouple the dios disk-IO semaphore from GOMAXPROCS (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8434
- date: 2026-07-30 | asker: michal-billtech | answered by: (closed) | server version context: 2.14.2
- question (one line): Filestore IO concurrency is min(16, max(4, GOMAXPROCS)); on network storage Raft vote fsyncs serialize and elections fail.

### Claims
- [OPS][SIZE] In 2.14.2 filestore disk-IO concurrency is sized from GOMAXPROCS: min(16, max(4, cores)), or half the cores above 32; every Raft vote does an O_SYNC write plus directory fsync through that semaphore — michal-billtech [UNVERIFIED, cites filestore.go]. (A "disk io setting" to tune was later referenced by wallyqs for 2.14.6 in discussion 7863.)

## MQTT support should be horizontally scalable (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/3116
- date: 2022-05-11 | asker: ianzhang1988 | answered by: kozlovic, derekcollison | server version context: 2.8
- question (one line): MQTT uses one `$MQTT_msgs` stream with R3 and thousands of consumers; 250k connections; can it scale out?

### Claims
- [SIZE][CONS] Horizontal scalability is limited by the number of Raft groups (one per stream or consumer); many consumers make Raft traffic exceed data traffic — kozlovic. "the more consumers you have, the more basic RAFT traffic will increase, potentially more than actual data flow."
- [PATTERN][SUBJ] Reduce consumer count by subscribing with wildcards (`foo/+`) and dispatching on the token — kozlovic.
- [CONS] `mqtt { stream_replicas: 5, consumer_replicas: 1 }` lets consumers be R1 under an R5 stream; consumer leaders spread across servers — kozlovic.
- [ANTI][OPS] "I would not recommend having 250k R3 consumers"; make them R1; do not use Ceph, use direct-attached or block storage like EBS — derekcollison.
- [OPS] Check file-descriptor limits (`ulimit`) when a cluster disables JetStream under load — derekcollison.
- [CONS] Consumers cannot span multiple streams — kozlovic.

## WorkQueue messages not deleted on non-leader nodes when used as mirror source (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/5450
- date: 2024-05-19 | asker: qiongzhu | answered by: derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10.14 / 2.11
- question (one line): Mirroring from a WorkQueue stream leaves inconsistent history across replicas.

### Claims
- [ANTI][STRM] Removing from one stream never affects a source or mirror; sourcing from a WorkQueue is by design not a supported use — derekcollison, jnmoyne. "Work queue stream exist in order to provide exactly once consumption ... not really to be sourced from."

## Messages stop being delivered from a WorkQueue stream (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/4736
- date: 2023-11-02 | asker: hpdobrica | answered by: Jarema, neilalexander, wallyqs | server version context: 2.9.22 to 2.10.26
- question (one line): Consumer on a WorkQueue stream stops after bursts; recreate fixes for minutes.

### Claims
- [OPS] Dozens of WQ and consumer reliability fixes landed through 2.10.25/2.10.26 (PR 6526); upgrade before reporting — neilalexander, wallyqs.
- [CONS] A consumer sequence advancing on a single message means it is being redelivered without ack; check client acking — Jarema.

## Frequent leader elections (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/7101
- date: 2025-07-24 | asker: dan-j | answered by: MauriceVanVeen, wallyqs | server version context: 2.10/2.11
- question (one line): 5-node cluster across 3 zones logs ~10 consumer leader elections every 5 minutes.

### Claims
- [OPS] "new consumer leader" lines for `oc_`-prefixed consumers are ephemeral R1 KV watchers being created, not real elections; 2.11.5 stopped logging them — MauriceVanVeen, wallyqs.

## k8s: Falling behind in health check, JetStream not current with meta leader (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/5976
- date: 2024-10-08 | asker: a-alinichenko | answered by: derekcollison, wallyqs | server version context: 2.10.21 / 2.11
- question (one line): Every restart, pods fail readiness with "JetStream is not current with the meta leader".

### Claims
- [OPS] On 2.10 change the readiness probe from `js-server-only` to `/` or `js-enabled-only` so the k8s service does not detach under heavy meta activity; 2.11 made the probe less sensitive — wallyqs.
- [OPS] `nats traffic` under the system account shows JS API operations per second — derekcollison.

## How to remove "offline" / inaccessible streams (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/6760
- date: 2025-04-03 | asker: tommyjcarpenter | answered by: derekcollison, ripienaar | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): Streams show as inaccessible, delete fails with "stream is offline (10118)".

### Claims
- [OPS] JetStream remembers server membership; new servers auto-join but departed peers must be removed manually with `nats server cluster peer-remove`, then delete orphaned streams with `-f` — derekcollison.
- [OPS] Inaccessible streams stop responding to server requests while thought reachable; the server should time out faster — ripienaar.

## KV performance issues in 2.10.7 (issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/4930
- date: 2024-01-09 | asker: pcsegal | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10.7 / 2.10.8
- question (one line): 250 goroutines/s doing KV get+update on one connection degrade to multi-second latency.

### Claims
- [CLNT][PATTERN] Use multiple connections for high-rate KV clients; a single connection can suffer head-of-line blocking from the server — derekcollison.

## Headers on KV entries (ADR issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/278
- date: 2024-04-23 | asker: cjohansen | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.10/2.11
- question (one line): Can a client put custom headers on KV entries, and will the KV API support headers or structured values?

### Claims
- [KV] KV does not support headers; KV is deliberately a small abstraction over streams that removes features; when needs do not fit, use streams — ripienaar. "KV is inherently about limitations ... Adding to it removes from its purpose."
- [KV][PATTERN] Structs are planned to be stored as one key per field (`123.name`, `123.age`); without transactions or batch writes, partial failures are the crux — ripienaar.
- [KV][SIZE] Real customers have multi-thousand-key structs; batch reads are point-in-time atomic even when paged — ripienaar.
- [KV][TOPO] KV buckets can be mirrored or sourced with subject transforms; master-master replication is not supported in general — ripienaar.

## ObjectStore questions (ADR issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/144
- date: 2022-08-11 | asker: aricart | answered by: scottf, aricart | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Object store metadata, links, deletes and chunk subject layout.

### Claims
- [OBJ] Object meta lives at `$O.<bucket>.M.<name-encoded>`, chunks at `$O.<bucket>.C.<nuid>`; deleted objects keep a tombstone meta; links reference bucket + name — scottf, aricart.
- [OBJ][SEC] Chunk subjects keyed by nuid mean cross-account exports cannot clamp access to one object — aricart.
- [OBJ] Optimization: a single-chunk object can be fetched with last-message-by-subject instead of a subscription — scottf.

## Message Ack Behavior (ADR issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/72
- date: 2021-11-22 | asker: scottf | answered by: kozlovic, aricart | server version context: 2.6
- question (one line): Unify repeat-ack and auto-ack behavior across clients.

### Claims
- [CLNT][CONS] Decision (ADR-15): repeat acks are a client no-op after a terminal ack (ACK/TERM/NAK) to save traffic; auto-ack happens after the callback returns, WPI inside the callback is allowed — kozlovic, aricart.

## Pull request MaxBytes and status handling (ADR issues 112 and 116)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/116
- date: 2022-06-06 | asker: scottf | answered by: derekcollison, aricart, kozlovic, wallyqs | server version context: 2.8/2.9
- question (one line): Which pull statuses are terminal and how should clients treat 408/409 and MaxBytes?

### Claims
- [CLNT][CONS] Pull responses use HTTP-like status codes and cannot abandon them; a message larger than the pull's max_bytes returns "409 Message Size Exceeds MaxBytes" (changed from 408) and stalls the pull — derekcollison, aricart.
- [CLNT][CONS] Pull requests stay publish-based rather than request/reply because request/reply breaks cross-account imports/exports — wallyqs, derekcollison.
- [CLNT][CONS] "409 Exceeded MaxWaiting" is transient (retry later); other 409s (consumer deleted, push based, limits exceeded) are terminal — aricart, derekcollison.
- [CLNT] 2.10 adds "409 Batch Completed" with Nats-Pending-Messages/Nats-Pending-Bytes headers (also on 408) so clients can size the next pull — Jarema (ADR issue 212).

## Consumer and Stream Name Validation (ADR issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/152
- date: 2022-09-14 | asker: aricart | answered by: ripienaar, scottf, Jarema | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): What characters are legal in stream, consumer and bucket names?

### Claims
- [OPS][STRM] Stream, durable, consumer and account names are "filename-safe" (printable except `.`, `*`, `>`, `/`, `\`, max 255 chars); KV and Object bucket names are restricted to A-Z a-z 0-9 dash underscore (ADR-6) — scottf.
- [ANTI][CONS] A space in a consumer name broke consumer creation with a cryptic error after a client upgrade — Jarema.

## KeyValue atomic delete and purge (ADR issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/271
- date: 2024-02-29 | asker: davidmcote | answered by: ripienaar, scottf, aricart | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): CAS-guarded delete/purge in KV?

### Claims
- [KV][PATTERN] KV delete/purge can be made atomic by sending `KV-Operation: DEL` with `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence: <revision>`; clients were asked to expose it everywhere — davidmcote (verified), ripienaar.

## More Robust Autoconfiguration/Service Discovery (ADR issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/issues/367
- date: 2025-08-19 | asker: nf-brentsaner | answered by: ripienaar | server version context: 2.11
- question (one line): SRV-record based server discovery with priorities and weights?

### Claims
- [CLNT][OPS] Clients will get a pluggable discovery interface with implementations in Orbit repos rather than built-in SRV support — ripienaar.

## JetStream cluster no metadata leader (k8s issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/k8s/issues/438
- date: 2022-02-23 | asker: skyrain | answered by: caleblloyd, wallyqs | server version context: helm chart 0.x
- question (one line): Enabling JetStream on an existing Helm cluster loops on "no metadata leader".

### Claims
- [OPS] The healthz probe fails until JetStream has quorum; enabling JetStream on a running StatefulSet upgrades one pod at a time so the first JS pod has no quorum; disable the startup/healthz check once during that upgrade — caleblloyd, wallyqs.
- [OPS] The chart needs working cluster DNS for StatefulSet stable network IDs (routes resolve `pod.svc.ns.svc.cluster.local`) — caleblloyd.

## Can not enable JetStream + Cluster when using Helm chart (k8s issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/k8s/issues/846
- date: 2023-12-14 | asker: marcel-vester | answered by: caleblloyd | server version context: chart 1.1.5
- question (one line): Cluster with JetStream and TLS fails; server_name empty.

### Claims
- [OPS] Do not set `config.cluster.merge.routes` in values; the chart sets routes automatically; override only non-default values — caleblloyd.

## Helm: store.file.path on NFS (k8s issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/k8s/issues/58
- date: 2020-05-13 | asker: samstride | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: STAN (pre-JetStream)
- question (one line): STAN file store on NFS via Helm.

### Claims
- [STALE?][OPS] STAN fault-tolerance mode required a shared ReadWriteMany filesystem with no replication; superseded by JetStream Raft replication — wallyqs.

## Config reload not supported for JetStream max memory and store (k8s issue)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/k8s/issues/311
- date: 2021-08-27 | asker: wallyqs | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.x through 2.12
- question (one line): HUP reload fails with "config reload not supported for jetstream dynamic max memory and store".

### Claims
- [OPS] JetStream store limits cannot be hot-reloaded; on Helm use the config checksum annotation to force a restart on config change — wallyqs.

## Subscribe to LEAFNODE.CONNECT and LEAFNODE.DISCONNECT events
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5902
- date: 2024-09-18 | asker: ZarkoRunjevac | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10.21
- question (one line): How to observe leaf node connect/disconnect from the hub?

### Claims
- [OPS][TOPO] From the system account subscribe to `$SYS.ACCOUNT.*.CONNECT` for all connection types (third token is the account) or `$SYS.ACCOUNT.*.LEAFNODE.>` for leaf nodes only; verified against Synadia Cloud — derekcollison.
- [OPS] Synadia Cloud server tags include cloud, cluster, country, geo, region, zone, pool, index, stack; a real-world placement-tag vocabulary — server advisory payload in thread.

## Fending off DoS attacks by auto-revoking auth keys
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/2783
- date: 2022-01-13 | asker: dsidirop | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.7
- question (one line): 100k accounts; can NATS auto-revoke a misbehaving account's credentials?

### Claims
- [SEC] No auto-revoke; contain abuse with server `max_connections`, per-account `limits { max_connections, max_payload }` and user permissions — derekcollison.
- [SEC][PATTERN] Keep the server-wide connection max higher than the sum of account maxes so an admin connection can still get in during an attack — derekcollison.

## Support S3 API for JetStream / S3 next level
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5486
- date: 2024-06-05 | asker: khalil-omer | answered by: derekcollison | server version context: 2.10 (planned 2.12+)
- question (one line): S3 as the durability layer with disks as caches (WarpStream style)?

### Claims
- [STRM][OPS] Synadia is considering "virtual blocks" to offload filestore blocks to S3 when not needed locally; timeframe "2.12 though" — derekcollison. [STALE?] (not shipped by 2.14 per later threads)
- [USECASE] The S3 offload/parquet sharing proposal (6478) has 42 upvotes with no maintainer commitment — thread evidence.

## How can I schedule message?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/7490
- date: 2025-10-29 | asker: sheldygg | answered by: MauriceVanVeen | server version context: 2.12
- question (one line): With `Nats-Schedule` the consumer receives the schedule message itself; bug?

### Claims
- [STRM] Message scheduling (ADR-51) stores the schedule message in the same stream (`--allow-schedules`); the target message is published to `Nats-Schedule-Target` after the delay, so consumers see both — MauriceVanVeen.

## KeyValue Revision is bucket wide? (per-key history)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/3466
- date: 2022-09-12 | asker: andrea-tomassi | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.9
- question (one line): Revision numbers are bucket-wide; how to fetch the n-1 value of one key?

### Claims
- [KV] Revision is a bucket-wide stream sequence; per-key revision "will be very hard in our current storage model"; history is optimized for gets, not history walks — ripienaar.
- [KV][OPS] A bucket's history can be raised after creation by editing the underlying stream — ripienaar.
- [PATTERN][KV] Pull a key's history with a lightweight R1 memory consumer filtered by subject and optionally start time — derekcollison.

## Doesn't NakWithDelay reduce the MaxAckPending counter?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4972
- date: 2024-01-18 | asker: AlexandrTQ | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Ten NakWithDelay(1m) messages exhaust MaxAckPending=10 and block the consumer.

### Claims
- [CONS] Any delivered message awaiting retry counts as pending because MaxAckPending is also used to manage ordering; the only option is to raise MaxAckPending — ripienaar.
- [CONS] Maintainers disagreed whether delayed NAKs should count; noted NAK already violates observed ordering — derekcollison (open design point).

## Can you provide a js.PublishBatch function?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5458
- date: 2024-05-21 | asker: yuzhou-nj | answered by: ripienaar, derekcollison | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Sync publish caps at ~1000 msg/s; batch publish API?

### Claims
- [STRM][CLNT] Sync JetStream publish is RTT bound (~1000/s at 1 ms RTT); batch publishing was planned "in a future version" (arrived as atomic batch publish in 2.12) — ripienaar. [STALE?]

## Removing records from KV that exceed the limit (LRU-style)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6418
- date: 2025-01-28 | asker: SergioWhite | answered by: derekcollison, jnmoyne | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Keep only the newest 100 keys in a bucket?

### Claims
- [KV][STRM] `MaxMsgsPerSubject` (KV history) caps versions per key; `MaxMsgs` with DiscardOld caps total messages in the bucket's stream; both can be set together — jnmoyne.
- [KV][ANTI] KV delete markers are messages too and may be the ones evicted by MaxMsgs; use the stream directly or `stream.purge` on the KV stream if that matters — jnmoyne.

## Increasing in message delivery delay
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/6822
- date: 2025-04-23 | asker: 1995parham | answered by: wallyqs | server version context: 2.10/2.11
- question (one line): Pull consumer delivery latency grows over time on an R3 stream.

### Claims
- [OPS] A consumer leader reading from a replica that is continuously catching up causes rising delivery delay; check with `nats server stream-check --expected N` and `nats server consumer-check --expected N` — wallyqs.

## Clarification for Ack Sequence
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5737
- date: 2024-08-01 | asker: kohlisid | answered by: derekcollison, ripienaar | server version context: 2.10
- question (one line): Why do consumer and stream sequences differ?

### Claims
- [CONS] Stream sequence is the stable message index; consumer sequence increments by one per delivery, so a redelivery has the same stream sequence, a new consumer sequence and NumDelivered=2 — derekcollison.
- [CONS][OPS] "Redelivered" counts in consumer info are server-lifetime counters; consumer state persists across restarts but the counter resets — derekcollison.
- [CONS] With a filter subject the two sequences never move in lock step; treat them as unrelated — ripienaar.

## How to troubleshoot messages not picked up by consumer (stuck WorkQueue message)
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/4928
- date: 2024-01-08 | asker: yonigibbs | answered by: derekcollison, scottf, wallyqs, neilalexander | server version context: 2.10.7 to 2.10.14
- question (one line): After a simulated JVM crash with NAKs mid-fetch, one message stays stuck until the consumer is recreated.

### Claims
- [CONS] If MaxDeliver is hit the ack floor moves past the message and an advisory is sent — derekcollison.
- [OPS] The stuck-message-after-crash bug was fixed in 2.10.14 (PR 5227) — wallyqs.
- [CONS][OPS] A consumer reporting sequences ahead of the stream is stalled; that happens when the stream's first/last sequence reset (store_dir wiped, e.g. `/tmp`); `sync: always` in the jetstream block can help durability on abrupt kills — neilalexander.
- [CLNT] Old-style Java fetch blocks until the batch is collected, skewing ack-wait timing; the simplified API delivers as messages arrive — scottf.
- [OPS] Deleting consumers to unstick them is considered a bug to report, not a procedure — neilalexander.

## What is the exact meaning of "Unprocessed Messages" in consumer info?
- url: https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/discussions/5994
- date: 2024-10-11 | asker: fmontorsi-equinix | answered by: ripienaar, Jarema | server version context: 2.10.16
- question (one line): What does Unprocessed mean and why does small MaxWaiting hurt throughput?

### Claims
- [CONS] Unprocessed = messages the consumer has never attempted to deliver — ripienaar.
- [CONS][SIZE] `MaxWaiting` caps outstanding pull requests; each `Consume()` client keeps 1-2 pulls pending, so MaxWaiting of 10 throttles 10 clients; the default 512 is there for a reason — Jarema.

## Coverage

- Threads read and captured: 165 (nats-server discussions, nats.go discussions, nats-server issues, nats-architecture-and-design issues, nats-io/k8s issues). nats.js has discussions disabled (verified via GraphQL `hasDiscussionsEnabled: false`), so nats.js was covered through the ADR repo instead.
- Queries run: 75 GraphQL discussion searches on nats-io/nats-server (all terms in the brief plus 34 gap-fillers such as "queue group", "R1 R3", "fsync", "nvme/iops", "availability zone", "GOMEMLIMIT", "number of subjects", "wildcard", "message ttl", "compression", "async publish", "max_msgs_per_subject", "auth callout", "MQTT", "kv watch", "large messages", "latency", "long polling", "million connections", "hub spoke", "network partition", "object store size", "kv bucket per", "websocket browser", "consumer R1 memory", "interest overlap", "durability", "gateway interest", "per subject limit", "batch/atomic publish", "priority groups", "counters"); 10 on nats.go; 5 on nats.js (empty); 16 `gh search issues` on nats-server; 6 on nats-architecture-and-design; 6 on nats-io/k8s. Total 118 queries.
- Total claims: 469.

### The 15 most valuable maintainer statements for designing a large NATS system
1. "In our global clusters we limit servers, at the moment, to 2k HA Assets" (replicated streams+consumers per server); use muxed streams with filtered consumers rather than many streams — derekcollison (5128).
2. Shard streams so no stream has more than ~20K consumers; consumer create rates above ~2K/s per cluster are a known limit; monitor raftz WAL growth; cap ~200K consumers per cluster or use R1 memory consumers — wallyqs (7863).
3. Each replicated consumer is a full Raft group; 16k R3 consumers means ~16k heartbeat msgs/s before any data; "I would not recommend having 250k R3 consumers", make them R1 — derekcollison (4831, 3116).
4. A single R3 stream does ~250k msgs/s with proper hardware; sync publishes are bounded by leader-to-fastest-follower RTT (10 ms RTT = ~1000/s per sync publisher); async publish batches AppendEntries — derekcollison (3495, 5551).
5. A stream lives in exactly one cluster; a super-cluster needs at least 3 clusters (odd count) for meta quorum; a stretch cluster tolerates ~100-150 ms RTT max and is a last resort — ripienaar (4961, 4502, 5317).
6. Imbalanced or poorly connected regions: run one hub cluster and connect other regions as leaf nodes with their own JS domains; leaf nodes that never talk east-west should share one cluster name to stop interest-graph propagation — jnmoyne, derekcollison (7438, 5974).
7. Edge fleets: cloud side uses muxed streams holding N fleet nodes in fixed-capacity "cells"; never a 1:1 cloud stream per fleet member; stream sources are editable at any time and have no hard limit — derekcollison, jnmoyne (5889).
8. A Kafka partition, not a topic, equals a NATS stream; partition with `{{partition(N,tokens)}}` subject mapping (account level for multiple streams, per-stream transform for consumers); one stream per subject is rarely right, split only for different retention — derekcollison, jnmoyne, Jarema (6315, 6437, 6100).
9. Strict per-key order needs MaxAckPending=1 (one message at a time); parallelize with one consumer per partition or Orbit partitioned consumer groups (2.11 pinned consumers); a NAK counts as outstanding so order holds — jnmoyne, ripienaar (7296, 3908, 5211).
10. Subject cardinality costs RAM for the radix index (~100 MB per million small subjects) but not throughput; "It's rarely a good idea" to have one KV or stream per customer: 33,931 streams took over 10 minutes to restart — jnmoyne (8333, 3533).
11. Server sizing: at least 4 cores and 16 GB with SSD for JetStream; not below 3 GB memory; GOMEMLIMIT at ~75% of the container limit; JetStream `max_memory` is store reservation, not process memory; limits and disk accounting apply to raw (uncompressed) bytes — wallyqs, ripienaar, derekcollison (6397, 5739, 5259).
12. Leaf-node origin streams for hub sourcing should use Limits retention with MaxAge equal to the longest expected outage plus MaxBytes; Interest and WorkQueue there can lose or leak messages; sourcing from a WorkQueue is unsupported by design — derekcollison, jnmoyne (4694, 5450).
13. KV is a deliberately limited abstraction over streams: no headers, bucket-wide revisions, slow key listing, delete markers count as messages, MaxAge overrides per-key TTL; when it does not fit, use the stream directly (purge by subject, direct gets, transforms for aggregation) — ripienaar, MauriceVanVeen, jnmoyne (278, 5334, 7264, 2015).
14. Payloads: 1 MB default, 8 MB the practical ceiling ("don't come and complain" above it), 64 MB hard cap; 2-3 MB is a good rule; Object store for large blobs; a client's pending buffer is 64 MB by default before slow-consumer disconnect — jnmoyne, ripienaar, neilalexander, wallyqs (7068, 6320, 6501, 1981).
15. Operations: always stop with lame duck (USR2) or restarts re-scan all blocks; JetStream store limits need a restart not a HUP; departed peers must be removed manually; client discovery is cluster-scoped so cross-cluster DR needs DNS ordering; avoid Fargate and Ceph, prefer EC2-class hosts with direct-attached or EBS block storage — wallyqs, derekcollison, ripienaar (7681, 8001, 6760, 7328, 7738, 3116).
