- Underneath, NATS is a pub/sub engine with a high-performance subject router; queuing and request-reply are built on it, and multiple queue groups plus plain subscribers can coexist on one subject. "Underneath the covers it is a pub sub engine with an extremely high performance routing mechanism." (~19:24)
- NATS is not an enterprise messaging system: no persistence, transactions, enhanced delivery models, or store-and-forward; it is trivial to build those on top. "It's really not a queuing product per se, it's not a store and forward mechanism." (~21:26)
- Distributed queuing works across the cluster: queue group members can attach to any server, unlike early EMS where you had to attach to the queue's home server. "You can attach to any server you want... and it just works." (~24:30)
- The protocol is text-based by choice; Derek and Redis' author agree computers are fast enough that text framing does not matter for performance. "Computers are so fast I don't think text-based matters anymore and that's actually the truth." (~24:30)
- Subscription IDs are per-connection closures: `SUB foo 1` then `SUB foo bar 3` joins queue group bar; publishing delivers one copy to the plain sub and one to a single member of the group. "You see that we got two messages... one was for one, one was for two." (~31:50)
- The ping interval exists because cloud hosts vanish without the socket closing; either side can initiate pings so dead peers are detected. "In cloud platforms a lot of times that happens... the machine just goes away but nobody that's connected to the socket thinks they did." (~35:54)
- Auto-pruning of the interest graph: `UNSUB <sid> <max>` sets a circuit breaker propagated across the cluster, so a requester of 10,000 responders receives maybe 6–7 replies instead of discarding all 10,000 client-side. "Your client library might see six, seven, maybe... most messaging platforms you have to throw away all 10,000 on the client." (~36:55)
- The interest graph flows toward subscribers and data flows the reverse way; the server tracks delivered counts so an UNSUB-after-N takes effect exactly. "The interest graph flows towards me, data flows in the reverse way." (~39:01)
- Once the byte count on PUB is read, the server is in binary mode for exactly that many bytes and never inspects the payload. "Once it hits that it's in binary mode... I don't look inside of the payload whatsoever." (~51:23)

## STRM: Streams: layout, retention, limits, replication, storage (1565 claims)


**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — What is NATS**

- For at-least-once / exactly-once, persistent streaming, de-coupled flow control, and Key/Value, use JetStream, which is built into the server "but needs to be enabled".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Compare NATS**

- NATS persistence: memory and file; "Messages can be replayed by time, count, or sequence number, and durable subscriptions are supported." Rabbit: queue semantics, "no message replay is available".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Security (concept)**

- JetStream provides encryption at rest.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — NATS Adaptive Deployment Architectures**

- JetStream on leaf nodes: local streams mirrored to global streams upstream; "mirroring is store and forward and therefore can recover from connectivity outages".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Core NATS**

- Core NATS is best-effort at-most-once; JetStream adds at-least-once and exactly-once.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Queue Groups**

- "Stream as a queue": use `WorkQueuePolicy` retention with pull consumers for horizontal scaling, "or using an explicit ack push consumer with a queue group of subscribers" [STALE? push-consumer guidance].

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream (concept overview)**

- JetStream captures messages and replays them; "Unlike NATS Core which requires you to have an active subscription to process messages as they happen".
- With a cluster of JetStream-enabled servers "you can enable data replication and thus guard against failures".
- Design goals: easy to configure/operate/observe; secure with NATS 2.0 security; horizontally scalable at high ingestion rate; self-healing; payload agnostic; "must not have third party dependencies".
- Traditional temporal decoupling is imperfect: "durable subscribers need to be created before the messages get published"; "queues are meant for workload distribution and consumption, not to be used as a mechanism for message replay."
- JetStream provides both consume-as-published (queueing) and replay-on-demand (streaming).
- Stream limits: max message age, max total bytes, max message count, max individual message size, max number of consumers.
- Discard policy is mandatory: discard old deletes oldest; discard new rejects and "the JetStream publish call returns an error indicating that a limit was reached".
- Retention: `limits` (default, replay); `work queue` (removed as consumed, "exactly-once consumption"); `interest` (kept while consumers haven't delivered it). "regardless of the retention policy selected, the limits (and the discard policy) always apply."
- Storage: memory or file; replication 1 (none), 2, or 3 "for Fault Tolerance" (contradicts R=5 max stated later on same page and in streams.md).
- JetStream uses "a NATS optimized RAFT distributed quorum algorithm" with immediate consistency, not eventual consistency.
- Writes are formally Linearizable; reads are in essence serializable (single global order, controllable via compare-and-publish); no atomic batching of multiple operations.
- Monotonic writes/reads guaranteed, but "We don't guarantee read your writes at this time, as reads through direct get requests may be served by followers or mirrors." Send gets to the stream leader for more consistent results.
- Storage (Stream) is configured separately from consumption (Consumers).
- Replication guidance: "Replicas=1 - Cannot operate during an outage of the server servicing the stream. Highly performant." "Replicas=2 - No significant benefit at this time. We recommend using Replicas=3 instead." "Replicas=3 - Can tolerate the loss of one server ... An ideal balance". "Replicas=4 - No significant benefit over Replicas=3 except marginally in a 5 node cluster." "Replicas=5 - Can tolerate simultaneous loss of two servers ... at the expense of performance."
- "Rather than defaulting to the maximum, we suggest selecting the best option based on the use case behind the stream." Typical: file-based R=3; easily rebuilt/temporary streams can be memory R=1; R=5 is the replication factor limit.
- Mirrors between JetStream domains offer disaster recovery; a stream can source from one or more streams.
- File streams flush writes to the OS synchronously but by default do not fsync immediately; `sync_interval` default is 2 minutes; "The data will be fsync-ed no later than this interval."
- Non-replicated: an OS failure (power loss, not just process kill) may lose acknowledged messages. Replicated: acknowledged after quorum, but simultaneous OS failures before fsync can lose recently acked messages; a data-losing server may rejoin and "form a new majority with nodes that have never received or persisted a given message".
- `sync_interval: always` fsyncs after every message before ack; "combined with replication in different data centers or availability zones, provides the strongest durability guarantees but at the slowest performance." It has a server-wide performance impact.
- Defaults chosen for "a typical production deployment scenario across multiple availability zones"; divergence for an R3 stream across 3 AZs needs a specific 5-step chain of failures.
- Mitigation: don't auto-restart an OS-failed server until a majority has the new writes, or peer-remove it and re-admit as a wiped peer to recover over the network.
- Hybrid durability: add a dedicated cluster with `server_tags: ["sync:always"]` and `jetstream { sync_interval: always }`, then `nats stream add --replicas 3 --tag sync:always` for only the streams that need it.
- Flow control is decoupled, per client-server link, not end-to-end; publishers aren't limited to the slowest consumer. JetStream publish can be sync or async ("batched").
- Base QoS is at-least-once: rare failures make a publisher wrongly believe a publish failed and republish, or lose a consumer ack causing redelivery, leading to "perceived 'message duplication' at the application level".
- Exactly-once = publisher attaches a unique message ID header tracked by the server "for a configurable rolling period of time" plus a double-acknowledgment on the consumer side.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Streams**

- Streams capture normal NATS subjects; plain publish gives unacknowledged delivery; "it's better to use the JetStream publish calls instead as the JetStream server will reply with an acknowledgement".
- "Relatively speaking the Stream is the most resource consuming component so being able to combine related data in this manner is important to consider." e.g. store all `ORDERS.*` in one stream and consume subsets; a stream may also add `SHIPPING.state`.
- Deduplication uses the `Nats-Msg-Id` header within a sliding window.
- Stream names must be unique per account and cannot contain whitespace, `.`, `*`, `>`, path separators, or non-printable characters.
- Replicas max is 5. MaxAge and DuplicateWindow are in nanoseconds. MaxConsumers `-1` = unlimited. MaxMsgSize counts payload plus headers.
- NoAck (default false) is "mandatory when archiving messages which have a reply subject set. E.g. requests in an Request/Reply communication"; otherwise JetStream replies with an empty ack on the reply subject.
- Not editable after creation: Name, Storage, MaxConsumers, Retention, DenyDelete, DenyPurge, FirstSeq, AllowMsgCounter. Mirror became editable in 2.12.0. Sealed can be set once. AllowMsgTTL and AllowMsgSchedules can only be enabled.
- Version introductions: MaxMsgsPerSubject 2.3.0; Sealed/DenyDelete/DenyPurge/AllowRollup 2.6.2; RePublish 2.8.3; AllowDirect/MirrorDirect/DiscardNewPerSubject 2.9.0; Metadata/Compression(s2)/FirstSeq/SubjectTransform/ConsumerLimits 2.10.0; AllowMsgTTL/SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL 2.11.0; AllowAtomicPublish/AllowMsgCounter/AllowMsgSchedules 2.12.0; AllowBatchPublish 2.14.0.
- AllowDirect: with more than one replica "each replica will respond to direct get requests ... not only the leader." MirrorDirect lets a mirror serve direct gets for the origin.
- DiscardNewPerSubject requires DiscardNew and MaxMsgsPerSubject.
- Compression is file-storage only; options: none or `s2` (Snappy).
- Storage default is `File`.
- A mirror cannot have subjects. Default subject = stream name. Removing a subject from a stream doesn't remove stored messages; overlapping consumers still see them.
- LimitsPolicy: whichever of MaxMsgs/MaxBytes/MaxAge/MaxMsgsPerSubject is hit first deletes messages.
- WorkQueuePolicy: FIFO, each message consumed once, enforced by "only allowing one consumer to be created per subject" (filters must not overlap); message deleted once acked.
- InterestPolicy with zero consumers deletes messages immediately: "consumers need to be bound to the stream ahead of messages being published"; deleted once acked by all consumers filtering on the subject.
- Limits still apply under Interest/WorkQueue: with MaxMsgs and default discard old, "messages will be automatically deleted even if the consumer did not receive them."
- Interest streams may defer deleting messages after the last interested consumer is removed "until those messages reach the start of the stream", for performance.
- In WorkQueue streams, messages that hit the consumer's `MaxDeliver` "will remain in the stream and must be manually deleted via the JetStream API."
- DiscardOld is default; DiscardNew rejects new messages that would exceed a limit; discard applies only if at least one limit is defined.
- Placement: "A given stream, including all replicas (not mirrors), are bound to a single cluster." Default: created in the cluster the client is connected to "assuming it has sufficient storage available."
- Explicit placement is useful "to co-locate with the most active clients (publishers or consumers) or may be required for data sovereignty reasons."
- Placement by cluster requires every server to set `cluster { name }`; super-cluster clusters must have distinct names.
- Tags (`server_tags`, e.g. `cloud:aws`, `region:us-east1`, `az:a`) plus `jetstream.unique_tag: "az"` force replicas onto servers with different tag values (one replica per AZ). Cluster and tags can be combined.
- Sources/mirrors replicate asynchronously and may have their own retention, replication, and storage; changes to the copy don't affect the origin.
- "We suggest to use Sources in new configurations." For a read-only replica: configure the stream without listen subjects, or disable listen subjects via client authorizations.
- Sources aggregate one or more streams plus direct client writes into "a single interleaved stream", with subject transform and filtering.
- A mirror sources exactly one stream; clients cannot publish to it, but messages can be deleted on demand and consumers work normally.
- AllowRollup + `Nats-Rollup: all|sub` purges prior messages; "A common use case for rollup is for state snapshots".
- RePublish: "For high scale needs where, currently, a dedicated consumer may add too much overhead, clients can establish a core NATS subscription to the destination subject". Fields Source (default `>`), Destination, HeadersOnly (adds `Nats-Msg-Size`). Reply subject is removed on republished messages even with no-ack.
- SubjectTransform rewrites the subject before storing.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Headers**

- "`Nats-` is a reserved namespace. Please use a different prefix for your own headers."
- Publish headers: `Nats-Msg-Id` (dedup within Duplicate Window, 2.2.0); `Nats-Expected-Stream`; `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` and `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence` (stream-level optimistic concurrency); `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence` (2.3.1, subject-level); `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence-Subject` (2.11, wildcard subject to check against); `Nats-Rollup` (2.6.2, `all`/`sub`, wildcards "will result in undefined behavior"); `Nats-TTL` (2.11, go duration, requires stream flag).
- Republish/direct-get headers set by server: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Subject`, `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Last-Sequence` (2.8.3), `Nats-Time-Stamp`, `Nats-Num-Pending` (2.10.0), `Nats-UpTo-Sequence` (2.11.0). "Do not set these headers on client published messages."
- `Nats-Stream-Source` on sourced messages holds origin stream (with domain hash if cross-domain), original sequence, filters, transforms, original subject; "parse conservatively".
- Scheduler (2.12, repeating in 2.14, ADR-51): `Nats-Schedule` (`@at ...`, crontab, `@hourly`, `@every 5m`), `Nats-Schedule-Target` must differ from schedule subject, `Nats-Schedule-TTL`, `Nats-Schedule-Rollup`, `Nats-Schedule-Source` (2.14, no wildcards), `Nats-Schedule-Time-Zone` (default UTC).
- Atomic batch publish (2.12, ADR-50): `Nats-Batch-Id` (<=64 chars), `Nats-Batch-Sequence` from 1, `Nats-Batch-Commit` `1` or `eob` (2.14); other value terminates the batch.
- Fast-ingest (2.14) is selected by reply subject ending `.$FI`, can combine with dedup headers, "MUST NOT be combined with atomic batch publish."
- Internal: `Nats-Required-Api-Level` (2.12; servers >= 2.11 error if unsupported), `Nats-Request-Info` on cross-account messages, `Nats-Marker-Reason` (`MaxAge|Remove|Purge`, 2.11, ADR-48), `Nats-Incr` KV counters (2.12, ADR-49), `Nats-Counter-Sources`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Example configuration (ORDERS)**

- ORDERS pipeline: one stream for `ORDERS.*`; pull consumers NEW (`ORDERS.received`) and DISPATCH (`ORDERS.processed`) with explicit ack scale horizontally as work queues; each stage publishes the next message back into the same stream; a MONITOR push consumer with ack none gets all messages.
- Example: `--max-age=1y --storage file --retention limits --max-msgs=-1 --max-bytes=-1 --max-msg-size=-1 --discard=old`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Source and Mirror Streams**

- Source/mirror "are designed to be robust and will recover from a loss of connection. They are suitable for geographic distribution over high latency and unreliable connections." Even a leaf node connecting "every few days" still syncs.
- Another use case: connecting streams cross-account.
- Options: Name, StartSeq, StartTime, FilterSubject (not with SubjectTransforms), SubjectTransforms (multiple, disjoint subjects while keeping order; not with FilterSubject), Domain ("commonly used in a hub cluster and leafnode topology").
- "Deletes in the origin stream are NOT replicated through a source or mirror agreement."
- "All configurations are made on the receiving side"; origin needs no config; no cleanup on origin if receiver disappears.
- One stream can be origin for many streams: "fan out topologies where data needs to be distributed reliable to a large number (up to millions) of client connections."
- Leaf nodes and domains supported via the API prefix.
- "Sourcing messages does not retain sequence numbers. But it retain the in stream sequence of messages. Between streams sourced to the same target, the sequence of messages is undefined."
- "Mirrored messages retains the sequence numbers and timestamps of the origin stream." Mirrors + MirrorDirect can be used "for (geographic) load distribution".
- Source/mirror are one-way replication, not full sync; "Quickly deleting messages after publishing them may result in inconsistent replication due to the asynchronous nature".
- Recovery interval after a disconnect is 10-20s.
- Mirror/source agreements "do not create a visible consumer in the origin stream" (before 2.14 behavior; see below).
- Sourcing from WorkQueue/Interest streams supported since 2.14 with a visible durable consumer; before 2.14 it is "not supported ... the behavior is undefined" though not forbidden.
- 2.14 "bring your own" sourcing consumer (`Consumer.Name`, `Consumer.DeliverSubject`) must use `AckFlowControl`; useful for monitoring or "when you're not in control of 'the other side' ... from a security point of view."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Source and Mirror configuration example**

- "Streams with source and mirror configurations are best managed through a client API"; from CLI use a JSON config (`nats stream add --config`).
- Cross-domain source/mirror uses `external.api: "$JS.domainA.API"` with empty `deliver`.
- Example shows `duplicate_window: 120000000000` ns (2 minutes).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream walkthrough**

- CLI defaults when creating a stream: storage file, replication 1, retention limits, discard old, all limits -1 (unlimited), duplicate window 2m0s, rollups no, deletion allowed, purge allowed, "Direct Get: true".
- A Core NATS subscriber only receives messages published after it started; replaying history requires a consumer.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Subject Mapping and Transforms**

- Deterministic partitioning keeps per-subject order while scaling: insert a partition token in the stream's subject transform, then a consumer per partition via subject filters.
- At extreme publish rates "a single nats-server process is acting as the RAFT leader (coordinator) for any given stream and can therefore become a limiting factor"; partition into several smaller streams so leaders spread across JetStream servers.
- In mirror/source/republish, transforms are filters (non-matching ignored); the stream-level `subject_transform` only rewrites matches and leaves others untouched.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Clustering**

- "Clustering in JetStream is required for a highly available and scalable system." It uses a NATS-optimized RAFT that combines the data plane for replication with consensus messages.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Administration (cluster)**

- When choosing replicas "we suggest 1, 3 or 5". Replica count can be edited after creation.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream on Leaf Nodes (domains)**

- Leaf nodes can "provide a local NATS network even when the connection to a hub or the cloud is down"; JetStream supports this via "independent JetStream islands" (domains).
- `domain` in the jetstream block disambiguates which JetStream answers `$JS.API.>`; the API is also exposed as `$JS.<domain>.API.>`.
- When `domain` is set, JetStream traffic on the system account and `$JS.API.>` traffic are suppressed across the leaf link, so clients use the local JetStream; other domains are reached via `$JS.<domain>.API`.
- Each domain is an independent namespace: the same stream name may exist in different domains within one account.
- Regular message flow is not restricted by domains: if streams in two domains (same account) subscribe to the same subject, both store the message while the leaf link is up. Avoid with different subjects, different accounts, or isolated accounts.
- Known issue: with more than one JetStream-enabled leaf in a different cluster, the connected cluster also needs JetStream enabled and a domain set. Known issue: extending a central JetStream (leaf without domain) requires the central JetStream to be clustered.
- "If you want to connect a leaf to the hub and get commands, even when the leaf node connection is offline, mirroring a stream located in the hub is the way to go."
- "if you want to aggregate streams located in any number of leaf nodes use source ... it is recommended to aggregate them in the hub for processing via source."
- Source/mirror copy data so access "is independent of the leaf node connection being online" and avoid a custom program: "This is the recommended way to exchange persistent data across domains."
- Cross-account JetStream import renames `$JS.hub.API` to e.g. `JS.acc@hub.API`; "the general recommendation is to export the domain specific API `$JS.<domain>.API` as this allows you to pin the export to a particular domain."
- "Known issue: Currently, across accounts, push consumer are not supported."
- Minimum cross-account exports for source/mirror: `$JS.<domain>.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.*` (service, response_type stream), a delivery stream `deliver.<acc>.<domain>.>`, and `$JS.FC.<stream>.<consumer>.>`; for client pull consumers add `$JS.<domain>.API.CONSUMER.MSG.NEXT.<stream>.<consumer>` and `$JS.ACK.<stream>.<consumer>.>`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Configuring JetStream (resource management)**

- JetStream is compatible with NATS 2.0 multi-tenancy: "fully isolated JetStream environments for different accounts."
- "JetStream environments in leaf nodes should be isolated in their own JetStream domain".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Configuration (server config reference)**

- "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."
- "each JetStream enabled server MUST use its own individual storage directory"; "JetStream does not implement standby and fault tolerance through a shared file system"; shared directories: "Access conflicts are not detected. We do not recommend such a setup."
- JetStream server defaults: `store_dir /tmp/nats/jetstream`, `max_memory_store` 75% of available memory, `max_file_store 1TB`, `max_outstanding_catchup 64MB` (2.9.0), `max_buffered_msgs 10.000` and `max_buffered_size 128MB` (2.11.0, OOM protection during write bursts), `request_queue_limit 10.000` (2.11.0), `sync_interval 2m` (2.10.0), `strict true` (2.11.0).
- `domain` (2.2.3): "Isolates the JetStream cluster to the local cluster. Recommended use with leaf nodes."
- `extension_hint` (2.2.3) `no_extend`/`will_extend` only matters when the system account is shared between leaf and hub: a standalone leaf extending the hub domain needs `will_extend`; a leaf cluster with a different domain should set `no_extend` or "JetStream will NOT become ready on first startup until the hub can be connected." Only matters at initial start.
- Encryption at rest: `cipher` `chacha`/`chachapoly` or `aes` (2.3.0); key of at least 32 bytes recommended; `prev_encryption_key` (2.10.0) for rotation. TPM-based encryption (2.11.0) with `keys_file`, `encryption_password`, `pcr` default 22.
- `sync_interval`: "By default JetStream relies on stream replication in the cluster to guarantee data is available after an OS crash. If you run JetStream without replication or with a replication of just 2 you may want to shorten the fsync/sync interval." `always` "will slow down the throughput to a few hundred msg/s."
- `unique_tag` (2.8.0) "MUST be the same across all nodes in a cluster AND supercluster"; with `az` tags an R3 stream lands in all three AZs.
- `cluster_traffic` (2.11.0): `system` (default; all replication/RAFT traffic in the system account, as in all prior versions) or `owner` (traffic in the stream's own account).
- Server-wide `limits`: `max_ack_pending`, `max_ha_assets` (RAFT assets per node; not counting R1), `max_request_batch` ("Use with caution. May break existing clients"), `duplicate_window` (max allowed; "default for new streams is 120s").

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Multi Tenancy using Accounts**

- Cross-account JetStream: "in most use cases people want a setup where a stream in one account is mirrored or sourced in another account ... as this is a more 'locked-down' way to share messages", rather than letting apps use a stream in another account directly. References synadia-labs/cross-account-jetstream-sourcing (static security, "probably the best one to start with") and jetstream-leaf-nodes-demo (operator mode).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Administration (CLI intro), Account Information**

- "JetStream is fully usable by only using core NATS" commands (`nats pub`/`nats sub`).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Naming Streams, Consumers, and Accounts**

- Stream, consumer (durable) and account names appear in both the JetStream subject namespace and the filesystem, so they must follow subject rules and be file-system friendly.
- Guidelines: alphanumeric; no spaces/tabs/`.`/`>`/`*`; no path separators; "keep names under 32 characters"; avoid reserved file names (NUL, LPT1); "some file systems are case insensitive so do not use stream or account names that would collide" (`Foo` vs `foo` on Windows/macOS).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Data Replication (mirrors/sources admin)**

- Tiered example: ORDERS and RETURNS are memory-based, short-retention, R3; ARCHIVE sources both, file-based, long retention, R3, and accepts direct publishes; REPORT mirrors ARCHIVE, unclustered (R1), one-month retention, no listen subjects.
- A mirror copies from exactly one stream, "as far as possible IDs and ordering will match exactly the source"; a mirror has no listen subjects; a stream with a mirror cannot also have sources; mirrors support filter, start sequence, start time.
- With sources "We can therefore not maintain absolute ordering, but data from 1 single source will be in the correct order but mixed in with other streams"; timestamps may appear out of order.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Disaster Recovery**

- "For R1 streams, data is persisted on one server node only. If that server node is unrecoverable then recovery from backup is the sole option."
- Automatic recovery conditions: stream is R3 or greater; remaining replicas meet quorum floor(R/2)+1; a free node exists in the stream's cluster; impacted nodes are peer-removed from the meta group.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Encryption at Rest**

- "although encryption at rest by the NATS server is fully supported, we recommend using file system encryption where available" because it is throughput-optimized, adds no server burden, and removes secret management from NATS.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Streams / Consumers (JetStream admin CLI walkthrough)**

- `nats pub` to a stream subject is unacknowledged; `nats req` shows the `+OK` publish ack "if you want to be sure your messages got to JetStream and were persisted."
- After `nats str purge`, sequence numbers keep advancing (FirstSeq 1,000,001 / LastSeq 1,000,000 in example), i.e. purge does not reset sequences.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Monitoring (endpoints reference)**

- `/jsz`: "If you're in a clustered environment, it is recommended to retrieve the information from the stream's leader in order to get the most accurate and up-to-date data" (`leader-only=true`); `raft=true` includes RAFT details.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Running**

- JetStream default store is /tmp; "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Installing (hardware requirements)**

- JetStream minimums (file storage, R3 on 3 nodes, pull consumers): 1 core / 32 MiB for 1,000 msg/s; 1 core / 64 MiB for 10,000 msg/s; 3 nodes 1 core / 256 MiB for 100,000 msg/s. "these are minimum configurations".
- "For production deployment of JetStream, we recommend starting with at least 4 CPU cores and 8 GiB of memory".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — MQTT**

- "For an MQTT client to connect to the NATS server, the user's account must be JetStream enabled" because sessions and retained messages (even QoS 0) are persisted.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Anatomy of a NATS Client Application**

- JetStream contexts are lightweight: "while it is safe to share a JS context between threads, for best performance do not be afraid to have a context per thread."
- Two stream use cases: temporal decoupling (replay) and queuing (distributed work queue).
- "Streams can be (and often are) administratively defined ahead of time".
- Core publish to a stream subject is stored but unacknowledged; "you will get higher quality of service by publishing using the JetStream Context's publish call" because it is acknowledged after storage; hence sync and async variants.
- At-least-once corner cases: double publication, ack loss, or crash after processing before ack; dedup plus double-ack give exactly-once.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Developing with JetStream**

- "Using streaming and its associated higher qualities of service is the facet of messaging with the highest cost in terms of compute and storage."
- Streaming is ideal when: producers/consumers are highly decoupled and may be online at different times; a historical record/replay is required; the last message is needed for initialization while the producer may be offline; consumers are unknown a priori "This is often a false assumption"; data outlives the application; consumers need their own pace; decoupled flow control; exactly-once.
- "no assumptions should ever be made of who will receive and process data in the future, or for what purpose."
- Core publish to a stream subject is stored, "but that's not really the intent ... look at it more as a convenience that you can use to help ease the migration ... rather the desired end state or ideal design."
- JetStream publish acks mean the publisher "can safely discard any state it has for that publication"; sync and async both imply flow control; exactly-once needs a unique publication ID header.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Concepts (functionalities)**

- Retention: `WorkQueue` deletes as consumed; `Limits` provides on-demand individual or distributed replay from the beginning or a point in time.
- Mirror/source topology example: a short-retention capture stream feeds "any number of other streams configured for message consumption in a queue" so consumers work "without impacting that original stream and at their own pace."
- JetStream at-least-once/exactly-once make clients "automatically recover from getting disconnected ... without any message loss"; for slow consumers "the 'buffering' of the messages ... happen in a stream (which can be much larger than a server buffer)".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Getting Started / Using Source**

- Default store is /tmp; "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Model Deep Dive**

- WorkQueuePolicy: "you can not have any overlapping consumers defined on the Stream - each subject captured by the stream can only have one consumer at a time".
- MaxMsgs/MaxBytes/MaxAge "apply as upper bounds" in every retention policy; WorkQueue removes on ack by the consumer, Interest when all consumers for the subject acked.
- `MaxMsgSize` can cap stream messages below the server's 1 MiB default (e.g. 1024 bytes).
- Dedup via `Nats-Msg-Id` consults "only the message ID not the body"; default window 2 minutes; "we would caution against large windows."
- Stream publish acks only for `Request()`; `NoAck: true` disables stream acks.
- File storage per-message overhead without headers: record length 4 + seq 8 + ts 8 + subj_len 2 + subject + payload + hash 8; "A 5 byte hello message without headers will take 39 bytes." With headers add hdr_len 4 + headers.
- "if you are publishing many small messages the overhead will be, relatively speaking, quite large ... it's worth trying to optimize the subject length."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream contexts / Managing streams and consumers / Publishing to streams**

- Streams and durable consumers "can be defined administratively outside the application ... in which case the application only needs to know about the well-known names of the durable consumers".
- Add stream is idempotent: it succeeds on an existing stream "only if the existing stream matches exactly the attributes specified".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — NATS API Reference (JetStream wire API)**

- JetStream is a set of services over core NATS; with a domain the API prefix is `$JS.{domain}.API`.
- Subject patterns are designed so ACLs can "limit users to a specific Stream or Consumer and to specific verbs"; response permissions ensure only the receiver of a message can Ack it.
- Classic source/mirror uses 5 subjects: `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.<stream>[.<consumer>.<filter>]` (outbound), `$JS.FC.<stream>.>` (outbound), `$JSC.R.<uid>` (inbound reply), `$JS.S.<uid>`/`$JS.M.<uid>`/custom deliver (inbound). "all 5 subjects may need to be considered" for permissions/imports.
- "If this subject [`$JS.FC.<stream>.>`] is not forwarded, the consumer my stall under high load." If `$JS.ACK.<stream>.>` is not forwarded, pull consumers with ack `all`/`explicit` fail.
- Source/mirror retries consumer creation "every 10s to 60s" when the origin is unreachable; active consumers heartbeat at 1/s.
- "Do not delete and recreate the original stream! Please flush/purge the stream instead. The target stream remembers the last sequence id to be delivered. A delete will reset the sequence ID."
- `$JS.FC` is not domain-prefixed, so "identically named streams in different domains cannot be reliably sourced/mirrored into the same account. Please create unique stream names".
- 2.14 consumer-based sourcing: origin consumer must be `flow_control` type, supports WorkQueue/Interest streams; "It is strongly recommended ... pre-creating consumers"; auto-creation exists for backwards compatibility but "Please avoid relying on this feature." Uses `$JS.API.CONSUMER.RESET`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — nats bench (benchmarking guide)**

- `nats bench js pub sync` is for latency, "not good to measure throughput"; `async` batches with acks measures throughput; `batch` (atomic) "has the side effect of potentially helping throughout, especially for smaller messages."
- "by default JetStream flushes disk writes synchronously, meaning that even if the nats-server process is killed suddenly no messages will be lost as the OS already has them in it's buffer"; only a whole-host crash needs sync-after-every-write (at a latency cost). `--persistasync` on R1 gives memory-like throughput.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-6: Naming Rules**

- `stream-name`, `durable-name`, `consumer-name`, `account-name` are `filename-safe`: printable except dot, asterisk, gt, fwd-slash, backslash, "maximum 255 characters"; on Windows also excludes `< : " | ?`. "The server will reject names (return an API error) when it cannot build a valid path."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-10: JetStream Extended Purge**

- Purge API `$JS.API.STREAM.PURGE.<stream>` returns `success` and `purged` (count).
- Options: `seq` = upper-bound sequence, non-inclusive; `keep` = max messages retained; "The options `seq` and `keep` are mutually exclusive"; `filter` = subject (wildcards allowed).
- `filter`+`keep` keeps at most N per filter; "To `keep` _N_ number of messages for multiple subjects, invoke `purge` with different `filter`s."
- "If no options are provided, all messages are purged."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-12: JetStream Encryption At Rest**

- Server-side encryption at rest is "an alternative to an encrypted filesystem or block storage that would be provided by a cloud provider."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-20: JetStream based Object Stores**

- Backing stream config: `rollup_hdrs: true`, `allow_direct: true`, `discard: "new"`, `max_age` = TTL, `max_bytes`, storage, replicas, placement; compression bool maps to stream `compression: "s2"`.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-22: JetStream Publish Retries on No Responders**

- In clustered JetStream "there can be occasional blips in leadership which can result in a number of `no responders available` errors during the election."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-28: JetStream RePublish**

- RePublish lets subscribers "monitor messages that have been ingested by a stream ... without incurring the overhead of defining and using a JS Consumer"; use cases: dashboards, no-side-effect monitoring of WQ/interest streams, "KV or Object Store update events as an alternative to watches, e.g. an option for cache invalidation."
- "Re-publish occurs only after the original published message is ingested in the stream (with quorum for R>1 streams) and is _At-Most-Once_ QoS."
- Config `republish { src (default `>`), dest (required), headers_only (default false) }`; "Destination MUST have at least 1 non-wildcard token"; "Destination MAY not match or subset the subject filter(s) of the stream"; "RePublish option configuration MAY be edited after stream creation."
- RePublished headers: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Subject` (original), `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Last-Sequence` ("last message ingested to the same original subject (or 0 if none or deleted)"); with headers_only also `Nats-Msg-Size`. Application headers preserved.
- Loop prevention only checks the immediate stream: "It is possible to create a loop condition between two streams sharing an overlap in republish destinations and subject filters within a single account."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-31: JetStream Direct Get**

- The classic `$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.<stream>` API "All such reads are routed to the current stream leader ... tracked as administrative and incur tracking overhead."
- Direct Get "enables all stream peers (R>1), not just the stream leader, to respond to stream read calls as a service responder _queue group_" from their local store; "the number of servers eligible to respond to read requests is the same as the replica count of the stream."
- Mirrors with `mirror_direct: true` join the upstream's Direct Get queue group `_sys_` on `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<SRC>` and `.<SRC>.>`; mirrors "can be strategically placed for client latency-reduction" and "may be available to clients when the upstream is offline."
- `mirror_direct` lives on the mirror stream's config; "it has no meaning when set on a non-mirror stream"; independent of the mirror's own `allow_direct`.
- On mirror create, `mirror_direct` is aligned to the upstream's `allow_direct` when the upstream is visible (pedantic mode rejects disagreement; non-pedantic silently aligns); for External/cross-domain upstreams the user value is kept.
- "The mirror only joins the upstream queue group once it has caught up to within a small lag window of the source"; a fresh mirror "does not yet contribute to read availability."
- `mirror_direct` "is captured on the mirror at create time and is not automatically refreshed when the upstream's `allow_direct` changes later"; operator must update upstream AND re-issue `STREAM.UPDATE` on each mirror. "it's suggested that users always set `mirror_direct` to their desired value."
- Read-after-write: the classic Get API "provides read-after-write coherency by routing requests to a stream's current peer leader"; "_Direct Get_ does not assure read-after-write coherency as responders may be non-leader stream servers ... or MIRROR downstream servers."
- `allow_direct` default `false`, opt-in; "The server does not enable it implicitly"; KV helper sets it for buckets. Auto-promotion on `max_msgs_per_subject > 0` "existed only briefly and was removed in server v2.9.0."
- If `allow_direct` is false "there will be no responder at the Direct Get API ... Clients that make requests will receive no reply message and will time out."
- Request fields: `seq`, `last_by_subj`, `next_by_subj`, `batch`, `max_bytes`, `start_time` (2.11), `multi_last`, `up_to_seq`, `up_to_time`.
- Subject-Appended form `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<stream>.<subject>` is a `last_by_subj` shortcut so "subject-based interest restrictions ... such that only specific subjects in stream may be read" can be applied via permissions/imports. Payload with this form is a `408` error.
- Batched requests send "multiple messages without any flow control"; if `max_bytes` unset "the server will use the `max_pending` configuration setting or the server default (currently 64MB)."
- Batch ends with a zero-length message, `Status: 204`, `Description: EOB`, headers `Nats-Num-Pending` and `Nats-Last-Sequence`. Old servers "can be detected by the absence of the `Nats-Num-Pending` header in the first reply."
- `batch: 0` or omitted = single-message Get with no EOB; batch with neither `seq` nor `start_time` defaults to `seq: 1`; both supplied is "implementation-defined and clients should pick one."
- Multi-subject get "may only allow matching up to 1024 subjects. Any more will result in a `413` status reply."
- `multi_last` + `up_to_seq`/`up_to_time` gives "consistent point in time reads" ("temporal querying"), e.g. reading a KV record as it was at seq 3.
- Multi pagination: pass EOB's `Nats-UpTo-Sequence` back as `up_to_seq` (stable snapshot) and `Nats-Last-Sequence + 1` as `seq` (inclusive lower bound); ends when `Nats-Num-Pending` is 0.
- Status codes: 204 EOB, 404 no match, 408 empty/invalid request, 413 too many subjects. Success = `NATS/1.0` with no code.
- Reply headers: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Time-Stamp`, `Nats-Subject`, plus batch/multi headers; payload is "A _regular_ (not JSON-encoded) NATS message."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-33: Metadata for Stream and Consumer**

- Both stream and consumer config gain a `metadata` map of string→string; previously "The only solution was using `Description` field, which is a not ergonomic workaround."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-35: JetStream Filestore Compression**

- Motivation: "filestore encryption can almost completely prevent host filesystem compression or deduplication from working"; server compresses "before encryption takes place."
- Stream config field `compression`: `"none"` or `"s2"`; settable on create and update, shown in info. Clients need no change to publish/consume.
- Blocks are compressed asynchronously "when they cease to be the tail block" to avoid hurting publish throughput; compaction/truncation compress synchronously.
- Block-level (not per-message) compression chosen because it "provides significantly better compression ratios" on repetitive structured data such as JSON; checksum stays uncompressed for integrity checks without decompressing.
- Changing the algorithm later only affects new blocks; "this will not result in existing blocks being proactively compressed or decompressed."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-36: Subject Mapping Transforms in Streams**

- Rationale: core-level mapping needs server config or the account key; stream-level transforms "makes it very easy for the application developers or the NATS administrators to define and manage those mappings."
- Transforms can be applied in a mirror, in each source, at stream ingress (`subject_transform {src,dest}` at top level, applied "before limits are applied"; "it does not filter messages, it only transforms"), and in RePublish.
- Ingress transform "enables the ability to insert a partition number as a token in the message subjects."
- "there can not be any subject mapping transformation without an associated subject filter"; empty `dest` = filter only, no transform.
- Mirrors/sources take `subject_transforms: [{src,dest}]`; "if you use the `subject_transforms` array then you can _NOT_ also use the single string subject filters."
- "it is now possible to source not just from different streams but also from the same stream more than once."
- Ordering: a single source with multiple non-overlapping filters "the ordering of the messages is guaranteed to be preserved"; multiple sources from the same stream may overlap (duplicating messages) "but the order of the messages between the sources is not guaranteed to be preserved."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-43: JetStream Per-Message TTL**

- Motivation: KV tombstones "forever clog up the buckets with noise"; server-applied limits could leave short-TTL tombstones to notify KV watchers; some messages (schema/type hints) need infinite retention inside a stream with MaxAge.
- Header `Nats-TTL` takes seconds or a Go duration (`1h`); deadline = stream timestamp + duration.
- `Nats-TTL: never` "will result in a message that will never be expired. This applies to both per-message TTL processing and stream-level age limits: a `never` message is not removed by the stream's `MaxAge` setting."
- Unparsable values, or durations "below the 1 second minimum (including a literal `0`)", cause an error in the Pub Ack and the message is discarded (err_code 10165 `invalid per-message TTL`). Publishing `Nats-TTL` to a stream with the feature disabled → 10166 `per-message TTL is disabled`.
- Limit markers: when age-based removal (stream MaxAge or per-message TTL) removes the last message on a subject, the server places a marker with `Nats-Marker-Reason: MaxAge` and `Nats-TTL` = `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` (e.g. `1m0s`). "This behavior is off by default unless opted in on the `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL`."
- `Nats-Marker-Reason: Remove` (delete API) and `Purge` (purge API) markers are specified but "As of Server version 2.14 this feature is not currently implemented."
- "Sources and Mirrors will always accept and store messages with `Nats-TTL` header present, even if the `AllowMsgTTL` setting is disabled"; with it disabled "the messages are just stored" (enables audit-trail replication of tombstones).
- "Mirrors may not enable `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` since it would insert new messages into the Stream it might make it impossible to match sequences" (err 10052 `subject delete markers forbidden on mirrors`).
- Config: `allow_msg_ttl` bool, `subject_delete_marker_ttl` duration. Restrictions: `AllowMsgTTL` "can be enabled on existing streams but not disabled" (10052 `message TTL status can not be disabled`); both TTLs have "a minimum value of 1 second"; requires API level 1; `AllowRollup` must be true and `DenyPurge` false (auto-set unless pedantic).
- "Unless `MaxMsgsPer` equals 1 the server treats `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` as the minimum effective `Nats-TTL`. A publish with a `Nats-TTL` below this floor is **not** rejected — instead the server raises the effective TTL to the floor and rewrites the stored `Nats-TTL` header."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-44: Versioning for JetStream Assets**

- Server-set metadata keys: `_nats.ver` (hosting server version), `_nats.level` (hosting API level), `_nats.req.level` (required level to start the asset); e.g. consumer `PauseUntil` set → required level 1. Also created-version/level keys on create.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-49: JetStream Distributed Counter CRDT**

- A stream opts in with `allow_msg_counter: true`; then "All subjects in the stream must be counters." Publishing with `Nats-Incr` loads the last value on the subject, adds, and stores the new total in the body `{"val":"101"}`; PubAck returns `val` "avoiding a Get to get the latest value."
- Only addition/subtraction; "automatically behave as a CRDT and be order independent." Header must match `^[+-]\d+$` (BigInt; `0` valid); unparsable → reject. Server "will always use `big.Int`". Value is a JSON string "since JavaScript would only support up to `2^53`."
- Counter streams reject messages without `Nats-Incr`; reject messages carrying `Nats-Rollup`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Subject-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Stream`, or `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id`; `Nats-Incr` to a non-counter stream is rejected.
- Received via Source (feature off) or Mirror: "the message is stored verbatim."
- Source-aware tracking: `Nats-Counter-Sources` header (keyed by source stream name + pre-transform subject) holds last seen `val` per source; on a sourced message the server rewrites `Nats-Incr` to the delta vs last seen value, so recounts stay correct "even if some messages from the source were lost"; adding a source with existing value 10 yields first `Nats-Incr: 10`. Source keys "is not ever removed."
- "aggregated counters will always be eventually consistent with their sources, even if the aggregating stream also has local additions or subtractions."
- Global counters: regions publish on e.g. `count.es.hits`, sourcing rewrites to `count.eu.hits` then `count.hits`; aggregate streams may listen on no subject; mirror ES→EU then source into aggregate to keep both regional and total values.
- Resets: "a purge will not replicate, a roll-up would replicate and destroy the entire counter everywhere so the only real option is to publish a negative value"; preferred reset = negative value then purge up to that message; subject purge only for full deletes.
- Config restrictions: error on Mirror; only Limits retention; "can only be enabled during creation"; no Discard New; not with Per-Message TTL; "Message schedules (see ADR-51) are not supported"; requires API level 2.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-50: JetStream Batch Publishing**

- Goals: performance, "Atomic Batch writes - where an entire batch is stored or abandoned", and batching RAFT append entries (the last is out of scope here).
- Atomic use case: a KV user record spanning 5 keys (address) "Performing updates on these related keys is not safe today as writes might fail after a first update resulting in an address line in one city but a post code in another."
- Atomic protocol: first message is a *request* with `Nats-Batch-Id:<uuid>` and `Nats-Batch-Sequence:1` (server replies error or zero-byte); subsequent messages increment the sequence (optional reply gets zero-byte ack); final message has `Nats-Batch-Commit:1` (stored) or `Nats-Batch-Commit:eob` (2.14; not stored, `BatchSize` excludes it) and receives the pub ack.
- Batch ID max 64 characters (err 10179); missing sequence 10175; sequence exceeds server limit "default 1000" (10199); batch not enabled 10174; incomplete/abandoned 10176; unsupported header `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` 10177; duplicate `Nats-Msg-Id` inside a batch 10201.
- Atomic server limits: "Each stream can only have 50 batches in flight"; "Each server can only have 1,000 batches in flight"; abandoned after "10 seconds since the last message" (advisory, no error reply); "Each batch can have maximum 1000 messages."
- Gaps in batch sequence reject the batch; expected-header checks (`ExpectedLastSeq` etc.) are evaluated "at the time when the batch is committed under lock"; "Only the first message of the batch may contain `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence`"; `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence` only valid if no earlier batch entry writes the same subject.
- "If a stream is operating on the `PersistMode: async` mode, any batch published to it must fail" (atomic). `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` unsupported in batches. Dedup via `Nats-Msg-Id` supported "Starting from 2.12.1"; duplicates reject the batch.
- Abandonment advisory `io.nats.jetstream.advisory.v1.stream_batch_abandoned` with reasons `timeout`, `large`, `incomplete`, `unsupported`.
- Pub ack gains `batch` (id) and `count` (size); ack sequence is the final message's; earlier messages occupy the preceding sequences.
- Fast-ingest batches (2.14): "not reliable, meaning messages can be lost and the batch will not be abandoned"; "not pre-staged and so will not be limited to 1000 messages"; "The goal is to replace Async publish with one built on these behaviors." Motivation includes ObjectStore concurrent-writer failures "due to pending API counts."
- Fast-ingest control channel: reply subject `<prefix>.<uuid>.<initial flow>.<gap ok|fail>.<batch seq>.<operation>.$FI`; operations 0 start, 1 append, 2 commit+store, 3 commit EOB, 4 ping; "this must be an old style inbox" subscribed to `<prefix>.uuid.>` so unsubscribing short-circuits acks on error.
- "The client MUST wait for the first reply" before blasting messages; server dictates actual flow: starts low (e.g. client asks 100, server starts at 1), "usually doubles" to ramp up, "usually halves" to slow down, never exceeds the client's initial flow ("the server must treat the initial flow parameters as the upper bound").
- `BatchFlowAck {"type":"ack","seq":N,"msgs":M}`: with `gap: fail` "messages up to and including Sequence were persisted"; with `gap: ok` "_some_ of the messages ... were persisted." Acks are cumulative: a later ack implies earlier ones were received ("critical to avoid unrecoverable stalls").
- Outstanding acks guidance: 1 = flow-controlled async; "Outstanding acks = 2 ... generally optimal"; 3 only for high RTT "not a default".
- `BatchFlowGap {"type":"gap","last_seq":10,"seq":15}` is informational, may arrive out of order, "MUST NOT be used to know whether ... was persisted." With `fail` the batch is abandoned and final ack `BatchSize` = last received before gap; with `ok` the batch continues. Leader change in `ok` mode continues with a gap message; in `fail` mode abandons.
- `BatchFlowErr {"type":"err","seq":N,"error":{...}}` sent immediately on expected-header failures; PubAck never carries both error and persisted info, hence the separate message. Single-message batch that immediately commits returns a plain `PubAck`.
- Fast-ingest errors: 10205 not enabled, 10206 invalid pattern, 10207 ID > 64, 10208 unknown ID. Limits: "Each stream can only have 1,000 batches in flight"; "Each server can only have 50,000 batches in flight"; 10 s idle abandon; "no maximum size for fast ingest batches"; "`PersistMode: async` set are compatible with fast ingest."
- Config: `allow_atomic` (API level 2) and `allow_batched` (API level 3); both toggleable via update, may coexist; `allow_atomic` + `PersistMode: async` "must error."
- "Mirrors can't enable these settings, and will ignore the various headers"; sourcing streams may enable them but "sources will ignore the batching headers when sourced."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-51: JetStream Message Scheduler**

- One message holds a cron-like schedule and the stream produces new messages into the same stream on that schedule; "the last message on a subject holds the current schedule. In other words every schedule must have its own unique subject."
- Use cases: delayed publish (`@at <RFC3339>`), recurring publish (`@hourly`, cron, `@every 1m`), and subject sampling (`Nats-Schedule-Source` republishes the last message on a subject on a schedule; wildcards not supported; falls back to the schedule's own body if the source has no message).
- Headers on the schedule message: `Nats-Schedule`, `Nats-Schedule-Target` (must be a subject in the same stream), `Nats-Schedule-Source`, `Nats-Schedule-TTL` (requires `AllowMsgTTL`), `Nats-Schedule-Time-Zone` (cron only), `Nats-Schedule-Rollup` (only `sub`). Produced messages get `Nats-Scheduler`, `Nats-Schedule-Next` (next time, or `purge` for one-shot), plus `Nats-TTL`/`Nats-Rollup` if requested; other headers pass through verbatim.
- "If a message is made with a schedule in the past it is immediately sent. If a server was down for a month and a scheduled message is recovered ... it will be sent immediately. To avoid this, add a `Nats-TTL` header."
- Many delayed messages for one target: put schedules on `orders.schedule.<UUID>` with `Nats-Schedule-Target: orders`.
- Cron is 6-field (seconds first); predefined `@yearly/@annually`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily/@midnight`, `@hourly`; `@every <go duration>` "The minimum supported interval is `1s`; shorter intervals are rejected."
- Time zones via `time.LoadLocation()` names (IANA recommended; abbreviations "are ambiguous ... not DST-aware"); fixed offsets like `+02:00` rejected; empty header rejected; "Operators must therefore install and keep tzdata up to date on every server"; DST-boundary schedules "could be skipped" or "executed twice."
- Stopping a schedule: delete its message by sequence, purge its subject (wildcards allowed), or atomically publish to another subject with `Nats-Schedule-Next: purge` and `Nats-Scheduler: <schedule subject>`; may combine with `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence(-Subject)` to stop only if the schedule still exists. `Nats-Scheduler` may not equal the publish subject (err 10212) "because ... the cancel message would be purged together with the schedule via the auto-applied `Nats-Rollup: sub`."
- Config `allow_msg_schedules`: denied on Source or Mirror; "Stream should not support Discard New"; "can be enabled on existing streams but not disabled"; requires API level 2; implicitly enables `AllowRollup` and clears `DenyPurge` (server auto-applies `Nats-Rollup: sub` to schedules, so a new schedule on the same subject replaces the prior one).
- Stream subjects should include a wildcard like `schedules.>` for schedule subjects, plus the target subjects.
- Retention interaction: "Once a schedule message is removed from storage, by any mechanism, its schedule stops firing" (MaxAge shorter than the interval, MaxMsgs/MaxBytes/DiscardOld, WorkQueue ack, Interest with no interest). "**Limits** is the simplest configuration ... recommended."
- With Interest retention: option 1 pin a filtered consumer on schedule subjects (not recommended: "the pinning consumer becomes load-bearing configuration"); option 2 keep schedules in a dedicated WorkQueue stream and have the Interest stream source the target subjects ("generally the more robust configuration").

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-52: No Headers support for Direct Get [STALE?]**

- Proposed `no_hdr` option on `JSApiMsgGetRequest` to return body only (motivated by ADR-49 counters); "headers like `Nats-Sequence` will also be unset." Not implemented; superseded by nothing (ADR-31 remains the Direct Get spec).

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-56: JetStream Consistency Models**

- `PersistMode: async` "will result in asynchronous flushing of data to disk ... at the expense of data loss during severe disruptions in power, server or disk subsystems"; "The Publish Ack will be sent before the data is known to be written to disk."
- Stream-level `async` overrides server `sync: always` for that stream. Modes: `default`+`sync:always` = flushed and synced; `default` without `sync:always` = flushed, synced per sync interval; `async` = PubAck first, writes batched in memory, background write.
- "this mode cannot support batch publishing at all" (atomic batches; ADR-50 later allows fast-ingest with async).
- "Setting it on anything other than a R1 stream will result in an error"; stated verbatim: "Scaling a R1 stream up to greater resiliency levels will fail if the `PersistMode` is not set to `async`" (ADR wording; reads as if intended "is set to async"). Default is unset/`default` and the server leaves it unset in INFO; any explicit value requires API level 2.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-8: JetStream based Key-Value Stores**

- Bucket = stream `KV_<Bucket>` with subjects `$KV.<Bucket>.>`; history = `max_msgs_per_subject`.
- Fixed stream settings: `discard: new`, `rollup_hdrs: true`, `deny_delete: true`, `allow_direct: true` ("can be modified out-of-band only if desired, but not through KV bucket update"); `max_msg_size` caps value size; `max_bytes` caps bucket; "Maximum number of keys cannot currently be limited"; placement, republish, metadata allowed; compression → `s2`; storage file; R value varies.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-59: JetStream Stream Sourcing and Mirroring**

- Mirroring = "an exact, read-only copy of a single upstream stream ... primarily used for read scaling, disaster recovery, and geographic distribution." Sourcing = aggregate one or more upstreams "suitable for data aggregation, fan-in patterns, and building derived data views." Both work in one account, across accounts, and across domains.
- `StreamSource` fields: `name` (required), `opt_start_seq` / `opt_start_time` (mutually exclusive; "Only applies on first creation"; if both set "`opt_start_seq` takes precedence"), `filter_subject` vs `subject_transforms` (mutually exclusive), `external {api, deliver}`.
- Mirror behaviour: "Messages are delivered in the same order and with the same sequence numbers and timestamps as the upstream stream"; read-only; "cannot have `subjects` configured"; retention/limits independent of upstream; "A stream can mirror at most one stream. Multiple streams can mirror the same stream"; `mirror` and `sources` mutually exclusive.
- "Mirror configuration **cannot be changed** after creation"; promote a mirror by removing the origin's subjects, then removing the mirror config and adding the subjects to the former mirror.
- `mirror_direct` on the mirror lets it serve `$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.<UPSTREAM>`; "particularly useful for KV store mirrors where reads should land on the closest replica"; joins only after catching up "within a small lag window"; captured at create, not auto-refreshed; "we recommend that operators always set `mirror_direct` explicitly."
- With `mirror_direct: true` the upstream's StreamInfo gets an `alternates` list "sorted by RTT proximity."
- Mirrors cannot use: `subjects`, `sources`, `first_seq`, `allow_msg_counter`, `allow_atomic`, `allow_msg_schedules`, `subject_delete_marker_ttl`. Mirrors can use: stream-level `subject_transform`, `republish`, `compression`, `allow_msg_ttl`.
- Sourcing: "Messages from each individual source maintain their relative ordering. When sourcing from multiple streams, messages are interleaved in arrival order. There is no guaranteed ordering across different sources." A sourced stream "**can** also have its own `subjects`."
- Sources "can be added, updated or removed after stream creation." Duplicate-source detection key = stream name + filter subject + subject transforms + external API prefix; same upstream may be sourced multiple times with different filters.
- Sourced streams cannot use `mirror` or `allow_msg_schedules`.
- Multiple `subject_transforms` per source: `src` patterns "must not overlap"; `dest` optional (defaults to src). Order of application: source-level filter/transform first, then stream-level `subject_transform`.
- `Nats-Stream-Source` header: `<stream-index[:hash]> <sequence> <filter-subject|>> <dest-subject|>> <original-subject>`; multiple transforms joined with `\f`; on daisy-chaining "the server replaces any existing `Nats-Stream-Source` header so the header always reflects the immediate upstream origin."
- Reconnection "uses exponential backoff with jitter"; resumes "from the last successfully stored sequence — no manual intervention is required."
- Upstream expiry: gap in upstream `sseq` with contiguous `dseq` → skip markers recorded and continue; gap in `dseq` → consumer "must be recreated to redeliver." "This gap detection is reliable only for streams using the **Limits** retention policy."
- Internal replication consumers have "a short inactive threshold (10 seconds)."
- "Work queue streams are **not recommended** as upstream streams" (replication consumers "bypass the work queue's subject overlap validation", breaking single-consumer-per-partition). "Interest retention streams are **not recommended**" (messages may be removed while the replication consumer is absent). Limits retention "is the recommended and best-supported."
- "In a cluster, only the stream leader manages the replication consumers. If leadership changes, the new leader takes over replication from the last known position."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-60: JetStream reliable stream sourcing/mirroring on WQ/Interest streams (updates ADR-59)**

- Pre-2.14 sourcing/mirroring uses "an ephemeral ordered push consumer using `AckNone`"; "really reliable if the stream that's being mirrored/sourced is a Limits stream" but on WorkQueue/Interest "any messages that are sent are immediately acknowledged and removed. If this message is not received on the other end, this message will be lost"; on Interest "interest will be lost while there's no active connection ... This also results in messages being lost."
- Fix: when the upstream is WQ or Interest the server "upgrade[s]" to a durable consumer, replicated if the upstream is replicated, reused for the life of the source config, best-effort deleted on removal.
- "Durable sourcing": user pre-creates the durable consumer (monitorable, pausable, security-controlled); stream source config carries `consumer: {name, deliver_subject}`; then `OptStartSeq`, `OptStartTime`, `FilterSubject` "are not allowed" on the source and must live on the consumer; enables `DeliverPolicy=last_per_subject` and `ReplayPolicy=original` sourcing.
- "WorkQueue streams don't allow having multiple consumers with overlapping filter subjects" so a durable sourcing consumer blocks other overlapping consumers; "an Interest or Limits stream should be used" in that case.
- Guidance: "It's generally recommended to use sourcing defined in the stream configuration for most use cases"; durable sourcing is for security needs, advanced consumer options, or bootstrapping a leaf node before it connects ("all available messages will be reliably mirrored/sourced" once connected).
- Server handles manual resets of a sourcing consumer: forward resets skip messages; backward resets "should guarantee that mirrored messages are not duplicated"; a server consumer create/update for durable sourcing "will implicitly also perform a consumer reset."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-62: JetStream desired state reconciliation**

- Scale up stream: consumers without explicit replicas scale too; "Interest/WorkQueue consumers are also scaled up to match the stream's replica count." Scale down: "Prefers keeping the stream leader and online and caught up peers"; R1 consumers on a doomed peer are moved first.

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream stream defaults and size constants (server/stream.go, server/jetstream.go, server/jetstream_api.go)**

- Maximum stream replicas. `StreamMaxReplicas = 5` (server/stream.go:730); rejected with "maximum replicas is 5" (server/stream.go:1733-1734). Replicas default to 1 when 0 (server/stream.go:1730-1731)
- Default duplicate (dedup) window. `StreamDefaultDuplicatesWindow = 2 * time.Minute` (server/stream.go:1674). Applied only when Duplicates==0 and stream is not a mirror/source; capped to MaxAge if MaxAge is shorter, and to server `jetstream.limits.duplicate_window` if set (server/stream.go:1776-1793)
- Storage defaults to file when unset (server/stream.go:1723-1724)
- MaxMsgs, MaxMsgsPer, MaxBytes, MaxMsgSize, MaxConsumers: 0 normalizes to -1 (unlimited) (server/stream.go:1740-1768)
- Stream/consumer name max 255 chars. `JSMaxNameLen = 255` (server/jetstream_api.go:389); description max 4096 `JSMaxDescriptionLen = 4 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:381); metadata max 128 KiB `JSMaxMetadataLen = 128 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:385)
- JetStream API request queue limit before the server reacts (drops/warns). `JSDefaultRequestQueueLimit = 10_000` (server/jetstream_api.go:393)
- Default JetStream store limits: max_file_store default 1 TiB `JetStreamMaxStoreDefault = 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024`; max_memory_store fallback 256 MiB `JetStreamMaxMemDefault = 1024 * 1024 * 256` "only used when we can't determine system memory" (server/jetstream.go:2716-2723)
- Dynamic JetStream config: when max_memory_store unset, uses 75% of system memory (or GOMEMLIMIT if lower): `jsc.MaxMemory = sysMem / 4 * 3`; when max_file_store unset, uses available disk of store dir `diskAvailable(jsc.StoreDir)`; no store_dir means os.TempDir()/nats/jetstream with warning "Temporary storage directory used, data could be lost on system reboot" (server/jetstream.go:2728-2768)
- Stream internal inbound queue caps: `streamDefaultMaxQueueMsgs = 100_000`, `streamDefaultMaxQueueBytes = 128 * 1024 * 1024` (server/stream.go:458-461)
- Batch publish limits: `streamDefaultMaxBatchTimeout = 10 * time.Second`; atomic batches `MaxAtomicBatchInflightPerStream = 50`, `MaxAtomicBatchInflightTotal = 1000`, `MaxAtomicBatchSize = 1000`; fast batches `MaxFastBatchInflightPerStream = 1000`, `MaxFastBatchInflightTotal = 50_000` (server/stream.go:464-473); overridable via `jetstream.limits` MaxBatchSize / MaxBatchInflightPerStream / MaxBatchInflightTotal (server/stream.go:7402-7424)
- Multi/batch direct get returns at most 1024 messages per request. `const maxAllowedResponses = 1024` "TODO(dlc) - Make configurable?" (server/stream.go:5991-5992)
- Per-message header block limited to 65535 bytes (`len(hdr) > math.MaxUint16` -> "header exceeds maximum") (server/stream.go:6962-6970)
- Stream max_msg_size defaults: if stream MaxMsgSize <= 0, falls back to account max payload, then server MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE (1 MiB); subject length estimate default 256 for wildcard-only streams `defaultMaxSubject = 256` (server/stream.go:1396-1427)
- Server max_payload is enforced on the JetStream publish path: header+payload must fit in `MaxPayload` (server/stream.go:6935-6947); stream max_msg_size checked on header+msg (server/stream.go:6951-6960)
- Source/mirror consumer heartbeat 1s; stalled check every 10s. `sourceHealthHB = 1 * time.Second`, `sourceHealthCheckInterval = 10 * time.Second` (server/stream.go:3118-3123)
- Mirror/source consumer re-setup retry: base backoff 5s * (2*fails), capped at 2 minutes; requests throttled to no more than one per 2s. `retryBackOff = 5 * time.Second`, `retryMaximum = 2 * time.Minute` (server/stream.go:3441-3454), `sourceConsumerRetryThreshold = 2 * time.Second` (server/stream.go:3925)
- Interest-retention consistency check runs every 2 minutes with 30s jitter. `defaultCheckInterestStateT = 2 * time.Minute`, `defaultCheckInterestStateJ = 30` (server/stream.go:8673-8676)
- Persist modes: `default` (flush before pub ack) and `async` ("The publish acknowledgement may be sent before the persisting completes. This means writes could be lost if they weren't flushed prior to a hard kill of the server.") (server/stream.go:189-197)
- JetStream publish headers: `Nats-Msg-Id`, `Nats-Expected-Stream`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence-Subject`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id`, `Nats-Rollup` (values `sub`/`all`), `Nats-TTL`, `Nats-Incr`, `Nats-Batch-Id`/`Nats-Batch-Sequence`/`Nats-Batch-Commit`, `Nats-Schedule*` (server/stream.go:653-678, 706-708)
- Direct-get response headers: `Nats-Stream`, `Nats-Sequence`, `Nats-Time-Stamp`, `Nats-Subject`, `Nats-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Num-Pending`, `Nats-UpTo-Sequence`; EOB status `NATS/1.0 204 EOB` (server/stream.go:695-702, 5982-5987)
- Delete-marker reasons: `MaxAge`, `Purge`, `Remove` (`Nats-Marker-Reason`) (server/stream.go:712-716)
- Dedup: "Dedupe detection. This is done at the cluster level for dedupe detection above the lower layers." Mirrors cannot dedupe on their own ("If we're mirroring we can't deduplicate on our own"); a duplicate returns the ORIGINAL sequence with `"duplicate": true` in the PubAck (server/stream.go:6754-6775)
- Sourcing into a discard-new stream (for example a work queue) repeatedly hits limits and re-creates the source consumer at the failed sequence: "Can happen temporarily all the time during normal operations when the sourcing stream is discard new (example use case is for sourcing into a work queue)" (server/stream.go:4590-4612)
- Filesystem permission error while writing a message shuts down JetStream entirely: "Filesystem permission denied while writing msg, disabling JetStream" (server/stream.go:7124-7129)
- Standalone server exceeding JetStream resource limits returns insufficient resources and steps down the stream leader (server/stream.go:6974-6987)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream stream validation rules (server/stream.go checkStreamCfgLocked / configUpdateCheckLocked)**

- Stream name required, can not contain '.', '*', '>', '\\', '/' (server/stream.go:1692-1693); max 255 chars (1695-1696); description max 4096 (1698-1699); metadata max 131072 bytes (1706-1707)
- MaxAge must be 0 or >= 100ms ("max age needs to be >= 100ms") (server/stream.go:1772-1773)
- Duplicates window can not be larger than MaxAge, can not exceed server `jetstream.limits.duplicate_window`, and must be >= 100ms if set (server/stream.go:1797-1806)
- `deny_purge` with `allow_rollup_hdrs` rejected: "roll-ups require the purge permission" (server/stream.go:1808-1810)
- Counter streams (`allow_msg_counter`) can not use discard new, message TTLs, or message schedules, and must be limits retention (server/stream.go:1813-1826)
- `discard_new_per_subject` requires discard=new AND max_msgs_per_subject > 0 (server/stream.go:1829-1836; re-checked on update 2368-2375)
- `subject_delete_marker_ttl` must be >= 1s; non-pedantic auto-enables allow_msg_ttl and allow_rollup_hdrs (and clears deny_purge) (server/stream.go:1838-1855)
- Message schedules can not use discard new; auto-enable rollup (server/stream.go:1858-1868)
- Async persist mode only on file storage, only R1, and not with atomic batch publish (server/stream.go:1870-1880)
- Mirror streams can not set: first_seq, subjects, sources, allow_msg_counter, allow_atomic, allow_batched, allow_msg_schedules; mirror filter_subject and subject_transforms are mutually exclusive; subject delete markers forbidden on mirrors ("would result in new tombstones which would use up sequence numbers, diverging from the origin stream") (server/stream.go:1909-1953)
- Mirror subject transforms may not overlap each other (server/stream.go:1955-1969)
- Mirror max_msg_size can not be smaller than origin's (server/stream.go:1982-1985); source max_msg_size same rule (2083-2086)
- Mirror inherits `mirror_direct` from origin's `allow_direct` (server/stream.go:1988-2001)
- Sources: duplicate source (same name+filter+transform identity) rejected; filter_subject and subject_transforms mutually exclusive; transforms may not overlap; the same durable consumer can not be reused for multiple sources of the same stream; sources with message schedules rejected (server/stream.go:2013-2072)
- External delivery prefix must be a valid publish subject and must not collide with sourced stream subjects; external api prefix must not collide with `$JS.API` (server/stream.go:2100-2119)
- Source/mirror cycles are detected across streams ("detected cycle"), including cycles hidden behind mirrors (server/stream.go:2121-2163)
- If no subjects, sources, or mirror, the stream name is used as the subject (server/stream.go:2166-2170)
- Duplicate subjects rejected (server/stream.go:2184-2186)
- Capturing `>` requires `no_ack: true` AND replicas = 1 (server/stream.go:2188-2196)
- Subjects overlapping `$JS.>`, `$JSC.>`, `$NRG.>` (except `$JS.EVENT.>`) or `$SYS.>` (except `$SYS.ACCOUNT.>`) require `no_ack: true` (server/stream.go:2198-2211)
- A stream's own subjects may not overlap each other ("subject %q overlaps with %q") "which would cause duplicate entries (assuming no MsgID)" (server/stream.go:2212-2218)
- Stream needs at least one subject or be a source/mirror (server/stream.go:2225-2228)
- If the account tier has `max_bytes_required`, MaxBytes must be > 0; MaxBytes may not exceed the tier's per-stream byte limit (server/stream.go:2231-2235)
- Republish destination may not collide with the stream's subjects ("forms a cycle"); empty source means `>` (server/stream.go:2247-2284)
- `placement.preferred` is not permitted (server/stream.go:2291-2294)
- Standalone (non-clustered) server rejects replicas > 1 with JSStreamReplicasNotSupportedErr (server/stream.go:771-774, 2335-2338)
- On stream update, immutable: name, storage type, retention to/from workqueue ("Can only change retention from limits to interest or back"), unsealing, cancelling deny_delete, cancelling deny_purge, mirror config (except removing it to "promote" the mirror to a normal stream), disabling allow_msg_ttl, changing allow_msg_counter, disabling allow_msg_schedules, persist_mode (server/stream.go:2331-2394)
- Sealing a stream forces MaxAge=0, Discard=new, DenyDelete=DenyPurge=true, AllowRollup=false (server/stream.go:2398-2403)
- Stream update reserves only the MaxBytes delta against account limits so raising MaxBytes on a stream that already consumes reservation is possible (server/stream.go:2408-2460)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream file store sizing (server/filestore.go, server/store.go)**

- File store block sizes: limits-retention streams 8 MiB; work-queue/interest streams 4 MiB; KV 4 MiB; encrypted stores capped at 2 MiB ("large blocks can result in worsened perf since many writes on disk involve re-encrypting the entire block"). `defaultLargeBlockSize = 8 * 1024 * 1024`, `defaultMediumBlockSize = 4 * 1024 * 1024`, `defaultKVBlockSize = defaultMediumBlockSize`, `maximumEncryptedBlockSize = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (server/filestore.go:360-375, 809-843)
