- Rule of thumb: if you are just inserting events into a database with indexed timestamps, you do not need strict ordering; only decision-making state machines do. "a lot of people think that they need ordering but often ... they're just putting them in a database" (~25:26)
- A filtered consumer is not as fast as a SQL aggregation query, but it answers ad hoc questions without copying data to another store and stays live for new matches. "is this going to be as fast as a SQL query if you're doing aggregation ... no it won't be" (~35:37)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Stream processing: the easy way (with NATS and Benthos)**

- Lightweight analytics does not always need a stateful stream processor; the speaker scopes this to lightweight pipelines, not terabyte-scale stateful jobs. "you don't always need to have a big stateful stream processor in order to do a lot of work" (~23:26)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Transcending microservices with NATS | RethinkConn '22**

- The many separate stacks (RPC, message queue, durable job queue, append-only log, KV) all reduce to sending, receiving, or asking a question; one substrate can replace them. "we're either sending or receiving data or we're asking it a question" (~13:15)
- HTTP cannot do fan-in/fan-out roll calls (one request, many responders); NATS pub/sub patterns apply to microservices, not just queues and jobs. "you can't just ping a URL and have a roll call come back via HTTP" (~17:17)
- Concern that adopting a non-HTTP/non-gRPC protocol will cause problems is unfounded; NATS' role is connecting the components within the system, with UIs layered on the edge. "people get a little nervous ... the answer is no" (~25:28)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Where are we now and where to next? | RethinkConn '22**

- Service mesh was built to solve point-to-point, location-based addressing; NATS lacks that flaw, so discovery (a no-op once connected), load balancing, traffic management, and canary testing come built in without Kubernetes. "service mesh ... was built to solve a fundamental design flaw which was point-to-point location-based addressing" (~17:20)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Short break and Q&A! | RethinkConn '22**

- Replicas vs mirrors: an R3 stream is one system; a publish is not acknowledged until a quorum of replicas agrees and commits to stable storage (file) or memory. Mirrors and sources are kept in sync asynchronously and self-heal. "you're not going to get an acknowledgement back until a quorum of those servers that are hosting that asset agree" (~12:12)
- Mirrors are strictly read-only, bit-for-bit replicas including sequence and timestamps; a publish or KV put against a mirror fails when the origin is unavailable. "mirrors are read-only. If the origin server is not around and you try to do a publish or a KV put, that will fail" (~18:23)
- The server binary is identical for leaf, cluster, and supercluster roles; only the relationships (client, gateway, cluster, leaf node connection types) differ. "The binary is exactly the same" (~21:24)
- JetStream KV has no value-based constructs (push, pop, Redis data-type semantics); it is a payload per key, like memcached, so tightly Redis-typed workloads will not map. "the NATS key value store does not have any kind of like value-based constructs in it" (~23:28)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Derek Collison RethinkConn 2025 Keynote and Closing Remarks**

- Global microservices on NATS across regions, clouds and edge need no DNS tricks, load balancers, API gateways or service meshes. "no DNS tricks are needed, no load balancers or GSLBs, no API gateways, no service meshes are required" (~02:20)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Synadia RethinkConn 2024: Synadia CEO Derek Collison Keynote**

- NATS challenges two assumptions, location dependence and one-to-one communication; other technologies only appear location independent and need much extra tooling to fake it. "Technologies today can make this look like they are not location dependent or that all communications are truly one to one, but they are under the covers" (~02:00)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Synadia RethinkConn 2024: Synadia Roadmap with Byron Ruth**

- Server-side filtering is subject-level only (per-token wildcards); filtering on headers or message body is not supported by the server and will not be; a message-processing callout to an external service is the planned way. "if you wanted to filter based on headers or the message body... that's not supported in the server and it won't be" (~04:30)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Introducing Synadia Insights: Catch the NATS Failures Nothing Else Reports**

- In `nats stream report`, "Lost" counts messages the disk failed to keep (corruption, hardware failure); messages removed to honor a retention limit are discarded, not lost, so Lost stays zero. "To NATS, lost means messages on the disk failed to keep... Messages deleted on purpose to honor a limit aren't lost." (~07:10)
- A consumer's unprocessed/pending count shows only what it will still receive (at most the stream's current contents), not what it will never receive. "2,000 is what analytics is about to receive. It says nothing at all about the 10,000 it never will" (~08:00)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Event-Driven Systems Need a Security Gateway — Meet Synadia Protect for NATS**

- Traditional brokers (JMS, Solace, MQ, AMQP) secure the connection with TLS/mTLS and apply ACLs to addresses, but offer no content-based policies, unlike REST API gateways. "there are zero content based policies to be applicable at this level" (~02:00)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Rethinking Connectivity - Hyper-Connectivity & The Intelligent Edge**

- Today's limitations: DNS, hostnames and IPs as the addressing basis, poll-based HTTP everywhere, VPC-perimeter security that edge breaks, location-dependent monolithic backends, and layers built on one-to-one HTTP. "we're still kind of using IP addresses to get machines to talk to each other and maybe that's not scaling" (~04:40)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — A New Way of Thinking | NATS 2.0 and Connectivity**

- Core NATS is deliberately payload-agnostic, like a phone that carries any language; schema and encoding helpers belong in clients and the ecosystem, not the core. "the core NATS will remain payload agnostic" (~44:20)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Customer Story - PowerFlex Solves Intermittent Connectivity at the Edge w/ NATS - RethinkConn 2025**

- Message loss with core NATS was real but much rarer than newcomers reading the docs expect. "you start thinking oh no NATS will drop messages, wasn't really that common but it definitely happened" (~03:04)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Customer Story - MachineMetrics on Industrial IoT & Predictive Analytics w/ NATS at RethinkConn 2025**

- The distinctive NATS property is that data addressing (subjects) is decoupled from the access point (server URLs), unlike REST where the URI is both identifier and server. "NATS... really decouples the addressing of data from the access point of data" (~25:33)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Customer Lightning Talk - ACI Worldwide at RethinkConn 2025**

- A distributed KV built into the messaging system is hard to get from other messaging systems and was a decisive plus for card payments. "the KV... it's one of the main items that is not so easy to achieve with other messaging systems" (~05:12)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Synadia RethinkConn 2024: Franco Sabini from Fineco Bank on NATS**

- Compared with Kafka and Solace, NATS needs no knob-tuning to work out of the box. "you don't need to pull levers, change flags... when it works it works" (~13:17)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Simple Solutions for Complex Problems - How Workiva uses NATS as a Microservices and RPC transport**

- Delivery guarantees have many definitions (handed to transport, enqueued, processing started, finished), each with different costs; guaranteed ordered exactly-once is expensive and, by some definitions, impossible. "guaranteed ordered exactly once delivery they're really expensive to provide and depending on your definition they might be impossible" (~04:09)
- Delivery is not processing; business-level guarantees must be built in the business layer because infrastructure can't provide them. "if you need business level guarantees you really have to build those into the business layer because the infrastructure can't provide that" (~06:10)
- TCP guaranteeing packet delivery doesn't give application-level guarantees; the end-to-end argument applies. "your application doesn't care about packets and bytes it cares about messages" (~07:10)
- NATS needs no external coordination service (ZooKeeper/etcd) and has minimal configuration, which is key to operational simplicity. "you don't have to deal with configuring like zookeeper etcd these other external dependencies" (~13:17)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — Workloads - Distributed cloud-to-edge compute with NATS Execution Engine**

- "The edge" has no single definition (mainframe, cloud, ESP32 on a farm); workloads must be movable to whatever the user's edge is. "The edge is not concrete, but one of the key values of Nex was these workloads need to be able to move to whatever edge" (~06:16)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — NATS KubeCon Tutorial on Twitch**

- NATS v2 is backward compatible and a drop-in replacement for v1; users saw an automatic performance boost, and subject cardinality with millions of subscriptions is handled. "You could actually, if you're on v1, use v2 as a drop-in replacement." (~23:40)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — The Zen of High Performance Messaging with NATS by Waldemar Quevedo Salinas**

- Choosing reliability over guaranteed delivery does not constrain application guarantees; per the end-to-end argument, guarantees belong in the application layer, and "we can always build stronger guarantees on top but never remove them from below." "We can always build stronger guarantees on top but we can always remove them from below." (~31:57)

**Source class: Talks and videos (YouTube transcripts) — SCaLE 13x Derek Collison  NATS A new nervous system for distributed cloud platforms**

- Multicast effectively failed operationally and is disallowed on cloud platforms; for fan-out of roughly 30 or fewer receivers, sending the message N times from one point is faster. "For certain types of N, probably depending on your message size, 30 or so or less, it actually is faster to send it 30 times." (~07:12)
- NATS queuing is a subscribe operation ("distributed queuing"), not a publish operation that physically enqueues; only one member of a queue group receives a given message while plain subscribers still get it. "Subscribe is what I call distributed queuing." (~13:17)
- Exactly-once done correctly requires transactional semantics down to disk hardware; Derek considers it "a problem that doesn't really need a solution" compared to idempotent designs. "Exactly once is a problem that doesn't really need a solution." (~15:21)
- The protocol is text-based by choice; Derek and Redis' author agree computers are fast enough that text framing does not matter for performance. "Computers are so fast I don't think text-based matters anymore and that's actually the truth." (~24:30)

## SIZE: Numbers: defaults, limits, bounds (817 claims)


**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — What is NATS**

- The NATS service infrastructure scales from a single nats-server on an end device to a global super-cluster; "the `nats-server` process is less than 20 MB in size!"

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Compare NATS**

- "Core NATS: 48 known client types, 11 supported by maintainers, 18 contributed by the community. NATS Streaming: 7 client types supported by maintainers".
- Kafka: "Clients are tied to partitions defined within clusters"; servers need a JVM, "eight cores, 64 GB to128 GB of RAM, two or more 8-TB SAS/SSD disks, and a 10-Gig NIC" (cites Cloudera sizing).
- Pulsar "requires a JVM and requires at least 6 Linux machines or VMs. 3 running ZooKeeper. 3 running a Pulsar broker and a BookKeeper bookie."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Subject-Based Messaging**

- "There is no hard limit to subject size, but it is recommended to keep the maximum number of tokens in your subjects to a reasonable value. E.g. a maximum of 16 tokens and the subject length to less than 256 characters."
- "NATS can manage 10s of millions of subjects efficiently"; subjects are ephemeral and disappear when no longer subscribed.
- Subscriptions are cached in server memory: "when increasing your subscribed subject count to more than one million you will need more than 1GB of server memory and it will grow linearly from there."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Publish-Subscribe / Messages**

- `max_payload` default is 1 MB, "can be increased up to 64 MB if needed (though we recommend keeping the max message size to something more reasonable like 8 MB)."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Queueing / Pub-Sub / Request-Reply walkthroughs, Walkthrough setup**

- Server listens for clients on TCP 4222; `-m 8222` enables HTTP monitoring.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream (concept overview)**

- Stream limits: max message age, max total bytes, max message count, max individual message size, max number of consumers.
- Replication guidance: "Replicas=1 - Cannot operate during an outage of the server servicing the stream. Highly performant." "Replicas=2 - No significant benefit at this time. We recommend using Replicas=3 instead." "Replicas=3 - Can tolerate the loss of one server ... An ideal balance". "Replicas=4 - No significant benefit over Replicas=3 except marginally in a 5 node cluster." "Replicas=5 - Can tolerate simultaneous loss of two servers ... at the expense of performance."
- File streams flush writes to the OS synchronously but by default do not fsync immediately; `sync_interval` default is 2 minutes; "The data will be fsync-ed no later than this interval."
- Object Store stores arbitrarily large objects by chunking, versus values "limited to 1Mb by default".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Streams**

- Replicas max is 5. MaxAge and DuplicateWindow are in nanoseconds. MaxConsumers `-1` = unlimited. MaxMsgSize counts payload plus headers.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Consumers**

- MaxAckPending default is 1000; -1 means unlimited (no flow control); applies across all bound subscriptions; delivery is suspended at the limit.
- MaxDeliver default is -1 (redeliver until acked); messages at max delivery count "will stay in the stream."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Example configuration (ORDERS)**

- Example: `--max-age=1y --storage file --retention limits --max-msgs=-1 --max-bytes=-1 --max-msg-size=-1 --discard=old`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Source and Mirror Streams**

- One stream can be origin for many streams: "fan out topologies where data needs to be distributed reliable to a large number (up to millions) of client connections."
- Recovery interval after a disconnect is 10-20s.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Key/Value store (concept)**

- Bucket limits: max bucket size, max single value size, TTL. History default is 1 (only latest value/operation stored).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Source and Mirror configuration example**

- Example shows `duplicate_window: 120000000000` ns (2 minutes).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream walkthrough**

- CLI defaults when creating a stream: storage file, replication 1, retention limits, discard old, all limits -1 (unlimited), duplicate window 2m0s, rollups no, deletion allowed, purge allowed, "Direct Get: true".
- Consumer defaults shown: Ack Wait 30.00s, Max Ack Pending 1,000, Max Waiting Pulls 512.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Subject Mapping and Transforms**

- At extreme publish rates "a single nats-server process is acting as the RAFT leader (coordinator) for any given stream and can therefore become a limiting factor"; partition into several smaller streams so leaders spread across JetStream servers.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — KV walkthrough / Object Store walkthrough**

- Default bucket: History Kept 1, unlimited bucket size/value size/age, backing stream `KV_<name>`, file storage.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Clustering Configuration**

- `connect_retries` default `0` (no retry) for discovered routes; when enabled, attempts once per second. `connect_backoff` (2.12.0) starts at 1s up to 30s.
- `pool_size` default `3`; `compression` default `accept`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — v2 Routes**

- Before 2.10.0 two servers shared a single route connection for all accounts, "which could lead to slow down and increased memory usage"; 2.10.0+ creates 3 route connections by default (`pool_size`).
- Route compression (2.10.0) uses S2; default off (mode `accept` doesn't initiate). Modes: off, accept, s2_fast, s2_better, s2_best, s2_auto. Modes need not match between peers.
- `s2_auto` default `rtt_thresholds: [10ms, 50ms, 100ms]`: under 10ms none, then s2_fast, s2_better, s2_best.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Clustering**

- "A quorum is 1/2 cluster size + 1": cluster of 3 needs at least 2 JetStream servers up to store new messages; cluster of 5 needs 3.
- "Generally, we recommend 3 or 5 JetStream enabled servers in a NATS cluster." With 5, place 2+2+1 across three zones so "you can lose any one 'zone' at any time and continue operating."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Administration (cluster)**

- When choosing replicas "we suggest 1, 3 or 5". Replica count can be edited after creation.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Super-cluster with Gateways**

- Each node makes one outbound connection to a single node in every remote cluster; with 3 gateway nodes locally there are 3 outbound connections per remote cluster. Cluster connections are N(N-1)/2; for 3 clusters of 5 nodes: full mesh 105 vs gateway 30; of 30 nodes: 4005 vs 180.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Gateway Configuration**

- `connect_retries` default 0 (once per second when enabled); `connect_backoff` (2.12.0) 1s to 30s.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Leaf Nodes**

- Default leaf node port is 7422.
- NGS free account example limits: 10 connections, leaf nodes not allowed, 1.0 GB data, 2 exports, 7 imports, 1.0 kB max payload, 10 subscriptions.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — LeafNode Configuration**

- Leaf `compression` defaults to `s2_auto` (unlike routes which default to accept).
- `first_info_timeout` default `1s` prevents waiting forever when the port isn't a leaf-accepting NATS server.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream on Leaf Nodes (domains)**

- 2021 CLI output shows a pull consumer default Max Ack Pending of 20,000 (contradicts 1,000 in newer walkthrough output, nats-concepts/jetstream/js_walkthrough.md).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Configuring JetStream (resource management)**

- Resources are dynamically determined by default, but "It's recommended that you set specific limits": example `max_mem: 1G`, `max_file: 100G`, `domain: acme`.
- Since v2.10.21 "the NATS JetStream API has a limit of 10K inflight requests after which it will start to drop requests"; tunable via `request_queue_limit` (example 1000). "When the request limit is reached, all pending requests are dropped". Log: "JetStream API queue limit reached, dropping N requests"; advisory `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.API.LIMIT_REACHED`; clients must retry.
- `limits { max_ha_assets }` caps the number of R3/R5 streams and consumers per server (example 2000).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Configuration (server config reference)**

- Numbers support units: 1K = 1000, 1KB = 1024. String values starting with a digit must be quoted (e.g. `token: "3secret"`).
- Defaults: `host 0.0.0.0`, `port 4222`; no TLS by default; gateway/leafnodes/mqtt/websocket/cluster inactive by default.
- `ping_interval` default `2m`, `ping_max` 2; "it is recommended to keep this value bigger than what clients use". `write_deadline` default `10s`: exceeding it closes the connection (slow consumer).
- Limits defaults: `max_connections 64K`, `max_control_line 4KB` (subject plus queue group), `max_payload 1MB` ("It is not recommended to use values over 8MB but max_payload can be set up to 64MB"; must be <= `max_pending`), `max_pending 64MB` per client connection, `max_subscriptions 0` unlimited.
- JetStream server defaults: `store_dir /tmp/nats/jetstream`, `max_memory_store` 75% of available memory, `max_file_store 1TB`, `max_outstanding_catchup 64MB` (2.9.0), `max_buffered_msgs 10.000` and `max_buffered_size 128MB` (2.11.0, OOM protection during write bursts), `request_queue_limit 10.000` (2.11.0), `sync_interval 2m` (2.10.0), `strict true` (2.11.0).
- `sync_interval`: "By default JetStream relies on stream replication in the cluster to guarantee data is available after an OS crash. If you run JetStream without replication or with a replication of just 2 you may want to shorten the fsync/sync interval." `always` "will slow down the throughput to a few hundred msg/s."
- Account JetStream settings: `max_memory`/`max_file` (sums must be under the server limit), `max_streams`, `max_consumers` ("per stream(!)"), `max_ack_pending` (2.8.0), `max_bytes_required` (2.7.0, default false), `store_max_stream_bytes`/`memory_max_stream_bytes` (2.8.0).
- Server-wide `limits`: `max_ack_pending`, `max_ha_assets` (RAFT assets per node; not counting R1), `max_request_batch` ("Use with caution. May break existing clients"), `duplicate_window` (max allowed; "default for new streams is 120s").
- `lame_duck_duration` default `2m` ("cannot be set lower than 30 seconds"); `lame_duck_grace_period` default `10s`; started with `nats-server --signal ldm`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Authentication (intro), timeout, tokens, username/password, NKeys, TLS auth**

- Auth `timeout` default is 1 second more than `tls_timeout`; invalid values default to 1s; numeric seconds only (fractional ok). "long timeouts can be an opportunity for abuse"; must exceed the TLS timeout since it includes the TLS upgrade.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Enabling TLS**

- TLS defaults: `min_version "1.2"`, handshake `timeout` 2 seconds; `ca_file` absent = system trust store; `insecure` skips verification for outgoing connections only and is "NOT Recommended".
- TLS `timeout`: increase if clients disconnect during handshake, but "an extended timeout exposes your server to attacks where a client doesn't upgrade to TLS and thus consumes resources."
- `connection_rate_limit` (2.7.0) caps new TLS client connections per second server-wide (example 1000); excess get "Connection throttling is active. Please try again later."; default 0 disables; not applied to cluster/gateway/leaf/websocket/MQTT listeners. Rationale: "TLS handshakes are expensive, and a burst of reconnecting clients can keep the server busy".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Account lookup using Resolver / Memory Resolver**

- `full` resolver: `allow_delete` (default false; deletes rename to `.delete`), `interval "2m"` state comparison with one random peer, `limit 1000` JWTs. "Not every server in a cluster needs to be set to full. You need enough to still serve your workload adequately, while some servers are offline."
- `cache` resolver: LRU subset, `limit 1000`, `ttl "2m"`; "does NOT accept account push messages from nsc and therefore is not suitable for stand-alone operation without a full resolver present."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Upgrading a Cluster**

- "The support policy for the server is the current release as well as one patch version release prior" (e.g. 2.8.4 -> 2.8.3 downgrade supported); earlier downgrades "may work, but is not recommended." Downgrade path = same rolling procedure.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Lame Duck Mode**

- LDM: stop accepting new connections, 10 second grace period, then evict clients over `lame_duck_duration` (default 2 minutes).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Slow Consumers**

- `write_deadline` can be raised (example `2s`) for bursts, but "Be sure you are not just postponing a slow consumer error." "Increasing buffer sizes is not typically recommended unless you are handling temporary bursts of data. Often, increasing buffer capacity will only postpone slow consumer problems."
- Default subscriber pending limits: `65536` messages and `65536*1024` bytes; on reaching them the client drops messages and continues ("aligned with NATS at most once delivery"); the app must detect and recover. A local error doesn't mean the server flagged the subscription.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Naming Streams, Consumers, and Accounts**

- Guidelines: alphanumeric; no spaces/tabs/`.`/`>`/`*`; no path separators; "keep names under 32 characters"; avoid reserved file names (NUL, LPT1); "some file systems are case insensitive so do not use stream or account names that would collide" (`Foo` vs `foo` on Windows/macOS).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Disaster Recovery**

- Example backup: 813 MiB uncompressed became 13 MiB compressed in 3368 chunks.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Encryption at Rest**

- Performance cost observed from "as little as 1% decrease to more than 30%" on a MacBook Pro test; encrypted files may be larger.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Monitoring (endpoints reference)**

- `/connz` pages 1024 connections by default; "The server will default to holding the last 10,000 closed connections."
- Sample `/varz` shows defaults: max_connections 65536, ping_interval 120s, ping_max 2, auth_timeout 1, max_control_line 4096, max_payload 1048576, max_pending 67108864, tls_timeout 0.5 (older default), write_deadline 2s (older default; config page says 10s). Records: contradicts running-a-nats-service/configuration/README.md (`write_deadline` 10s) and tls.md (timeout 2s).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Running a NATS service (introduction)**

- Server binary is "less than 20 MB"; runs from Raspberry Pi to large servers, bare metal, VMs, containers.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Environmental considerations**

- In public clouds "you get what you pay for": non-network-optimized instances may give 10 Gb/s for ~30 minutes then drop (e.g. to 5 Gb/s); choose network-optimized instances for sustained bandwidth. Local SSD gives best latency; network block storage (EBS) can give highest throughput but general-purpose tiers burst then drop IOPS; choose IO-optimized storage for sustained IOPS.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Installing (hardware requirements)**

- "The NATS server itself has minimal hardware requirements to support small edge devices".
- "For high throughput use cases, the network interface card (NIC) or the available bandwidth are often the bottleneck".
- Core NATS minimums (containers, GOMEMLIMIT at 90%): 1 core / 32 MiB handles 100 publishers at 1000 msg/s each (100,000 msg/s total) on a single server; 3-node cluster 1 core / 32-64 MiB at 100,000 msg/s total.
- JetStream minimums (file storage, R3 on 3 nodes, pull consumers): 1 core / 32 MiB for 1,000 msg/s; 1 core / 64 MiB for 10,000 msg/s; 3 nodes 1 core / 256 MiB for 100,000 msg/s. "these are minimum configurations".
- "For production deployment of JetStream, we recommend starting with at least 4 CPU cores and 8 GiB of memory".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — NATS and Docker / JetStream in Docker / NGS leaf nodes in Docker / Swarm**

- The Docker image is "under 10 MB"; default ports 4222 (clients), 8222 (monitoring), 6222 (routes); the image protects routes with credentials `ruser:T0pS3cr3t` by default.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — WebSocket Configuration**

- WebSocket `handshake_timeout` example `2s` includes the TLS handshake; `compression` requires both sides to support it.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — MQTT**

- QoS 1/2 redelivery after `ack_wait` (default 30 seconds); `max_ack_pending` valid 0..65535, session total cannot exceed 65535, `#` subscriptions count double; changes apply only to new subscriptions.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — FAQ**

- `max_payload` default 1 MB, max 64 MB, "we recommend keeping the max message size to something more reasonable like 8 MB."
- "As of nats-server v0.8.0, there is no hard limit on the maximum number of subjects."
- Default max connections per server is 65,536; "Most systems can handle several thousand NATS connections per server without any changes" but OS limits (e.g. macOS) and TCP buffer sizes may need tuning.
- With clusters, superclusters and leaf nodes "one can build a NATS deployment supporting many millions of connections."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Automatic Reconnections**

- Go defaults: `Timeout` 2s dial; `PingInterval` 2 minutes; `MaxPingsOut` 2 (then ErrStaleConnection); `AllowReconnect` true; `MaxReconnect` 60 (negative = forever); `ReconnectWait` 2s; `ReconnectJitter` 100ms (no TLS); `ReconnectJitterTLS` 1s; `ReconnectBufSize` 8 MiB ("Once this has been exhausted publish operations will return an error"); `RetryOnFailedConnect` false.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Connecting to a Cluster / timeouts / misc / name / noecho / ping-pong / security**

- Ping interval x max pings outstanding sets how fast a stale connection is detected, including partitions the OS doesn't notice; default interval "is typically on the order of minutes"; example: interval 20s and 5 max pings closes after 100s. The server doesn't initiate PING/PONG while traffic flows.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Receiving: async, sync, drain, queues, unsubscribe, wildcards, structure**

- "the timeout for drain should generally be higher than the timeout for a simple message request-reply".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Developing with JetStream**

- "Using streaming and its associated higher qualities of service is the facet of messaging with the highest cost in terms of compute and storage."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Getting Started / Using Source**

- `-js` defaults "to 1TB of disk and 75% of available memory".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Model Deep Dive**

- `MaxMsgSize` can cap stream messages below the server's 1 MiB default (e.g. 1024 bytes).
- File storage per-message overhead without headers: record length 4 + seq 8 + ts 8 + subj_len 2 + subject + payload + hash 8; "A 5 byte hello message without headers will take 39 bytes." With headers add hdr_len 4 + headers.
- "if you are publishing many small messages the overhead will be, relatively speaking, quite large ... it's worth trying to optimize the subject length."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Consumers (developer guide)**

- "Pull consumers create less CPU load on the NATS servers and therefore scale better"; the difference shows "if you have sustained high message rates."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Key Value Store (developer guide) / Object Store (developer guide)**

- History default 1; "The maximum history size is 64, if you need more your use case will be better implemented using the Stream functionality directly (where you can set the max number of messages per subject to any value you want)".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — NATS API Reference (JetStream wire API)**

- Source/mirror retries consumer creation "every 10s to 60s" when the origin is unreachable; active consumers heartbeat at 1/s.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — nats bench (benchmarking guide)**

- Example numbers (single laptop, 2.12.1): core publish with no subscriber 14.8M msgs/s at 16 bytes; sync request-reply latency ~50.87 microseconds; larger messages lower msg/s but raise byte throughput.
- `nats bench js pub sync` is for latency, "not good to measure throughput"; `async` batches with acks measures throughput; `batch` (atomic) "has the side effect of potentially helping throughout, especially for smaller messages."
- Example replay: ordered ephemeral consumer 1.2M msgs/s (128 B); durable fetch with 2 clients 1.13M msgs/s aggregate; sync direct get ~33k/s at ~30 microseconds; KV put ~30k/s, KV get 16 clients ~103k/s aggregate.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — WebSocket (overview) / Windows Service / Server flags**

- Flags: `-a` binds `0.0.0.0` by default; `-p` 4222; `--tls` enables TLS without client verification; `--no_advertise` stops advertising cluster info to clients.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Legacy: NATS Streaming (STAN) and nats-account-server**

- STAN clustering is not horizontally scalable (single leader); "The cluster size should probably be limited to 3 to 5 nodes"; odd number, minimum three "to avoid split-brain".

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-1: JetStream JSON API Design**

- Paged APIs (e.g. `$JS.API.STREAM.NAMES`) return `total`, `offset`, `limit`; default page limit shown is 1024; pass `{"offset": N}` to page.
- Sequence fields are unsigned 64-bit ("JetStream can store up to the limit of an unsigned 64bit integer messages"); this "exceeds what is possible with JSON, languages might need to have custom JSON parsers."
- Some fields are platform-dynamic (e.g. `max_deliver`): "in practise you have to assume they are 64bit integer."
- `max_msg_size` is a signed 32-bit integer, min -1 (unlimited), max 2147483647.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-4: NATS Message Headers**

- Field names must be printable ASCII 33-126 except colon; field body any ASCII except CR/LF.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-6: Naming Rules**

- `stream-name`, `durable-name`, `consumer-name`, `account-name` are `filename-safe`: printable except dot, asterisk, gt, fwd-slash, backslash, "maximum 255 characters"; on Windows also excludes `< : " | ?`. "The server will reject names (return an API error) when it cannot build a valid path."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-7: NATS Server Error Codes**

- Error code ranges: `1xxxx` JetStream, `2xxxx` MQTT.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-13: Pull Subscribe internals**

- Pull request body fields: `batch` (min 1, "There is not a limit on the batch size at the level of the library"), `no_wait` (bool, default false), `expires` (ns from now; <= 0 means no expiry). "No wait takes precedence over expires if both are supplied."
- "At most, a consumer can only have 512 inflight pull requests, though this can be changed when creating the consumer with the `max_waiting` option." `num_waiting` in consumer info counts inflight pulls.
- Example consumer defaults shown: `ack_wait` 30s, `max_deliver` -1, `max_waiting` 512, `max_ack_pending` 20000.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-17: Ordered Consumer**

- Forced config: ack_policy none, max_deliver 1, flow_control true, mem_storage true, num_replicas 1; defaults `idle_heartbeat` 5s, `ack_wait` "something large like 22 hours."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-15: JetStream Subscribe Workflow [STALE?]**

- Heartbeat alarm: "The time allowed before an alarm is raised should be 3 times the idle heartbeat interval."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-20: JetStream based Object Stores**

- Default chunk size: "128k (128 * 1024)"; "Clients may tune this as appropriate." Can be overridden per object via `max_chunk_size`.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-21: NATS Configuration Contexts**

- Context keys: `url` (default `nats://localhost:4222`, comma-separated), `token`, `user`, `password`, `creds`, `nkey`, `cert`, `key`, `ca`, `nsc`, `jetstream_domain`, `jetstream_api_prefix`, `jetstream_event_prefix`, `inbox_prefix`, `user_jwt`, `tls_first`, `windows_cert_store`, `windows_cert_match_by`, `windows_cert_match`, `windows_ca_certs_match`. All optional, none `omitempty`.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-22: JetStream Publish Retries on No Responders**

- Go default retry: "waits for `250ms` and will retry 2 times sending the message (so that in total it would have attempted to send the message 3 times)." Options `RetryWait`, `RetryAttempts`; `RetryAttempts(-1)` retries until the context/AckWait deadline.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-26: NATS Authorization Callouts**

- Example config uses `authorization { timeout: 1s ... }`.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-31: JetStream Direct Get**

- `allow_direct` default `false`, opt-in; "The server does not enable it implicitly"; KV helper sets it for buckets. Auto-promotion on `max_msgs_per_subject > 0` "existed only briefly and was removed in server v2.9.0."
- Batched requests send "multiple messages without any flow control"; if `max_bytes` unset "the server will use the `max_pending` configuration setting or the server default (currently 64MB)."
- Multi-subject get "may only allow matching up to 1024 subjects. Any more will result in a `413` status reply."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-32: Service API**

- Service `name` "can only have `A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dash, underscore`"; `version` must be validated as SemVer with the official regex; `metadata` "Must be immutable once set."
- "All service request handlers operate under the default queue group `q`" so scaling = add/stop instances; use different `queueGroup` to fan out a request to multiple instances for fastest responder. Endpoints may opt out of queue groups (normal subscribe).

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-33: Metadata for Stream and Consumer**

- "the size of it is limited to 128KB. Size is equal to len of all keys and values summed."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-36: Subject Mapping Transforms in Streams**

- Example configs show `duplicate_window: 120000000000` (2 minutes) as the default dedup window.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-37: JetStream Simplification**

- "pull requests issued by clients should have client-side timeouts in addition to server-side timeout (`expiry`). Client-side timeout value should always be larger than expiry."
- Consume defaults: `max_messages` "probably between 100 and 1000"; `expires` default 30s, minimum 1s; `idle_heartbeat` = 1/2 of expires, min 500ms, max 30s; `threshold_messages` 50% of max_messages; `threshold_bytes` 50% of max_bytes. Must work when `max_messages` is 1.
- Message size for byte accounting = `len(subject) + len(ackReply) + len(hdr) + len(msg)` (server's formula, transport subject excluded).
- "`Consume()` should always use idle heartbeats"; warning if timer reaches "2 * request's idle_heartbeat"; timer reset on any message; "Heartbeat errors are not terminal."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-38: OCSP Peer Verification**

- `ocsp_peer` in a `tls` map: short form bool (default false) or long form with `verify` (false), `ca_timeout` (2s), `allowed_clockskew` (30s), `warn_only` (false), `unknown_is_good` (false), `allow_when_ca_unreachable` (false), `cache_ttl_when_next_update_unset` (3600s).
- `ocsp_cache`: default `true`/`local` when any listener has ocsp_peer; long form `type` (local|none), `local_store` (default `_rc_`, "Setting a fully qualified directory path for `local_store` is recommended"), `preserve_revoked` (false), `save_interval` (300s, min 1s).

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-40: NATS Connection**

- `handshake_first` values: `false` (default), `true` (enforced; "Clients that do not use this flow will fail to connect"), a duration (hybrid wait), `auto` ("By default it waits 50ms for TLS upgrade before sending the INFO").
- Defaults: ping interval 2 minutes; max pings out 2; retry on failed initial connect false; max reconnects "3 / none" ("can also be a footgun and surprise for users who do not expect that the client can give up entirely"); connection timeout 5s; tls required false; ignore advertised servers false; retain servers order false.
- `Maximum Payload Violation` → disconnect; "clients should test payload sizes and fail publishes that exceed the server configuration." `maximum subscriptions exceeded` "is not terminal to the connection."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-42: Pull Consumer Priority Groups**

- "In the initial implementation we should limit `PriorityGroups` to one per consumer only and error should one be made with multiple groups." Group names must match ADR-6 `limited-term` "and may not exceed 16 characters."
- Pull fields: `group` (mandatory; unknown group = error), `min_pending`, `min_ack_pending`, `failover` (seconds; min 5, max 3600; nearest failover value wins; nearer pulls reset timers). "As of NATS Server 2.14 the `failover` option is not implemented; the server silently ignores the field."
- "The `PriorityTimeout` is recommended to be sufficiently above the `Expires` value of the pull request"; with 2-minute timeout "a recommended maximum value of `Expires` could be 1 minute"; a new pull acts as a liveness heartbeat for the pin.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-43: JetStream Per-Message TTL**

- Unparsable values, or durations "below the 1 second minimum (including a literal `0`)", cause an error in the Pub Ack and the message is discarded (err_code 10165 `invalid per-message TTL`). Publishing `Nats-TTL` to a stream with the feature disabled → 10166 `per-message TTL is disabled`.
- "Unless `MaxMsgsPer` equals 1 the server treats `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` as the minimum effective `Nats-TTL`. A publish with a `Nats-TTL` below this floor is **not** rejected — instead the server raises the effective TTL to the floor and rewrites the stored `Nats-TTL` header."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-44: Versioning for JetStream Assets**

- API Support Level: 0 = < 2.11.0, 1 = 2.11.x, 2 = 2.12.x; "we do not require strict SemVer adherence" (may bump mid-release). Advertised in `jsz`, `varz`, `$JS.API.INFO`, and logged at JetStream startup.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-47: Request Many**

- Config: total timeout (always used; defaults to connection request timeout; first wait always uses total); stall timer (optional; "Less than 1 or greater than or equal to the total timeout behaves the same as if not supplied"); max messages; sentinel predicate ("standard sentinel ... a message with a null/nil or empty payload").
- Strategies: "Timeout or Wait" (default, total only); "Stall" ("lessor of 1/10th of the total wait time ... or the default connection timeout"); "Max Responses".

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-50: JetStream Batch Publishing**

- Batch ID max 64 characters (err 10179); missing sequence 10175; sequence exceeds server limit "default 1000" (10199); batch not enabled 10174; incomplete/abandoned 10176; unsupported header `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` 10177; duplicate `Nats-Msg-Id` inside a batch 10201.
- Atomic server limits: "Each stream can only have 50 batches in flight"; "Each server can only have 1,000 batches in flight"; abandoned after "10 seconds since the last message" (advisory, no error reply); "Each batch can have maximum 1000 messages."
- Outstanding acks guidance: 1 = flow-controlled async; "Outstanding acks = 2 ... generally optimal"; 3 only for high RTT "not a default".
- Fast-ingest errors: 10205 not enabled, 10206 invalid pattern, 10207 ID > 64, 10208 unknown ID. Limits: "Each stream can only have 1,000 batches in flight"; "Each server can only have 50,000 batches in flight"; 10 s idle abandon; "no maximum size for fast ingest batches"; "`PersistMode: async` set are compatible with fast ingest."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-51: JetStream Message Scheduler**

- Cron is 6-field (seconds first); predefined `@yearly/@annually`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily/@midnight`, `@hourly`; `@every <go duration>` "The minimum supported interval is `1s`; shorter intervals are rejected."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-53: Feature flags**

- Flag table: `js_ack_fc_v2` = "Use domain/account-aware JetStream ACK and FC subjects (ADR-15 v2 format)", type Opt-in, introduced 2.14, default flip TBD. In 2.14 the server "uses the V1 ack/fc format by default, but supports parsing the V2 format."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-56: JetStream Consistency Models**

- "Setting it on anything other than a R1 stream will result in an error"; stated verbatim: "Scaling a R1 stream up to greater resiliency levels will fail if the `PersistMode` is not set to `async`" (ADR wording; reads as if intended "is set to async"). Default is unset/`default` and the server leaves it unset in INFO; any explicit value requires API level 2.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-8: JetStream based Key-Value Stores**

- History: "The maximum allowed size is 64. The minimum allowed size is 1. When creating a stream, 1 should be used when the user does not supply a value."
- TTL via `max_age`; if set: "if `max_age` is greater than 2 minutes, `duplicate_window` must be set to 2 minutes"; "if `max_age` is less than or equal to 2 minutes, `duplicate_window` must be set the same as `max_age`"; if no TTL "The server will set it to 2 minutes if not supplied." (Note: server applies this logic itself if `duplicate_window` is omitted.)
- Fixed stream settings: `discard: new`, `rollup_hdrs: true`, `deny_delete: true`, `allow_direct: true` ("can be modified out-of-band only if desired, but not through KV bucket update"); `max_msg_size` caps value size; `max_bytes` caps bucket; "Maximum number of keys cannot currently be limited"; placement, republish, metadata allowed; compression → `s2`; storage file; R value varies.
- Limit markers need `allow_msg_ttl: true` and `subject_delete_marker_ttl` > 1 s; require API level 1 (2.11+) "clients should assert this using the `$JS.API.INFO` call or similar means (not connected server version)."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-59: JetStream Stream Sourcing and Mirroring**

- Internal replication consumers have "a short inactive threshold (10 seconds)."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-61: Unsafe meta group quorum rescue for disaster recovery**

- On accept: lowers effective quorum, "starts a 5 minute rescue timeout", logs WARN and emits advisory `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.SERVER.META_RESCUE` (`io.nats.jetstream.advisory.v1.meta_rescue` with `prev_quorum`, `new_quorum`, cluster, domain). During rescue, empty-log peers' votes count only when the candidate has data.
- Rejection error code `10224` (400) "JetStream system rescue not applied: {err}" (leader known, not voting member, empty log, out of bounds, node closed).

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — Core protocol and connection defaults (server/const.go)**

- Server version string in this checkout. `VERSION = "2.15.0-dev"` (server/const.go:69)
- Wire protocol version; proto 1 adds client `echo` in CONNECT. `PROTO = 1` (server/const.go:75); comment: "Clients should not send echo unless proto in INFO is >= 1." (server/const.go:72-73)
- Default client port. `DEFAULT_PORT = 4222` (server/const.go:78); default host all interfaces `DEFAULT_HOST = "0.0.0.0"` (server/const.go:86)
- Maximum protocol control line. `MAX_CONTROL_LINE_SIZE = 4096` bytes; comment "4k should be plenty since payloads sans connect/info string are separate." (server/const.go:88-90)
- Default maximum message payload. `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = (1024 * 1024)` = 1 MiB; comment "Should be using something different if > 1MB payloads are needed." (server/const.go:92-94)
- Server warns when max_payload is set above 8 MiB and may reject it in future. `MAX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE = (8 * 1024 * 1024)`; comment "the size at which the server will warn about max_payload being too high. In the future, the server may enforce/reject max_payload above this value." (server/const.go:96-99)
- Default maximum outbound pending bytes per client before slow-consumer disconnect. `MAX_PENDING_SIZE = (64 * 1024 * 1024)` = 64 MiB (server/const.go:101-102)
- Default max connections. `DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS = (64 * 1024)` = 65536 (server/const.go:105)
- TLS handshake wait time. `TLS_TIMEOUT = 2 * time.Second` (server/const.go:108); leafnode TLS timeout same `DEFAULT_LEAF_TLS_TIMEOUT = 2 * time.Second` (server/const.go:165)
- TLS-handshake-first fallback delay before server sends INFO first. `DEFAULT_TLS_HANDSHAKE_FIRST_FALLBACK_DELAY = 50 * time.Millisecond` (server/const.go:114)
- Authorization wait time. `AUTH_TIMEOUT = 2 * time.Second` (server/const.go:117)
- Ping interval to clients and max outstanding pings before disconnect. `DEFAULT_PING_INTERVAL = 2 * time.Minute`, `DEFAULT_PING_MAX_OUT = 2` (server/const.go:120-123)
- Write/flush deadline. `DEFAULT_FLUSH_DEADLINE = 10 * time.Second` (server/const.go:132)
- Default monitoring HTTP port. `DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT = 8222` (server/const.go:135)
- Route solicitation: initial 1s, backing off to max 30s; reconnect delay 1s; dial timeout 1s. `DEFAULT_ROUTE_CONNECT = 1 * time.Second`, `DEFAULT_ROUTE_CONNECT_MAX = 30 * time.Second`, `DEFAULT_ROUTE_RECONNECT = 1 * time.Second`, `DEFAULT_ROUTE_DIAL = 1 * time.Second` (server/const.go:147-156)
- Route connection pool size default (connections per route peer). `DEFAULT_ROUTE_POOL_SIZE = 3` (server/const.go:159)
- Leafnode reconnect interval 1s; leafnode INFO wait 1s; default leafnode port 7422. `DEFAULT_LEAF_NODE_RECONNECT = time.Second` (server/const.go:162), `DEFAULT_LEAFNODE_INFO_WAIT = 1 * time.Second` (server/const.go:203), `DEFAULT_LEAFNODE_PORT = 7422` (server/const.go:206)
- Closed-connection history retained for /connz. `DEFAULT_MAX_CLOSED_CLIENTS = 10000` (server/const.go:192)
- Lame duck mode: clients closed spread over 2 minutes, after a 10 second grace period. `DEFAULT_LAME_DUCK_DURATION = 2 * time.Minute` (server/const.go:196), `DEFAULT_LAME_DUCK_GRACE_PERIOD = 10 * time.Second` (server/const.go:200)
- Failed route/gateway/leaf connect attempts logged every 3600 attempts (~hourly) for never-connected endpoints; every attempt (1) for reconnects. `DEFAULT_CONNECT_ERROR_REPORTS = 3600`, `DEFAULT_RECONNECT_ERROR_REPORTS = 1` (server/const.go:208-220)
- RTT measurement interval to clients/routes/gateways/leafs. `DEFAULT_RTT_MEASUREMENT_INTERVAL = time.Hour` (server/const.go:224)
- `allow_responses` permission defaults: 1 response, 2 minute expiry. `DEFAULT_ALLOW_RESPONSE_MAX_MSGS = 1`, `DEFAULT_ALLOW_RESPONSE_EXPIRATION = 2 * time.Minute` (server/const.go:228-232)
- Service export response threshold (time server expects a service response to be delivered; drives cleanup of reverse mappings). `DEFAULT_SERVICE_EXPORT_RESPONSE_THRESHOLD = 2 * time.Minute` (server/const.go:237)
- Service latency sampling default 100%. `DEFAULT_SERVICE_LATENCY_SAMPLING = 100` (server/const.go:241)
- Account resolver fetch timeout. `DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 1900 * time.Millisecond` (server/const.go:250)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream consumer defaults (server/consumer.go, server/jetstream_api.go)**

- Default AckWait for explicit/all ack consumers. `JsAckWaitDefault = 30 * time.Second` (server/consumer.go:572); applied when `config.AckWait == 0 && (AckExplicit || AckAll)` (server/consumer.go:649-650)
- Default inactive threshold before an ephemeral consumer is deleted. `JsDeleteWaitTimeDefault = 5 * time.Second` (server/consumer.go:575). Comment: "Ephemerals will always have inactive thresholds." The effective timer adds 100ms + up to 900ms random jitter; pull consumers with an explicit threshold also get that jitter (server/consumer.go:1464-1481)
- Flow control default max outstanding pending bytes. `JsFlowControlMaxPending = 32 * 1024 * 1024` = 32 MiB (server/consumer.go:577)
- Default MaxAckPending for non-AckNone consumers when unset. `JsDefaultMaxAckPending = 1000`; lowered to server `jetstream.limits.max_ack_pending` or account `max_ack_pending` if those are smaller (server/consumer.go:579, 672-680)
- Default pinned-client TTL (grace before re-pin). `JsDefaultPinnedTTL = 2 * time.Minute` (server/consumer.go:582, 691-692)
- Default MaxWaiting (pull request wait queue) for pull consumers. `JSWaitQueueDefaultMax = 512` (server/jetstream_api.go:756; applied server/consumer.go:645-646)
- MaxDeliver default is -1 meaning unlimited; 0 is normalized to -1 (server/consumer.go:588-594)
- Priority group names: regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9/_=-]{1,16}$` (server/consumer.go:49)
- Ephemeral deletion retry schedule in clustered mode: start 30s, max 5min. `defaultConsumerNotActiveStartInterval = 30 * time.Second`, `defaultConsumerNotActiveMaxInterval = 5 * time.Minute` (server/consumer.go:2145-2148)
- Ack reply subject token counts: v1 = 9 tokens, v2 = 11 tokens. `expectedNumReplyTokensV1 = 9`, `expectedNumReplyTokensV2 = 11` (server/consumer.go:6129-6132)
- Pull request headers: `Nats-Pending-Messages`, `Nats-Pending-Bytes`, `Nats-Pin-Id` (server/consumer.go:43-45); batch-completed status `NATS/1.0 409 Batch Completed` (server/consumer.go:53)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream consumer validation rules (server/consumer.go checkConsumerCfg / addConsumerWithAssignment / checkNewConsumerConfig)**

- Description max 4 KiB. `JSMaxDescriptionLen = 4 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:381; consumer.go:786)
- Metadata total (sum of key+value lengths) max 128 KiB. `JSMaxMetadataLen = 128 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:385; consumer.go:966-972)
- Max consumers per stream enforced from stream `max_consumers` or the account limit, whichever is more restrictive ("if account limits is more restrictive than stream config we prefer the account limits") (server/consumer.go:1121-1136)
- Durable name max 255 chars. `JSMaxNameLen = 255` "Picked 255 as it seems to be a widely used file name limit" (server/jetstream_api.go:388-389; consumer.go:1216-1219)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream stream defaults and size constants (server/stream.go, server/jetstream.go, server/jetstream_api.go)**

- Maximum stream replicas. `StreamMaxReplicas = 5` (server/stream.go:730); rejected with "maximum replicas is 5" (server/stream.go:1733-1734). Replicas default to 1 when 0 (server/stream.go:1730-1731)
- Default duplicate (dedup) window. `StreamDefaultDuplicatesWindow = 2 * time.Minute` (server/stream.go:1674). Applied only when Duplicates==0 and stream is not a mirror/source; capped to MaxAge if MaxAge is shorter, and to server `jetstream.limits.duplicate_window` if set (server/stream.go:1776-1793)
- Storage defaults to file when unset (server/stream.go:1723-1724)
- MaxMsgs, MaxMsgsPer, MaxBytes, MaxMsgSize, MaxConsumers: 0 normalizes to -1 (unlimited) (server/stream.go:1740-1768)
- Stream/consumer name max 255 chars. `JSMaxNameLen = 255` (server/jetstream_api.go:389); description max 4096 `JSMaxDescriptionLen = 4 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:381); metadata max 128 KiB `JSMaxMetadataLen = 128 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:385)
- JetStream API request queue limit before the server reacts (drops/warns). `JSDefaultRequestQueueLimit = 10_000` (server/jetstream_api.go:393)
- Default JetStream store limits: max_file_store default 1 TiB `JetStreamMaxStoreDefault = 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024`; max_memory_store fallback 256 MiB `JetStreamMaxMemDefault = 1024 * 1024 * 256` "only used when we can't determine system memory" (server/jetstream.go:2716-2723)
- Dynamic JetStream config: when max_memory_store unset, uses 75% of system memory (or GOMEMLIMIT if lower): `jsc.MaxMemory = sysMem / 4 * 3`; when max_file_store unset, uses available disk of store dir `diskAvailable(jsc.StoreDir)`; no store_dir means os.TempDir()/nats/jetstream with warning "Temporary storage directory used, data could be lost on system reboot" (server/jetstream.go:2728-2768)
- Stream internal inbound queue caps: `streamDefaultMaxQueueMsgs = 100_000`, `streamDefaultMaxQueueBytes = 128 * 1024 * 1024` (server/stream.go:458-461)
- Batch publish limits: `streamDefaultMaxBatchTimeout = 10 * time.Second`; atomic batches `MaxAtomicBatchInflightPerStream = 50`, `MaxAtomicBatchInflightTotal = 1000`, `MaxAtomicBatchSize = 1000`; fast batches `MaxFastBatchInflightPerStream = 1000`, `MaxFastBatchInflightTotal = 50_000` (server/stream.go:464-473); overridable via `jetstream.limits` MaxBatchSize / MaxBatchInflightPerStream / MaxBatchInflightTotal (server/stream.go:7402-7424)
- Multi/batch direct get returns at most 1024 messages per request. `const maxAllowedResponses = 1024` "TODO(dlc) - Make configurable?" (server/stream.go:5991-5992)
- Per-message header block limited to 65535 bytes (`len(hdr) > math.MaxUint16` -> "header exceeds maximum") (server/stream.go:6962-6970)
- Stream max_msg_size defaults: if stream MaxMsgSize <= 0, falls back to account max payload, then server MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE (1 MiB); subject length estimate default 256 for wildcard-only streams `defaultMaxSubject = 256` (server/stream.go:1396-1427)
- Server max_payload is enforced on the JetStream publish path: header+payload must fit in `MaxPayload` (server/stream.go:6935-6947); stream max_msg_size checked on header+msg (server/stream.go:6951-6960)
- Source/mirror consumer heartbeat 1s; stalled check every 10s. `sourceHealthHB = 1 * time.Second`, `sourceHealthCheckInterval = 10 * time.Second` (server/stream.go:3118-3123)
- Mirror/source consumer re-setup retry: base backoff 5s * (2*fails), capped at 2 minutes; requests throttled to no more than one per 2s. `retryBackOff = 5 * time.Second`, `retryMaximum = 2 * time.Minute` (server/stream.go:3441-3454), `sourceConsumerRetryThreshold = 2 * time.Second` (server/stream.go:3925)
- Interest-retention consistency check runs every 2 minutes with 30s jitter. `defaultCheckInterestStateT = 2 * time.Minute`, `defaultCheckInterestStateJ = 30` (server/stream.go:8673-8676)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — RAFT (NRG) timing, quorum and backpressure (server/raft.go)**

- Election timeout is random in [4s, 9s]. `minElectionTimeoutDefault = 4 * time.Second`, `maxElectionTimeoutDefault = 9 * time.Second` (server/raft.go:298-299)
- Campaign timeout random in [100ms, 800ms]. `minCampaignTimeoutDefault = 100 * time.Millisecond`, `maxCampaignTimeoutDefault = 8 * minCampaignTimeoutDefault` (server/raft.go:300-301)
- Leader heartbeat interval 1s. `hbIntervalDefault = 1 * time.Second` (server/raft.go:302)
- Lost quorum is declared after 10s without quorum heartbeats and checked every 10s; lost-quorum advisory/signal every 20s. `lostQuorumIntervalDefault = hbIntervalDefault * 10`, `lostQuorumCheckIntervalDefault = hbIntervalDefault * 10`, `lostQuorumSignalIntervalDefault = 20 * time.Second` (server/raft.go:303-305)
- Observer-mode election timer 48h (an observer effectively never campaigns). `observerModeIntervalDefault = 48 * time.Hour` (server/raft.go:306)
- Peer remove timeout and unsafe quorum rescue timeout both 5 minutes. `peerRemoveTimeoutDefault = 5 * time.Minute`, `rescueQuorumTimeoutDefault = 5 * time.Minute` (server/raft.go:307-308)
- Leader steps down when overrun: more than 100,000 uncommitted OR more than 100,000 committed-but-unapplied entries. `pauseQuorumThreshold = 100_000` (server/raft.go:4966); comment "Stepping down means the system gets to 'breathe' for a bit, until a new leader can be elected." (server/raft.go:995-1011)
- Pending append-entry cache: warn at 10,000 (every 5,000), stop caching at 20,000. `paeDropThreshold = 20_000`, `paeWarnThreshold = 10_000`, `paeWarnModulo = 5_000` (server/raft.go:4967-4969, 5016-5028)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream cluster placement and catch-up (server/jetstream_cluster.go)**

- Placement rejects a peer when the stream's MaxBytes exceeds the peer's available storage for that storage type (available = MaxStore/MaxMemory minus max(reserved, used)) (server/jetstream_cluster.go:9510-9538)
- Placement rejects a peer whose HA asset count exceeds `jetstream.limits.max_ha_assets` (strictly >, because `_meta_` counts as one) (server/jetstream_cluster.go:9539-9544)
- Stream catch-up inactivity: start timeout 5s, activity timeout 30s. `defaultStreamCatchupStartInterval = 5 * time.Second`, `defaultStreamCatchupActivityInterval = 30 * time.Second` (server/jetstream_cluster.go:11893-11896); errors include "catchup stalled", "catchup failed, too many retries", "corrupt stream snapshot detected" (11882-11890)
- Stream migration check intervals 50ms fast / 500ms fallback (server/jetstream_cluster.go:5446-5449)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream file store sizing (server/filestore.go, server/store.go)**

- File store block sizes: limits-retention streams 8 MiB; work-queue/interest streams 4 MiB; KV 4 MiB; encrypted stores capped at 2 MiB ("large blocks can result in worsened perf since many writes on disk involve re-encrypting the entire block"). `defaultLargeBlockSize = 8 * 1024 * 1024`, `defaultMediumBlockSize = 4 * 1024 * 1024`, `defaultKVBlockSize = defaultMediumBlockSize`, `maximumEncryptedBlockSize = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (server/filestore.go:360-375, 809-843)
- When stream MaxBytes is set, block size = MaxBytes/4 + 1 ("25% overhead"), clamped to [32000 B, 8 MiB]; otherwise falls to 4 MiB in the middle range. `FileStoreMinBlkSize = 32 * 1000`, `FileStoreMaxBlkSize = maxBlockSize` (8 MiB) (server/filestore.go:378-381, 809-828)
- Background fsync interval default 2 minutes (`sync_interval`); write cache buffer expiry 10s; idle FDs closed after 30s; per-block subject index expires after 2 min idle; flush coalescing waits at most 8ms. `defaultSyncInterval = 2 * time.Minute`, `defaultCacheBufferExpiration = 10 * time.Second`, `closeFDsIdle = 30 * time.Second`, `defaultFssExpiration = 2 * time.Minute`, `maxFlushWait = 8 * time.Millisecond` (server/filestore.go:329-340)
- Compaction minimum threshold 2 MiB. `compactMinimum = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (server/filestore.go:376-377)
- Per-message on-disk overhead: 22-byte record header + 8-byte checksum (+ subject length + 4). `msgHdrSize = 22`, `checksumSize = 8`, `fileStoreMsgSizeEstimate = emptyRecordLen + slen + 4 + maxPayload` (server/filestore.go:1111-1114, 9722-9724)
- Store directory and file permissions 0700/0600 (server/filestore.go:163-166)
- Raft WAL replay on startup pauses apply when more than 32 MiB is queued. `const maxQsz = 32 * 1024 * 1024` (server/raft.go:575)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — Routes, gateways, leaf nodes (server/route.go, server/gateway.go, server/leafnode.go)**

- Route ping interval capped at 30s (below client default 2 min) because S2-auto compression uses RTT from ping/pong. `defaultRouteMaxPingInterval = 30 * time.Second` (server/route.go:132-141)
- Gateway timers: solicit delay 1s, connect delay 1s backing off to 30s max, reconnect 1s, recent-sub expiration 2s, ping at most every 15s regardless of traffic. `defaultSolicitGatewaysDelay = time.Second`, `defaultGatewayConnectDelay = time.Second`, `defaultGatewayConnectMaxDelay = 30 * time.Second`, `defaultGatewayReconnectDelay = time.Second`, `defaultGatewayRecentSubExpiration = 2 * time.Second`, `gwMaxPingInterval = 15 * time.Second` (server/gateway.go:35-58)
- Gateway switches an account from optimistic to interest-only after 1000 remote unsubs/no-interest notices. `defaultGatewayMaxRUnsubBeforeSwitch = 1000` (server/gateway.go:41)
- Leaf node reconnect delays: 30s after a loop is detected, 30s after a permission violation, 30s when leaf and hub share the same cluster name. `leafNodeReconnectDelayAfterLoopDetected = 30 * time.Second`, `leafNodeReconnectAfterPermViolation = 30 * time.Second`, `leafNodeReconnectDelayAfterClusterNameSame = 30 * time.Second` (server/leafnode.go:48-56)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — Client connection handling: slow consumers, stalls, buffers (server/client.go, server/opts.go)**

- Slow consumer by pending bytes: a CLIENT whose outbound pending exceeds max_pending (default 64 MiB) is closed with "Slow Consumer Detected: MaxPending of %d Exceeded" (server/client.go:2595-2612)
- Stall gate: when a client's outbound pending exceeds 75% of max_pending, fast producers publishing to it are stalled. `c.out.pb > c.out.mp/4*3` (server/client.go:2615-2621). Stall durations: 2ms minimum, 5ms when at/over the limit, at most 10ms total per readLoop pass. `stallClientMinDuration = 2 * time.Millisecond`, `stallClientMaxDuration = 5 * time.Millisecond`, `stallTotalAllowed = 10 * time.Millisecond` (server/client.go:124-127, 3708-3722)
- Slow consumer by write deadline: an i/o timeout on flush (write_deadline, default 10s) marks the connection slow consumer; routes count each event once; a write timeout before CONNECT is handled as slow consumer without incrementing the counter "as that can be misleading" (server/client.go:1944-1985)
- Per-connection read buffer grows from 512 B to 64 KiB and shrinks to 64 B; readLoop reports if a pass takes over 2s. `startBufSize = 512`, `minBufSize = 64`, `maxBufSize = 65536`, `readLoopReport = 2 * time.Second` (server/client.go:110-116)
- Server will not send an RTT PING before the first PONG, capped at 2s. `maxNoRTTPingBeforeFirstPong = 2 * time.Second` (server/client.go:118-122)
- Permission/result caches per client: 512 sublist results, 256 deny-perm, 128 perm entries; reply-permission tracking limit 4096 entries pruned every 1s. `maxResultCacheSize = 512`, `maxDenyPermCacheSize = 256`, `maxPermCacheSize = 128`, `replyPermLimit = 4096`, `replyPruneTime = time.Second` (server/client.go:471-479)
- On close, a minimal flush uses a 100ms write deadline. `lowWriteDeadline = 100 * time.Millisecond` (server/client.go:6002)
- Baseline option defaults (server/opts.go setBaselineOptions:5998-6190): max_connections 65536, ping_interval 2m, ping_max 2, tls timeout 2s, auth_timeout = tls timeout + 1s when TLS is configured else 2s (`getDefaultAuthTimeout` server/opts.go:6192-6200), cluster pool_size 3, max_control_line 4096, max_payload 1 MiB, max_pending 64 MiB, write_deadline 10s, max_closed_clients 10000, lame_duck_duration 2m, lame_duck_grace_period 10s, leafnode reconnect 1s, leafnode first_info_timeout 1s
- JetStream option defaults: max_memory_store -1 (dynamic), max_file_store -1 (dynamic), sync_interval 2m, request_queue_limit 10000, info queue limit = request queue limit, concurrent IOs 4096. `defaultConcurrentIOs = 4096` (server/dios.go:21; server/opts.go:6171-6189)
- Server-wide `jetstream.limits` fields: max_request_batch, max_ack_pending, max_ha_assets ("maximum of Streams and Consumers that may have more than 1 replica"), max_duplicate_window, max_batch_inflight_per_stream, max_batch_inflight_total, max_batch_size, max_batch_timeout (server/opts.go:375-384)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream account limits, reservations and naming (server/jetstream.go, server/server.go)**

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Partitioned Consumer Groups in NATS JetStream: Ordered, Scalable Processing**

- Effective parallelism = `min(partitions, members)`. Partition count is fixed at creation and immutable; members are cheap to add/remove up to that ceiling. A 5th member on 4 partitions idles as standby.
- Size partitions for peak future parallelism; raising later requires deleting the group and re-hashing every key.
- Cap the elastic work-queue buffer above one second of throughput; hitting `max_buffered_msgs`/`max_buffered_bytes` pauses sourcing for at least a second, causing periodic stalls.

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Supercluster with JetStream**

- The meta layer is a Raft group, so electing its leader needs a quorum; in practice the supercluster needs an odd number of servers in total. "Since this is a Raft group as well, electing a leader requires a quorum across servers. What this means in practice is that there needs to be an odd number of servers across the supercluster."
- JetStream superclusters should have at least three clusters, or use the arbiter pattern to reach an odd server count. "Supercluster deployments with JetStream-enabled servers should include at least three clusters or use the arbiter pattern."
- For production, run three nodes per cluster so that R3 streams can be created. "for a production deployment it is recommended to have three nodes per cluster to support R3 streams."
- Stream replicas never cross gateway connections; with one node per cluster only R1 streams can be created. "In this test setup, only R1 streams can be created since streams replicas do not cross gateway connections."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Regional and Cross Region Streams (Supercluster)**

- A three-node cross-region cluster has one node per region; if more AZs per region are wanted, a six- or nine-node cross-region cluster may be desirable. "If may be desirable to have a six or nine node cross-region cluster if more AZs per region are desired."
- Observed defaults in `nats server info` output (2.10.1): Max Payload 1.0 MiB, Max Conn 65,536, TLS Timeout 2.00s, Write Deadline 10.00s, JetStream "Always sync writes to disk: false", "Write sync Frequency: 2m0s".

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Regional and Cross Region Streams (Cluster)**

- NATS placement tags cannot express logical OR or exclusive OR, so valid replica combinations must be precomputed and encoded as tags on the servers. "NATS does not currently support declaring tags with logical OR (or exclusive OR), so valid combinations can be precomputed as tags and then used when creating streams."
- Each of the nine servers carries exactly two `xr:` tags (e.g. `rg1-az1` has `xr:123, xr:132`), so that every `xr:` combination matches exactly three servers, one per region.
- Observed output: in a nine-node full-mesh cluster each server shows `Routes 32` and `GWs 0`; the seed routes list only three nodes and the rest discover each other.

In practice, the wait time would be dependent on how much data needs to be migrated."
