## ANTI: Explicit don'ts / rejected configs (973 claims)


**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — What is NATS**

- Core NATS "is a fire-and-forget messaging system. It will only hold messages in memory and will never write messages directly to disk."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Subject-Based Messaging**

- "you should refrain from over-complicating your subject design at the start of the project."
- "Name business or physical entities. Refrain from encoding too much data into the subject." "Encode (business) intent into the subject, not technical details." Pragmatic: `orders.online.store123.order171711`; not useful: a 11-token subject encoding server, payment, tier, carrier, verb.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Sequence Numbers (concept)**

- Persisted-message systems solve this too "but sometimes are overkill for the problem at hand and usually cause additional management and operational cost."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream (concept overview)**

- "NATS does not intend to compete with the feature set of such tools" (in-memory DBs, deployment tools); goal is a reasonably complete data storage/replication set for microservices, edge, server management.
- "Rather than defaulting to the maximum, we suggest selecting the best option based on the use case behind the stream." Typical: file-based R=3; easily rebuilt/temporary streams can be memory R=1; R=5 is the replication factor limit.
- "most processing is not idem-potent and requires higher qualities of service ... you will want to use acknowledged consumers."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Streams**

- InterestPolicy with zero consumers deletes messages immediately: "consumers need to be bound to the stream ahead of messages being published"; deleted once acked by all consumers filtering on the subject.
- Limits still apply under Interest/WorkQueue: with MaxMsgs and default discard old, "messages will be automatically deleted even if the consumer did not receive them."
- In WorkQueue streams, messages that hit the consumer's `MaxDeliver` "will remain in the stream and must be manually deleted via the JetStream API."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Consumers**

- Granular permissions: single filter uses `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.{stream}.{consumer}.{filter}`; multiple filters use `$JS.API.CONSUMER.DURABLE.CREATE.{stream}.{consumer}` without the filter token, so "Use a different strategy for granular permissions."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Headers**

- "`Nats-` is a reserved namespace. Please use a different prefix for your own headers."
- Fast-ingest (2.14) is selected by reply subject ending `.$FI`, can combine with dedup headers, "MUST NOT be combined with atomic batch publish."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Source and Mirror Streams**

- Source/mirror are one-way replication, not full sync; "Quickly deleting messages after publishing them may result in inconsistent replication due to the asynchronous nature".
- Sourcing from WorkQueue/Interest streams supported since 2.14 with a visible durable consumer; before 2.14 it is "not supported ... the behavior is undefined" though not forbidden.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Object Store (concept)**

- "Object store is not a distributed storage system. All files in a bucket will need to fit on the target file system."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Subject Mapping and Transforms**

- Strict ordering otherwise requires "one at a time" per consumer/queue-group via max acks pending, "which in turn hurts scalability".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Administration (cluster)**

- "Peer-removing nodes from the cluster is a destructive operation, and decreases the size of the cluster." The node should be offline; if online, JetStream is disabled on it; it must not restart under the same `server_name` if its disk was wiped.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Super-cluster with Gateways**

- "all servers of this cluster need to have a gateway configuration with the same name" and "every gateway node needs to be able to connect to any other gateway node and vice versa. Everything else is considered a misconfiguration."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Gateway Configuration**

- Certificate rotation: clusters rarely rotate at the same time; "Make sure that the ca_file contains both old and new root or intermediate CAs." Using only the CA from an issuance bundle "is ill-advised"; keep a separate verification bundle so "when DC-B rolls before DC-A, it will not be cut off from your supercluster." Reload config to apply.
- Behind a load balancer set `advertise` to the LB hostname/port; "Otherwise, they will advertise their own private IP and port, and can generate failures and downtime if any reconnection is required."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Leaf Nodes**

- "If one node in a cluster is configured as leaf node, all nodes need to. Likewise, if one server in a cluster accepts leaf node connections, all servers need to."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — LeafNode Configuration**

- `handshake_first: true` must be set on both accepting side and remote; a mismatch fails the connection in either direction.
- WebSocket leaf remotes (2.2.0): all URLs in a list must be `ws`; mixing `ws` and `nats` prevents startup. TLS is decided by presence of a tls config, not by `wss://`.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream on Leaf Nodes (domains)**

- "Every server in a cluster and super cluster needs to have the same domain name"; domains can change only across a leaf node connection; domain names must be unique.
- Regular message flow is not restricted by domains: if streams in two domains (same account) subscribe to the same subject, both store the message while the leaf link is up. Avoid with different subjects, different accounts, or isolated accounts.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Configuring JetStream (resource management)**

- Without accounts enabled, "all users in the server would have access to JetStream." Per-account limits: `max_mem`, `max_file`, `max_streams`, `max_consumers` (example 512M / 1G / 10 / 100).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Configuration (server config reference)**

- "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."
- "each JetStream enabled server MUST use its own individual storage directory"; "JetStream does not implement standby and fault tolerance through a shared file system"; shared directories: "Access conflicts are not detected. We do not recommend such a setup."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Enabling Monitoring**

- "`nats-server` does not have authentication/authorization for the monitoring endpoint. When you plan to open your nats-server to the internet make sure to not expose the monitoring port as well." Monitoring binds `0.0.0.0` by default; bind to localhost or firewall it.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Multi Tenancy using Accounts**

- "think of one account as a messaging container for one application ... more accounts with few (even one) clients is a better design topology than a large account with many users with complex authorization configuration."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Authorization**

- "It is important to not break request-reply patterns": add `_INBOX.>` rules, or use `allow_responses`. Unauthorized pub/sub fails, is logged, and errors back to the client.
- With `allow_responses` "the reply subject is not constrained to the publish allow or deny list"; for explicit control "do not use allow_responses and instead define allow/deny lists under the publish permission map."
- Any client allowed to subscribe to `_INBOX.>` "can receive all responses published"; sensitive installs should narrow the inbox prefix or use accounts for isolation.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Enabling TLS**

- TLS `timeout`: increase if clients disconnect during handshake, but "an extended timeout exposes your server to attacks where a client doesn't upgrade to TLS and thus consumes resources."
- Self-signed certs: "DO NOT USE these certificates in production!!!" Use a public CA if outsiders connect, in-house CA for internal apps, environment CA (e.g. Kubernetes) for a single environment.
- Cluster advertises IPs by default, which "may result in a failed TLS hostname verification with an IP SANs error"; set `advertise`/`cluster_advertise` to verifiable names.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Account lookup using Resolver / Memory Resolver**

- NATS-based resolver stores JWTs in a local, not shared, directory ("you can't have more than one nats-servers using the same directory"); all servers in the cluster/super-cluster must use it; sync is eventually consistent via the system account.
- `cache` resolver: LRU subset, `limit 1000`, `ttl "2m"`; "does NOT accept account push messages from nsc and therefore is not suitable for stand-alone operation without a full resolver present."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Auth Callout**

- Order: implement the service, plan migration, then configure; "enabling the configuration before deploying a service could cause issues for existing systems."
- In centralized mode "existing users defined in the config file will be ignored"; the auth service must authenticate all users including system account users and the implicit no-auth user, so port users first.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Slow Consumers**

- `write_deadline` can be raised (example `2s`) for bursts, but "Be sure you are not just postponing a slow consumer error." "Increasing buffer sizes is not typically recommended unless you are handling temporary bursts of data. Often, increasing buffer capacity will only postpone slow consumer problems."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Profiling NATS**

- Profiling "is an advanced operation for development purposes only"; use the monitoring port for day-to-day stats.
- The `prof_port` endpoint has no auth, binds `0.0.0.0` by default, must not be exposed to the internet; it does not support config reload.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Naming Streams, Consumers, and Accounts**

- Guidelines: alphanumeric; no spaces/tabs/`.`/`>`/`*`; no path separators; "keep names under 32 characters"; avoid reserved file names (NUL, LPT1); "some file systems are case insensitive so do not use stream or account names that would collide" (`Foo` vs `foo` on Windows/macOS).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Disaster Recovery**

- "For R1 streams, data is persisted on one server node only. If that server node is unrecoverable then recovery from backup is the sole option."
- "Memory storage streams do not support snapshots. Only file-based storage streams can be backed up."
- Administering interactively with the CLI leaves no desired state to recreate from: "This is not the ideal way to administer the server, we recommend Configuration Management".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Monitoring (endpoints reference)**

- Monitoring has no auth and binds `0.0.0.0` by default; don't expose it to the internet.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Environmental considerations**

- Load balancers are possible "but you don't need to": NATS balances across seed URLs (clients randomize DNS A records) and reconnects automatically. "If you have a cluster with 3 seed nodes you often get more network throughput than going through a load balancer".
- "if you want to use TLS for authentication you do not want the load balancer to be the TLS termination point."
- "Client connections and routes are permanent. Therefore a load balancer will not distribute messages from one client connections between servers"; a common failure is "redundant, but disconnected (non-clustered) servers to which the clients will randomly connect." Advertising must be off or point at the LB address.
- Load balancers can cause idle-detection, packet-inspection protocol, and ephemeral-port problems at scale; routes or gateways through LBs "could results in JetStream lost quorum periods and create undue re-synchronization and protocol overhead traffic."
- In public clouds "you get what you pay for": non-network-optimized instances may give 10 Gb/s for ~30 minutes then drop (e.g. to 5 Gb/s); choose network-optimized instances for sustained bandwidth. Local SSD gives best latency; network block storage (EBS) can give highest throughput but general-purpose tiers burst then drop IOPS; choose IO-optimized storage for sustained IOPS.
- Container resource limits: nats-server uses resources in proportion to traffic and bursts; set limits accordingly or the orchestrator kills it. It "will try to use all host memory, not the resource limits set for the container, unless you specify GOMEMLIMIT" (available in the official Helm charts).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Running**

- JetStream default store is /tmp; "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Installing (hardware requirements)**

- "We highly recommend testing to see if smaller, cheaper machines suffice for your workload - often they do!" Start small and adjust after load testing; ensure a sufficient NIC.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — MQTT**

- Clustered retained messages are best-effort: "applications that rely on the presence of a retained message should connect on the server that produced them." Replication factor is set automatically from cluster size.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Anatomy of a NATS Client Application**

- Core subscribers "must be able to keep up with the flow of messages ... or it will otherwise become a slow consumer".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Connecting to a Cluster / timeouts / misc / name / noecho / ping-pong / security**

- `max_control_line` limits combined subject + queue group length; "It is not recommended to set this to a value that is higher than the one of other clients or the nats-server."
- Tokens "are only as safe as they are secret ... It is highly recommended to use one of the other NATS authentication mechanisms."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Reconnect: buffer, disable, events, max, random, wait**

- "The Core NATS client libraries try as much as possible to be fire and forget, and you should use JetStream functionalities to get higher qualities of service" when connection interruptions drop messages.
- Thundering herd: "all of the clients try to reconnect immediately, thus creating a denial of service attack"; libraries randomize server order so "no one server bears the brunt"; randomization can be disabled.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Events: connection events, slow consumers (client side)**

- Pending limits (count and bytes, e.g. 1,000 messages or 5mb) help with bursty publishers, not continuous mismatch; "Disabling these limits can be dangerous in production" and setting them to 0 "is also a dangerous proposition in production."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Developing with JetStream**

- "Using streaming and its associated higher qualities of service is the facet of messaging with the highest cost in terms of compute and storage."
- "no assumptions should ever be made of who will receive and process data in the future, or for what purpose."
- For request-reply, "Relying on a messaging system to resend here is considered an anti-pattern."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — JetStream Getting Started / Using Source**

- Default store is /tmp; "the best place to store JetStream data would be locally on a fast SSD. One should specifically avoid NAS or NFS storage for JetStream."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — Key Value Store (developer guide) / Object Store (developer guide)**

- History default 1; "The maximum history size is 64, if you need more your use case will be better implemented using the Stream functionality directly (where you can set the max number of messages per subject to any value you want)".

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — NATS API Reference (JetStream wire API)**

- "If this subject [`$JS.FC.<stream>.>`] is not forwarded, the consumer my stall under high load." If `$JS.ACK.<stream>.>` is not forwarded, pull consumers with ack `all`/`explicit` fail.
- "Do not delete and recreate the original stream! Please flush/purge the stream instead. The target stream remembers the last sequence id to be delivered. A delete will reset the sequence ID."
- `$JS.FC` is not domain-prefixed, so "identically named streams in different domains cannot be reliably sourced/mirrored into the same account. Please create unique stream names".
- Flow control messages (`NATS/1.0 100 FlowControl Request`) "must be replied to, otherwise the consumer may stall"; Synadia clients handle it (`msg.Respond(nil)`).

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — nats bench (benchmarking guide)**

- Benchmarks can fill streams quickly; purge or delete `benchstream` afterwards to reclaim memory and files. Changing stream attributes between runs requires deleting the stream.

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — nsc (basics, streams, services, signing keys, revocation, managed operators), NATS tools overview**

- "if someone gets a hold of an account or operator nkey they can do everything you can do as you."

**Source class: Legacy NATS docs (nats-io/nats.docs) — In Depth JWT Guide**

- NKEY backups "should therefore best be offline and access to them should be severely restricted"; identity NKEYs "should be archived and then removed" from the nsc store once signing keys exist, so a breach doesn't force "a flag-day change-over of identities."
- After `nsc push`, if fewer servers respond than exist "it is best practice to resolve this issue and retry"; if only one server holds a new account and dies, "the pushed account is not available to the network at large" so "make sure that initially, more servers respond than what you are comfortable with losing".
- Sign-up requestor credentials: "Do not use this JWT/NKEY for anything else but contacting the sign up service"; allow publish only to the well-known subject; back up the account signing NKEY so requestors need not be replaced.
- System account: "It is NOT recommended to use this account to facilitate communication between your own applications. Its sole purpose is to facilitate communication with and between nats-server."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-7: NATS Server Error Codes**

- Do not parse error description strings: "If users are parsing our error strings it means our error text form part of the Public API, we can never improve errors."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-11: Hostname resolution**

- Rationale: "Some users have DNS where the order almost never change ... would cause all clients to connect to the same server."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-17: Ordered Consumer**

- Cannot be a pull consumer, durable, bind/direct, or use queue/deliver groups.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-18: URL support for all client options [STALE?]**

- Client authors decided NOT to encode connect options in URLs: URLs "could expose sensitive information in logs", parity across clients "would be forever churn", and URL-vs-option precedence is ambiguous.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-19: API prefixes for materialized JetStream views**

- Implication: JetStream must "NOT start the first token after the API prefix with `$`"; "JetStream will never expose any functionality under `$JS.API.$KV.>`."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-15: JetStream Subscribe Workflow [STALE?]**

- "If a queue name is provided, configuring heartbeat or flow control is a mistake, since the server would send those message to random members."
- "For pull subscriptions ack policy of "none" or "all" is an error."
- Errors to raise: non-queue sub on a consumer with `DeliverGroup`; queue name mismatch with `DeliverGroup`; pull sub on a consumer with `DeliverSubject`; "only a deliver subject can be changed for an existing JS consumer."
- Auto-deleting a library-created consumer on Unsubscribe/Drain breaks queue groups: the first member creates it and deleting it "will cause member2 to stop receiving messages."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-28: JetStream RePublish**

- Loop prevention only checks the immediate stream: "It is possible to create a loop condition between two streams sharing an overlap in republish destinations and subject filters within a single account."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-31: JetStream Direct Get**

- `mirror_direct` "is captured on the mirror at create time and is not automatically refreshed when the upstream's `allow_direct` changes later"; operator must update upstream AND re-issue `STREAM.UPDATE` on each mirror. "it's suggested that users always set `mirror_direct` to their desired value."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-32: Service API**

- "Handler subject does not contain the `$SRV` prefix. This prefix is reserved for internal handlers."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-33: Metadata for Stream and Consumer**

- "`_nats` is a reserved prefix" for server/client internals; "Server can lock its metadata to be immutable and deny any changes." Example `_nats.mirror.domain`.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-34: JetStream Consumers Multiple Filters**

- "Subjects can't overlap each other and have to fit the interest of the Stream. In case of overlapping subjects, error (10136) will be returned."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-37: JetStream Simplification**

- Problem with legacy API: clients "create and update a consumer definition on the fly as `subscribe()` ... is invoked. This leads to some unexpected behaviors as different clients ... attempt to consume from the same consumer." Also forced Push vs Pull choice.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-38: OCSP Peer Verification**

- Adding OCSP responder dependency "necessarily adds a single point of failure (SPOF) from the NATS Server point of view and will in any case slow overall connection time"; mitigated by a local response cache.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-39: Certificate Store**

- `cert_store` replaces `cert_file`/`key_file`; configuring both errors at startup: `'cert_file' and 'cert_store' may not both be configured`; `key_file` is ignored if `cert_store` is set.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-42: Pull Consumer Priority Groups**

- "In the initial implementation we should limit `PriorityGroups` to one per consumer only and error should one be made with multiple groups." Group names must match ADR-6 `limited-term` "and may not exceed 16 characters."
- "This is only supported on Pull Consumers, configuring this on a Push consumer must raise an error."
- "we cannot support updating a consumer from one with groups to one without and vice versa ... We also cannot switch between different policies." Only `PriorityTimeout` is updatable today.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-43: JetStream Per-Message TTL**

- Unparsable values, or durations "below the 1 second minimum (including a literal `0`)", cause an error in the Pub Ack and the message is discarded (err_code 10165 `invalid per-message TTL`). Publishing `Nats-TTL` to a stream with the feature disabled → 10166 `per-message TTL is disabled`.
- "Mirrors may not enable `SubjectDeleteMarkerTTL` since it would insert new messages into the Stream it might make it impossible to match sequences" (err 10052 `subject delete markers forbidden on mirrors`).

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-44: Versioning for JetStream Assets**

- "tools like Terraform and NACK will need to understand to ignore these fields when doing their remediation loops."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-48: TTL Support for Key-Value Buckets (updates ADR-8)**

- "do not accept a TTL for other API ... a TTL on `Put()` might mean older revisions could come back from the dead once the TTL expires."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-49: JetStream Distributed Counter CRDT**

- Counter streams reject messages without `Nats-Incr`; reject messages carrying `Nats-Rollup`, `Nats-Expected-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Subject-Last-Sequence`, `Nats-Expected-Stream`, or `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id`; `Nats-Incr` to a non-counter stream is rejected.
- Resets: "a purge will not replicate, a roll-up would replicate and destroy the entire counter everywhere so the only real option is to publish a negative value"; preferred reset = negative value then purge up to that message; subject purge only for full deletes.
- Config restrictions: error on Mirror; only Limits retention; "can only be enabled during creation"; no Discard New; not with Per-Message TTL; "Message schedules (see ADR-51) are not supported"; requires API level 2.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-50: JetStream Batch Publishing**

- "If a stream is operating on the `PersistMode: async` mode, any batch published to it must fail" (atomic). `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` unsupported in batches. Dedup via `Nats-Msg-Id` supported "Starting from 2.12.1"; duplicates reject the batch.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-51: JetStream Message Scheduler**

- "If a message is made with a schedule in the past it is immediately sent. If a server was down for a month and a scheduled message is recovered ... it will be sent immediately. To avoid this, add a `Nats-TTL` header."
- Config `allow_msg_schedules`: denied on Source or Mirror; "Stream should not support Discard New"; "can be enabled on existing streams but not disabled"; requires API level 2; implicitly enables `AllowRollup` and clears `DenyPurge` (server auto-applies `Nats-Rollup: sub` to schedules, so a new schedule on the same subject replaces the prior one).
- Retention interaction: "Once a schedule message is removed from storage, by any mechanism, its schedule stops firing" (MaxAge shorter than the interval, MaxMsgs/MaxBytes/DiscardOld, WorkQueue ack, Interest with no interest). "**Limits** is the simplest configuration ... recommended."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-52: No Headers support for Direct Get [STALE?]**

- Proposed `no_hdr` option on `JSApiMsgGetRequest` to return body only (motivated by ADR-49 counters); "headers like `Nats-Sequence` will also be unset." Not implemented; superseded by nothing (ADR-31 remains the Direct Get spec).

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-56: JetStream Consistency Models**

- "this mode cannot support batch publishing at all" (atomic batches; ADR-50 later allows fast-ingest with async).
- "Setting it on anything other than a R1 stream will result in an error"; stated verbatim: "Scaling a R1 stream up to greater resiliency levels will fail if the `PersistMode` is not set to `async`" (ADR wording; reads as if intended "is set to async"). Default is unset/`default` and the server leaves it unset in INFO; any explicit value requires API level 2.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-58: Key-Value Store Roadmap and future considerations (updates ADR-8)**

- "The existing domain based mirrors that are supported in KeyValueConfig will be deprecated but supported for the foreseeable future."
- Mirrors "are not called `Bucket` and may not have the `KV_` string name prefix as they are not buckets ... we have done this in the leafnode mode and decided it's not a good pattern." Requires `mirror_direct: true` and origin `allow_direct`; "We should also set the options to deny deletes and purges."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-8: JetStream based Key-Value Stores**

- TTL accepted only on `Create()` (not `Put`) because Put "might have the effect of surfacing history once the latest value is removed."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-59: JetStream Stream Sourcing and Mirroring**

- "Mirror configuration **cannot be changed** after creation"; promote a mirror by removing the origin's subjects, then removing the mirror config and adding the subjects to the former mirror.
- Mirrors cannot use: `subjects`, `sources`, `first_seq`, `allow_msg_counter`, `allow_atomic`, `allow_msg_schedules`, `subject_delete_marker_ttl`. Mirrors can use: stream-level `subject_transform`, `republish`, `compression`, `allow_msg_ttl`.
- Sourced streams cannot use `mirror` or `allow_msg_schedules`.
- "Cycle detection **does not** apply across external streams in different domains. It is the operator's responsibility to ensure that cross-domain configurations do not create replication cycles." Within an account the server prevents cycles when subjects overlap.
- "Work queue streams are **not recommended** as upstream streams" (replication consumers "bypass the work queue's subject overlap validation", breaking single-consumer-per-partition). "Interest retention streams are **not recommended**" (messages may be removed while the replication consumer is absent). Limits retention "is the recommended and best-supported."

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-60: JetStream reliable stream sourcing/mirroring on WQ/Interest streams (updates ADR-59)**

- With `AckFlowControl` "the consumer cannot have an `AckWait` or `BackOff` setting ... or an error will be returned"; "`MaxDeliver` must be set to `-1`."
- "WorkQueue streams don't allow having multiple consumers with overlapping filter subjects" so a durable sourcing consumer blocks other overlapping consumers; "an Interest or Limits stream should be used" in that case.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-61: Unsafe meta group quorum rescue for disaster recovery**

- Disaster trap: grow 3→5 for a migration, turn off the 2 extras without peer-removing, then lose one original: "only 2 peers remain reachable, the metagroup loses quorum ... With no quorum there is no leader to process a peer-remove either."
- "The API is intentionally unsafe. Lowering the meta quorum weakens the guarantees Raft relies on ... misuse against a not-actually-wedged meta layer can split-brain the meta group"; must be documented "as a last-resort disaster recovery tool." No client library changes.

**Source class: NATS ADRs (nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design) — ADR-62: JetStream desired state reconciliation**

- Pre-2.15 flaw: the Raft layer "automatically adds peers that it hears from ... During a scale-down, move, or peer-remove it means a peer that was meant to be evicted can silently reappear." Progress was inferred from peer-list shape ("more peers than configured replicas" meant "a move is in progress").
- Peer remove (`$JS.API.STREAM.PEER.REMOVE.<stream>` / `$JS.API.SERVER.REMOVE`): removes immediately and assigns a replacement if available, else "the group will run under-replicated"; removing the last (R1) peer "moves the stream to a new peer without preserving the data"; "Prefer evacuating a stream peer if it's still able to catch up." Valid no-quorum escape: peer-remove dead nodes then scale config down to match; "Be careful though with peer-removing liberally when peers are planned to come back ... it does not get re-added."
- Overlap rules: scale/retention changes may stack; "A move change while another move is in progress is not allowed"; "Scale or retention changes while a move is in progress is not allowed"; consumers can be scaled independently at any time (but may keep moving until stream ops finish).
- "Upgrading directly to 2.15 is **not recommended**"; path is 2.14 → 2.14-compat (adds desired-state encoding only) → 2.15; during mixed versions "any in-flight operation stalls" until all servers are on 2.15. Downgrading below 2.14-compat "is **not recommended**"; let pending changes settle first. Inconsistent state after a direct upgrade/downgrade "may be (partially) repaired by performing a rolling restart of all nodes while on the same version."

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — Core protocol and connection defaults (server/const.go)**

- Server warns when max_payload is set above 8 MiB and may reject it in future. `MAX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE = (8 * 1024 * 1024)`; comment "the size at which the server will warn about max_payload being too high. In the future, the server may enforce/reject max_payload above this value." (server/const.go:96-99)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream consumer validation rules (server/consumer.go checkConsumerCfg / addConsumerWithAssignment / checkNewConsumerConfig)**

- Consumer name/durable name can not contain '.', '*', '>', '\\', '/' (server/consumer.go:713-718)
- Consumer replicas may not exceed the parent stream's replicas (server/consumer.go:721-722)
- On Interest or WorkQueue retention streams, consumer replicas MUST equal stream replicas. Comment: "This is REQUIRED for now." (server/consumer.go:728-736)
- AckFlowControl requires: push (DeliverSubject), FlowControl=true, Heartbeat exactly 1s ("flow control ack policy heartbeat needs to be 1s"), MaxAckPending > 0, no AckWait/BackOff, no MaxDeliver (server/consumer.go:754-778)
- len(BackOff) must be <= MaxDeliver when MaxDeliver != -1 (server/consumer.go:782-783; also on update 2521-2522)
- Description max 4 KiB. `JSMaxDescriptionLen = 4 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:381; consumer.go:786)
- Push consumer: deliver subject must be literal (no wildcards), must be valid, must not form a delivery cycle back into the stream, MaxWaiting must be 0, MaxAckPending>0 requires ack policy != none, heartbeat if set must be >= 100ms (server/consumer.go:791-809)
- Pull consumer: AckNone not allowed on WorkQueue stream; RateLimit not allowed; Heartbeat not allowed; FlowControl not allowed; MaxRequestExpires if set must be >= 1ms; MaxRequestBatch may not exceed server `jetstream.limits.max_request_batch` (server/consumer.go:811-835)
- MaxAckPending may not exceed server limit, account limit, or stream consumer_limits.max_ack_pending; InactiveThreshold may not exceed stream consumer_limits.inactive_threshold (server/consumer.go:837-848)
- Direct consumers must be push and ephemeral (server/consumer.go:851-858)
- FilterSubject and FilterSubjects can not both be set (server/consumer.go:863-865); empty string in FilterSubjects rejected (server/consumer.go:872-876)
- Multiple filter subjects may not overlap (subset match in either direction) (server/consumer.go:881-888)
- DeliverPolicy/start conflicts: all/last/new/last_per_subject reject OptStartSeq or OptStartTime; by_start_sequence requires OptStartSeq and rejects OptStartTime; by_start_time requires OptStartTime and rejects OptStartSeq; last_per_subject requires a filter subject (server/consumer.go:899-946)
- FlowControl without Heartbeat rejected (server/consumer.go:956-957)
- If both Durable and Name set they must match (server/consumer.go:960-964)
- Metadata total (sum of key+value lengths) max 128 KiB. `JSMaxMetadataLen = 128 * 1024` (server/jetstream_api.go:385; consumer.go:966-972)
- Priority policy: not allowed on push consumers; requires at least one PriorityGroups entry; group names must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9/_=-]{1,16}$`. Conversely PriorityGroups or PinnedTTL with policy none are rejected (server/consumer.go:974-998)
- Consumer creation rejected when the stream placement has a `preferred` server: "preferred server not permitted in placement" (server/consumer.go:1000-1003)
- Create with action=create on an existing consumer with a different config fails with "consumer already exists" (server/consumer.go:1088-1096)
- Max consumers per stream enforced from stream `max_consumers` or the account limit, whichever is more restrictive ("if account limits is more restrictive than stream config we prefer the account limits") (server/consumer.go:1121-1136)
- WorkQueue streams: consumers must be AckExplicit (or AckFlowControl); must be DeliverAll; a second consumer must have a filter and its filter must not overlap with any existing consumer's filters (partition must be unique). Pre-2.9.7 servers missed some overlap orderings ("foo.*.bar" then "foo.>"); on recovery such a consumer is only warned about and "should be administratively deleted" (server/consumer.go:1140-1176)
- Durable name max 255 chars. `JSMaxNameLen = 255` "Picked 255 as it seems to be a widely used file name limit" (server/jetstream_api.go:388-389; consumer.go:1216-1219)
- Immutable on consumer update: deliver policy, storage type (memory), start sequence, start time, ack policy, replay policy, heartbeat, flow control, max waiting; can not switch pull<->push; changing deliver subject to one with existing interest fails (server/consumer.go:2467-2525)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream stream defaults and size constants (server/stream.go, server/jetstream.go, server/jetstream_api.go)**

- Maximum stream replicas. `StreamMaxReplicas = 5` (server/stream.go:730); rejected with "maximum replicas is 5" (server/stream.go:1733-1734). Replicas default to 1 when 0 (server/stream.go:1730-1731)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream stream validation rules (server/stream.go checkStreamCfgLocked / configUpdateCheckLocked)**

- Stream name required, can not contain '.', '*', '>', '\\', '/' (server/stream.go:1692-1693); max 255 chars (1695-1696); description max 4096 (1698-1699); metadata max 131072 bytes (1706-1707)
- MaxAge must be 0 or >= 100ms ("max age needs to be >= 100ms") (server/stream.go:1772-1773)
- Duplicates window can not be larger than MaxAge, can not exceed server `jetstream.limits.duplicate_window`, and must be >= 100ms if set (server/stream.go:1797-1806)
- `deny_purge` with `allow_rollup_hdrs` rejected: "roll-ups require the purge permission" (server/stream.go:1808-1810)
- Counter streams (`allow_msg_counter`) can not use discard new, message TTLs, or message schedules, and must be limits retention (server/stream.go:1813-1826)
- `discard_new_per_subject` requires discard=new AND max_msgs_per_subject > 0 (server/stream.go:1829-1836; re-checked on update 2368-2375)
- `subject_delete_marker_ttl` must be >= 1s; non-pedantic auto-enables allow_msg_ttl and allow_rollup_hdrs (and clears deny_purge) (server/stream.go:1838-1855)
- Message schedules can not use discard new; auto-enable rollup (server/stream.go:1858-1868)
- Async persist mode only on file storage, only R1, and not with atomic batch publish (server/stream.go:1870-1880)
- Mirror streams can not set: first_seq, subjects, sources, allow_msg_counter, allow_atomic, allow_batched, allow_msg_schedules; mirror filter_subject and subject_transforms are mutually exclusive; subject delete markers forbidden on mirrors ("would result in new tombstones which would use up sequence numbers, diverging from the origin stream") (server/stream.go:1909-1953)
- Mirror subject transforms may not overlap each other (server/stream.go:1955-1969)
- Mirror max_msg_size can not be smaller than origin's (server/stream.go:1982-1985); source max_msg_size same rule (2083-2086)
- Sources: duplicate source (same name+filter+transform identity) rejected; filter_subject and subject_transforms mutually exclusive; transforms may not overlap; the same durable consumer can not be reused for multiple sources of the same stream; sources with message schedules rejected (server/stream.go:2013-2072)
- External delivery prefix must be a valid publish subject and must not collide with sourced stream subjects; external api prefix must not collide with `$JS.API` (server/stream.go:2100-2119)
- Source/mirror cycles are detected across streams ("detected cycle"), including cycles hidden behind mirrors (server/stream.go:2121-2163)
- Duplicate subjects rejected (server/stream.go:2184-2186)
- Capturing `>` requires `no_ack: true` AND replicas = 1 (server/stream.go:2188-2196)
- Subjects overlapping `$JS.>`, `$JSC.>`, `$NRG.>` (except `$JS.EVENT.>`) or `$SYS.>` (except `$SYS.ACCOUNT.>`) require `no_ack: true` (server/stream.go:2198-2211)
- A stream's own subjects may not overlap each other ("subject %q overlaps with %q") "which would cause duplicate entries (assuming no MsgID)" (server/stream.go:2212-2218)
- Stream needs at least one subject or be a source/mirror (server/stream.go:2225-2228)
- If the account tier has `max_bytes_required`, MaxBytes must be > 0; MaxBytes may not exceed the tier's per-stream byte limit (server/stream.go:2231-2235)
- Republish destination may not collide with the stream's subjects ("forms a cycle"); empty source means `>` (server/stream.go:2247-2284)
- `placement.preferred` is not permitted (server/stream.go:2291-2294)
- Standalone (non-clustered) server rejects replicas > 1 with JSStreamReplicasNotSupportedErr (server/stream.go:771-774, 2335-2338)
- On stream update, immutable: name, storage type, retention to/from workqueue ("Can only change retention from limits to interest or back"), unsealing, cancelling deny_delete, cancelling deny_purge, mirror config (except removing it to "promote" the mirror to a normal stream), disabling allow_msg_ttl, changing allow_msg_counter, disabling allow_msg_schedules, persist_mode (server/stream.go:2331-2394)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — RAFT (NRG) timing, quorum and backpressure (server/raft.go)**

- Scale-up peers with an empty log are forced into observer mode until they receive data from the leader: "We need to protect against losing state due to the new peers starting with an empty log. Therefore, these empty servers can't try to become leader until they at least have _some_ state." (server/raft.go:338-341, 640-648)
- `Recovering` flag: "If a server recovers with an empty log, we know to protect against data loss." (server/raft.go:333-336)
- RescueQuorum (unsafe, disaster-recovery): quorum can only be lowered, only when no leader is known, only on a voting non-observer member, and NEVER on a server with an empty log ("a lowered quorum could let it be elected off empty votes while the lost peers hold the only copies of the data... If all servers are empty, this requires a cluster bootstrap"); the rescue auto-expires after `rescueQuorumTimeout` (5 min) (server/raft.go:1248-1300)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream cluster placement and catch-up (server/jetstream_cluster.go)**

- Placement fails when fewer than r peers are eligible OR fewer than quorum (r/2+1) of them are online. `quorum := r/2 + 1` (server/jetstream_cluster.go:9566-9578). Error string: "no suitable peers for placement" plus reasons: peer offline, exclude tag set, insufficient storage, server tag not unique, miscellaneous issue, jetstream not enabled in cluster, tags not matched [...], tags excluded [...] (server/jetstream_cluster.go:9233-9282)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — Routes, gateways, leaf nodes (server/route.go, server/gateway.go, server/leafnode.go)**

- Insecure TLS on routes/gateways/leafnodes logs: "TLS certificate chain and hostname of solicited ... will not be verified. DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION!" (server/route.go:127-128, server/gateway.go:71, server/leafnode.go:46)
- Leaf loop detection: each account subscribes to a `$LDS.<nuid>` subject; seeing your own LDS subject come back over a leaf means a loop; error text "Loop detected for leafnode account=%q. Delaying attempt to reconnect for %v" and the connection is closed as a protocol violation (server/leafnode.go:58-59, 2497, 2963-2969, 3061-3073)
- Same cluster name on both ends of a leaf connection is rejected (ErrLeafNodeHasSameClusterName) with 30s reconnect delay (server/leafnode.go:3503-3509)
- JetStream over leaf nodes: `$JS.API.>`, `$KV.>`, `$OBJ.>` are denied on the leaf account unless the system account is shared, domains match, and extension is not disabled. "If domain names mismatch always deny." With different domains the log says "JetStream using domains: local %q, remote %q"; cross-domain access uses the `$JS.<domain>.API.>` mapping instead (server/leafnode.go:2034-2124)
- Extending JetStream via leaf node is mutually exclusive with a `default_js_domain` mapping to the empty domain: "As soon as one mapping to "" is found, disable the ability to extend JS via a leaf node." (server/leafnode.go:2040-2048)
- Guard against duplicate domain names: outgoing `$JS.<domain>.API.>` is denied on the leaf link when not extending, "This guards against a hub and a spoke having the same domain name. But not two spokes having the same one" (server/leafnode.go:2125-2134)

- Import authorization: "service import not authorized" / "stream import not authorized" when the exporter has not granted the importing account (server/accounts.go:1583-1586; server/errors.go:138-147)
- Stream import prefix can not contain wildcard tokens; duplicate stream imports rejected: "stream import prefix can not contain wildcard tokens", "stream import already exists" (server/errors.go:140-144)
- Service latency sampling must be 1-100: "bad sampling percentage, should be 1-100" (server/errors.go:118)
- Connection-level -ERR strings: "maximum payload exceeded", "maximum control line exceeded", "maximum connections exceeded", "maximum account active connections exceeded", "maximum subscriptions exceeded", "subject has exceeded number of tokens limit", "authentication timeout", "authentication expired", "credentials have been revoked", "reserved internal subject", "invalid publish subject", "subscribe permission violation", "no responders requires headers support", "attempted to connect to route port"/"leaf node port"/"gateway port" (server/errors.go:22-215)

- Peer-remove refuses when it would remove the only peer: "removing the only peer on a stream will result in data loss, use --force to force" (cli/stream_command.go:1092-1094)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — JetStream account limits, reservations and naming (server/jetstream.go, server/server.go)**

- Asset (stream/consumer) names may not contain whitespace, '.', '*', '>', '\\', '/'. `isValidAssetName` (server/jetstream.go:2811-2816); general names (domains, etc.) forbid whitespace, '.', '*', '>' (`isValidName` server/jetstream.go:2804-2809)
- Startup warnings: "Maximum payloads over 8.0 MB are generally discouraged and could lead to poor performance" (server/server.go:2349-2352); "Trusted Operators should utilize a System Account" (server/server.go:2346-2348); "The option `default_js_domain` is a temporary backwards compatibility measure and will be removed" (server/server.go:2354-2356); "Temporary storage directory used, data could be lost on system reboot" (server/jetstream.go:235)

**Source class: Code and tooling (nats-server, jsm.go, natscli) — Hot reload restrictions and misc server internals (server/reload.go, server/sublist.go, server/monitor.go)**

- Config reload is refused for: jetstream storage directory ("config reload not supported for jetstream storage directory"), switching from dynamic to fixed max memory/store ("...dynamic max memory and store"), decreasing max memory/store ("...decreasing jetstream max memory and store"), any max memory/store change while JS stays enabled, cluster host and cluster port (server/reload.go:1812-1822, 1855-1866, 1988-1997, 2783-2787)
- Subscribe is rejected with "subject has exceeded number of tokens limit" when `max_sub_tokens` is set and exceeded, and with "maximum subscriptions exceeded" at the account/user max_subscriptions (server/client.go:3087-3101)
- Queue-subscribe permissions: `allow = ["foo"]` permits plain or any queue sub; `allow = ["foo v1"]` permits only queue v1 on foo, no plain subs; queue group `_sys_` is reserved (server/client.go:3068-3083)
- Account max_connections and max_leafnodes: a CLIENT is refused with "maximum account active connections exceeded" when the account total is reached; a LEAF gets the same error at the leaf limit, or "leafnode loop detected" if the account already has a leaf from that remote cluster (server/client.go:897-908; server/accounts.go:590-602)

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — JetStream Anti-Patterns: Avoid these pitfalls to scale more efficiently**

- Consumer info is a monitoring/debugging call, not for operational decision-making. "intended to provide insights for monitoring or debugging"
- "Beyond 100,000 consumers, the potential for issues increases significantly." Consumers cost state management and cluster replication (Raft traffic, meta-leader load).
- Multiple disjoint subject filters per consumer arrived in 2.10, but "More than a few hundred disjoint subject filters will likely lead to slowness and instability." Cost: more subject indexing/matching and scanning more message blocks.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — How to Design NATS Subject Hierarchies (Patterns, Pitfalls & Best Practices)**

- Multi-dimensional patterns are "powerful but expensive"; don't adopt speculatively.
- Never put high-cardinality per-message data (correlation IDs, request IDs) in subjects; it burns the subject cache. "The right place for a correlation ID is a message header."
- Don't reuse `Nats-Msg-Id` as a correlation header; JetStream reserves it for dedup.
- Anti-patterns: flat subjects (no wildcards, no clean permissions, no filters); payload data in subjects; inconsistent casing/separators; no evolution plan. "Schemas change. If you haven't decided how, you've decided to break things."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Partitioned Consumer Groups in NATS JetStream: Ordered, Scalable Processing**

- `max_ack_pending = 1` restores strict order but serializes the whole stream: no throughput, single point of failure.
- A member drains all its partitions serially through one consumer; "piling more partitions onto a member is parked ownership, not added throughput."
- Pinning is affinity plus failover, not a distributed lock; windows exist where a client believes it is pinned after the server re-pinned, and buffered messages cannot be revoked. Handlers must be idempotent.
- Size partitions for peak future parallelism; raising later requires deleting the group and re-hashing every key.
- Cap the elastic work-queue buffer above one second of throughput; hitting `max_buffered_msgs`/`max_buffered_bytes` pauses sourcing for at least a second, causing periodic stalls.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Pull Consumer Priority Groups in NATS JetStream: Overflow, Pinned, and Prioritized Routing**

- Pinning is "not a hard guarantee"; an old client may believe it's pinned after the server moved on. Handler "must be idempotent."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Mirror, Merge, or Consume: How to Choose Your Edge-to-Core Streaming Pattern**

- Mirror is a full-copy operation: storage "scale[s] with edge volume rather than with actual consumption."
- Most common failure: "defaulting to mirror when consume would be more appropriate, because mirror feels safer." Result: a firehose where "downstream consumers ... end up doing in application code the filtering that should have happened at the ingest boundary."
- Inverse failure: consume when merge is needed, turning a unified query into "a distributed coordination problem that the application has to solve."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Stop Building Firehoses: Flow Control Isn't a Performance Optimization — It's an Architectural Decision**

- "Publish everything, let consumers filter" bakes routing into application code: "Each consumer receives the full stream and discards most of it"; the system is "Decoupled on the surface but is actually tightly coupled at the routing layer."
- Struggling edge systems share: client-side filtering, translation microservices, manual canaries, untested reconnection behavior after multi-hour disconnects.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Why "Just Retry" Will Kill Your Edge System**

- Retry assumes "the service was temporarily unavailable"; at the edge the failure mode is "the network doesn't exist right now and won't for… unknown hours." Retrying "burns CPU. It piles up in-memory state."
- Retry storms on reconnect: "every backed-up message hitting the core at once, overwhelming consumers who had no idea the edge was disconnected." "They're the predictable outcome of applying online-system thinking to offline-tolerant problems."
- "If you're pushing directly to an upstream queue or API without local durability, you have data degradation and loss risk."
- Tests must include disconnection; testing only always-on networks means "testing the happy path and shipping the edge case."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — You Don't Need Two Platforms: The Case for Hybrid Eventing**

- Bridge services between pub/sub and streaming platforms are a single point of failure and a "coordination seam"; the cost includes "deployment scripts, monitoring dashboards, credential configurations, client library versions."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — MQTT vs. NATS for Fleet Management: Hub-and-Spoke vs. Distributed Mesh**

- "Deploying a local MQTT broker solves the latency problem but creates a separate instance with its own configuration, ACLs, and monitoring." Federation risks "message loops, duplicates, and inconsistent topic namespaces"; bridges "can lose messages during disruptions or restarts."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Multi-Region Consistency: Have Your Cake and Eat it Too!**

- Virtual stream limits: no work-queue or interest retention (limits only); not for KV if the same key is modified from different regions; consumers are per-region (no global durable); message deletes are not propagated; no compare-and-set because read/write sequences differ.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Understanding JetStream Memory Usage Patterns**

- "Use fewer subjects per stream when possible"; "Long-lived consumers are more memory-efficient than short-lived ones"; separate meta leadership from nodes handling high-volume streams.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS for Retail: Manage Thousands of Nodes at the Edge by Reducing East-West Traffic**

- Leaf nodes "generally do not communicate directly with one another unless there's legitimate interest," but with JetStream subscription propagation creates overhead "particularly noticeable during startup": "when the Nth leaf node starts, it receives N-1 leaf subscriptions."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Rethinking Microservices: Using NATS to Dramatically Simplify Your Microservices**

- Production code should use cancellation tokens and "distributed locks or NATS optimistic concurrency control" for concurrency.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Per-Message TTL: Unlocking Ephemeral State Patterns in NATS**

- Pre-2.11 alternatives were "One stream/bucket per TTL tier" (fragmented), client-side expiry (error-prone, duplicated), or an extra datastore.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Mirror Streams in NATS JetStream: One-Way Replication Made Simple**

- Work-queue retention has only partial mirror support and is "not resilient over intermittent connections"; interest retention with mirrors is unsupported and undefined.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Atomic Batch Publishing in NATS 2.12: All-or-Nothing Message Guarantees**

- Batches rejected if: ID > 64 chars; sequence gaps; stream uses async persist mode; duplicate messages present (as of 2.12.1). Batches cannot cross streams.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Distributed Counters in NATS JetStream: A CRDT-Based Approach to Global Counting**

- Incompatible with counters: mirrors ("would replay raw deltas and double-count"), `DiscardNew`, Interest/WorkQueue retention, per-message TTL, `Nats-Rollup`, `Nats-Expected-*` headers. `AllowMsgCounter` "cannot be turned off." Subject purge does not replicate across sourced counters; reset by publishing a negative delta then purging.
- `Nats-Counter-Sources` grows with every source ever attached; subject transforms during sourcing may hide leaf subjects, so "mirror-then-source if you need both views." Typed Go API is in `orbit.go/counters`.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Delayed Message Scheduling in NATS JetStream**

- The `NakWithDelay` retry workaround "does not scale well when you have thousands of pending scheduled messages" because it ties up consumer state.
- `AllowMsgSchedules: true` "cannot be reverted" and cannot be enabled on source or mirror streams. Put `schedules.>` and delivery subjects in the same stream.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Monitoring NATS: From HTTP Scrapes to System Events**

- `nats sub '$SYS.>'` is fine for exploration; narrow subscriptions in production to avoid volume. Persist system events in JetStream for audit/replay. Surveyor collects system-account data into Prometheus without per-server HTTP ports or sidecars.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS Server 2.14 Release**

- Object store "currently uses async publish underneath and lacks proper flow control for concurrent uploads."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Recovering Quorum After Renaming Servers**

- Rename servers one at a time; remove the stale offline record before the next rename. Changing Helm `serverNamePrefix` during an upgrade renames all servers at once, doubling the recorded peer set and losing quorum. "This setting should only be changed before the first installation."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS at System Initiative**

- Synadia guidance: "you might not want to create and destroy thousands of durable JetStream consumers in short bursts."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS JetStream: Streams, Consumers, and Durable Messaging**

- Don'ts: assume MaxDeliver = DLQ; push by default; "one consumer for everything"; skip idempotency. "still plan for rare duplicates" even with Nats-Msg-Id dedup.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Deploying a scalable NATS cluster part 1: core architecture and considerations**

- Default max payload 1 MB; keep below 1 MB; 64 MB configurable but "generally advised against"; chunk or use external storage instead.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Building Distributed State Stores with NATS JetStream: KV and Object Storage Patterns**

- Don't embed volatile data in key names (`cache.response.{hash}.expires-{timestamp}`); use dots for hierarchy; watch with `*`/`>`.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Replace Redis with NATS: Atomic Counters and Microsecond Key-Value**

- Counter streams need `AllowMsgCounter: true`, `AllowDirect: true`, Limits retention set at creation only; cannot be mirrors; incompatible with per-message TTL; every subject becomes a counter.
- "The working set must fit in memory" for microsecond figures; "NATS is optimized for streaming, not random access"; high-churn random updates are slow because "overwriting a KV key deletes the previous message in the backing stream."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — From Solace to NATS: One Platform for Messaging, Streaming, and the Edge**

- Solace "exclusive queues with active/standby consumption and partitioned ordering require separate designs"; "Request-reply in NATS uses ephemeral inboxes."
- "NATS is a runtime platform. It does not ship a bundled event design environment"; plan for Event Portal replacement (AsyncAPI). Coexist via bridging; migrate "project by project rather than as a big-bang cutover."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Migrating from TIBCO to NATS: A Modernization Guide for Financial Services**

- "Do not deploy NATS the way you deployed RV daemons. It technically works to run a local NATS server per host and treat it as an `rvd`, but you forfeit most of the operational benefits."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — 14 factors of adaptive edge (part one)**

- Legacy brokers give "high-latency and inconsistent delivery of key data to or between edge clients"; apps are forced to "trombone" data to cloud data centers.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Your Perimeter Is Already Gone — Edge Security Isn't a Checkbox**

- Default/hardcoded and shared, unrotated credentials; compromised devices injecting plausible bad data for months; lateral movement via over-scoped credentials; supply-chain (BadBox 2.0 on "more than 10 million devices").

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — The Edge Isn't a Place — It's an Operating Reality**

- "Encrypt everything and trust the network" is perimeter thinking.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS and Certificate Authorities - Intermediate Rolls**

- "use the CA which signed your own cert" for peer validation is wrong; when Let's Encrypt rolls intermediates "this cluster B will no longer trust the certificates of clusters A or C", causing a supercluster schism.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — Rethinking the System of Record**

- Event logs are "optimized for writing, but when it comes to reading, we must go through the entire log"; ad hoc queries need materialized views.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — The cost of the stitched stack: why AI stalls before it reaches the edge**

- Typical cloud-edge stacks use "five vendors, three protocols, and a pile of bespoke glue" (message broker, IoT broker, replication middleware, protocol gateways, integration code) and end up "slow, expensive, and brittle"; "the bottleneck is rarely the model; it's the system wrapped around it."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS JetStream Explained: Streams, Consumers, and Durable Messaging (NATS Explorer)**

- Don't put "everything in JetStream just in case"; live dashboards on Core NATS, important subsets in streams; JetStream adds "disk I/O and ack overhead."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — The Real-Time Problem Hiding Inside Your AI Data Problem**

- Adding real-time paths one at a time creates N-squared connectivity; each hop has its own auth, retry, and ordering semantics; separate stacks for streams and requests "double operational surface."

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — NATS JetStream as a Durable Job Queue in .NET**

- "Publish the result FIRST, then ack the job." Crash before publish = redelivery; crash between publish and ack = harmless duplicate if processing is idempotent by job ID. Never ack before publishing results.

**Source class: Blog posts and articles — RPC vs NATS: It's Not About Sync vs Async — It's About Who Owns Completion**

- Publisher-side retry created duplicate orders "when the first publish actually succeeded but the ack was slow"; a consumer that partially committed then crashed had redelivery rejected by dedup, losing the order. Dedup check "has to be in the same transaction as the actual work."
- Don't use "Request-reply where the reply is supposed to happen later, via a different message." Failed messages need a DLQ; track lag, processing time, error rate, redelivery rate.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Jetstream Max Consumers per Stream**

- 50M traditional consumers per stream is not supported; consumers can be heavyweight state machines with consensus (NRG) — derekcollison. "you can not use a traditional consumer here"

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Ordering guarantees per entity**

- Automatic partition rebalancing (Kafka/Pulsar style) was not available out of the box in 2023 — arnarg (later addressed by Orbit pcgroups in 2025).

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Use thousands of leaf nodes at the edge**

- A central stream sourcing from 1000+ edge domains needs every edge listed in `sources` manually; no auto-discovery of leaf JetStream sources exists (as of 2025-12), acknowledged as a management gap — derekcollison.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Duplicate messages on a leafnode cluster connected to a supercluster**

- A leaf node bridges NATS systems; a super-cluster is a single system, so a leaf cluster must connect once to the super-cluster, not to each member cluster — derekcollison. "the LN connections from cluster 3 in Asia should only connect once to the supercluster, not to each cluster 1 & 2."

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — 2 Node High Availability cluster for nats stream**

- A 2-node JetStream cluster gives durability but blocks all streams when either server is down until both return — derekcollison. "if any of the servers has an issue the system and all streams will be blocked until both servers are back"

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Source stream from multiple leaf nodes**

- Do not create a 1:1 stream on the cloud side for every fleet member — derekcollison. "We do not recommend cloud side has a 1:1 stream for every fleet member."

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — locks/leases with KV similar to SETNX**

- "Exclusive worker token" pattern (inbox stream with MaxMsgsPerSubject=1 sourced into a WorkQueue stream with DiscardNewPerSubject) was tested in production and discarded: sourcing retries every 2 s while a token is held, flooding logs, and messages that exhaust MaxDeliver stay in the WorkQueue and block the subject — rafsawicki [UNVERIFIED, user report].

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — JetStream file-store ~65x slower than memory-store on KV mirror (83% of seq space is deleted)**

- Do not pass a `FilterSubject` that matches everything on a mirror: a mirror has no ingest subjects so the server cannot recognize the filter as "all", the 4x messages-vs-subjects heuristic uses the huge first/last range, and every message lookup does an expensive per-subject-state read. Removing the filter gave 150k+ msg/s — MauriceVanVeen. "best is to just not pass a filter subject if you don't intend on filtering"

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Automatic Message Payload Preservation in DLQ Stream**

- Including payloads in DLQ advisories was rejected on user feedback: payloads can be sensitive and advisories often leave NATS; a per-consumer opt-in might be acceptable — ripienaar.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Is $JS.ACK purposefully domain-unaware? Potential interference with leaf nodes**

- Identically named streams and consumers in different leaf domains sharing a hub can cross-talk on ACK subjects; workaround is deny rules on `$JS.ACK` across the leaf link — cbecker (asker workaround, confirmed problem by derekcollison).

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Leaf-node JetStream retention policy for hub-sourced streams**

- Some users run WorkQueue on the leaf origin stream, but there were reports of messages not cleaned up after long outages — derekcollison. [STALE?] (2.11 work planned)

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — What are strategies for moving a stream to a different set of nodes in the cluster?**

- Data loss risk: if R3 on 1,2,3 loses 1 and 4 joins, removing 2 before 4 has fully synced every stream in every account can lose data — ripienaar.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Hot scaling core NATS (no JetStream) for bursty traffic**

- Fargate is "not, imo, a good place to run nats"; EC2-style hosts are better for this workload — ripienaar.
- 18M subscriptions came from per-team subjects `usecase.$user_id`; collapse to `$team.$user.>` style namespacing to shrink the interest graph. "Just punting the hard work of having multiple teams onto the software will forever cause failures" — ripienaar.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Time-sensitive messages (expiry and deferred delivery)**

- Re-injecting a message with the same Nats-Msg-Id inside the dedup window makes it vanish; requires a new ID plus an Original-Id header — andreib1 [UNVERIFIED, user report].

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Should we use hostPath for jetstream cluster running in K8S**

- Do not use hostPath: a rescheduled pod lands on a node with no data and forces a full resync; use StatefulSet PVCs with SSD classes (gp3, premium-rwo) as the Helm chart does — MILLERMARRU [UNVERIFIED, non-maintainer, matches chart defaults].

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Inquiry on hardcoded stream state flush timeout to 2 minutes**

- Lowering sync did not prevent stale stream state after abrupt kill in the asker's test (issue 6600); single-node file streams are exposed to unclean shutdown — souravagrawal [UNVERIFIED].

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Prevent a NATS user from creating durable consumers**

- The API subject alone does not distinguish durable from ephemeral creation (both use `CONSUMER.CREATE.<stream>.<name>`), so a pure permission rule cannot block durables — 0xeb-bp [UNVERIFIED, protocol trace shown].

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — How to find number of subscriptions on jetstream**

- Core publishing into a stream subject works but returns no ack and gives no back pressure; use JetStream publish — Jarema.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Ephemeral Consumer Cleanup Rate? (nats.go)**

- Creating and discarding consumers at API-call rate "will not really work well"; use message get APIs (batched direct get, ADR-31 batches) instead — ripienaar.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Sourcing streams between hub and leaf instances, both directions (nats.go)**

- If the sourcing stream also lists the same subjects as the origin, and core traffic flows across the leaf link, both streams capture the message directly and the source adds it again, duplicating — jnmoyne. Fix: sourcing stream has no `subjects`, only `sources` with a filter — cbrake (verified).

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Aggregate KV? (nats.go)**

- When the source is itself a mirror, the transform source must use the ORIGIN bucket's subject prefix (`$KV.kv1.>`), not the mirror bucket's name; the CLI's automatic transform used the mirror name and yielded nothing — uli42 (verified fix).

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Need help in understanding MaxAckPending behaviour (nats.go)**

- Many long NAKs indicate a design problem; move such messages to a different stream rather than inflating MaxAckPending — kozlovic.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — How to resume fetching messages after restart (nats.go)**

- Unacked messages with MaxAckPending 10 and AckWait 1 h block delivery of the next messages after restart — zerlok (root cause of a similar report) [UNVERIFIED, plausible].

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — k8s: OOM killed when using JetStream WorkQueue on cpu:1 and mem:1GB machines (issue)**

- A 64 MiB max_payload (default 1 MB) drove large allocations; bring it back down and use Object store for large blobs — neilalexander.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Cluster size scalability question (issue)**

- One KV or stream per customer is "ultimately not a good design pattern"; 33,931 streams took over 10 minutes to restart on 48 CPUs because restore was serial; prefer few buckets with millions of hierarchical keys and per-user permissions on `$JS.API` subjects — jnmoyne, williamstein (measured).

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Cannot use Subscribe when ephemeral consumers reach ~30,000 (issue)**

- Creating and abandoning tens of thousands of consumers continuously prompted an architecture-review recommendation rather than a tuning fix — derekcollison.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Include payload in term advisories (issue)**

- Parked because of data-leakage feedback; blanket publishing of payloads "wouldn't help or work for many" — ripienaar.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — MQTT support should be horizontally scalable (issue)**

- "I would not recommend having 250k R3 consumers"; make them R1; do not use Ceph, use direct-attached or block storage like EBS — derekcollison.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — WorkQueue messages not deleted on non-leader nodes when used as mirror source (issue)**

- Removing from one stream never affects a source or mirror; sourcing from a WorkQueue is by design not a supported use — derekcollison, jnmoyne. "Work queue stream exist in order to provide exactly once consumption ... not really to be sourced from."

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Consumer and Stream Name Validation (ADR issue)**

- A space in a consumer name broke consumer creation with a cryptic error after a client upgrade — Jarema.

**Source class: GitHub discussions and issues — Removing records from KV that exceed the limit (LRU-style)**

- KV delete markers are messages too and may be the ones evicted by MaxMsgs; use the stream directly or `stream.purge` on the KV stream if that matters — jnmoyne.

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Supercluster Arbiter**

- Observed output (unexplained in narrative): in the recorded run the cross-cluster `stream add --cluster=west --replicas=3` failed with `nats: error: could not create Stream: raft: corrupt peer state (10049)`; the meta table at that moment showed `east-az3` with `Current false`, `Active 2.35s`, `Lag 3`, i.e. one peer not yet caught up shortly after startup. The narrative does not comment on this, so treat it as an observed timing artifact, not documented behaviour.

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Regional and Cross Region Streams (Supercluster)**

- Cross-region replication costs latency; accept the trade-off only for streams that are critical for availability and can tolerate somewhat higher latency. "This of course comes at a cost of latency, but this trade-off may be appropriate for streams that are critical for availability, but can tolerate slightly higher latencies."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Replace cluster nodes**

- The demo waits only 60 s after lame-ducking and another 60 s after peer removal before the next node; this is described as aggressive and demo-only. In practice the wait depends on how much data must be migrated. "This script choose a fairly aggressive wait time (for demo purpsoes) of only 60 seconds ... In practice, the wait time would be dependent on how much data needs to be migrated."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Private Inbox**

- Observed output: connecting with `--inbox-prefix _INBOX_joe` while the user is only allowed `_INBOX.>` fails with `Permissions Violation for Subscription to "_INBOX_joe.<random>"`; the custom prefix must be in the user's subscribe allow list.

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Private Inbox using JWT**

- A JWT user with only publish allows and no explicit subscribe allow can still subscribe to `>`, so joe could subscribe to `pam.>`; add an explicit `--allow-sub` to close this. "Since we didn't set an explicit allow for subscriptions, these users can still subscribe to `>` which means joe could subscribe to `pam.>` and vice versa."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Programmatic NKeys and JWTs**

- nsc stores and organizes every nkey and JWT for you; if you create accounts or users dynamically you must store and manage the keypairs and JWTs yourself. "If you opt to create accounts or users dynamically, keep in mind you need to store and manage the keypairs and JWTs yourself."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Limits-based Stream**

- By default no limits are set, "which would require manually managing the ever-growing stream." Turn limits on and let the server truncate if any of them fit.
- No two streams can have overlapping subjects, "otherwise the primary messages would be persisted twice."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Interest-based Stream**

- With no consumers, published messages are immediately deleted from an interest stream. "By definition, they are immediately deleted from the stream since there are no consumers."
- Interest retention is additive to stream limits; with `max-msgs` = 1 and discard-old, each new message deletes the prior one "regardless if any of the consumer subscriptions were available to process the message."
- A late consumer cannot retroactively show interest; messages deleted before it was created are gone. "this reinforces that a late consumer cannot retroactively show interest."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Work-queue Stream**

- Consumers on a work-queue stream must have non-overlapping (disjoint) filter subjects, unlike limits- and interest-based streams which support overlapping consumers. "if multiple consumers are bound to a work-queue stream, they must have disjoint filter subjects."
- Work-queue retention is additive to limits: with `max-msgs` = 1 and discard-old, every new message deletes the prior one regardless of whether any subscription processed it.
- A work-queue stream allows "at most one consumer with interest on a subject at any given time"; creating a second unfiltered consumer fails until the first is deleted.

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Pull Consumers**

- Messages within one batch are ordered relative to each other, but each subscriber handles its batch independently, so cross-subscriber order is not guaranteed. For deterministic partitioning "for scalable order processing" the text points to deterministic subject token partitioning (subject mapping).

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Pull Consumer - Applying Limits**

- Consumer configuration can be changed on demand, with one exception: `MaxWaiting` "cannot be updated on a consumer as of now. This must be set up front when the consumer is created."

**Source class: NATS by Example narratives + new docs Learn deep dives — Push Consumers (legacy)**

- Push consumers "can get unwieldy and confusing" when the subscriber cannot keep up, processing errors occur, or the subscription is interrupted: redeliveries interleave with newly pushed messages.
- Helper-created durables (SubscribeSync with nats.Durable) are deleted when `Unsubscribe` or `Drain` is called: "these helpers should only be used if neither of those methods are called."
